text_en_arberry: We have indeed turned about for men in this Koran every manner of similitude; man is the most disputatious of things.

text_ar: وَمَا مَنَعَ ٱلنَّاسَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوٓا۟ إِذْ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ رَبَّهُمْ إِلَّآ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ سُنَّةُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ قُبُلًۭا
text_en_primary: And nothing prevents people from believing when guidance comes to them and from seeking their Lord’s forgiveness except ˹their demand˺ to meet the same fate of earlier deniers or that the torment would confront them face to face.
text_en_yusufali: And what is there to keep back men from believing, now that Guidance has come to them, nor from praying for forgiveness from their Lord, but that (they ask that) the ways of the ancients be repeated with them, or the Wrath be brought to them face to face?
text_en_pickthall: And naught hindereth mankind from believing when the guidance cometh unto them, and from asking forgiveness of their Lord unless (it be that they wish) that the judgment of the men of old should come upon them or (that) they should be confronted with the Doom.
text_en_arberry: And naught prevented men from believing when the guidance came unto them, and seeking their Lord’s forgiveness, but that the wont of the ancients should come upon them, or that the chastisement should come upon them face to face.

text_ar: وَمَا نُرْسِلُ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ ۚ وَيُجَٰدِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِٱلْبَٰطِلِ لِيُدْحِضُوا۟ بِهِ ٱلْحَقَّ ۖ وَٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ ءَايَٰتِى وَمَآ أُنذِرُوا۟ هُزُوًۭا
text_en_primary: We do not send the messengers except as deliverers of good news and warners. But the disbelievers argue in falsehood, ˹hoping˺ to discredit the truth with it, and make a mockery of My revelations and warnings.
text_en_yusufali: We only send the apostles to give Glad Tidings and to give warnings: But the unbelievers dispute with vain argument, in order therewith to weaken the truth, and they treat My Signs as a jest, as also the fact that they are warned!
text_en_pickthall: We send not the messengers save as bearers of good news and warners. Those who disbelieve contend with falsehood in order to refute the Truth thereby. And they take Our revelations and that wherewith they are threatened as a jest.
text_en_arberry: And We send not the Envoys, but good tidings to bear, and warning. Yet do the unbelievers dispute with falsehood, that they may rebut thereby the truth. They have taken My signs, and what they are warned of, in mockery.

text_ar: وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّن ذُكِّرَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِۦ فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهَا وَنَسِىَ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ ۚ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَن يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًۭا ۖ وَإِن تَدْعُهُمْ إِلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ فَلَن يَهْتَدُوٓا۟ إِذًا أَبَدًۭا
text_en_primary: And who does more wrong than those who, when reminded of their Lord’s revelations, turn away from them and forget what their own hands have done? We have certainly cast veils over their hearts—leaving them unable to comprehend this ˹Quran˺—and deafness in their ears. And if you ˹O Prophet˺ invite them to ˹true˺ guidance, they will never be ˹rightly˺ guided.
text_en_yusufali: And who doth more wrong than one who is reminded of the Signs of his Lord, but turns away from them, forgetting the (deeds) which his hands have sent forth? Verily We have set veils over their hearts lest they should understand this, and over their ears, deafness, if thou callest them to guidance, even then will they never accept guidance.
text_en_pickthall: And who doth greater wrong than he who hath been reminded of the revelations of his Lord, yet turneth away from them and forgetteth what his hands send forward (to the Judgment) ? Lo! on their hearts We have placed coverings so that they understand not, and in their ears a deafness. And though thou call them to the guidance, in that case they can never be led aright.
text_en_arberry: And who does greater evil than he who, being reminded of the signs of his Lord, turns away from them and forgets what his hands have forwarded? Surely We have laid veils on their hearts lest they understand it, and in their ears heaviness; and though thou callest them to the guidance, yet they will not be guided ever.

text_ar: وَرَبُّكَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ذُو ٱلرَّحْمَةِ ۖ لَوْ يُؤَاخِذُهُم بِمَا كَسَبُوا۟ لَعَجَّلَ لَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابَ ۚ بَل لَّهُم مَّوْعِدٌۭ لَّن يَجِدُوا۟ مِن دُونِهِۦ مَوْئِلًۭا
text_en_primary: Your Lord is the All-Forgiving, Full of Mercy. If He were to seize them ˹immediately˺ for what they commit, He would have certainly hastened their punishment. But they have an appointed time, from which they will find no refuge.
text_en_yusufali: But your Lord is Most forgiving, full of Mercy. If He were to call them (at once) to account for what they have earned, then surely He would have earned, then surely He would have hastened their punishment: but they have their appointed time, beyond which they will find no refuge.
text_en_pickthall: Thy Lord is the Forgiver, Full of Mercy. If He took them to task (now) for what they earn, He would hasten on the doom for them; but theirs is an appointed term from which they will find no escape.
text_en_arberry: But thy Lord is the All-forgiving, full of mercy. If He should take them to task for that they have earned, He would hasten for them the chastisement; but they have a tryst, from which they will find no escape.

text_ar: وَتِلْكَ ٱلْقُرَىٰٓ أَهْلَكْنَٰهُمْ لَمَّا ظَلَمُوا۟ وَجَعَلْنَا لِمَهْلِكِهِم مَّوْعِدًۭا
text_en_primary: Those ˹are the˺ societies We destroyed when they persisted in wrong, and We had set a time for their destruction.
text_en_yusufali: Such were the populations we destroyed when they committed iniquities; but we fixed an appointed time for their destruction.
text_en_pickthall: And (all) those townships! We destroyed them when they did wrong, and We appointed a fixed time for their destruction.
text_en_arberry: And those cities, We destroyed them when they did evil, and appointed for their destruction a tryst.

text_ar: وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِفَتَىٰهُ لَآ أَبْرَحُ حَتَّىٰٓ أَبْلُغَ مَجْمَعَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ أَوْ أَمْضِىَ حُقُبًۭا
text_en_primary: And ˹remember˺ when Moses said to his young assistant, “I will never give up until I reach the junction of the two seas, even if I travel for ages.”
text_en_yusufali: Behold, Moses said to his attendant, "I will not give up until I reach the junction of the two seas or (until) I spend years and years in travel."
text_en_pickthall: And when Moses said unto his servant: I will not give up until I reach the point where the two rivers meet, though I march on for ages.
text_en_arberry: And when Moses said to his page, ’I will not give up until I reach the meeting of the two seas, though I go on for many years.

text_ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَا مَجْمَعَ بَيْنِهِمَا نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا فَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُۥ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ سَرَبًۭا
text_en_primary: But when they ˹finally˺ reached the point where the seas met, they forgot their ˹salted˺ fish, and it made its way into the sea, slipping away ˹wondrously˺.
text_en_yusufali: But when they reached the Junction, they forgot (about) their Fish, which took its course through the sea (straight) as in a tunnel.
text_en_pickthall: And when they reached the point where the two met, they forgot their fish, and it took its way into the waters, being free.
text_en_arberry: Then, when they reached their meeting, they forgot their fish, and it took its way into the sea, burrowing.

text_ar: فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَا قَالَ لِفَتَىٰهُ ءَاتِنَا غَدَآءَنَا لَقَدْ لَقِينَا مِن سَفَرِنَا هَٰذَا نَصَبًۭا
text_en_primary: When they had passed further, he said to his assistant, “Bring us our meal! We have certainly been exhausted by today’s journey.”
text_en_yusufali: When they had passed on (some distance), Moses said to his attendant: "Bring us our early meal; truly we have suffered much fatigue at this (stage of) our journey."
text_en_pickthall: And when they had gone further, he said unto his servant: Bring us our breakfast. Verily we have found fatigue in this our journey.
text_en_arberry: When they had passed over, he said to his page, ’Bring us our breakfast; indeed, we have encountered weariness from this our journey.’

text_ar: قَالَ أَرَءَيْتَ إِذْ أَوَيْنَآ إِلَى ٱلصَّخْرَةِ فَإِنِّى نَسِيتُ ٱلْحُوتَ وَمَآ أَنسَىٰنِيهُ إِلَّا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُۥ ۚ وَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُۥ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ عَجَبًۭا
text_en_primary: He replied, “Do you remember when we rested by the rock? ˹That is when˺ I forgot the fish. None made me forget to mention this except Satan. And the fish made its way into the sea miraculously.”
text_en_yusufali: He replied: "Sawest thou (what happened) when we betook ourselves to the rock? I did indeed forget (about) the Fish: none but Satan made me forget to tell (you) about it: it took its course through the sea in a marvellous way!"
text_en_pickthall: He said: Didst thou see, when we took refuge on the rock, and I forgot the fish - and none but Satan caused me to forget to mention it - it took its way into the waters by a marvel.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’What thinkest thou? When we took refuge in the rock, then I forgot the fish-and it was Satan himself that made me forget it so that I should not remember it -- and so it took its way into the sea in a manner marvellous.’

text_ar: قَالَ ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنَّا نَبْغِ ۚ فَٱرْتَدَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًۭا
text_en_primary: Moses responded, “That is ˹exactly˺ what we were looking for.” So they returned, retracing their footsteps.
text_en_yusufali: Moses said: "That was what we were seeking after:" So they went back on their footsteps, following (the path they had come).
text_en_pickthall: He said: This is that which we have been seeking. So they retraced their steps again.
text_en_arberry: Said he, ’This is what we were seeking!’ And so they returned upon their tracks, retracing them.

text_ar: فَوَجَدَا عَبْدًۭا مِّنْ عِبَادِنَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ رَحْمَةًۭ مِّنْ عِندِنَا وَعَلَّمْنَٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّا عِلْمًۭا
text_en_primary: There they found a servant of Ours, to whom We had granted mercy from Us and enlightened with knowledge of Our Own.
text_en_yusufali: So they found one of Our servants, on whom We had bestowed Mercy from Ourselves and whom We had taught knowledge from Our own Presence.
text_en_pickthall: Then found they one of Our slaves, unto whom We had given mercy from Us, and had taught him knowledge from Our presence.
text_en_arberry: Then they found one of Our servants unto whom We had given mercy from Us, and We had taught him knowledge proceeding from Us.

text_ar: قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ هَلْ أَتَّبِعُكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ رُشْدًۭا
text_en_primary: Moses said to him, “May I follow you, provided that you teach me some of the right guidance you have been taught?”
text_en_yusufali: Moses said to him: "May I follow thee, on the footing that thou teach me something of the (Higher) Truth which thou hast been taught?"
text_en_pickthall: Moses said unto him: May I follow thee, to the end that thou mayst teach me right conduct of that which thou hast been taught ?
text_en_arberry: Moses said to him, ’Shall I follow thee so that thou teachest me, of what thou hast been taught, right judgment.’

text_ar: قَالَ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِىَ صَبْرًۭا
text_en_primary: He said, “You certainly cannot be patient ˹enough˺ with me.
text_en_yusufali: (The other) said: "Verily thou wilt not be able to have patience with me!"
text_en_pickthall: He said: Lo! thou canst not bear with me.
text_en_arberry: Said he, ’Assuredly thou wilt not be able to bear with me patiently.

text_ar: وَكَيْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلَىٰ مَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِۦ خُبْرًۭا
text_en_primary: And how can you be patient with what is beyond your ˹realm of˺ knowledge?”
text_en_yusufali: "And how canst thou have patience about things about which thy understanding is not complete?"
text_en_pickthall: How canst thou bear with that whereof thou canst not compass any knowledge ?
text_en_arberry: And how shouldst thou bear patiently that thou hast never encompassed in thy knowledge?’

text_ar: قَالَ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ صَابِرًۭا وَلَآ أَعْصِى لَكَ أَمْرًۭا
text_en_primary: Moses assured ˹him˺, “You will find me patient, Allah willing, and I will not disobey any of your orders.”
text_en_yusufali: Moses said: "Thou wilt find me, if God so will, (truly) patient: nor shall I disobey thee in aught."
text_en_pickthall: He said: Allah willing, thou shalt find me patient and I shall not in aught gainsay thee.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’Yet thou shalt find me, if God will, patient; and I shall not rebel against thee in anything.’

text_ar: قَالَ فَإِنِ ٱتَّبَعْتَنِى فَلَا تَسْـَٔلْنِى عَن شَىْءٍ حَتَّىٰٓ أُحْدِثَ لَكَ مِنْهُ ذِكْرًۭا
text_en_primary: He responded, “Then if you follow me, do not question me about anything until I ˹myself˺ clarify it for you.”
text_en_yusufali: The other said: "If then thou wouldst follow me, ask me no questions about anything until I myself speak to thee concerning it."
text_en_pickthall: He said: Well, if thou go with me, ask me not concerning aught till I myself make mention of it unto thee.
text_en_arberry: Said he, ’Then if thou followest me, question me not on anything until I myself introduce the mention of it to thee.’

text_ar: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا رَكِبَا فِى ٱلسَّفِينَةِ خَرَقَهَا ۖ قَالَ أَخَرَقْتَهَا لِتُغْرِقَ أَهْلَهَا لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْـًٔا إِمْرًۭا
text_en_primary: So they set out, but after they had boarded a ship, the man made a hole in it. Moses protested, “Have you done this to drown its people? You have certainly done a terrible thing!”
text_en_yusufali: So they both proceeded: until, when they were in the boat, he scuttled it. Said Moses: "Hast thou scuttled it in order to drown those in it? Truly a strange thing hast thou done!"
text_en_pickthall: So they twain set out till, when they were in the ship, he made a hole therein. (Moses) said: Hast thou made a hole therein to drown the folk thereof ? Thou verily hast done a dreadful thing.
text_en_arberry: So they departed; until, when they embarked upon the ship, he made a hole in it. He said, ’What, hast thou made a hole in it so as to drown its passengers? Thou hast indeed done a grievous thing.’

text_ar: قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِىَ صَبْرًۭا
text_en_primary: He replied, “Did I not say that you cannot have patience with me?”
text_en_yusufali: He answered: "Did I not tell thee that thou canst have no patience with me?"
text_en_pickthall: He said: Did I not tell thee that thou couldst not bear with me ?
text_en_arberry: Said he, ’Did I not say that thou couldst never bear with me patiently?’

text_ar: قَالَ لَا تُؤَاخِذْنِى بِمَا نَسِيتُ وَلَا تُرْهِقْنِى مِنْ أَمْرِى عُسْرًۭا
text_en_primary: Moses pleaded, “Excuse me for forgetting, and do not be hard on me.”
text_en_yusufali: Moses said: "Rebuke me not for forgetting, nor grieve me by raising difficulties in my case."
text_en_pickthall: (Moses) said: Be not wroth with me that I forgot, and be not hard upon me for my fault.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’Do not take me to task that I forgot, neither constrain me to do a thing too difficult.’

text_ar: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا لَقِيَا غُلَٰمًۭا فَقَتَلَهُۥ قَالَ أَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًۭا زَكِيَّةًۢ بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍۢ لَّقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْـًۭٔا نُّكْرًۭا
text_en_primary: So they proceeded until they came across a boy, and the man killed him. Moses protested, “Have you killed an innocent soul, who killed no one? You have certainly done a horrible thing.”
text_en_yusufali: Then they proceeded: until, when they met a young man, he slew him. Moses said: "Hast thou slain an innocent person who had slain none? Truly a foul (unheard of) thing hast thou done!"
text_en_pickthall: So they twain journeyed on till, when they met a lad, he slew him. (Moses) said: What! Hast thou slain an innocent soul who hath slain no man ? Verily thou hast done a horrid thing.
text_en_arberry: So they departed; until, when they met a lad, he slew him. He said, ’What, hast thou slain a soul innocent, and that not to retaliate for a soul slain? Thou hast indeed done a horrible thing.’

text_ar: ۞ قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكَ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِىَ صَبْرًۭا
text_en_primary: He answered, “Did I not tell you that you cannot have patience with me?”
text_en_yusufali: He answered: "Did I not tell thee that thou canst have no patience with me?"
text_en_pickthall: He said: Did I not tell thee that thou couldst not bear with me ?
text_en_arberry: Said he, ’Did I not say that thou couldst never bear with me patiently?’

text_ar: قَالَ إِن سَأَلْتُكَ عَن شَىْءٍۭ بَعْدَهَا فَلَا تُصَٰحِبْنِى ۖ قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِن لَّدُنِّى عُذْرًۭا
text_en_primary: Moses replied, “If I ever question you about anything after this, then do not keep me in your company, for by then I would have given you enough of an excuse.”
text_en_yusufali: (Moses) said: "If ever I ask thee about anything after this, keep me not in thy company: then wouldst thou have received (full) excuse from my side."
text_en_pickthall: (Moses) said: If I ask thee after this concerning aught, keep not company with me. Thou hast received an excuse from me.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’If I question thee on anything after this, then keep me company no more; thou hast already experienced excuse sufficient on my part.’

text_ar: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَتَيَآ أَهْلَ قَرْيَةٍ ٱسْتَطْعَمَآ أَهْلَهَا فَأَبَوْا۟ أَن يُضَيِّفُوهُمَا فَوَجَدَا فِيهَا جِدَارًۭا يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ فَأَقَامَهُۥ ۖ قَالَ لَوْ شِئْتَ لَتَّخَذْتَ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًۭا
text_en_primary: So they moved on until they came to the people of a town. They asked them for food, but the people refused to give them hospitality. There they found a wall ready to collapse, so the man set it right. Moses protested, “If you wanted, you could have demanded a fee for this.”
text_en_yusufali: Then they proceeded: until, when they came to the inhabitants of a town, they asked them for food, but they refused them hospitality. They found there a wall on the point of falling down, but he set it up straight. (Moses) said: "If thou hadst wished, surely thou couldst have exacted some recompense for it!"
text_en_pickthall: So they twain journeyed on till, when they came unto the folk of a certain township, they asked its folk for food, but they refused to make them guests. And they found therein a wall upon the point of falling into ruin, and he repaired it. (Moses) said: If thou hadst wished, thou couldst have taken payment for it.
text_en_arberry: So they departed; until, when they reached the people of a city, they asked the people for food, but they refused to receive them hospitably. There they found a wall about to tumble down, and so he set it up. He said, ’If thou hadst wished, thou couldst have taken a wage for that.’

text_ar: قَالَ هَٰذَا فِرَاقُ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنِكَ ۚ سَأُنَبِّئُكَ بِتَأْوِيلِ مَا لَمْ تَسْتَطِع عَّلَيْهِ صَبْرًا
text_en_primary: He replied, “This is the parting of our ways. I will explain to you what you could not bear patiently.
text_en_yusufali: He answered: "This is the parting between me and thee: now will I tell thee the interpretation of (those things) over which thou wast unable to hold patience.
text_en_pickthall: He said: This is the parting between thee and me! I will announce unto thee the interpretation of that thou couldst not bear with patience.
text_en_arberry: Said he, ’This is the parting between me and thee. Now I will tell thee the interpretation of that thou couldst not bear patiently.

text_ar: أَمَّا ٱلسَّفِينَةُ فَكَانَتْ لِمَسَٰكِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ فَأَرَدتُّ أَنْ أَعِيبَهَا وَكَانَ وَرَآءَهُم مَّلِكٌۭ يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصْبًۭا
text_en_primary: “As for the ship, it belonged to some poor people, working at sea. So I intended to damage it, for there was a ˹tyrant˺ king ahead of them who seizes every ˹good˺ ship by force.
text_en_yusufali: "As for the boat, it belonged to certain men in dire want: they plied on the water: I but wished to render it unserviceable, for there was after them a certain king who seized on every boat by force.
text_en_pickthall: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working on the river, and I wished to mar it, for there was a king behind them who is taking every ship by force.
text_en_arberry: As for the ship, it belonged to certain poor men, who toiled upon the sea; and I desired to damage it, for behind them there was a king who was seizing every ship by brutal force.

text_ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلْغُلَٰمُ فَكَانَ أَبَوَاهُ مُؤْمِنَيْنِ فَخَشِينَآ أَن يُرْهِقَهُمَا طُغْيَٰنًۭا وَكُفْرًۭا
text_en_primary: “And as for the boy, his parents were ˹true˺ believers, and we feared that he would pressure them into defiance and disbelief.
text_en_yusufali: "As for the youth, his parents were people of Faith, and we feared that he would grieve them by obstinate rebellion and ingratitude (to God and man).
text_en_pickthall: And as for the lad, his parents were believers and we feared lest he should oppress them by rebellion and disbelief.
text_en_arberry: As for the lad, his parents were believers; and we were afraid he would impose on them insolence and unbelief;

text_ar: فَأَرَدْنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَهُمَا رَبُّهُمَا خَيْرًۭا مِّنْهُ زَكَوٰةًۭ وَأَقْرَبَ رُحْمًۭا
text_en_primary: So we hoped that their Lord would give them another, more virtuous and caring in his place.
text_en_yusufali: "So we desired that their Lord would give them in exchange (a son) better in purity (of conduct) and closer in affection.
text_en_pickthall: And we intended that their Lord should change him for them for one better in purity and nearer to mercy.
text_en_arberry: so we desired that their Lord should give to them in exchange one better than he in purity, and nearer in tenderness.

text_ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلْجِدَارُ فَكَانَ لِغُلَٰمَيْنِ يَتِيمَيْنِ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ وَكَانَ تَحْتَهُۥ كَنزٌۭ لَّهُمَا وَكَانَ أَبُوهُمَا صَٰلِحًۭا فَأَرَادَ رَبُّكَ أَن يَبْلُغَآ أَشُدَّهُمَا وَيَسْتَخْرِجَا كَنزَهُمَا رَحْمَةًۭ مِّن رَّبِّكَ ۚ وَمَا فَعَلْتُهُۥ عَنْ أَمْرِى ۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَأْوِيلُ مَا لَمْ تَسْطِع عَّلَيْهِ صَبْرًۭا
text_en_primary: “And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and under the wall was a treasure that belonged to them, and their father had been a righteous man. So your Lord willed that these children should come of age and retrieve their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. I did not do it ˹all˺ on my own. This is the explanation of what you could not bear patiently.”
text_en_yusufali: "As for the wall, it belonged to two youths, orphans, in the Town; there was, beneath it, a buried treasure, to which they were entitled: their father had been a righteous man: So thy Lord desired that they should attain their age of full strength and get out their treasure - a mercy (and favour) from thy Lord. I did it not of my own accord. Such is the interpretation of (those things) over which thou wast unable to hold patience."
text_en_pickthall: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was beneath it a treasure belonging to them, and their father had been righteous, and thy Lord intended that they should come to their full strength and should bring forth their treasure as a mercy from their Lord; and I did it not upon my own command. Such is the interpretation of that wherewith thou couldst not bear.
text_en_arberry: As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan lads in the city, and under it was a treasure belonging to them. Their father was a righteous man; and thy Lord desired that they should come of age and then bring forth their treasure as a mercy from thy Lord. I did it not of my own bidding. This is the interpretation of that thou couldst not bear patiently.’

text_ar: وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَن ذِى ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ ۖ قُلْ سَأَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْهُ ذِكْرًا
text_en_primary: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about Ⱬul-Qarnain. Say, “I will relate to you something of his narrative.”
text_en_yusufali: They ask thee concerning Zul-qarnain. Say, "I will rehearse to you something of his story."
text_en_pickthall: They will ask thee of Dhu’l-Qarneyn. Say: I shall recite unto you a remembrance of him.
text_en_arberry: They will question thee concerning Dhool Karnain. Say: ’I will recite to you a mention of him.

text_ar: إِنَّا مَكَّنَّا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ سَبَبًۭا
text_en_primary: Surely We established him in the land, and gave him the means to all things.
text_en_yusufali: Verily We established his power on earth, and We gave him the ways and the means to all ends.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! We made him strong in the land and gave him unto every thing a road.
text_en_arberry: We established him in the land, and We gave him a way to everything;

text_ar: فَأَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا
text_en_primary: So he travelled a course,
text_en_yusufali: One (such) way he followed,
text_en_pickthall: And he followed a road
text_en_arberry: and he followed a way

text_ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ فِى عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍۢ وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًۭا ۗ قُلْنَا يَٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِمَّآ أَن تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّآ أَن تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًۭا
text_en_primary: until he reached the setting ˹point˺ of the sun, which appeared to him to be setting in a spring of murky water, where he found some people. We said, “O Ⱬul-Qarnain! Either punish them or treat them kindly.”
text_en_yusufali: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it set in a spring of murky water: Near it he found a People: We said: "O Zul-qarnain! (thou hast authority,) either to punish them, or to treat them with kindness."
text_en_pickthall: Till, when he reached the setting-place of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring, and found a people thereabout. We said: O Dhu’l- Qarneyn! Either punish or show them kindness.
text_en_arberry: until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring, and he found nearby a people. We said, ’O Dhool Karnain, either thou shalt chastise them, or thou shalt take towards them a way of kindness.’

text_ar: قَالَ أَمَّا مَن ظَلَمَ فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُۥ ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ فَيُعَذِّبُهُۥ عَذَابًۭا نُّكْرًۭا
text_en_primary: He responded, “Whoever does wrong will be punished by us, then will be returned to their Lord, Who will punish them with a horrible torment.
text_en_yusufali: He said: "Whoever doth wrong, him shall we punish; then shall he be sent back to his Lord; and He will punish him with a punishment unheard-of (before).
text_en_pickthall: He said: As for him who doeth wrong, we shall punish him, and then he will be brought back unto his Lord, Who will punish him with awful punishment!
text_en_arberry: He said, ’As for the evildoer, him we shall chastise, then he shall be returned to his Lord and He shall chastise him with a horrible chastisement.

text_ar: وَأَمَّا مَنْ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا فَلَهُۥ جَزَآءً ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ ۖ وَسَنَقُولُ لَهُۥ مِنْ أَمْرِنَا يُسْرًۭا
text_en_primary: As for those who believe and do good, they will have the finest reward, and we will assign them easy commands.”
text_en_yusufali: "But whoever believes, and works righteousness,- he shall have a goodly reward, and easy will be his task as We order it by our Command."
text_en_pickthall: But as for him who believeth and doeth right, good will be his reward, and We shall speak unto him a mild command.
text_en_arberry: But as for him who believes, and does righteousness, he shall receive as recompense the reward most fair, and we shall speak to him, of our command, easiness.’

text_ar: ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا
text_en_primary: Then he travelled a ˹different˺ course
text_en_yusufali: Then followed he (another) way,
text_en_pickthall: Then he followed a road
text_en_arberry: Then he followed a way

text_ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَطْلِعَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَطْلُعُ عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍۢ لَّمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُم مِّن دُونِهَا سِتْرًۭا
text_en_primary: until he reached the rising ˹point˺ of the sun. He found it rising on a people for whom We had provided no shelter from it.
text_en_yusufali: Until, when he came to the rising of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had provided no covering protection against the sun.
text_en_pickthall: Till, when he reached the rising-place of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had appointed no shelter therefrom.
text_en_arberry: until, when he reached the rising of the sun, he found it rising upon a people for whom We had not appointed any veil to shade them from it.

text_ar: كَذَٰلِكَ وَقَدْ أَحَطْنَا بِمَا لَدَيْهِ خُبْرًۭا
text_en_primary: So it was. And We truly had full knowledge of him.
text_en_yusufali: (He left them) as they were: We completely understood what was before him.
text_en_pickthall: So (it was). And We knew all concerning him.
text_en_arberry: So; and We encompassed in knowledge what was with him.

text_ar: ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا
text_en_primary: Then he travelled a ˹third˺ course
text_en_yusufali: Then followed he (another) way,
text_en_pickthall: Then he followed a road
text_en_arberry: Then he followed a way

text_ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ بَيْنَ ٱلسَّدَّيْنِ وَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمَا قَوْمًۭا لَّا يَكَادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ قَوْلًۭا
text_en_primary: until he reached ˹a pass˺ between two mountains. He found in front of them a people who could hardly understand ˹his˺ language.
text_en_yusufali: Until, when he reached (a tract) between two mountains, he found, beneath them, a people who scarcely understood a word.
text_en_pickthall: Till, when he came between the two mountains, he found upon their hither side a folk that scarce could understand a saying.
text_en_arberry: until, when he reached between the two barriers, he found this side of them a people scarcely able to understand speech.

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ يَٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِنَّ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ مُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَهَلْ نَجْعَلُ لَكَ خَرْجًا عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَجْعَلَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُمْ سَدًّۭا
text_en_primary: They pleaded, “O Ⱬul-Qarnain! Surely Gog and Magog are spreading corruption throughout the land. Should we pay you tribute, provided that you build a wall between us and them?”
text_en_yusufali: They said: "O Zul-qarnain! the Gog and Magog (People) do great mischief on earth: shall we then render thee tribute in order that thou mightest erect a barrier between us and them?
text_en_pickthall: They said: O Dhu’l-Qarneyn! Lo! Gog and Magog are spoiling the land. So may we pay thee tribute on condition that thou set a barrier between us and them ?
text_en_arberry: They said, ’O Dhool Karnain, behold, Gog and Magog are doing corruption in the earth; so shall we assign to thee a tribute, against thy setting up a barrier between us and between them?’

text_ar: قَالَ مَا مَكَّنِّى فِيهِ رَبِّى خَيْرٌۭ فَأَعِينُونِى بِقُوَّةٍ أَجْعَلْ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ رَدْمًا
text_en_primary: He responded, “What my Lord has provided for me is far better. But assist me with resources, and I will build a barrier between you and them.
text_en_yusufali: He said: "(The power) in which my Lord has established me is better (than tribute): Help me therefore with strength (and labour): I will erect a strong barrier between you and them:
text_en_pickthall: He said: That wherein my Lord hath established me is better (than your tribute). Do but help me with strength (of men), I will set between you and them a bank.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’That wherein my Lord has established me is better; so aid me forcefully, and I will set up a rampart between you and between them.

text_ar: ءَاتُونِى زُبَرَ ٱلْحَدِيدِ ۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا سَاوَىٰ بَيْنَ ٱلصَّدَفَيْنِ قَالَ ٱنفُخُوا۟ ۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَعَلَهُۥ نَارًۭا قَالَ ءَاتُونِىٓ أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْرًۭا
text_en_primary: Bring me blocks of iron!” Then, when he had filled up ˹the gap˺ between the two mountains, he ordered, “Blow!” When the iron became red hot, he said, “Bring me molten copper to pour over it.”
text_en_yusufali: "Bring me blocks of iron." At length, when he had filled up the space between the two steep mountain-sides, He said, "Blow (with your bellows)" Then, when he had made it (red) as fire, he said: "Bring me, that I may pour over it, molten lead."
text_en_pickthall: Give me pieces of iron - till, when he had levelled up (the gap) between the cliffs, he said: Blow! - till, when he had made it a fire, he said: Bring me molten copper to pour thereon.
text_en_arberry: Bring me ingots of iron!’ Until, when he had made all level between the two cliffs, he said, ’Blow!’ Until, when he had made it a fire, he said, ’Bring me, that I may pour molten brass on it.’

text_ar: فَمَا ٱسْطَٰعُوٓا۟ أَن يَظْهَرُوهُ وَمَا ٱسْتَطَٰعُوا۟ لَهُۥ نَقْبًۭا
text_en_primary: And so the enemies could neither scale nor tunnel through it.
text_en_yusufali: Thus were they made powerless to scale it or to dig through it.
text_en_pickthall: And (Gog and Magog) were not able to surmount, nor could they pierce (it).
text_en_arberry: So they were unable either to scale it or pierce it.

text_ar: قَالَ هَٰذَا رَحْمَةٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّى ۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ رَبِّى جَعَلَهُۥ دَكَّآءَ ۖ وَكَانَ وَعْدُ رَبِّى حَقًّۭا
text_en_primary: He declared, “This is a mercy from my Lord. But when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, He will level it to the ground. And my Lord’s promise is ever true.”
text_en_yusufali: He said: "This is a mercy from my Lord: But when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, He will make it into dust; and the promise of my Lord is true."
text_en_pickthall: He said: This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord cometh to pass, He will lay it low, for the promise of my Lord is true.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’This is a mercy from my Lord. But when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, He will make it into powder; and my Lord’s promise is ever true.’

text_ar: ۞ وَتَرَكْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ يَمُوجُ فِى بَعْضٍۢ ۖ وَنُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَجَمَعْنَٰهُمْ جَمْعًۭا
text_en_primary: On that Day, We will let them and We will gather all ˹people˺ together.
text_en_yusufali: On that day We shall leave them to surge like waves on one another: the trumpet will be blown, and We shall collect them all together.
text_en_pickthall: And on that day we shall let some of them surge against others, and the Trumpet will be blown. Then We shall gather them together in one gathering.
text_en_arberry: Upon that day We shall leave them surging on one another, and the Trumpet shall he blown, and We shall gather them together,

text_ar: وَعَرَضْنَا جَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ لِّلْكَٰفِرِينَ عَرْضًا
text_en_primary: On that Day We will display Hell clearly for the disbelievers,
text_en_yusufali: And We shall present Hell that day for Unbelievers to see, all spread out,-
text_en_pickthall: On that day we shall present hell to the disbelievers, plain to view,
text_en_arberry: and upon that day We shall present Gehenna to the unbelievers

text_ar: ٱلَّذِينَ كَانَتْ أَعْيُنُهُمْ فِى غِطَآءٍ عَن ذِكْرِى وَكَانُوا۟ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَمْعًا
text_en_primary: those who turned a blind eye to My Reminder and could not stand listening ˹to it˺.
text_en_yusufali: (Unbelievers) whose eyes had been under a veil from remembrance of Me, and who had been unable even to hear.
text_en_pickthall: Those whose eyes were hoodwinked from My reminder, and who could not bear to hear.
text_en_arberry: whose eyes were covered against My remembrance, and they were not able to hear.

text_ar: أَفَحَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَن يَتَّخِذُوا۟ عِبَادِى مِن دُونِىٓ أَوْلِيَآءَ ۚ إِنَّآ أَعْتَدْنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ نُزُلًۭا
text_en_primary: Do the disbelievers think they can ˹simply˺ take My servants as lords instead of Me? We have surely prepared Hell as an accommodation for the disbelievers.
text_en_yusufali: Do the Unbelievers think that they can take My servants as protectors besides Me? Verily We have prepared Hell for the Unbelievers for (their) entertainment.
text_en_pickthall: Do the disbelievers reckon that they can choose My bondmen as protecting friends beside Me ? Lo! We have prepared hell as a welcome for the disbelievers.
text_en_arberry: What, do the unbelievers reckon that they may take My servants as friends, apart from Me? We have prepared Gehenna for the unbelievers’ hospitality.

text_ar: قُلْ هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُم بِٱلْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَٰلًا
text_en_primary: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Shall we inform you of who will lose the most deeds?
text_en_yusufali: Say: "Shall we tell you of those who lose most in respect of their deeds?-
text_en_pickthall: Say: Shall We inform you who will be the greatest losers by their works ?
text_en_arberry: Say: ’Shall We tell you who will be the greatest losers in their works?

text_ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا
text_en_primary: ˹They are˺ those whose efforts are in vain in this worldly life, while they think they are doing good!”
text_en_yusufali: "Those whose efforts have been wasted in this life, while they thought that they were acquiring good by their works?"
text_en_pickthall: Those whose effort goeth astray in the life of the world, and yet they reckon that they do good work.
text_en_arberry: Those whose striving goes astray in the present life, while they think that they are working good deeds.

text_ar: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ وَلِقَآئِهِۦ فَحَبِطَتْ أَعْمَٰلُهُمْ فَلَا نُقِيمُ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وَزْنًۭا
text_en_primary: It is they who reject the signs of their Lord and their meeting with Him, rendering their deeds void, so We will not give their deeds any weight on Judgment Day.
text_en_yusufali: They are those who deny the Signs of their Lord and the fact of their having to meet Him (in the Hereafter): vain will be their works, nor shall We, on the Day of Judgment, give them any weight.
text_en_pickthall: Those are they who disbelieve in the revelations of their Lord and in the meeting with Him. Therefor their works are vain, and on the Day of Resurrection We assign no weight to them.
text_en_arberry: Those are they that disbelieve in the signs of their Lord and the encounter with Him; their works have failed, and on the Day of Resurrection We shall not assign to them any weight.

text_ar: ذَٰلِكَ جَزَآؤُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ بِمَا كَفَرُوا۟ وَٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ ءَايَٰتِى وَرُسُلِى هُزُوًا
text_en_primary: That is their reward: Hell, for their disbelief and mockery of My signs and messengers.
text_en_yusufali: That is their reward, Hell, because they rejected Faith, and took My Signs and My Messengers by way of jest.
text_en_pickthall: That is their reward: hell, because they disbelieved, and made a jest of Our revelations and Our messengers.
text_en_arberry: That is their recompense -- Gehenna for that they were unbelievers and took My signs and My messengers in mockery.

text_ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ كَانَتْ لَهُمْ جَنَّٰتُ ٱلْفِرْدَوْسِ نُزُلًا
text_en_primary: Indeed, those who believe and do good will have the Gardens of Paradise as an accommodation,
text_en_yusufali: As to those who believe and work righteous deeds, they have, for their entertainment, the Gardens of Paradise,
text_en_pickthall: Lo! those who believe and do good works, theirs are the Gardens of Paradise for welcome,
text_en_arberry: But those who believe, and do deeds of righteousness -- the Gardens. of Paradise shall be their hospitality,

text_ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يَبْغُونَ عَنْهَا حِوَلًۭا
text_en_primary: where they will be forever, never desiring anywhere else.
text_en_yusufali: Wherein they shall dwell (for aye): no change will they wish for from them.
text_en_pickthall: Wherein they will abide, with no desire to be removed from thence.
text_en_arberry: therein to dwell forever, desiring no removal out of them.’

text_ar: قُل لَّوْ كَانَ ٱلْبَحْرُ مِدَادًۭا لِّكَلِمَٰتِ رَبِّى لَنَفِدَ ٱلْبَحْرُ قَبْلَ أَن تَنفَدَ كَلِمَٰتُ رَبِّى وَلَوْ جِئْنَا بِمِثْلِهِۦ مَدَدًۭا
text_en_primary: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “If the ocean were ink for ˹writing˺ the Words of my Lord, it would certainly run out before the Words of my Lord were finished, even if We refilled it with its equal.”
text_en_yusufali: Say: "If the ocean were ink (wherewith to write out) the words of my Lord, sooner would the ocean be exhausted than would the words of my Lord, even if we added another ocean like it, for its aid."
text_en_pickthall: Say: Though the sea became ink for the Words of my Lord, verily the sea would be used up before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even though We brought the like thereof to help.
text_en_arberry: Say:. ’If the sea were ink for the Words of my Lord, the sea would be spent before the Words of my Lord are spent, though We brought replenishment the like of it.’

text_ar: قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ بَشَرٌۭ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌۭ وَٰحِدٌۭ ۖ فَمَن كَانَ يَرْجُوا۟ لِقَآءَ رَبِّهِۦ فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلًۭا صَٰلِحًۭا وَلَا يُشْرِكْ بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَحَدًۢا
text_en_primary: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I am only a man like you, ˹but˺ it has been revealed to me that your God is only One God. So whoever hopes for the meeting with their Lord, let them do good deeds and associate none in the worship of their Lord.”
text_en_yusufali: Say: "I am but a man like yourselves, (but) the inspiration has come to me, that your God is one God: whoever expects to meet his Lord, let him work righteousness, and, in the worship of his Lord, admit no one as partner.
text_en_pickthall: Say: I am only a mortal like you. My Lord inspireth in me that your God is only One God. And whoever hopeth for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work, and make none sharer of the worship due unto his Lord.
text_en_arberry: Say: ’I am only a mortal the like of you; it is revealed to me that your God is One God. So let him, who hopes for the encounter with his Lord, work righteousness, and not associate with his Lord’s service anyone.

text_ar: كٓهيعٓصٓ
text_en_primary: Kãf-Ha-Ya-’Aĩn- sãd.
text_en_yusufali: Kaf. Ha. Ya. ’Ain. Sad.
text_en_pickthall: Kaf. Ha. Ya. A’in. Sad.
text_en_arberry: Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad

text_ar: ذِكْرُ رَحْمَتِ رَبِّكَ عَبْدَهُۥ زَكَرِيَّآ
text_en_primary: ˹This is˺ a reminder of your Lord’s mercy to His servant Zachariah,
text_en_yusufali: (This is) a recital of the Mercy of thy Lord to His servant Zakariya.
text_en_pickthall: A mention of the mercy of thy Lord unto His servant Zachariah.
text_en_arberry: The mention of thy Lord’s mercy unto His servant Zachariah;

text_ar: إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥ نِدَآءً خَفِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: when he cried out to his Lord privately,
text_en_yusufali: Behold! he cried to his Lord in secret,
text_en_pickthall: When he cried unto his Lord a cry in secret,
text_en_arberry: when he called upon his Lord secretly

text_ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى وَهَنَ ٱلْعَظْمُ مِنِّى وَٱشْتَعَلَ ٱلرَّأْسُ شَيْبًۭا وَلَمْ أَكُنۢ بِدُعَآئِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: saying, “My Lord! Surely my bones have become brittle, and grey hair has spread across my head, but I have never been disappointed in my prayer to You, my Lord!
text_en_yusufali: Praying: "O my Lord! infirm indeed are my bones, and the hair of my head doth glisten with grey: but never am I unblest, O my Lord, in my prayer to Thee!
text_en_pickthall: Saying: My Lord! Lo! the bones of me wax feeble and my head is shining with grey hair, and I have never been unblest in prayer to Thee, my Lord.
text_en_arberry: saying, ’O my Lord, behold the bones within me are feeble and my head is all aflame with hoariness. And in calling on Thee, my Lord, I have never been hitherto unprosperous.

text_ar: وَإِنِّى خِفْتُ ٱلْمَوَٰلِىَ مِن وَرَآءِى وَكَانَتِ ٱمْرَأَتِى عَاقِرًۭا فَهَبْ لِى مِن لَّدُنكَ وَلِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: And I am concerned about ˹the faith of˺ my relatives after me, since my wife is barren. So grant me, by Your grace, an heir,
text_en_yusufali: "Now I fear (what) my relatives (and colleagues) (will do) after me: but my wife is barren: so give me an heir as from Thyself,-
text_en_pickthall: Lo! I fear my kinsfolk after me, since my wife is barren. Oh, give me from Thy presence a successor
text_en_arberry: And now I fear my kinsfolk after I am gone; and my wife is barren. So give me, from Thee, a kinsman

text_ar: يَرِثُنِى وَيَرِثُ مِنْ ءَالِ يَعْقُوبَ ۖ وَٱجْعَلْهُ رَبِّ رَضِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: who will inherit ˹prophethood˺ from me and the family of Jacob, and make him, O  Lord, pleasing ˹to You˺!”
text_en_yusufali: "(One that) will (truly) represent me, and represent the posterity of Jacob; and make him, O my Lord! one with whom Thou art well-pleased!"
text_en_pickthall: Who shall inherit of me and inherit (also) of the house of Jacob. And make him, my Lord, acceptable (unto Thee).
text_en_arberry: who shall be my inheritor and the inheritor of the House of Jacob; and make him, my Lord, well-pleasing.’

text_ar: يَٰزَكَرِيَّآ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَٰمٍ ٱسْمُهُۥ يَحْيَىٰ لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: ˹The angels announced,˺ “O Zachariah! Indeed, We give you the good news of ˹the birth of˺ a son, whose name will be John—a name We have not given to anyone before.”
text_en_yusufali: (His prayer was answered): "O Zakariya! We give thee good news of a son: His name shall be Yahya: on none by that name have We conferred distinction before."
text_en_pickthall: (It was said unto him): O Zachariah! Lo! We bring thee tidings of a son whose name is John; we have given the same name to none before (him).
text_en_arberry: ’O Zachariah, We give thee good tidings of a boy, whose name is John. No namesake have We given him aforetime.’

text_ar: قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَٰمٌۭ وَكَانَتِ ٱمْرَأَتِى عَاقِرًۭا وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ ٱلْكِبَرِ عِتِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: He wondered, “My Lord! How can I have a son when my wife is barren, and I have become extremely old?”
text_en_yusufali: He said: "O my Lord! How shall I have a son, when my wife is barren and I have grown quite decrepit from old age?"
text_en_pickthall: He said: My Lord! How can I have a son when my wife is barren and I have reached infirm old age ?
text_en_arberry: He said, ’O my Lord, how shall I have a son, seeing my wife is barren, and I have attained to the declining of old age?’

text_ar: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكَ هُوَ عَلَىَّ هَيِّنٌۭ وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِن قَبْلُ وَلَمْ تَكُ شَيْـًۭٔا
text_en_primary: An angel replied, “So will it be! Your Lord says, ‘It is easy for Me, just as I created you before, when you were nothing!’”
text_en_yusufali: He said: "So (it will be) thy Lord saith, ’that is easy for Me: I did indeed create thee before, when thou hadst been nothing!’"
text_en_pickthall: He said: So (it will be). Thy Lord saith: It is easy for Me, even as I created thee before, when thou wast naught.
text_en_arberry: Said He, ’So it shall be; thy Lord says, "Easy is that for Me, seeing that I created thee aforetime, when thou wast nothing."’

text_ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱجْعَل لِّىٓ ءَايَةًۭ ۚ قَالَ ءَايَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ ٱلنَّاسَ ثَلَٰثَ لَيَالٍۢ سَوِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: Zachariah said, “My Lord! Grant me a sign.” He responded, “Your sign is that you will not ˹be able to˺ speak to people for three nights, despite being healthy.”
text_en_yusufali: (Zakariya) said: "O my Lord! give me a Sign." "Thy Sign," was the answer, "Shall be that thou shalt speak to no man for three nights, although thou art not dumb."
text_en_pickthall: He said: My Lord! Appoint for me some token. He said: Thy token is that thou, with no bodily defect, shalt not speak unto mankind three nights.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’Lord, appoint to me some sign.’ Said He, ’Thy sign is that thou shall not speak to men, though being without fault, three nights.’

text_ar: فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلْمِحْرَابِ فَأَوْحَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِمْ أَن سَبِّحُوا۟ بُكْرَةًۭ وَعَشِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: So he came out to his people from the sanctuary, signalling to them to glorify ˹Allah˺ morning and evening.
text_en_yusufali: So Zakariya came out to his people from him chamber: He told them by signs to celebrate God’s praises in the morning and in the evening.
text_en_pickthall: Then he came forth unto his people from the sanctuary, and signified to them: Glorify your Lord at break of day and fall of night.
text_en_arberry: So he came forth unto his people from the Sanctuary, then he made signal to them, ’Give you glory at dawn and evening.’

text_ar: يَٰيَحْيَىٰ خُذِ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ بِقُوَّةٍۢ ۖ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ ٱلْحُكْمَ صَبِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: ˹It was later said,˺ “O John! Hold firmly to the Scriptures.” And We granted him wisdom while ˹he was still˺ a child,
text_en_yusufali: (To his son came the command): "O Yahya! take hold of the Book with might": and We gave him Wisdom even as a youth,
text_en_pickthall: (And it was said unto his son): O John! Hold fast the Scripture. And we gave him wisdom when a child,
text_en_arberry: ’O John, take the Book forcefully’; and We gave him judgment, yet a little child,

text_ar: وَحَنَانًۭا مِّن لَّدُنَّا وَزَكَوٰةًۭ ۖ وَكَانَ تَقِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: as well as purity and compassion from Us. And he was God-fearing,
text_en_yusufali: And piety (for all creatures) as from Us, and purity: He was devout,
text_en_pickthall: And compassion from Our presence, and purity; and he was devout,
text_en_arberry: and a tenderness from Us, and purity; and he was godfearing,

text_ar: وَبَرًّۢا بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَكُن جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: and kind to his parents. He was neither arrogant nor disobedient.
text_en_yusufali: And kind to his parents, and he was not overbearing or rebellious.
text_en_pickthall: And dutiful toward his parents. And he was not arrogant, rebellious.
text_en_arberry: and cherishing his parents, not arrogant, rebellious.

text_ar: وَسَلَٰمٌ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوْمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَيًّۭا
text_en_primary: Peace be upon him the day he was born, and the day of his death, and the day he will be raised back to life!
text_en_yusufali: So Peace on him the day he was born, the day that he dies, and the day that he will be raised up to life (again)!
text_en_pickthall: Peace on him the day he was born, and the day he dieth and the day he shall be raised alive!
text_en_arberry: ’Peace be upon him, the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he is raised up alive!’

text_ar: وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مَرْيَمَ إِذِ ٱنتَبَذَتْ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا مَكَانًۭا شَرْقِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Mary when she withdrew from her family to a place in the east,
text_en_yusufali: Relate in the Book (the story of) Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place in the East.
text_en_pickthall: And make mention of Mary in the Scripture, when she had withdrawn from her people to a chamber looking East,
text_en_arberry: And mention in the Book Mary when she withdrew from her people to an eastern place,

text_ar: فَٱتَّخَذَتْ مِن دُونِهِمْ حِجَابًۭا فَأَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَيْهَا رُوحَنَا فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا بَشَرًۭا سَوِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: screening herself off from them. Then We sent to her Our angel, ˹Gabriel,˺ appearing before her as a man, perfectly formed.
text_en_yusufali: She placed a screen (to screen herself) from them; then We sent her our angel, and he appeared before her as a man in all respects.
text_en_pickthall: And had chosen seclusion from them. Then We sent unto her Our Spirit and it assumed for her the likeness of a perfect man.
text_en_arberry: and she took a veil apart from them; then We sent unto her Our Spirit that presented himself to her a man without fault.

text_ar: قَالَتْ إِنِّىٓ أَعُوذُ بِٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ مِنكَ إِن كُنتَ تَقِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: She appealed, “I truly seek refuge in the Most Compassionate from you! ˹So leave me alone˺ if you are God-fearing.”
text_en_yusufali: She said: "I seek refuge from thee to (God) Most Gracious: (come not near) if thou dost fear God."
text_en_pickthall: She said: Lo! I seek refuge in the Beneficent One from thee, if thou art God-fearing.
text_en_arberry: She said, ’I take refuge in the All-merciful from thee!

text_ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِأَهَبَ لَكِ غُلَٰمًۭا زَكِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: He responded, “I am only a messenger from your Lord, ˹sent˺ to bless you with a pure son.”
text_en_yusufali: He said: "Nay, I am only a messenger from thy Lord, (to announce) to thee the gift of a holy son.
text_en_pickthall: He said: I am only a messenger of thy Lord, that I may bestow on thee a faultless son.
text_en_arberry: If thou fearest God ... He said, ’I am but a messenger come from thy Lord, to give thee a boy most pure.

text_ar: قَالَتْ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَٰمٌۭ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِى بَشَرٌۭ وَلَمْ أَكُ بَغِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: She wondered, “How can I have a son when no man has ever touched me, nor am I unchaste?”
text_en_yusufali: She said: "How shall I have a son, seeing that no man has touched me, and I am not unchaste?"
text_en_pickthall: She said: How can I have a son when no mortal hath touched me, neither have I been unchaste ?
text_en_arberry: She said, ’How shall I have a son whom no mortal has touched, neither have I been unchaste?’

text_ar: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ هُوَ عَلَىَّ هَيِّنٌۭ ۖ وَلِنَجْعَلَهُۥٓ ءَايَةًۭ لِّلنَّاسِ وَرَحْمَةًۭ مِّنَّا ۚ وَكَانَ أَمْرًۭا مَّقْضِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: He replied, “So will it be! Your Lord says, ‘It is easy for Me. And so will We make him a sign for humanity and a mercy from Us.’ It is a matter ˹already˺ decreed.”
text_en_yusufali: He said: "So (it will be): Thy Lord saith, ’that is easy for Me: and (We wish) to appoint him as a Sign unto men and a Mercy from Us’:It is a matter (so) decreed."
text_en_pickthall: He said: So (it will be). Thy Lord saith: It is easy for Me. And (it will be) that We may make of him a revelation for mankind and a mercy from Us, and it is a thing ordained.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’Even so thy Lord has said: "Easy is that for Me; and that We may appoint him a sign unto men and a mercy from Us; it is a thing decreed."’

text_ar: ۞ فَحَمَلَتْهُ فَٱنتَبَذَتْ بِهِۦ مَكَانًۭا قَصِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: So she conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place.
text_en_yusufali: So she conceived him, and she retired with him to a remote place.
text_en_pickthall: And she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a far place.
text_en_arberry: So she conceived him, and withdrew with him to a distant place.

text_ar: فَأَجَآءَهَا ٱلْمَخَاضُ إِلَىٰ جِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ قَالَتْ يَٰلَيْتَنِى مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَٰذَا وَكُنتُ نَسْيًۭا مَّنسِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: Then the pains of labour drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She cried, “Alas! I wish I had died before this, and was a thing long forgotten!”
text_en_yusufali: And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm-tree: She cried (in her anguish): "Ah! would that I had died before this! would that I had been a thing forgotten and out of sight!"
text_en_pickthall: And the pangs of childbirth drove her unto the trunk of the palm- tree. She said: Oh, would that I had died ere this and had become a thing of naught, forgotten!
text_en_arberry: And the birthpangs surprised her by the trunk of the palm-tree. She said, ’Would I had died ere this, and become a thing forgotten!’

text_ar: فَنَادَىٰهَا مِن تَحْتِهَآ أَلَّا تَحْزَنِى قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: So a voice reassured her from below her, “Do not grieve! Your Lord has provided a stream at your feet.
text_en_yusufali: But (a voice) cried to her from beneath the (palm-tree): "Grieve not! for thy Lord hath provided a rivulet beneath thee;
text_en_pickthall: Then (one) cried unto her from below her, saying: Grieve not! Thy Lord hath placed a rivulet beneath thee,
text_en_arberry: But the one that was below her called to her, ’Nay, do not sorrow; see, thy Lord has set below thee a rivulet.

text_ar: وَهُزِّىٓ إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ تُسَٰقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًۭا جَنِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: And shake the trunk of this palm tree towards you, it will drop fresh, ripe dates upon you.
text_en_yusufali: "And shake towards thyself the trunk of the palm-tree: It will let fall fresh ripe dates upon thee.
text_en_pickthall: And shake the trunk of the palm-tree toward thee, thou wilt cause ripe dates to fall upon thee.
text_en_arberry: Shake also to thee the palm-trunk, and there shall come tumbling upon thee dates fresh and ripe.

text_ar: فَكُلِى وَٱشْرَبِى وَقَرِّى عَيْنًۭا ۖ فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْبَشَرِ أَحَدًۭا فَقُولِىٓ إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ صَوْمًۭا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِنسِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: So eat and drink, and put your heart at ease. But if you see any of the people, say, ‘I have vowed silence to the Most Compassionate, so I am not talking to anyone today.’”
text_en_yusufali: "So eat and drink and cool (thine) eye. And if thou dost see any man, say, ’I have vowed a fast to (God) Most Gracious, and this day will I enter into not talk with any human being’"
text_en_pickthall: So eat and drink and be consoled. And if thou meetest any mortal, say: Lo! I have vowed a fast unto the Beneficent, and may not speak this day to any mortal.
text_en_arberry: Eat therefore, and drink, and be comforted; and if thou shouldst see any mortal, say, "I have vowed to the All-merciful a fast, and today I will not speak to any man.

text_ar: فَأَتَتْ بِهِۦ قَوْمَهَا تَحْمِلُهُۥ ۖ قَالُوا۟ يَٰمَرْيَمُ لَقَدْ جِئْتِ شَيْـًۭٔا فَرِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: Then she returned to her people, carrying him. They said ˹in shock˺, “O Mary! You have certainly done a horrible thing!
text_en_yusufali: At length she brought the (babe) to her people, carrying him (in her arms). They said: "O Mary! truly an amazing thing hast thou brought!
text_en_pickthall: Then she brought him to her own folk, carrying him. They said: O Mary! Thou hast come with an amazing thing.
text_en_arberry: Then she brought the child to her folk carrying him; and they said, ’Mary, thou hast surely committed a monstrous thing!

text_ar: يَٰٓأُخْتَ هَٰرُونَ مَا كَانَ أَبُوكِ ٱمْرَأَ سَوْءٍۢ وَمَا كَانَتْ أُمُّكِ بَغِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: O  sister of Aaron! Your father was not an indecent man, nor was your mother unchaste.”
text_en_yusufali: "O sister of Aaron! Thy father was not a man of evil, nor thy mother a woman unchaste!"
text_en_pickthall: O sister of Aaron! Thy father was not a wicked man nor was thy mother a harlot.
text_en_arberry: Sister of Aaron, thy father was not a wicked man, nor was thy mother a woman unchaste.’

text_ar: فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ ۖ قَالُوا۟ كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَن كَانَ فِى ٱلْمَهْدِ صَبِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: So she pointed to the baby. They exclaimed, “How can we talk to someone who is an infant in the cradle?”
text_en_yusufali: But she pointed to the babe. They said: "How can we talk to one who is a child in the cradle?"
text_en_pickthall: Then she pointed to him. They said: How can we talk to one who is in the cradle, a young boy ?
text_en_arberry: Mary pointed to the child then; but they said, ’How shall we speak to one who is still in the cradle, a little child?’

text_ar: قَالَ إِنِّى عَبْدُ ٱللَّهِ ءَاتَىٰنِىَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَجَعَلَنِى نَبِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: ˹Jesus˺ declared, “I am truly a servant of Allah. He has destined me to be given the Scripture and to be a prophet.
text_en_yusufali: He said: "I am indeed a servant of God: He hath given me revelation and made me a prophet;
text_en_pickthall: He spake: Lo! I am the slave of Allah. He hath given me the Scripture and hath appointed me a Prophet,
text_en_arberry: He said, ’Lo, I am God’s servant; God has given me the Book, and made me a Prophet.

text_ar: وَجَعَلَنِى مُبَارَكًا أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُ وَأَوْصَٰنِى بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱلزَّكَوٰةِ مَا دُمْتُ حَيًّۭا
text_en_primary: He has made me a blessing wherever I go, and bid me to establish prayer and give alms-tax as long as I live,
text_en_yusufali: "And He hath made me blessed wheresoever I be, and hath enjoined on me Prayer and Charity as long as I live;
text_en_pickthall: And hath made me blessed wheresoever I may be, and hath enjoined upon me prayer and almsgiving so long as I remain alive,
text_en_arberry: Blessed He has made me, wherever I may be; and He has enjoined me to pray, and to give the alms, so long as I live,

text_ar: وَبَرًّۢا بِوَٰلِدَتِى وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْنِى جَبَّارًۭا شَقِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: and to be kind to my mother. He has not made me arrogant or defiant.
text_en_yusufali: "(He) hath made me kind to my mother, and not overbearing or miserable;
text_en_pickthall: And (hath made me) dutiful toward her who bore me, and hath not made me arrogant, unblest.
text_en_arberry: and likewise to cherish my mother; He has not made me arrogant, unprosperous.

text_ar: وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىَّ يَوْمَ وُلِدتُّ وَيَوْمَ أَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ أُبْعَثُ حَيًّۭا
text_en_primary: Peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I will be raised back to life!”
text_en_yusufali: "So peace is on me the day I was born, the day that I die, and the day that I shall be raised up to life (again)"!
text_en_pickthall: Peace on me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I shall be raised alive!
text_en_arberry: Peace be upon me, the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised up alive!’

text_ar: ذَٰلِكَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ ۚ قَوْلَ ٱلْحَقِّ ٱلَّذِى فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ
text_en_primary: That is Jesus, son of Mary. ˹And this is˺ a word of truth, about which they dispute.
text_en_yusufali: Such (was) Jesus the son of Mary: (it is) a statement of truth, about which they (vainly) dispute.
text_en_pickthall: Such was Jesus, son of Mary: (this is) a statement of the truth concerning which they doubt.
text_en_arberry: That is Jesus, son of Mary, in word of truth, concerning which they are doubting.

text_ar: مَا كَانَ لِلَّهِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ مِن وَلَدٍۢ ۖ سُبْحَٰنَهُۥٓ ۚ إِذَا قَضَىٰٓ أَمْرًۭا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
text_en_primary: It is not for Allah to take a son! Glory be to Him. When He decrees a matter, He simply tells it, “Be!” And it is!
text_en_yusufali: It is not befitting to (the majesty of) God that He should beget a son. Glory be to Him! when He determines a matter, He only says to it, "Be", and it is.
text_en_pickthall: It befitteth not (the Majesty of) Allah that He should take unto Himself a son. Glory be to Him! When He decreeth a thing, He saith unto it only: Be! and it is.
text_en_arberry: It is not for God to take a son unto Him. Glory be to Him! When He decrees a thing, He but says to it ’Be,’ and it is.

text_ar: وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّى وَرَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُوهُ ۚ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌۭ مُّسْتَقِيمٌۭ
text_en_primary: ˹Jesus also declared,˺ “Surely Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him ˹alone˺. This is the Straight Path.”
text_en_yusufali: Verily God is my Lord and your Lord: Him therefore serve ye: this is a Way that is straight.
text_en_pickthall: And lo! Allah is my Lord and your Lord. So serve Him. That is the right path.
text_en_arberry: Surely God is my Lord, and your Lord; So serve you Him. This is a straight path.

text_ar: فَٱخْتَلَفَ ٱلْأَحْزَابُ مِنۢ بَيْنِهِمْ ۖ فَوَيْلٌۭ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن مَّشْهَدِ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
text_en_primary: Yet their ˹various˺ groups have differed among themselves ˹about him˺, so woe to the disbelievers when they face a tremendous Day!
text_en_yusufali: But the sects differ among themselves: and woe to the unbelievers because of the (coming) Judgment of a Momentous Day!
text_en_pickthall: The sects among them differ: but woe unto the disbelievers from the meeting of an awful Day.
text_en_arberry: But the parties have fallen into variance among themselves; then woe to those who disbelieve for the scene of a dreadful day.

text_ar: أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِرْ يَوْمَ يَأْتُونَنَا ۖ لَٰكِنِ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ ٱلْيَوْمَ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
text_en_primary: How clearly will they hear and see on the Day they will come to Us! But today the wrongdoers are clearly astray.
text_en_yusufali: How plainly will they see and hear, the Day that they will appear before Us! but the unjust today are in error manifest!
text_en_pickthall: See and hear them on the Day they come unto Us! yet the evil-doers are to-day in error manifest.
text_en_arberry: How well they will hear and see on the day they come to Us! But the evildoers even today are in error manifest.

text_ar: وَأَنذِرْهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْحَسْرَةِ إِذْ قُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ وَهُمْ فِى غَفْلَةٍۢ وَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
text_en_primary: And warn them ˹O Prophet˺ of the Day of Regret, when all matters will be settled, while they are ˹engrossed˺ in heedlessness and disbelief.
text_en_yusufali: But warn them of the Day of Distress, when the matter will be determined: for (behold,) they are negligent and they do not believe!
text_en_pickthall: And warn them of the Day of anguish when the case hath been decided. Now they are in a state of carelessness, and they believe not.
text_en_arberry: Warn thou them of the day of anguish, when the matter shall be determined, and they yet heedless and unbelieving.

text_ar: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَرِثُ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَنْ عَلَيْهَا وَإِلَيْنَا يُرْجَعُونَ
text_en_primary: Indeed, it is We Who will succeed the earth and whoever is on it. And to Us they will ˹all˺ be returned.
text_en_yusufali: It is We Who will inherit the earth, and all beings thereon: to Us will they all be returned.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! We, only We, inherit the earth and all who are thereon, and unto Us they are returned.
text_en_arberry: Surely We shall inherit the earth and all that are upon it, and unto Us they shall be returned.

text_ar: وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ صِدِّيقًۭا نَّبِيًّا
text_en_primary: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Abraham. He was surely a man of truth and a prophet.
text_en_yusufali: (Also mention in the Book (the story of) Abraham: He was a man of Truth, a prophet.
text_en_pickthall: And make mention (O Muhammad) in the Scripture of Abraham. Lo! he was a saint, a prophet.
text_en_arberry: And mention in the Book Abraham; surely he was a true man, a Prophet.

text_ar: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ لِمَ تَعْبُدُ مَا لَا يَسْمَعُ وَلَا يُبْصِرُ وَلَا يُغْنِى عَنكَ شَيْـًۭٔا
text_en_primary: ˹Remember˺ when he said to his father, “O dear father! Why do you worship what can neither hear nor see, nor benefit you at all?
text_en_yusufali: Behold, he said to his father: "O my father! why worship that which heareth not and seeth not, and can profit thee nothing?
text_en_pickthall: When he said unto his father: O my father! Why worshippest thou that which heareth not nor seeth, nor can in aught avail thee ?
text_en_arberry: When he said to his father, ’Father, why worshippest thou that which neither hears nor sees, nor avails thee anything?

text_ar: يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّى قَدْ جَآءَنِى مِنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ مَا لَمْ يَأْتِكَ فَٱتَّبِعْنِىٓ أَهْدِكَ صِرَٰطًۭا سَوِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: O  dear father! I have certainly received some knowledge which you have not received, so follow me and I will guide you to the Straight Path.
text_en_yusufali: "O my father! to me hath come knowledge which hath not reached thee: so follow me: I will guide thee to a way that is even and straight.
text_en_pickthall: O my father! Lo! there hath come unto me of knowledge that which came not unto thee. So follow me, and I will lead thee on a right path.
text_en_arberry: Father, there has come to me knowledge such as came not to thee; so follow me, and I will guide thee on a level path.

text_ar: يَٰٓأَبَتِ لَا تَعْبُدِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ ۖ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَصِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: O  dear father! Do not worship Satan. Surely Satan is ever rebellious against the Most Compassionate.
text_en_yusufali: "O my father! serve not Satan: for Satan is a rebel against (God) Most Gracious.
text_en_pickthall: O my father! Serve not the devil. Lo! the devil is a rebel unto the Beneficent.
text_en_arberry: Father, serve not Satan; surely Satan is a rebel against the All-merciful.

text_ar: يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يَمَسَّكَ عَذَابٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ فَتَكُونَ لِلشَّيْطَٰنِ وَلِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: O  dear father! I truly fear that you will be touched by a torment from the Most Compassionate, and become Satan’s companion ˹in Hell˺.”
text_en_yusufali: "O my father! I fear lest a Penalty afflict thee from (God) Most Gracious, so that thou become to Satan a friend."
text_en_pickthall: O my father! Lo! I fear lest a punishment from the Beneficent overtake thee so that thou become a comrade of the devil.
text_en_arberry: Father, I fear that some chastisement from the All-merciful will smite thee, so that thou becomest a friend to Satan.

text_ar: قَالَ أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ عَنْ ءَالِهَتِى يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ ۖ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ لَأَرْجُمَنَّكَ ۖ وَٱهْجُرْنِى مَلِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: He threatened, “How dare you reject my idols, O  Abraham! If you do not desist, I will certainly stone you ˹to death˺. So be gone from me for a long time!”
text_en_yusufali: (The father) replied: "Dost thou hate my gods, O Abraham? If thou forbear not, I will indeed stone thee: Now get away from me for a good long while!"
text_en_pickthall: He said: Rejectest thou my gods, O Abraham ? If thou cease not, I shall surely stone thee. Depart from me a long while!
text_en_arberry: Said he, ’What, art thou shrinking from my gods, Abraham? Surely, if thou givest not over, I shall stone thee; so forsake me now for some while.’

text_ar: قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيْكَ ۖ سَأَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّىٓ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ بِى حَفِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: Abraham responded, “Peace be upon you! I will pray to my Lord for your forgiveness. He has truly been Most Gracious to me.
text_en_yusufali: Abraham said: "Peace be on thee: I will pray to my Lord for thy forgiveness: for He is to me Most Gracious.
text_en_pickthall: He said: Peace be unto thee! I shall ask forgiveness of my Lord for thee. Lo! He was ever gracious unto me.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’Peace be upon thee! I will ask my Lord to forgive thee; surely He is ever gracious to me.

text_ar: وَأَعْتَزِلُكُمْ وَمَا تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَدْعُوا۟ رَبِّى عَسَىٰٓ أَلَّآ أَكُونَ بِدُعَآءِ رَبِّى شَقِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: As I distance myself from ˹all of˺ you and from whatever you invoke besides Allah, I will ˹continue to˺ call upon my Lord ˹alone˺, trusting that I will never be disappointed in invoking my Lord.”
text_en_yusufali: "And I will turn away from you (all) and from those whom ye invoke besides God: I will call on my Lord: perhaps, by my prayer to my Lord, I shall be not unblest."
text_en_pickthall: I shall withdraw from you and that unto which ye pray beside Allah, and I shall pray unto my Lord. It may be that, in prayer unto my Lord, I shall not be unblest.
text_en_arberry: Now I will go apart from you and that you call upon, apart from God; I will call upon my Lord, and haply I shall not be, in calling upon my Lord, unprosperous.

text_ar: فَلَمَّا ٱعْتَزَلَهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ ۖ وَكُلًّۭا جَعَلْنَا نَبِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: So after he had left them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We granted him Isaac and Jacob, and made each of them a prophet.
text_en_yusufali: When he had turned away from them and from those whom they worshipped besides God, We bestowed on him Isaac and Jacob, and each one of them We made a prophet.
text_en_pickthall: So, when he had withdrawn from them and that which they were worshipping beside Allah, We gave him Isaac and Jacob. Each of them We made a prophet.
text_en_arberry: So, when he went apart from them and that they were serving, apart from God, We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and each We made a Prophet;

text_ar: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُم مِّن رَّحْمَتِنَا وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: We showered them with Our mercy, and blessed them with honourable mention.
text_en_yusufali: And We bestowed of Our Mercy on them, and We granted them lofty honour on the tongue of truth.
text_en_pickthall: And we gave them of Our mercy, and assigned to them a high and true renown.
text_en_arberry: and We gave them of Our mercy, and We appointed unto them a tongue of truthfulness, sublime.

text_ar: وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مُوسَىٰٓ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مُخْلَصًۭا وَكَانَ رَسُولًۭا نَّبِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Moses. He was truly a chosen man, and was a messenger and a prophet.
text_en_yusufali: Also mention in the Book (the story of) Moses: for he was specially chosen, and he was an apostle (and) a prophet.
text_en_pickthall: And make mention in the Scripture of Moses. Lo! he was chosen, and he was a messenger (of Allah), a prophet.
text_en_arberry: And mention in the Book Moses; he was devoted, and he was a Messenger, a Prophet.

text_ar: وَنَٰدَيْنَٰهُ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلْأَيْمَنِ وَقَرَّبْنَٰهُ نَجِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: We called him from the right side of Mount Ṭûr, and drew him near, speaking ˹with him˺ directly.
text_en_yusufali: And we called him from the right side of Mount (Sinai), and made him draw near to Us, for mystic (converse).
text_en_pickthall: We called him from the right slope of the Mount, and brought him nigh in communion.
text_en_arberry: We called to him from the right side Of the Mount, and We brought him near in communion.

text_ar: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥ مِن رَّحْمَتِنَآ أَخَاهُ هَٰرُونَ نَبِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: And We appointed for him—out of Our grace—his brother, Aaron, as a prophet.
text_en_yusufali: And, out of Our Mercy, We gave him his brother Aaron, (also) a prophet.
text_en_pickthall: And We bestowed upon him of Our mercy his brother Aaron, a prophet (likewise).
text_en_arberry: And We gave him his brother Aaron, of Our mercy, a Prophet.

text_ar: وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ إِسْمَٰعِيلَ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ صَادِقَ ٱلْوَعْدِ وَكَانَ رَسُولًۭا نَّبِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Ishmael. He was truly a man of his word, and was a messenger and a prophet.
text_en_yusufali: Also mention in the Book (the story of) Isma’il: He was (strictly) true to what he promised, and he was an apostle (and) a prophet.
text_en_pickthall: And make mention in the Scripture of Ishmael. Lo! he was a keeper of his promise, and he was a messenger (of Allah), a prophet.
text_en_arberry: And mention in the Book Ishmael; he was true to his promise, and he was a Messenger, a Prophet.

text_ar: وَكَانَ يَأْمُرُ أَهْلَهُۥ بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱلزَّكَوٰةِ وَكَانَ عِندَ رَبِّهِۦ مَرْضِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: He used to urge his people to pray and give alms-tax. And his Lord was well pleased with him.
text_en_yusufali: He used to enjoin on his people Prayer and Charity, and he was most acceptable in the sight of his Lord.
text_en_pickthall: He enjoined upon his people worship and almsgiving, and was acceptable in the sight of his Lord.
text_en_arberry: He bade his people to pray and to give the alms, and he was pleasing to his Lord.

text_ar: وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ إِدْرِيسَ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ صِدِّيقًۭا نَّبِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: And mention in the Book ˹O Prophet, the story of˺ Enoch. He was surely a man of truth and a prophet.
text_en_yusufali: Also mention in the Book the case of Idris: He was a man of truth (and sincerity), (and) a prophet:
text_en_pickthall: And make mention in the Scripture of Idris. Lo! he was a saint, a prophet;
text_en_arberry: And mention in the Book Idris; he was a true man, a Prophet.

text_ar: وَرَفَعْنَٰهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا
text_en_primary: And We elevated him to an honourable status.
text_en_yusufali: And We raised him to a lofty station.
text_en_pickthall: And We raised him to high station.
text_en_arberry: We raised him up to a high place.

text_ar: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ ٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ مِن ذُرِّيَّةِ ءَادَمَ وَمِمَّنْ حَمَلْنَا مَعَ نُوحٍۢ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّةِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَمِمَّنْ هَدَيْنَا وَٱجْتَبَيْنَآ ۚ إِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ خَرُّوا۟ سُجَّدًۭا وَبُكِيًّۭا ۩
text_en_primary: Those were ˹some of˺ the prophets who Allah has blessed from among the descendants of Adam, and of those We carried with Noah ˹in the Ark˺, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those We ˹rightly˺ guided and chose. Whenever the revelations of the Most Compassionate were recited to them, they fell down, prostrating and weeping.
text_en_yusufali: Those were some of the prophets on whom God did bestow His Grace,- of the posterity of Adam, and of those who We carried (in the Ark) with Noah, and of the posterity of Abraham and Israel of those whom We guided and chose. Whenever the Signs of (God) Most Gracious were rehearsed to them, they would fall down in prostrate adoration and in tears.
text_en_pickthall: These are they unto whom Allah showed favour from among the prophets, of the seed of Adam and of those whom We carried (in the ship) with Noah, and of the seed of Abraham and Israel, and from among those whom We guided and chose. When the revelations of the Beneficent were recited unto them, they fell down, adoring and weeping.
text_en_arberry: These are they whom God has blessed among the Prophets of the seed of Adam, and of those We bore with Noah, and of the seed of Abraham and Israel, and of those We guided and chose. When the signs of the All-merciful were recited to them, they fell down prostrate, weeping.

text_ar: ۞ فَخَلَفَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ أَضَاعُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ ٱلشَّهَوَٰتِ ۖ فَسَوْفَ يَلْقَوْنَ غَيًّا
text_en_primary: But they were succeeded by generations who neglected prayer and followed their lusts and so will soon face the evil consequences.
text_en_yusufali: But after them there followed a posterity who missed prayers and followed after lusts soon, then, will they face Destruction,-
text_en_pickthall: Now there hath succeeded them a later generation whom have ruined worship and have followed lusts. But they will meet deception.
text_en_arberry: Then there succeeded after them a succession who wasted the prayer, and followed lusts; so they shall encounter error

text_ar: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ شَيْـًۭٔا
text_en_primary: As for those who repent, believe, and do good, it is they who will be admitted into Paradise, never being denied any reward.
text_en_yusufali: Except those who repent and believe, and work righteousness: for these will enter the Garden and will not be wronged in the least,-
text_en_pickthall: Save him who shall repent and believe and do right. Such will enter the Garden, and they will not be wronged in aught -
text_en_arberry: save him who repents, and believes, and does a righteous deed; those -- they shall enter Paradise, and they shall not be wronged anything;

text_ar: جَنَّٰتِ عَدْنٍ ٱلَّتِى وَعَدَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ عِبَادَهُۥ بِٱلْغَيْبِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ وَعْدُهُۥ مَأْتِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: ˹They will be in˺ the Gardens of Eternity, promised in trust by the Most Compassionate to His servants. Surely His promise will be fulfilled.
text_en_yusufali: Gardens of Eternity, those which (God) Most Gracious has promised to His servants in the Unseen: for His promise must (necessarily) come to pass.
text_en_pickthall: Gardens of Eden, which the Beneficent hath promised to His slaves in the unseen. Lo! His promise is ever sure of fulfilment -
text_en_arberry: Gardens of Eden that the All-merciful promised His servants in the Unseen; His promise is ever performed.

text_ar: لَّا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًا إِلَّا سَلَٰمًۭا ۖ وَلَهُمْ رِزْقُهُمْ فِيهَا بُكْرَةًۭ وَعَشِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: There they will never hear any idle talk—only ˹greetings of˺ peace. And there they will have their provisions morning and evening.
