text_en_yusufali: They will not there hear any vain discourse, but only salutations of Peace: And they will have therein their sustenance, morning and evening.
text_en_pickthall: They hear therein no idle talk, but only Peace; and therein they have food for morn and evening.
text_en_arberry: There they shall hear no idle talk, but only ’Peace.’ There they shall have their provision at dawn and evening.

text_ar: تِلْكَ ٱلْجَنَّةُ ٱلَّتِى نُورِثُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا مَن كَانَ تَقِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: That is Paradise, which We will grant to whoever is devout among Our servants.
text_en_yusufali: Such is the Garden which We give as an inheritance to those of Our servants who guard against Evil.
text_en_pickthall: Such is the Garden which We cause the devout among Our bondmen to inherit.
text_en_arberry: That is Paradise which We shall give as an inheritance to those of Our servants who are godfearing.

text_ar: وَمَا نَتَنَزَّلُ إِلَّا بِأَمْرِ رَبِّكَ ۖ لَهُۥ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِينَا وَمَا خَلْفَنَا وَمَا بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ ۚ وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: “We only descend by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs whatever is before us, and whatever is behind us, and everything in between. And your Lord is never forgetful.
text_en_yusufali: (The angels say:) "We descend not but by command of thy Lord: to Him belongeth what is before us and what is behind us, and what is between: and thy Lord never doth forget,-
text_en_pickthall: We (angels) come not down save by commandment of thy Lord. Unto Him belongeth all that is before us and all that is behind us and all that is between those two, and thy Lord was never forgetful -
text_en_arberry: We come not down, save at the commandment of thy Lord. To Him belongs all that is before us, and all that is behind us, and all between that.

text_ar: رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فَٱعْبُدْهُ وَٱصْطَبِرْ لِعِبَٰدَتِهِۦ ۚ هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُۥ سَمِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: ˹He is the˺ Lord of the heavens, and the earth, and everything in between. So worship Him ˹alone˺, and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know of anyone equal to Him ˹in His attributes˺?”
text_en_yusufali: "Lord of the heavens and of the earth, and of all that is between them; so worship Him, and be constant and patient in His worship: knowest thou of any who is worthy of the same Name as He?"
text_en_pickthall: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them! Therefor, worship thou Him and be thou steadfast in His service. Knowest thou one that can be named along with Him ?
text_en_arberry: And thy Lord is never forgetful, Lord He of the heavens and earth and all that is between them. So serve Him, and be thou patient in His service; knowest thou any that can be named with His Name?

text_ar: وَيَقُولُ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ أَءِذَا مَا مِتُّ لَسَوْفَ أُخْرَجُ حَيًّا
text_en_primary: Yet ˹some˺ people ask ˹mockingly˺, “After I die, will I really be raised to life again?”
text_en_yusufali: Man says: "What! When I am dead, shall I then be raised up alive?"
text_en_pickthall: And man saith: When I am dead, shall I forsooth be brought forth alive ?
text_en_arberry: Man says, ’What, when I am dead shall I then be brought forth alive?’

text_ar: أَوَلَا يَذْكُرُ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَٰهُ مِن قَبْلُ وَلَمْ يَكُ شَيْـًۭٔا
text_en_primary: Do ˹such˺ people not remember that We created them before, when they were nothing?
text_en_yusufali: But does not man call to mind that We created him before out of nothing?
text_en_pickthall: Doth not man remember that We created him before, when he was naught ?
text_en_arberry: Will not man remember that We created him aforetime, when he was nothing?

text_ar: فَوَرَبِّكَ لَنَحْشُرَنَّهُمْ وَٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ ثُمَّ لَنُحْضِرَنَّهُمْ حَوْلَ جَهَنَّمَ جِثِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: By your Lord ˹O Prophet˺! We will surely gather them along with the devils, and then set them around Hell on their knees.
text_en_yusufali: So, by thy Lord, without doubt, We shall gather them together, and (also) the Evil Ones (with them); then shall We bring them forth on their knees round about Hell;
text_en_pickthall: And, by thy Lord, verily We shall assemble them and the devils, then We shall bring them, crouching, around hell.
text_en_arberry: Now, by thy Lord, We shall surely muster them, and the Satans, then We shall parade them about Gehenna hobbling on their knees.

text_ar: ثُمَّ لَنَنزِعَنَّ مِن كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ عِتِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: Then We will certainly begin by dragging out of every group the ones most defiant to the Most Compassionate.
text_en_yusufali: Then shall We certainly drag out from every sect all those who were worst in obstinate rebellion against (God) Most Gracious.
text_en_pickthall: Then We shall pluck out from every sect whichever of them was most stubborn in rebellion to the Beneficent.
text_en_arberry: Then We shall pluck forth from every party whichever of them was the most hardened in disdain of the All-merciful;

text_ar: ثُمَّ لَنَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِهَا صِلِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: And We truly know best who is most deserving of burning in it.
text_en_yusufali: And certainly We know best those who are most worthy of being burned therein.
text_en_pickthall: And surely We are Best Aware of those most worthy to be burned therein.
text_en_arberry: then We shall know very well those most deserving to burn there.

text_ar: وَإِن مِّنكُمْ إِلَّا وَارِدُهَا ۚ كَانَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ حَتْمًۭا مَّقْضِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: There is none of you who will not pass over it. ˹This is˺ a decree your Lord must fulfil.
text_en_yusufali: Not one of you but will pass over it: this is, with thy Lord, a Decree which must be accomplished.
text_en_pickthall: There is not one of you but shall approach it. That is a fixed ordinance of thy Lord.
text_en_arberry: Not one of you there is, but he shall go down to it; that for thy Lord is a thing decreed, determined.

text_ar: ثُمَّ نُنَجِّى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوا۟ وَّنَذَرُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ فِيهَا جِثِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: Then We will deliver those who were devout, leaving the wrongdoers there on their knees.
text_en_yusufali: But We shall save those who guarded against evil, and We shall leave the wrong-doers therein, (humbled) to their knees.
text_en_pickthall: Then We shall rescue those who kept from evil, and leave the evil- doers crouching there.
text_en_arberry: Then We shall deliver those that were godfearing; and the evildoers We shall leave there, hobbling on their knees.

text_ar: وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا بَيِّنَٰتٍۢ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ أَىُّ ٱلْفَرِيقَيْنِ خَيْرٌۭ مَّقَامًۭا وَأَحْسَنُ نَدِيًّۭا
text_en_primary: When Our clear revelations are recited to them, the disbelievers ask the believers ˹mockingly˺, “Which of the two of us is better in status and superior in assembly?”
text_en_yusufali: When Our Clear Signs are rehearsed to them, the Unbelievers say to those who believe, "Which of the two sides is best in point of position? Which makes the best show in council?"
text_en_pickthall: And when Our clear revelations are recited unto them, those who disbelieve say unto those who believe: Which of the two parties (yours or ours) is better in position, and more imposing as an army ?
text_en_arberry: When Our signs are recited to them as clear signs, the unbelievers say to the believers, ’Which of the two parties is better in station, fairer in assembly?’

text_ar: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَحْسَنُ أَثَٰثًۭا وَرِءْيًۭا
text_en_primary: ˹Imagine, O  Prophet˺ how many peoples We have destroyed before them, who were far better in luxury and splendour!
text_en_yusufali: But how many (countless) generations before them have we destroyed, who were even better in equipment and in glitter to the eye?
text_en_pickthall: How many a generation have We destroyed before them, who were more imposing in respect of gear and outward seeming!
text_en_arberry: And how many a generation We destroyed before them, who were fairer in furnishing and outward show!

text_ar: قُلْ مَن كَانَ فِى ٱلضَّلَٰلَةِ فَلْيَمْدُدْ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ مَدًّا ۚ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا رَأَوْا۟ مَا يُوعَدُونَ إِمَّا ٱلْعَذَابَ وَإِمَّا ٱلسَّاعَةَ فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ هُوَ شَرٌّۭ مَّكَانًۭا وَأَضْعَفُ جُندًۭا
text_en_primary: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Whoever is ˹entrenched˺ in misguidance, the Most Compassionate will allow them plenty of time, until—behold!—they face what they are threatened with: either the torment or the Hour. Only then will they realize who is worse in position and inferior in manpower.”
text_en_yusufali: Say: "If any men go astray, (God) Most Gracious extends (the rope) to them, until, when they see the warning of God (being fulfilled) - either in punishment or in (the approach of) the Hour,- they will at length realise who is worst in position, and (who) weakest in forces!
text_en_pickthall: Say: As for him who is in error, the Beneficent will verily prolong his span of life until, when they behold that which they were promised, whether it be punishment (in the world), or the Hour (of doom), they will know who is worse in position and who is weaker as an army.
text_en_arberry: Say: ’Whosoever is in error, let the All-merciful prolong his term for him! Till, when they see that they were threatened, whether the chastisement, or the Hour, then they shall surely know who is worse in place, and who is weaker in hosts.’

text_ar: وَيَزِيدُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱهْتَدَوْا۟ هُدًۭى ۗ وَٱلْبَٰقِيَٰتُ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ خَيْرٌ عِندَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابًۭا وَخَيْرٌۭ مَّرَدًّا
text_en_primary: And Allah increases in guidance those who are ˹rightly˺ guided. And the everlasting good deeds are far better with your Lord in reward and in outcome.
text_en_yusufali: "And God doth advance in guidance those who seek guidance: and the things that endure, Good Deeds, are best in the sight of thy Lord, as rewards, and best in respect of (their) eventual return."
text_en_pickthall: Allah increaseth in right guidance those who walk aright, and the good deeds which endure are better in thy Lord’s sight for reward, and better for resort.
text_en_arberry: And God shall increase those who were guided in guidance; and the abiding things, the deeds of righteousness, are better with thy Lord in reward, and better in return

text_ar: أَفَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى كَفَرَ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَقَالَ لَأُوتَيَنَّ مَالًۭا وَوَلَدًا
text_en_primary: Have you seen ˹O Prophet˺ the one who rejects Our revelations yet boasts, “I will definitely be granted ˹plenty of˺ wealth and children ˹if there is an afterlife˺.”?
text_en_yusufali: Hast thou then seen the (sort of) man who rejects Our Signs, yet says: "I shall certainly be given wealth and children?"
text_en_pickthall: Hast thou seen him who disbelieveth in Our revelations and saith: Assuredly I shall be given wealth and children ?
text_en_arberry: Hast thou seen him who disbelieves in Our signs and says, ’Assuredly I shall be given wealth and children’?

text_ar: أَطَّلَعَ ٱلْغَيْبَ أَمِ ٱتَّخَذَ عِندَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَهْدًۭا
text_en_primary: Has he looked into the unseen or taken a pledge from the Most Compassionate?
text_en_yusufali: Has he penetrated to the Unseen, or has he taken a contract with (God) Most Gracious?
text_en_pickthall: Hath he perused the Unseen, or hath he made a pact with the Beneficent ?
text_en_arberry: What, has he observed the Unseen, or taken a covenant with the All-merciful?

text_ar: كَلَّا ۚ سَنَكْتُبُ مَا يَقُولُ وَنَمُدُّ لَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ مَدًّۭا
text_en_primary: Not at all! We certainly record whatever he claims and will increase his punishment extensively.
text_en_yusufali: Nay! We shall record what he says, and We shall add and add to his punishment.
text_en_pickthall: Nay, but We shall record that which he saith and prolong for him a span of torment.
text_en_arberry: No, indeed! We shall assuredly write down all that he says, and We shall prolong for him the chastisement;

text_ar: وَنَرِثُهُۥ مَا يَقُولُ وَيَأْتِينَا فَرْدًۭا
text_en_primary: And We will inherit what he boasts of, and he will come before Us all by himself.
text_en_yusufali: To Us shall return all that he talks of and he shall appear before Us bare and alone.
text_en_pickthall: And We shall inherit from him that whereof he spake, and he will come unto Us, alone (without his wealth and children).
text_en_arberry: and We shall inherit from him that he says, and he shall come to Us alone.

text_ar: وَٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ ءَالِهَةًۭ لِّيَكُونُوا۟ لَهُمْ عِزًّۭا
text_en_primary: They have taken other gods, instead of Allah, seeking strength ˹and protection˺ through them.
text_en_yusufali: And they have taken (for worship) gods other than God, to give them power and glory!
text_en_pickthall: And they have chosen (other) gods beside Allah that they may be a power for them.
text_en_arberry: And they have taken to them other gods apart from God, that they might be for them a might.

text_ar: كَلَّا ۚ سَيَكْفُرُونَ بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدًّا
text_en_primary: But no! Those ˹gods˺ will deny their worship and turn against them.
text_en_yusufali: Instead, they shall reject their worship, and become adversaries against them.
text_en_pickthall: Nay, but they will deny their worship of them, and become opponents unto them.
text_en_arberry: No, indeed! They shall deny their service, and they shall be against them pitted.

text_ar: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا ٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ تَؤُزُّهُمْ أَزًّۭا
text_en_primary: Do you ˹O Prophet˺ not see that We have sent the devils against the disbelievers, constantly inciting them?
text_en_yusufali: Seest thou not that We have set the Evil Ones on against the unbelievers, to incite them with fury?
text_en_pickthall: Seest thou not that We have set the devils on the disbelievers to confound them with confusion ?
text_en_arberry: Hast thou not seen how We sent the Satans against the unbelievers, to prick them?

text_ar: فَلَا تَعْجَلْ عَلَيْهِمْ ۖ إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّ لَهُمْ عَدًّۭا
text_en_primary: So do not be in haste against them, for indeed We are ˹closely˺ counting down their days.
text_en_yusufali: So make no haste against them, for We but count out to them a (limited) number (of days).
text_en_pickthall: So make no haste against them (O Muhammad). We do but number unto them a sum (of days).
text_en_arberry: So hasten thou not against them; We are only numbering for them a number.

text_ar: يَوْمَ نَحْشُرُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ إِلَى ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ وَفْدًۭا
text_en_primary: ˹Watch for˺ the Day We will gather the righteous before the Most Compassionate as an honoured delegation,
text_en_yusufali: The day We shall gather the righteous to (God) Most Gracious, like a band presented before a king for honours,
text_en_pickthall: On the day when We shall gather the righteous unto the Beneficent, a goodly company.
text_en_arberry: On the day that We shall muster the godfearing to the All-merciful with pomp

text_ar: وَنَسُوقُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ وِرْدًۭا
text_en_primary: and drive the wicked to Hell like a thirsty herd.
text_en_yusufali: And We shall drive the sinners to Hell, like thirsty cattle driven down to water,-
text_en_pickthall: And drive the guilty unto hell, a weary herd,
text_en_arberry: and drive the evildoers into Gehenna herding,

text_ar: لَّا يَمْلِكُونَ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةَ إِلَّا مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ عِندَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَهْدًۭا
text_en_primary: None will have the right to intercede, except those who have taken a covenant from the Most Compassionate.
text_en_yusufali: None shall have the power of intercession, but such a one as has received permission (or promise) from (God) Most Gracious.
text_en_pickthall: They will have no power of intercession, save him who hath made a covenant with his Lord.
text_en_arberry: having no power of intercession, save those who have taken with the All-merciful covenant.

text_ar: وَقَالُوا۟ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَلَدًۭا
text_en_primary: They say, “The Most Compassionate has offspring.”
text_en_yusufali: They say: "(God) Most Gracious has begotten a son!"
text_en_pickthall: And they say: The Beneficent hath taken unto Himself a son.
text_en_arberry: And they say, ’The All-merciful has taken unto Himself a son.

text_ar: لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْـًٔا إِدًّۭا
text_en_primary: You have certainly made an outrageous claim,
text_en_yusufali: Indeed ye have put forth a thing most monstrous!
text_en_pickthall: Assuredly ye utter a disastrous thing
text_en_arberry: You have indeed advanced something hideous!

text_ar: تَكَادُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ وَتَنشَقُّ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَتَخِرُّ ٱلْجِبَالُ هَدًّا
text_en_primary: by which the heavens are about to burst, the earth to split apart, and the mountains to crumble to pieces
text_en_yusufali: At it the skies are ready to burst, the earth to split asunder, and the mountains to fall down in utter ruin,
text_en_pickthall: Whereby almost the heavens are torn, and the earth is split asunder and the mountains fall in ruins,
text_en_arberry: The heavens are wellnigh rent of it and the earth split asunder, and the mountains wellnigh fall down crashing for

text_ar: أَن دَعَوْا۟ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ وَلَدًۭا
text_en_primary: in protest of attributing children to the Most Compassionate.
text_en_yusufali: That they should invoke a son for (God) Most Gracious.
text_en_pickthall: That ye ascribe unto the Beneficent a son,
text_en_arberry: that they have attributed to the All-merciful a son;

text_ar: وَمَا يَنۢبَغِى لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا
text_en_primary: It does not befit ˹the majesty of˺ the Most Compassionate to have children.
text_en_yusufali: For it is not consonant with the majesty of (God) Most Gracious that He should beget a son.
text_en_pickthall: When it is not meet for (the Majesty of) the Beneficent that He should choose a son.
text_en_arberry: and it behoves not the All-merciful to take a son.

text_ar: إِن كُلُّ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّآ ءَاتِى ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَبْدًۭا
text_en_primary: There is none in the heavens or the earth who will not return to the Most Compassionate in full submission.
text_en_yusufali: Not one of the beings in the heavens and the earth but must come to (God) Most Gracious as a servant.
text_en_pickthall: There is none in the heavens and the earth but cometh unto the Beneficent as a slave.
text_en_arberry: None is there in the heavens and earth but he comes to the All-merciful as a servant;

text_ar: لَّقَدْ أَحْصَىٰهُمْ وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدًّۭا
text_en_primary: Indeed, He fully knows them and has counted them precisely.
text_en_yusufali: He does take an account of them (all), and hath numbered them (all) exactly.
text_en_pickthall: Verily He knoweth them and numbereth them with (right) numbering.
text_en_arberry: He has indeed counted them, and He has numbered them exactly.

text_ar: وَكُلُّهُمْ ءَاتِيهِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَرْدًا
text_en_primary: And each of them will return to Him on the Day of Judgment all alone.
text_en_yusufali: And everyone of them will come to Him singly on the Day of Judgment.
text_en_pickthall: And each one of them will come unto Him on the Day of Resurrection, alone.
text_en_arberry: Every one of them shall come to Him upon the Day of Resurrection, all alone.

text_ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ سَيَجْعَلُ لَهُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وُدًّۭا
text_en_primary: As for those who believe and do good, the Most Compassionate will ˹certainly˺ bless them with ˹genuine˺ love.
text_en_yusufali: On those who believe and work deeds of righteousness, will (God) Most Gracious bestow love.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! those who believe and do good works, the Beneficent will appoint for them love.
text_en_arberry: Surely those who believe and do deeds of righteousness -- unto them the All-merciful shall assign love.

text_ar: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَٰهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لِتُبَشِّرَ بِهِ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ وَتُنذِرَ بِهِۦ قَوْمًۭا لُّدًّۭا
text_en_primary: Indeed, We have made this ˹Quran˺ easy in your own language ˹O Prophet˺ so with it you may give good news to the righteous and warn those who are contentious.
text_en_yusufali: So have We made the (Qur’an) easy in thine own tongue, that with it thou mayest give Glad Tidings to the righteous, and warnings to people given to contention.
text_en_pickthall: And We make (this Scripture) easy in thy tongue, (O Muhammad) only that thou mayst bear good tidings therewith unto those who ward off (evil), and warn therewith the froward folk.
text_en_arberry: Now We have made it easy by thy tongue that thou mayest bear good tidings thereby to the godfearing, and warn a people stubborn.

text_ar: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْنٍ هَلْ تُحِسُّ مِنْهُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَوْ تَسْمَعُ لَهُمْ رِكْزًۢا
text_en_primary: ˹Imagine˺ how many peoples We have destroyed before them! Do you ˹still˺ see any of them, or ˹even˺ hear from them the slightest sound?
text_en_yusufali: But how many (countless) generations before them have We destroyed? Canst thou find a single one of them (now) or hear (so much as) a whisper of them?
text_en_pickthall: And how many a generation before them have We destroyed! Canst thou (Muhammad) see a single man of them, or hear from them the slightest sound ?
text_en_arberry: And how many a generation We destroyed before them! Dost thou perceive so much as one of them, or hear of them a whisper?

text_ar: طه
text_en_primary: Ṭa-Ha.
text_en_yusufali: Ta-Ha.
text_en_pickthall: Ta. Ha.
text_en_arberry: Ta Ha

text_ar: مَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِتَشْقَىٰٓ
text_en_primary: We have not revealed the Quran to you ˹O Prophet˺ to cause you distress,
text_en_yusufali: We have not sent down the Qur’an to thee to be (an occasion) for thy distress,
text_en_pickthall: We have not revealed unto thee (Muhammad) this Qur’an that thou shouldst be distressed,
text_en_arberry: We have not sent down the Koran upon thee for thee to be unprosperous,

text_ar: إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةًۭ لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ
text_en_primary: but as a reminder to those in awe ˹of Allah˺.
text_en_yusufali: But only as an admonition to those who fear (God),-
text_en_pickthall: But as a reminder unto him who feareth,
text_en_arberry: but only as a reminder to him who tears,

text_ar: تَنزِيلًۭا مِّمَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ ٱلْعُلَى
text_en_primary: ˹It is˺ a revelation from the One Who created the earth and the high heavens—
text_en_yusufali: A revelation from Him Who created the earth and the heavens on high.
text_en_pickthall: A revelation from Him Who created the earth and the high heavens,
text_en_arberry: a revelation from Him who created the earth and the high heavens;

text_ar: ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱسْتَوَىٰ
text_en_primary: the Most Compassionate, ˹Who is˺ established on the Throne.
text_en_yusufali: (God) Most Gracious is firmly established on the throne (of authority).
text_en_pickthall: The Beneficent One, Who is established on the Throne.
text_en_arberry: the All-compassionate sat Himself upon the Throne; to Him belongs

text_ar: لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحْتَ ٱلثَّرَىٰ
text_en_primary: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is in between and whatever is underground.
text_en_yusufali: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and on earth, and all between them, and all beneath the soil.
text_en_pickthall: Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, and whatsoever is between them, and whatsoever is beneath the sod.
text_en_arberry: all that is in the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and all that is underneath the soil.

text_ar: وَإِن تَجْهَرْ بِٱلْقَوْلِ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَعْلَمُ ٱلسِّرَّ وَأَخْفَى
text_en_primary: Whether you speak openly ˹or not˺, He certainly knows what is secret and what is even more hidden.
text_en_yusufali: If thou pronounce the word aloud, (it is no matter): for verily He knoweth what is secret and what is yet more hidden.
text_en_pickthall: And if thou speakest aloud, then lo! He knoweth the secret (thought) and (that which is yet) more hidden.
text_en_arberry: Be thou loud in thy speech, yet surely He knows the secret and that yet more hidden.

text_ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ لَهُ ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ
text_en_primary: Allah—there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. He has the Most Beautiful Names.
text_en_yusufali: God! there is no god but He! To Him belong the most Beautiful Names.
text_en_pickthall: Allah! There is no God save Him. His are the most beautiful names.
text_en_arberry: God -- there is no god but He. To Him belong the Names Most Beautiful.

text_ar: وَهَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَىٰٓ
text_en_primary: Has the story of Moses reached you ˹O Prophet˺?
text_en_yusufali: Has the story of Moses reached thee?
text_en_pickthall: Hath there come unto thee the story of Moses ?
text_en_arberry: Hast thou received the story of Moses?

text_ar: إِذْ رَءَا نَارًۭا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوٓا۟ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًۭا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدًۭى
text_en_primary: When he saw a fire, he said to his family, “Wait here, ˹for˺ I have spotted a fire. Perhaps I can bring you a torch from it, or find some guidance at the fire.”
text_en_yusufali: Behold, he saw a fire: So he said to his family, "Tarry ye; I perceive a fire; perhaps I can bring you some burning brand therefrom, or find some guidance at the fire."
text_en_pickthall: When he saw a fire and said unto his folk: Lo! Wait! I see a fire afar off. Peradventure I may bring you a brand therefrom or may find guidance at the fire.
text_en_arberry: When he saw a tire, and said to his family, ’Tarry you here; I observe a fire. Perhaps I shall bring you a brand from it, or I shall find at the fire guidance.’

text_ar: فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِىَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ
text_en_primary: But when he approached it, he was called, “O Moses!
text_en_yusufali: But when he came to the fire, a voice was heard: "O Moses!
text_en_pickthall: And when he reached it, he was called by name: O Moses!
text_en_arberry: When he came to it, a voice cried, ’Moses,

text_ar: إِنِّىٓ أَنَا۠ رَبُّكَ فَٱخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ ۖ إِنَّكَ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًۭى
text_en_primary: It is truly I. I am your Lord! So take off your sandals, for you are in the sacred valley of Ṭuwa.
text_en_yusufali: "Verily I am thy Lord! therefore (in My presence) put off thy shoes: thou art in the sacred valley Tuwa.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! I, even I, am thy Lord, So take off thy shoes, for lo! thou art in the holy valley of Tuwa.
text_en_arberry: I am thy Lord; put off thy shoes; thou art in the holy valley, Towa.

text_ar: وَأَنَا ٱخْتَرْتُكَ فَٱسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَىٰٓ
text_en_primary: I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed:
text_en_yusufali: "I have chosen thee: listen, then, to the inspiration (sent to thee).
text_en_pickthall: And I have chosen thee, so hearken unto that which is inspired.
text_en_arberry: I Myself have chosen thee; therefore give thou ear to this revelation.

text_ar: إِنَّنِىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعْبُدْنِى وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكْرِىٓ
text_en_primary: ‘It is truly I. I am Allah! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Me. So worship Me ˹alone˺, and establish prayer for My remembrance.
text_en_yusufali: "Verily, I am God: There is no god but I: So serve thou Me (only), and establish regular prayer for celebrating My praise.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! I, even I, am Allah, There is no God save Me. So serve Me and establish worship for My remembrance.
text_en_arberry: Verily I am God; there is no god but I; therefore serve Me, and perform the prayer of My remembrance.

text_ar: إِنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا لِتُجْزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفْسٍۭ بِمَا تَسْعَىٰ
text_en_primary: The Hour is sure to come. My Will is to keep it hidden, so that every soul may be rewarded according to their efforts.
text_en_yusufali: "Verily the Hour is coming - My design is to keep it hidden - for every soul to receive its reward by the measure of its Endeavour.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! the Hour is surely coming. But I will to keep it hidden, that every soul may be rewarded for that which it striveth (to achieve).
text_en_arberry: The Hour is coming; I would conceal it that every soul may be recompensed for its labours.

text_ar: فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَن لَّا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ فَتَرْدَىٰ
text_en_primary: So do not let those who disbelieve in it and follow their desires distract you from it, or you will be doomed.’”
text_en_yusufali: "Therefore let not such as believe not therein but follow their own lusts, divert thee therefrom, lest thou perish!"..
text_en_pickthall: Therefor, let not him turn thee aside from (the thought of) it who believeth not therein but followeth his own desire, lest thou perish.
text_en_arberry: Let none bar thee from it, that believes not in it but follows after his own caprice, or thou wilt perish.

text_ar: وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
text_en_primary: ˹Allah added,˺ “And what is that in your right hand, O  Moses?”
text_en_yusufali: "And what is that in the right hand, O Moses?"
text_en_pickthall: And what is that in thy right hand, O Moses ?
text_en_arberry: What is that, Moses, thou hast in thy right hand?’

text_ar: قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا۟ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى وَلِىَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخْرَىٰ
text_en_primary: He replied, “It is my staff! I lean on it, and with it I beat down ˹branches˺ for my sheep, and have other uses for it.”
text_en_yusufali: He said, "It is my rod: on it I lean; with it I beat down fodder for my flocks; and in it I find other uses."
text_en_pickthall: He said: This is my staff whereon I lean, and wherewith I bear down branches for my sheep, and He said: This is my staff whereon I lean, and wherewith I bear down branches for my sheep, and wherein I find other uses.
text_en_arberry: ’Why, it is my staff,’ said Moses. ’I lean upon it, and with it I beat down leaves to feed my sheep; other uses also I find in it.

text_ar: قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَٰمُوسَىٰ
text_en_primary: Allah said, “Throw it down, O  Moses!”
text_en_yusufali: (God) said, "Throw it, O Moses!"
text_en_pickthall: He said: Cast it down, O Moses!
text_en_arberry: Said He, ’Cast it down, Moses!’

text_ar: فَأَلْقَىٰهَا فَإِذَا هِىَ حَيَّةٌۭ تَسْعَىٰ
text_en_primary: So he did, then—behold!—it became a serpent, slithering.
text_en_yusufali: He threw it, and behold! It was a snake, active in motion.
text_en_pickthall: So he cast it down, and lo! it was a serpent, gliding.
text_en_arberry: and he cast it down, and behold it was a serpent sliding.

text_ar: قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ ۖ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ
text_en_primary: Allah said, “Take it, and have no fear. We will return it to its former state.
text_en_yusufali: (God) said, "Seize it, and fear not: We shall return it at once to its former condition"..
text_en_pickthall: He said: Grasp it and fear not. We shall return it to its former state.
text_en_arberry: Said He, ’Take it, and fear not; We will restore it to its first state.

text_ar: وَٱضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ ءَايَةً أُخْرَىٰ
text_en_primary: And put your hand under your armpit, it will come out ˹shining˺ white, unblemished, as another sign,
text_en_yusufali: "Now draw thy hand close to thy side: It shall come forth white (and shining), without harm (or stain),- as another Sign,-
text_en_pickthall: And thrust thy hand within thine armpit, it will come forth white without hurt. (That will be) another token.
text_en_arberry: Now clasp thy hand to thy arm-pit; it shall come forth white, without evil. That is a second sign.

text_ar: لِنُرِيَكَ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَا ٱلْكُبْرَى
text_en_primary: so that We may show you some of Our greatest signs.
text_en_yusufali: "In order that We may show thee (two) of our Greater Signs.
text_en_pickthall: That We may show thee (some) of Our greater portents,
text_en_arberry: So We would show thee some of Our greatest signs.

text_ar: ٱذْهَبْ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُۥ طَغَىٰ
text_en_primary: Go to Pharaoh, for he has truly transgressed ˹all bounds˺.”
text_en_yusufali: "Go thou to Pharaoh, for he has indeed transgressed all bounds."
text_en_pickthall: Go thou unto Pharaoh! Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds).
text_en_arberry: Go to Pharaoh; he has waxed insolent.’

text_ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى
text_en_primary: Moses prayed, “My Lord! Uplift my heart for me,
text_en_yusufali: (Moses) said: "O my Lord! expand me my breast;
text_en_pickthall: (Moses) said: My Lord! relieve my mind
text_en_arberry: ’Lord, open my breast,’ said Moses,

text_ar: وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى
text_en_primary: and make my task easy,
text_en_yusufali: "Ease my task for me;
text_en_pickthall: And ease my task for me;
text_en_arberry: ’and do Thou ease for me my task.

text_ar: وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةًۭ مِّن لِّسَانِى
text_en_primary: and remove the impediment from my tongue
text_en_yusufali: "And remove the impediment from my speech,
text_en_pickthall: And loose a knot from my tongue,
text_en_arberry: Unloose the knot upon my tongue, t

text_ar: يَفْقَهُوا۟ قَوْلِى
text_en_primary: so people may understand my speech,
text_en_yusufali: "So they may understand what I say:
text_en_pickthall: That they may understand my saying.
text_en_arberry: hat they may understand my words.

text_ar: وَٱجْعَل لِّى وَزِيرًۭا مِّنْ أَهْلِى
text_en_primary: and grant me a helper from my family,
text_en_yusufali: "And give me a Minister from my family,
text_en_pickthall: Appoint for me a henchman from my folk,
text_en_arberry: Appoint for me of my folk a familiar,

text_ar: هَٰرُونَ أَخِى
text_en_primary: Aaron, my brother.
text_en_yusufali: "Aaron, my brother;
text_en_pickthall: Aaron, my brother.
text_en_arberry: Aaron, my brother;

text_ar: ٱشْدُدْ بِهِۦٓ أَزْرِى
text_en_primary: Strengthen me through him,
text_en_yusufali: "Add to my strength through him,
text_en_pickthall: Confirm my strength with him
text_en_arberry: by him confirm my strength,

text_ar: وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِىٓ أَمْرِى
text_en_primary: and let him share my task,
text_en_yusufali: "And make him share my task:
text_en_pickthall: And let him share my task,
text_en_arberry: and associate him with me in my task.

text_ar: كَىْ نُسَبِّحَكَ كَثِيرًۭا
text_en_primary: so that we may glorify You much
text_en_yusufali: "That we may celebrate Thy praise without stint,
text_en_pickthall: That we may glorify Thee much
text_en_arberry: So shall we glorify Thee,

text_ar: وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيرًا
text_en_primary: and remember You much,
text_en_yusufali: "And remember Thee without stint:
text_en_pickthall: And much remember Thee.
text_en_arberry: and remember Thee abundantly.

text_ar: إِنَّكَ كُنتَ بِنَا بَصِيرًۭا
text_en_primary: for truly You have ˹always˺ been overseeing us.”
text_en_yusufali: "For Thou art He that (ever) regardeth us."
text_en_pickthall: Lo! Thou art ever Seeing us.
text_en_arberry: Surely Thou seest into us.’

text_ar: قَالَ قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
text_en_primary: Allah responded, “All that you requested has been granted, O  Moses!
text_en_yusufali: (God) said: "Granted is thy prayer, O Moses!"
text_en_pickthall: He said: Thou art granted thy request, O Moses.
text_en_arberry: Said He, ’Thou art granted, Moses, thy petition.

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَيْكَ مَرَّةً أُخْرَىٰٓ
text_en_primary: And surely We had shown You favour before,
text_en_yusufali: "And indeed We conferred a favour on thee another time (before).
text_en_pickthall: And indeed, another time, already We have shown thee favour,
text_en_arberry: Already another time We favoured thee,

text_ar: إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ
text_en_primary: when We inspired your mother with this:
text_en_yusufali: "Behold! We sent to thy mother, by inspiration, the message:
text_en_pickthall: When we inspired in thy mother that which is inspired,
text_en_arberry: when We revealed what was revealed unto thy mother:

text_ar: أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّۭ لِّى وَعَدُوٌّۭ لَّهُۥ ۚ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةًۭ مِّنِّى وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِىٓ
text_en_primary: ‘Put him into a chest, then put it into the river. The river will wash it ashore, and he will be taken by ˹Pharaoh,˺ an enemy of Mine and his.’ And I blessed you with lovability from Me ˹O Moses˺ so that you would be brought up under My ˹watchful˺ Eye.
text_en_yusufali: "’Throw (the child) into the chest, and throw (the chest) into the river: the river will cast him up on the bank, and he will be taken up by one who is an enemy to Me and an enemy to him’: But I cast (the garment of) love over thee from Me: and (this) in order that thou mayest be reared under Mine eye.
text_en_pickthall: Saying: Throw him into the ark, and throw it into the river, then the river shall throw it on to the bank, and there an enemy to Me and an enemy to him shall take him. And I endued thee with love from Me that thou mightest be trained according to My will,
text_en_arberry: "Cast him into the ark, and cast him into the river, and let the river throw him up on the shore. An enemy of Mine and his shall take him." And I loaded on thee love from Me, and to be formed in My sight,

text_ar: إِذْ تَمْشِىٓ أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكْفُلُهُۥ ۖ فَرَجَعْنَٰكَ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ ۚ وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًۭا فَنَجَّيْنَٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّٰكَ فُتُونًۭا ۚ فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِىٓ أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَىٰ قَدَرٍۢ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
text_en_primary: ˹Remember˺ when your sister came along and proposed, ‘Shall I direct you to someone who will nurse him?’ So We reunited you with your mother so that her heart would be put at ease, and she would not grieve. ˹Later˺ you killed a man ˹by mistake˺, but We saved you from sorrow, as well as other tests We put you through. Then you stayed for a number of years among the people of Midian. Then you came here as pre-destined, O  Moses!
text_en_yusufali: "Behold! thy sister goeth forth and saith, ’shall I show you one who will nurse and rear the (child)?’ So We brought thee back to thy mother, that her eye might be cooled and she should not grieve. Then thou didst slay a man, but We saved thee from trouble, and We tried thee in various ways. Then didst thou tarry a number of years with the people of Midian. Then didst thou come hither as ordained, O Moses!
text_en_pickthall: When thy sister went and said: Shall I show you one who will nurse him ? and we restored thee to thy mother that her eyes might be refreshed and might not sorrow. And thou didst kill a man and We delivered thee from great distress, and tried thee with a heavy trial. And thou didst tarry years among the folk of Midian. Then camest thou (hither) by (My) providence, O Moses,
text_en_arberry: when thy sister went out, saying, "Shall I point you to one to have charge of him?" So We returned thee to thy mother that she might rejoice, and not sorrow. Then thou slewest; a living soul, and We delivered thee out of grief, and We tried thee with many trials. Many years among the people of Midian thou didst sojourn, then camest hither, Moses, according to a decree.

text_ar: وَٱصْطَنَعْتُكَ لِنَفْسِى
text_en_primary: And I have selected you for My service.
text_en_yusufali: "And I have prepared thee for Myself (for service)"..
text_en_pickthall: And I have attached thee to Myself.
text_en_arberry: I have chosen thee for My service;

text_ar: ٱذْهَبْ أَنتَ وَأَخُوكَ بِـَٔايَٰتِى وَلَا تَنِيَا فِى ذِكْرِى
text_en_primary: Go forth, you and your brother, with My signs and never falter in remembering Me.
text_en_yusufali: "Go, thou and thy brother, with My Signs, and slacken not, either of you, in keeping Me in remembrance.
text_en_pickthall: Go, thou and thy brother, with My tokens, and be not faint in remembrance of Me.
text_en_arberry: go therefore, thou and thy brother; with My signs, and neglect not to remember Me.

text_ar: ٱذْهَبَآ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُۥ طَغَىٰ
text_en_primary: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh, for he has truly transgressed ˹all bounds˺.
text_en_yusufali: "Go, both of you, to Pharaoh, for he has indeed transgressed all bounds;
text_en_pickthall: Go, both of you, unto Pharaoh. Lo! he hath transgressed (the bounds).
text_en_arberry: Go to Pharaoh, for he has waxed insolent;

text_ar: فَقُولَا لَهُۥ قَوْلًۭا لَّيِّنًۭا لَّعَلَّهُۥ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشَىٰ
text_en_primary: Speak to him gently, so perhaps he may be mindful ˹of Me˺ or fearful ˹of My punishment˺.”
text_en_yusufali: "But speak to him mildly; perchance he may take warning or fear (God)."
text_en_pickthall: And speak unto him a gentle word, that peradventure he may heed or fear.
text_en_arberry: yet speak gently to him, that haply he may be mindful, or perchance fear.’

text_ar: قَالَا رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَن يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنَآ أَوْ أَن يَطْغَىٰ
text_en_primary: They both pleaded, “Our Lord! We fear that he may be quick to harm us or act tyrannically.”
text_en_yusufali: They (Moses and Aaron) said: "Our Lord! We fear lest he hasten with insolence against us, or lest he transgress all bounds."
text_en_pickthall: They said: Our Lord! Lo! we fear that he may be beforehand with us or that he may play the tyrant.
text_en_arberry: ’O our Lord,’ said Moses and Aaron, ’truly we fear he may exceed against us, or wax insolent.’

text_ar: قَالَ لَا تَخَافَآ ۖ إِنَّنِى مَعَكُمَآ أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ
text_en_primary: Allah reassured ˹them˺, “Have no fear! I am with you, hearing and seeing.
text_en_yusufali: He said: "Fear not: for I am with you: I hear and see (everything).
text_en_pickthall: He said: Fear not. Lo! I am with you twain, Hearing and Seeing.
text_en_arberry: ’Fear not,’ said He. ’Surely I shall be with you, hearing and seeing.

text_ar: فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ ۖ قَدْ جِئْنَٰكَ بِـَٔايَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّكَ ۖ وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ
text_en_primary: So go to him and say, ‘Indeed we are both messengers from your Lord, so let the Children of Israel go with us, and do not oppress them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And salvation will be for whoever follows the ˹right˺ guidance.
text_en_yusufali: "So go ye both to him, and say, ’Verily we are apostles sent by thy Lord: Send forth, therefore, the Children of Israel with us, and afflict them not: with a Sign, indeed, have we come from thy Lord! and peace to all who follow guidance!
text_en_pickthall: So go ye unto him and say: Lo! we are two messengers of thy Lord. So let the children of Israel go with us, and torment them not. We bring thee a token from thy Lord. And peace will be for him who followeth right guidance.
text_en_arberry: So go you both to Pharaoh, and say, "We are the Messengers of thy Lord, so send forth with us the Children of Israel and chastise them not; we have brought thee a sign from thy Lord; and peace be upon him who follows the guidance!

text_ar: إِنَّا قَدْ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْنَآ أَنَّ ٱلْعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
text_en_primary: It has indeed been revealed to us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies ˹the truth˺ and turns away.’”
text_en_yusufali: "’Verily it has been revealed to us that the Penalty (awaits) those who reject and turn away.’"
text_en_pickthall: Lo! it hath been revealed unto us that the doom will be for him who denieth and turneth away.
text_en_arberry: It has been revealed to us that chastisement shall light upon him who cries lies and turns his back."

text_ar: قَالَ فَمَن رَّبُّكُمَا يَٰمُوسَىٰ
text_en_primary: Pharaoh asked, “Who then is the Lord of you two, O  Moses?”
text_en_yusufali: (When this message was delivered), (Pharaoh) said: "Who, then, O Moses, is the Lord of you two?"
text_en_pickthall: (Pharaoh) said: Who then is the Lord of you twain, O Moses ?
text_en_arberry: Pharaoh said, ’Who is your Lord, Moses?’

text_ar: قَالَ رَبُّنَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ
text_en_primary: He answered, “Our Lord is the One Who has given everything its ˹distinctive˺ form, then guided ˹it˺.”
text_en_yusufali: He said: "Our Lord is He Who gave to each (created) thing its form and nature, and further, gave (it) guidance."
text_en_pickthall: He said: Our Lord is He Who gave unto everything its nature, then guided it aright.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided it.’

text_ar: قَالَ فَمَا بَالُ ٱلْقُرُونِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ
text_en_primary: Pharaoh asked, “And what about previous peoples?”
text_en_yusufali: (Pharaoh) said: "What then is the condition of previous generations?"
text_en_pickthall: He said: What then is the state of the generations of old ?
text_en_arberry: Pharaoh said, ’And what of the former generations?’

text_ar: قَالَ عِلْمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّى فِى كِتَٰبٍۢ ۖ لَّا يَضِلُّ رَبِّى وَلَا يَنسَى
text_en_primary: He replied, “That knowledge is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither falters nor forgets ˹anything˺.”
text_en_yusufali: He replied: "The knowledge of that is with my Lord, duly recorded: my Lord never errs, nor forgets,-
text_en_pickthall: He said: The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither erreth nor forgetteth,
text_en_arberry: Said Moses, ’The knowledge of them is with my Lord, in a Book; my Lord goes not astray, nor forgets --

text_ar: ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ مَهْدًۭا وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلًۭا وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزْوَٰجًۭا مِّن نَّبَاتٍۢ شَتَّىٰ
text_en_primary: ˹He is the One˺ Who has laid out the earth for ˹all of˺ you, and set in it pathways for you, and sends down rain from the sky, causing various types of plants to grow,
text_en_yusufali: "He Who has, made for you the earth like a carpet spread out; has enabled you to go about therein by roads (and channels); and has sent down water from the sky." With it have We produced diverse pairs of plants each separate from the others.
text_en_pickthall: Who hath appointed the earth as a bed and hath threaded roads for you therein and hath sent down water from the sky and thereby We have brought forth divers kinds of vegetation,
text_en_arberry: He who appointed the earth to be a cradle for you, and therein threaded roads for you, and sent down water out of heaven, and therewith We have brought forth divers kinds of plants.

text_ar: كُلُوا۟ وَٱرْعَوْا۟ أَنْعَٰمَكُمْ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلنُّهَىٰ
text_en_primary: ˹so˺ eat and graze your cattle. Surely in this are signs for people of sound judgment.
text_en_yusufali: Eat (for yourselves) and pasture your cattle: verily, in this are Signs for men endued with understanding.
text_en_pickthall: (Saying): Eat ye and feed your cattle. Lo! herein verily are portents for men of thought.
text_en_arberry: Do you eat, and pasture your cattle! Surely in that are signs for men possessing reason.

text_ar: ۞ مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرَىٰ
text_en_primary: From the earth We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you back again.
text_en_yusufali: From the (earth) did We create you, and into it shall We return you, and from it shall We bring you out once again.
text_en_pickthall: Thereof We created you, and thereunto We return you, and thence We bring you forth a second time.
text_en_arberry: Out of the earth We created you, and We shall restore you into it, and bring you forth from it a second time.’

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبَىٰ
text_en_primary: And We certainly showed Pharaoh all of Our signs, but he denied them and refused ˹to believe˺.
text_en_yusufali: And We showed Pharaoh all Our Signs, but he did reject and refuse.
text_en_pickthall: And We verily did show him all Our tokens, but he denied them and refused.
text_en_arberry: So We showed Pharaoh all Our signs, but he cried lies, and refused.

text_ar: قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا بِسِحْرِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
text_en_primary: He said, “Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, O  Moses?
text_en_yusufali: He said: "Hast thou come to drive us out of our land with thy magic, O Moses?
text_en_pickthall: He said: Hast come to drive us out from our land by thy magic, O Moses ?
text_en_arberry: ’Hast thou come, Moses,’ he said, ’to expel us out of our land

text_ar: فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍۢ مِّثْلِهِۦ فَٱجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًۭا لَّا نُخْلِفُهُۥ نَحْنُ وَلَآ أَنتَ مَكَانًۭا سُوًۭى
text_en_primary: We can surely meet you with similar magic. So set for us an appointment that neither of us will fail to keep, in a central place.”
text_en_yusufali: "But we can surely produce magic to match thine! So make a tryst between us and thee, which we shall not fail to keep - neither we nor thou - in a place where both shall have even chances."
text_en_pickthall: But we surely can produce for thee magic the like thereof; so appoint a tryst between us and you, which neither we nor thou shall fail to keep, at a place convenient (to us both).
text_en_arberry: by thy sorcery? We shall assuredly bring thee sorcery the like of it; therefore appoint a tryst between us and thee, a place mutually agreeable, and we shall not fail it, neither thou.’

text_ar: قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ ٱلزِّينَةِ وَأَن يُحْشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحًۭى
text_en_primary: Moses said, “Your appointment is on the Day of the Festival, and let the people be gathered mid-morning.”
text_en_yusufali: Moses said: "Your tryst is the Day of the Festival, and let the people be assembled when the sun is well up."
text_en_pickthall: (Moses) said: Your tryst shall be the day of the feast, and let the people assemble when the sun hath risen high.
text_en_arberry: ’Your tryst shall be upon the Feast Day.’ said Moses. ’Let the people be mustered at the high noon.’

text_ar: فَتَوَلَّىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُۥ ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ
text_en_primary: Pharaoh then withdrew, orchestrated his scheme, then returned.
text_en_yusufali: So Pharaoh withdrew: He concerted his plan, and then came (back).
text_en_pickthall: Then Pharaoh went and gathered his strength, then came (to the appointed tryst).
text_en_arberry: Pharaoh then withdrew, and gathered his guile. Thereafter he came again,

text_ar: قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰ وَيْلَكُمْ لَا تَفْتَرُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًۭا فَيُسْحِتَكُم بِعَذَابٍۢ ۖ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ
text_en_primary: Moses warned the magicians, “Woe to you! Do not fabricate a lie against Allah, or He will wipe you out with a torment. Whoever fabricates ˹lies˺ is bound to fail.”
text_en_yusufali: Moses said to him: Woe to you! Forge not ye a lie against God, lest He destroy you (at once) utterly by chastisement: the forger must suffer frustration!"
text_en_pickthall: Moses said unto them: Woe unto you! Invent not a lie against Allah, lest He extirpate you by some punishment. He who lieth faileth miserably.
text_en_arberry: and Moses said to them, ’O beware! Forge not a lie against God, lest He destroy you with a chastisement. Whoso forges has ever failed.’

text_ar: فَتَنَٰزَعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا۟ ٱلنَّجْوَىٰ
text_en_primary: So the magicians disputed the matter among themselves, conversing privately.
text_en_yusufali: So they disputed, one with another, over their affair, but they kept their talk secret.
text_en_pickthall: Then they debated one with another what they must do, and they kept their counsel secret.
text_en_arberry: And they disputed upon their plan between them, and communed secretly

text_ar: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنْ هَٰذَٰنِ لَسَٰحِرَٰنِ يُرِيدَانِ أَن يُخْرِجَاكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِمَا وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ ٱلْمُثْلَىٰ
text_en_primary: They concluded, “These two are only magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic, and do away with your most cherished traditions.
text_en_yusufali: They said: "These two are certainly (expert) magicians: their object is to drive you out from your land with their magic, and to do away with your most cherished institutions.
text_en_pickthall: They said: Lo! these are two wizards who would drive you out from your country by their magic, and destroy your best traditions;
text_en_arberry: saying, ’These two men are sorcerers and their purpose is to expel you out of your land by their sorcery, and to extirpate your justest way.

text_ar: فَأَجْمِعُوا۟ كَيْدَكُمْ ثُمَّ ٱئْتُوا۟ صَفًّۭا ۚ وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مَنِ ٱسْتَعْلَىٰ
text_en_primary: So orchestrate your plan, then come forward in ˹perfect˺ ranks. And whoever prevails today will certainly be successful.”
text_en_yusufali: "Therefore concert your plan, and then assemble in (serried) ranks: He wins (all along) today who gains the upper hand."
text_en_pickthall: So arrange your plan, and come in battle line. Whoso is uppermost this day will be indeed successful.
text_en_arberry: So gather your guile; then come in battle-line. Whoever today gains the upper hand shall surely prosper.

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِىَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ
text_en_primary: They said, “O Moses! Either you cast, or let us be the first to cast.”
text_en_yusufali: They said: "O Moses! whether wilt thou that thou throw (first) or that we be the first to throw?"
text_en_pickthall: They said: O Moses! Either throw first, or let us be the first to throw ?
text_en_arberry: They said, ’Moses, either thou wilt cast, or we shall be the first to cast.’

text_ar: قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا۟ ۖ فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ
text_en_primary: Moses responded, “No, you go first.” And suddenly their ropes and staffs appeared to him—by their magic—to be slithering.
text_en_yusufali: He said, "Nay, throw ye first!" Then behold their ropes and their rods-so it seemed to him on account of their magic - began to be in lively motion!
text_en_pickthall: He said: Nay, do ye throw! Then lo! their cords and their staves, by their magic, appeared to him as though they ran.
text_en_arberry: ’No,’ said Moses. ’Do you cast!’ And lo, it seemed to him, by their sorcery, their ropes and their staffs were sliding;

text_ar: فَأَوْجَسَ فِى نَفْسِهِۦ خِيفَةًۭ مُّوسَىٰ
text_en_primary: So Moses concealed fear within himself.
text_en_yusufali: So Moses conceived in his mind a (sort of) fear.
text_en_pickthall: And Moses conceived a fear in his mind.
text_en_arberry: and Moses conceived a fear within him.

text_ar: قُلْنَا لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ
text_en_primary: We reassured ˹him˺, “Do not fear! It is certainly you who will prevail.
text_en_yusufali: We said: "Fear not! for thou hast indeed the upper hand:
text_en_pickthall: We said: Fear not! Lo! thou art the higher.
text_en_arberry: We said unto him, ’Fear not; surely thou art the uppermost.

text_ar: وَأَلْقِ مَا فِى يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوٓا۟ ۖ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا۟ كَيْدُ سَٰحِرٍۢ ۖ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ
text_en_primary: Cast what is in your right hand, and it will swallow up what they have made, for what they have made is no more than a magic trick. And magicians can never succeed wherever they go.”
text_en_yusufali: "Throw that which is in thy right hand: Quickly will it swallow up that which they have faked what they have faked is but a magician’s trick: and the magician thrives not, (no matter) where he goes."
text_en_pickthall: Throw that which is in thy right hand! It will eat up that which they have made. Lo! that which they have made is but a wizard’s artifice, and a wizard shall not be successful to whatever point (of skill) he may attain.
text_en_arberry: Cast down what is in thy right hand, and it shall swallow what they have fashioned; for they have fashioned only the guile of a sorcerer, and the sorcerer prospers not; wherever he goes.’

text_ar: فَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًۭا قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَٰرُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ
text_en_primary: So the magicians fell down in prostration, declaring, “We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.”
text_en_yusufali: So the magicians were thrown down to prostration: they said, "We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses".
text_en_pickthall: Then the wizards were (all) flung down prostrate, crying: We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.
text_en_arberry: And the sorcerers cast themselves down prostrating. ’We believe,’ they said, ’in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.’

text_ar: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ ۖ فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍۢ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِى جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخْلِ وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَآ أَشَدُّ عَذَابًۭا وَأَبْقَىٰ
text_en_primary: Pharaoh threatened, “How dare you believe in him before I give you permission? He must be your master who taught you magic. I will certainly cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and crucify you on the trunks of palm trees. You will really see whose punishment is more severe and more lasting.”
text_en_yusufali: (Pharaoh) said: "Believe ye in Him before I give you permission? Surely this must be your leader, who has taught you magic! be sure I will cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will have you crucified on trunks of palm-trees: so shall ye know for certain, which of us can give the more severe and the more lasting punishment!"
text_en_pickthall: (Pharaoh) said: Ye put faith in him before I give you leave. Lo! he is your chief who taught you magic. Now surely I shall cut off your hands and your feet alternately, and I shall crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and ye shall know for certain which of us hath sterner and more lasting punishment.
text_en_arberry: Pharaoh said, ’Have you believed him before I gave you leave? Why, he is the chief of you, the same that taught you sorcery; I shall assuredly cut off alternately your hands and feet, then I shall crucify you upon the trunks of palm-trees; you shall know of a certainty which of us is more terrible in chastisement, and more abiding.’

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنَا ۖ فَٱقْضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ ۖ إِنَّمَا تَقْضِى هَٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَآ
text_en_primary: They responded, “By the One Who created us! We will never prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us. So do whatever you want! Your authority only covers the ˹fleeting˺ life of this world.
text_en_yusufali: They said: "Never shall we regard thee as more than the Clear Sings that have come to us, or than Him Who created us! so decree whatever thou desirest to decree: for thou canst only decree (touching) the life of this world.
text_en_pickthall: They said: We choose thee not above the clear proofs that have come unto us, and above Him Who created us. So decree what thou wilt decree. Thou wilt end for us only this life of the world.
text_en_arberry: They said, ’We will not prefer thee over the clear signs that have come to us, nor over Him who originated us. Decide then what thou wilt decide; thou canst only decide touching this present life.

text_ar: إِنَّآ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَا وَمَآ أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحْرِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ
text_en_primary: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord so He may forgive our sins and that magic you have forced us to practice. And Allah is far superior ˹in reward˺ and more lasting ˹in punishment˺.”
text_en_yusufali: "For us, we have believed in our Lord: may He forgive us our faults, and the magic to which thou didst compel us: for God is Best and Most Abiding."
text_en_pickthall: Lo! we believe in our Lord, that He may forgive us our sins and the magic unto which thou didst force us. Allah is better and more lasting.
text_en_arberry: We believe in our Lord, that He may pardon us our offences, and the sorcery thou hast constrained us to practise; God is better, and more abiding.’

text_ar: إِنَّهُۥ مَن يَأْتِ رَبَّهُۥ مُجْرِمًۭا فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ
text_en_primary: Whoever comes to their Lord as an evildoer will certainly have Hell, where they can neither live nor die.
text_en_yusufali: Verily he who comes to his Lord as a sinner (at Judgment),- for him is Hell: therein shall he neither die nor live.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! whoso cometh guilty unto his Lord, verily for him is hell. There he will neither die nor live.
text_en_arberry: Whosoever comes unto his Lord a sinner, for him awaits Gehenna wherein he shall neither die nor live.

text_ar: وَمَن يَأْتِهِۦ مُؤْمِنًۭا قَدْ عَمِلَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱلدَّرَجَٰتُ ٱلْعُلَىٰ
text_en_primary: But whoever comes to Him as a believer, having done good, they will have the highest ranks:
text_en_yusufali: But such as come to Him as Believers who have worked righteous deeds,- for them are ranks exalted,-
text_en_pickthall: But whoso cometh unto Him a believer, having done good works, for such are the high stations;
text_en_arberry: And whoso comes unto Him a believer having done deeds of righteousness, those -- for them await the most sublime degrees;

text_ar: جَنَّٰتُ عَدْنٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا ۚ وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ
text_en_primary: the Gardens of Eternity, under which rivers flow, where they will stay forever. That is the reward of those who purify themselves.
text_en_yusufali: Gardens of Eternity, beneath which flow rivers: they will dwell therein for aye: such is the reward of those who purify themselves (from evil).
text_en_pickthall: Gardens of Eden underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide for ever. That is the reward of him who groweth.
text_en_arberry: Gardens of Eden, underneath which rivers flow, therein dwelling forever; that is the recompense of the self-purified.

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِى فَٱضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقًۭا فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ يَبَسًۭا لَّا تَخَٰفُ دَرَكًۭا وَلَا تَخْشَىٰ
text_en_primary: And We surely inspired Moses, ˹saying,˺ “Leave with My servants ˹at night˺ and strike a dry passage for them across the sea. Have no fear of being overtaken, nor be concerned ˹of drowning˺.”
text_en_yusufali: We sent an inspiration to Moses: "Travel by night with My servants, and strike a dry path for them through the sea, without fear of being overtaken (by Pharaoh) and without (any other) fear."
text_en_pickthall: And verily We inspired Moses, saying: Take away My slaves by night and strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing not to be overtaken, neither being afraid (of the sea).
text_en_arberry: Also We revealed unto Moses, ’Go with My servants by night; strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing not overtaking, neither afraid.’

text_ar: فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِۦ فَغَشِيَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ
text_en_primary: Then Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers—but how overwhelming were the waters that submerged them!
text_en_yusufali: Then Pharaoh pursued them with his forces, but the waters completely overwhelmed them and covered them up.
text_en_pickthall: Then Pharaoh followed them with his hosts and there covered them that which did cover them of the sea.
text_en_arberry: Pharaoh followed them with his hosts, but they were overwhelmed by the sea;

text_ar: وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُۥ وَمَا هَدَىٰ
text_en_primary: And ˹so˺ Pharaoh led his people astray, and did not guide ˹them rightly˺.
text_en_yusufali: Pharaoh led his people astray instead of leading them aright.
text_en_pickthall: And Pharaoh led his folk astray, he did not guide them.
text_en_arberry: so Pharaoh had led his people astray, and was no guide to them.

text_ar: يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ قَدْ أَنجَيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ وَوَٰعَدْنَٰكُمْ جَانِبَ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلْأَيْمَنَ وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ
text_en_primary: O Children of Israel! We saved you from your enemy, and made an appointment with you
text_en_yusufali: O ye Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a Covenant with you on the right side of Mount (Sinai), and We sent down to you Manna and quails:
text_en_pickthall: O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and we made a covenant with you on the holy mountain’s side, and sent down on you the manna and the quails,
text_en_arberry: Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy; and We made covenant with you upon the right side of the Mount, and sent down on you manna and quails:

text_ar: كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقْنَٰكُمْ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا۟ فِيهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِى ۖ وَمَن يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِى فَقَدْ هَوَىٰ
text_en_primary: ˹saying,˺ “Eat from the good things We have provided for you, but do not transgress in them, or My wrath will befall you. And whoever My wrath befalls is certainly doomed.
text_en_yusufali: (Saying): "Eat of the good things We have provided for your sustenance, but commit no excess therein, lest My Wrath should justly descend on you: and those on whom descends My Wrath do perish indeed!
text_en_pickthall: (Saying): Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you, and transgress not in respect thereof lest My wrath come upon you: and he on whom My wrath cometh, he is lost indeed.
text_en_arberry: ’Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you; but exceed not therein, or My anger shall alight on you; and on whomsoever My anger alights, that man is hurled to ruin.

text_ar: وَإِنِّى لَغَفَّارٌۭ لِّمَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا ثُمَّ ٱهْتَدَىٰ
text_en_primary: But I am truly Most Forgiving to whoever repents, believes, and does good, then persists on ˹true˺ guidance.”
text_en_yusufali: "But, without doubt, I am (also) He that forgives again and again, to those who repent, believe, and do right, who,- in fine, are ready to receive true guidance."
text_en_pickthall: And lo! verily I am Forgiving toward him who repenteth and believeth and doeth good, and afterward walketh aright.
text_en_arberry: Yet I am All-forgiving to him who repents and believes, and does righteousness, and at last is guided.’

text_ar: ۞ وَمَآ أَعْجَلَكَ عَن قَوْمِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
text_en_primary: ˹Allah asked,˺ “Why have you come with such haste ahead of your people, O  Moses?”
text_en_yusufali: (When Moses was up on the Mount, God said:) "What made thee hasten in advance of thy people, O Moses?"
text_en_pickthall: And (it was said): What hath made thee hasten from thy folk, O Moses ?
text_en_arberry: ’What has sped thee far from thy people, Moses?’

text_ar: قَالَ هُمْ أُو۟لَآءِ عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِى وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَىٰ
text_en_primary: He replied, “They are close on my tracks. And I have hastened to You, my Lord, so You will be pleased.”
text_en_yusufali: He replied: "Behold, they are close on my footsteps: I hastened to thee, O my Lord, to please thee."
text_en_pickthall: He said: They are close upon my track. I hastened unto Thee, my Lord, that Thou mightest be well pleased.
text_en_arberry: ’They are upon my tracks,’ Moses said. ’I have hastened, Lord, only that I may please Thee.’

text_ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِنۢ بَعْدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ
text_en_primary: Allah responded, “We have indeed tested your people in your absence, and the Samiri has led them astray.”
text_en_yusufali: (God) said: "We have tested thy people in thy absence: the Samiri has led them astray."
text_en_pickthall: He said: Lo! We have tried thy folk in thine absence, and As- Samiri hath misled them.
text_en_arberry: Said He, ’We have tempted thy people since thou didst leave them. The Samaritan has misled them into error.’

text_ar: فَرَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ غَضْبَٰنَ أَسِفًۭا ۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا ۚ أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْعَهْدُ أَمْ أَرَدتُّمْ أَن يَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُم مَّوْعِدِى
text_en_primary: So Moses returned to his people, furious and sorrowful. He said, “O my people! Had your Lord not made you a good promise?
text_en_yusufali: So Moses returned to his people in a state of indignation and sorrow. He said: "O my people! did not your Lord make a handsome promise to you? Did then the promise seem to you long (in coming)? Or did ye desire that Wrath should descend from your Lord on you, and so ye broke your promise to me?"
text_en_pickthall: Then Moses went back unto his folk, angry and sad. He said: O my people! Hath not your Lord promised you a fair promise ? Did the time appointed then appear too long for you, or did ye wish that wrath from your Lord should come upon you, that ye broke tryst with me ?
text_en_arberry: Then Moses returned very angry and sorrowful to his people, saying, ’My people, did your Lord not promise a fair promise to you? Did the time of the covenant seem so long to you, or did you desire that anger should alight on you from your Lord, so that you failed in your tryst with me?’

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ مَآ أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا وَلَٰكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَآ أَوْزَارًۭا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَٰهَا فَكَذَٰلِكَ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّامِرِىُّ
text_en_primary: They argued, “We did not break our promise to you of our own free will, but we were made to carry the burden of the people’s ˹golden˺ jewellery, then we threw it ˹into the fire˺, and so did the Samiri.”
text_en_yusufali: They said: "We broke not the promise to thee, as far as lay in our power: but we were made to carry the weight of the ornaments of the (whole) people, and we threw them (into the fire), and that was what the Samiri suggested.
text_en_pickthall: They said: We broke not tryst with thee of our own will, but we were laden with burdens of ornaments of the folk, then cast them (in the fire), for thus As-Samiri proposed.
text_en_arberry: ’We have not failed in our tryst with thee,’ they said, ’of our volition; but we were loaded with fardels, even the ornaments of the people, and we cast them, as the Samaritan also threw them, into the fire.’

text_ar: فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًۭا جَسَدًۭا لَّهُۥ خُوَارٌۭ فَقَالُوا۟ هَٰذَآ إِلَٰهُكُمْ وَإِلَٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِىَ
text_en_primary: Then he moulded for them an idol of a calf that made a lowing sound. They said, “This is your god and the god of Moses, but Moses forgot ˹where it was˺!”
text_en_yusufali: "Then he brought out (of the fire) before the (people) the image of a calf: It seemed to low: so they said: This is your god, and the god of Moses, but (Moses) has forgotten!"
text_en_pickthall: Then he produced for them a calf, of saffron hue, which gave forth a lowing sound. And they cried: This is your god and the god of Moses, but he hath forgotten.
text_en_arberry: (Then he brought out for them a Calf, a mere body that lowed; and they said, ’This is your god, and the god of Moses, whom he has forgotten.’

text_ar: أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًۭا وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ ضَرًّۭا وَلَا نَفْعًۭا
text_en_primary: Did they not see that it did not respond to them, nor could it protect or benefit them?
text_en_yusufali: Could they not see that it could not return them a word (for answer), and that it had no power either to harm them or to do them good?
text_en_pickthall: See they not, then, that it returneth no saying unto them and possesseth for them neither hurt nor use ?
text_en_arberry: What? Did they not see that thing returned no speech unto them, neither had any power to hurt or profit them?

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ قَالَ لَهُمْ هَٰرُونُ مِن قَبْلُ يَٰقَوْمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنتُم بِهِۦ ۖ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ فَٱتَّبِعُونِى وَأَطِيعُوٓا۟ أَمْرِى
text_en_primary: Aaron had already warned them beforehand, “O my people! You are only being tested by this, for indeed your ˹one true˺ Lord is the Most Compassionate. So follow me and obey my orders.”
text_en_yusufali: Aaron had already, before this said to them: "O my people! ye are being tested in this: for verily your Lord is (God) Most Gracious; so follow me and obey my command."
text_en_pickthall: And Aaron indeed had told them beforehand: O my people! Ye are but being seduced therewith, for lo! your Lord is the Beneficent, so follow me and obey my order.
text_en_arberry: Yet Aaron had aforetime said to them, ’My people, you have been tempted by this thing, no more; surety your Lord is the All-merciful; therefore follow me, and obey my commandment!’

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ لَن نَّبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عَٰكِفِينَ حَتَّىٰ يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ
text_en_primary: They replied, “We will not cease to worship it until Moses returns to us.”
text_en_yusufali: They had said: "We will not abandon this cult, but we will devote ourselves to it until Moses returns to us."
text_en_pickthall: They said: We shall by no means cease to be its votaries till Moses return unto us.
text_en_arberry: ’We will not cease,’ they said, ’to cleave to it, until Moses returns to us.’)

text_ar: قَالَ يَٰهَٰرُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذْ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ضَلُّوٓا۟
text_en_primary: Moses scolded ˹his brother˺, “O Aaron! What prevented you, when you saw them going astray,
text_en_yusufali: (Moses) said: "O Aaron! what kept thee back, when thou sawest them going wrong,
text_en_pickthall: He (Moses) said: O Aaron! What held thee back when thou didst see them gone astray,
text_en_arberry: Moses said, ’What prevented thee, Aaron, when thou sawest them in error,

text_ar: أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِ ۖ أَفَعَصَيْتَ أَمْرِى
text_en_primary: from following after me? How could you disobey my orders?”
text_en_yusufali: "From following me? Didst thou then disobey my order?"
text_en_pickthall: That thou followedst me not ? Hast thou then disobeyed my order ?
text_en_arberry: so that thou didst not follow after me? Didst thou then disobey my commandment?’

text_ar: قَالَ يَبْنَؤُمَّ لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِى وَلَا بِرَأْسِىٓ ۖ إِنِّى خَشِيتُ أَن تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ قَوْلِى
text_en_primary: Aaron pleaded, “O son of my mother! Do not seize me by my beard or ˹the hair of˺ my head. I really feared that you would say, ‘You have caused division among the Children of Israel, and did not observe my word.’”
text_en_yusufali: (Aaron) replied: "O son of my mother! Seize (me) not by my beard nor by (the hair of) my head! Truly I feared lest thou shouldst say, ’Thou has caused a division among the children of Israel, and thou didst not respect my word!’"
text_en_pickthall: He said: O son of my mother! Clutch not my beard nor my head! I feared lest thou shouldst say: Thou hast caused division among the Children of Israel, and hast not waited for my word.
text_en_arberry: ’Son of my mother,’ Aaron said, ’take me not by the beard, or the head! I was fearful that thou wouldst say, "Thou hast divided the Children of Israel, and thou hast not observed my word."

text_ar: قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكَ يَٰسَٰمِرِىُّ
text_en_primary: Moses then asked, “What did you think you were doing, O  Samiri?”
text_en_yusufali: (Moses) said: "What then is thy case, O Samiri?"
text_en_pickthall: (Moses) said: And what hast thou to say, O Samiri ?
text_en_arberry: Moses said, ’And thou, Samaritan, what was thy business?’

text_ar: قَالَ بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا۟ بِهِۦ فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةًۭ مِّنْ أَثَرِ ٱلرَّسُولِ فَنَبَذْتُهَا وَكَذَٰلِكَ سَوَّلَتْ لِى نَفْسِى
text_en_primary: He said, “I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful ˹of dust˺ from the hoof-prints of ˹the horse of˺ the messenger-angel ˹Gabriel˺ then cast it ˹on the moulded calf˺. This is what my lower-self tempted me into.”
text_en_yusufali: He replied: "I saw what they saw not: so I took a handful (of dust) from the footprint of the Apostle, and threw it (into the calf): thus did my soul suggest to me."
text_en_pickthall: He said: I perceived what they perceive not, so I seized a handful from the footsteps of the messenger, and then threw it in. Thus my soul commended to me.
text_en_arberry: ’I beheld what they beheld not,’ he said, ’and I seized a handful of dust from the messenger’s track, and cast it into the thing. So my soul prompted me.’

text_ar: قَالَ فَٱذْهَبْ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ أَن تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَ ۖ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًۭا لَّن تُخْلَفَهُۥ ۖ وَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِكَ ٱلَّذِى ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًۭا ۖ لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَنسِفَنَّهُۥ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ نَسْفًا
text_en_primary: Moses said, “Go away then! And for ˹the rest of your˺ life you will surely be crying, ‘Do not touch ˹me˺!’ that you cannot escape. Now look at your god to which you have been devoted: we will burn it up, then scatter it in the sea completely.”
text_en_yusufali: (Moses) said: "Get thee gone! but thy (punishment) in this life will be that thou wilt say, ’touch me not’; and moreover (for a future penalty) thou hast a promise that will not fail: Now look at thy god, of whom thou hast become a devoted worshipper: We will certainly (melt) it in a blazing fire and scatter it broadcast in the sea!"
text_en_pickthall: (Moses) said: Then go! and lo! in this life it is for thee to say: Touch me not! and lo! there is for thee a tryst thou canst not break. Now look upon thy god of which thou hast remained a votary. Verily we will burn it and will scatter its dust over the sea.
text_en_arberry: ’Depart!’ said Moses. ’It shall be thine all this life to cry "Untouchable!" And thereafter a tryst awaits thee thou canst not fail to keep Behold thy god, to whom all the day thou wast cleaving! We will surely burn it and scatter its ashes into the sea.

text_ar: إِنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ عِلْمًۭا
text_en_primary: ˹Then Moses addressed his people,˺ “Your only god is Allah, there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. He encompasses everything in ˹His˺ knowledge.”
text_en_yusufali: But the god of you all is the One God: there is no god but He: all things He comprehends in His knowledge.
text_en_pickthall: Your God is only Allah, than Whom there is no other God. He embraceth all things in His knowledge.
text_en_arberry: Your God is only the One God; there is no god, but He alone who in His knowledge embraces everything.’

text_ar: كَذَٰلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ مَا قَدْ سَبَقَ ۚ وَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَٰكَ مِن لَّدُنَّا ذِكْرًۭا
text_en_primary: This is how We relate to you ˹O Prophet˺ some of the stories of the past. And We have certainly granted you a Reminder from Us.
text_en_yusufali: Thus do We relate to thee some stories of what happened before: for We have sent thee a Message from Our own Presence.
text_en_pickthall: Thus relate We unto thee (Muhammad) some tidings of that which happened of old, and We have given thee from Our presence a reminder.
text_en_arberry: So We relate to thee stories of what has gone before, and We have given thee a remembrance from Us.

text_ar: مَّنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَحْمِلُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وِزْرًا
text_en_primary: Whoever turns away from it will surely bear the burden ˹of sin˺ on the Day of Judgment,
text_en_yusufali: If any do turn away therefrom, verily they will bear a burden on the Day of judgment;
text_en_pickthall: Whoso turneth away from it, he verily will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection,
text_en_arberry: Whosoever turns away from it, upon the Day of Resurrection He shall bear a fardel,

text_ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهِ ۖ وَسَآءَ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ حِمْلًۭا
text_en_primary: suffering its consequences forever. What an evil burden they will carry on Judgment Day!
text_en_yusufali: They will abide in this (state): and grievous will the burden be to them on that Day,-
text_en_pickthall: Abiding under it - an evil burden for them on the Day of Resurrection,
text_en_arberry: therein abiding forever; how evil upon the Day of Resurrection that burden for them!
