text_ar: يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِى ٱلصُّورِ ۚ وَنَحْشُرُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ زُرْقًۭا
text_en_primary: ˹Beware of˺ the Day the Trumpet will be blown,
text_en_yusufali: The Day when the Trumpet will be sounded: that Day, We shall gather the sinful, blear-eyed (with terror).
text_en_pickthall: The day when the Trumpet is blown. On that day we assemble the guilty white-eyed (with terror),
text_en_arberry: On the day the Trumpet is blown; and We shall muster the sinners upon that day with eyes staring,

text_ar: يَتَخَٰفَتُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا عَشْرًۭا
text_en_primary: They will whisper among themselves, “You stayed no more than ten days ˹on the earth˺.”
text_en_yusufali: In whispers will they consult each other: "Yet tarried not longer than ten (Days);
text_en_pickthall: Murmuring among themselves: Ye have tarried but ten (days).
text_en_arberry: whispering one to another, ’You have tarried only ten nights.’

text_ar: نَّحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذْ يَقُولُ أَمْثَلُهُمْ طَرِيقَةً إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا يَوْمًۭا
text_en_primary: We know best what they will say—the most reasonable of them will say, “You stayed no more than a day.”
text_en_yusufali: We know best what they will say, when their leader most eminent in conduct will say: "Ye tarried not longer than a day!"
text_en_pickthall: We are Best Aware of what they utter when their best in conduct say: Ye have tarried but a day.
text_en_arberry: We know very well what they will say, when the justest of them in the way will say, ’You have tarried only a day.’

text_ar: وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْجِبَالِ فَقُلْ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّى نَسْفًۭا
text_en_primary: And ˹if˺ they ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about the mountains, ˹then˺ say, “My Lord will wipe them out completely,
text_en_yusufali: They ask thee concerning the Mountains: say, "My Lord will uproot them and scatter them as dust;
text_en_pickthall: They will ask thee of the mountains (on that day). Say: My Lord will break them into scattered dust.
text_en_arberry: They will question thee concerning the mountains. Say: ’My Lord will scatter them as ashes;

text_ar: فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًۭا صَفْصَفًۭا
text_en_primary: leaving the earth level and bare,
text_en_yusufali: "He will leave them as plains smooth and level;
text_en_pickthall: And leave it as an empty plain,
text_en_arberry: then He will leave them a level hollow

text_ar: لَّا تَرَىٰ فِيهَا عِوَجًۭا وَلَآ أَمْتًۭا
text_en_primary: with neither depressions nor elevations to be seen.”
text_en_yusufali: "Nothing crooked or curved wilt thou see in their place."
text_en_pickthall: Wherein thou seest neither curve nor ruggedness.
text_en_arberry: wherein thou wilt see no crookedness neither any curving.’

text_ar: يَوْمَئِذٍۢ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلدَّاعِىَ لَا عِوَجَ لَهُۥ ۖ وَخَشَعَتِ ٱلْأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ فَلَا تَسْمَعُ إِلَّا هَمْسًۭا
text_en_primary: On that Day all will follow the caller ˹for assembly˺, ˹and˺ none will dare to deviate. All voices will be hushed before the Most Compassionate. Only whispers will be heard.
text_en_yusufali: On that Day will they follow the Caller (straight): no crookedness (can they show) him: all sounds shall humble themselves in the Presence of (God) Most Gracious: nothing shalt thou hear but the tramp of their feet (as they march).
text_en_pickthall: On that day they follow the summoner who deceiveth not, and voices are hushed for the Beneficent, and thou hearest but a faint murmur.
text_en_arberry: On that day they will follow the Summoner in whom is no crookedness; voices will be hushed to the All-merciful, so that thou hearest naught but a murmuring.

text_ar: يَوْمَئِذٍۢ لَّا تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةُ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَرَضِىَ لَهُۥ قَوْلًۭا
text_en_primary: On that Day no intercession will be of any benefit, except by those granted permission by the Most Compassionate and whose words are agreeable to Him.
text_en_yusufali: On that Day shall no intercession avail except for those for whom permission has been granted by (God) Most Gracious and whose word is acceptable to Him.
text_en_pickthall: On that day no intercession availeth save (that of) him unto whom the Beneficent hath given leave and whose word He accepteth.
text_en_arberry: Upon that day the intercession will not profit, save for him to whom the All-merciful gives leave, and whose speech He approves.

text_ar: يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِۦ عِلْمًۭا
text_en_primary: He ˹fully˺ knows what is ahead of them and what is behind them,
text_en_yusufali: He knows what (appears to His creatures as) before or after or behind them: but they shall not compass it with their knowledge.
text_en_pickthall: He knoweth (all) that is before them and (all) that is behind them, while they cannot compass it in knowledge.
text_en_arberry: He knows what is before them and behind them, and they comprehend Him not in knowledge.

text_ar: ۞ وَعَنَتِ ٱلْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَىِّ ٱلْقَيُّومِ ۖ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًۭا
text_en_primary: And all faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, All-Sustaining. And those burdened with wrongdoing will be in loss.
text_en_yusufali: (All) faces shall be humbled before (Him) - the Living, the Self-Subsisting, Eternal: hopeless indeed will be the man that carries iniquity (on his back).
text_en_pickthall: And faces humble themselves before the Living, the Eternal. And he who beareth (a burden of) wrongdoing is indeed a failure (on that day).
text_en_arberry: And faces shall be humbled unto the Living, the Eternal. He will have failed whose burden is of evildoing;

text_ar: وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌۭ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلْمًۭا وَلَا هَضْمًۭا
text_en_primary: But whoever does good and is a believer will have no fear of being wronged or denied ˹their reward˺.
text_en_yusufali: But he who works deeds of righteousness, and has faith, will have no fear of harm nor of any curtailment (of what is his due).
text_en_pickthall: And he who hath done some good works, being a believer, he feareth not injustice nor begrudging (of his wage).
text_en_arberry: but whosoever does deeds of righteousness, being a believer, shall fear neither wrong nor injustice.

text_ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ قُرْءَانًا عَرَبِيًّۭا وَصَرَّفْنَا فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلْوَعِيدِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْرًۭا
text_en_primary: And so We have sent it down as an Arabic Quran and varied the warnings in it, so perhaps they will shun evil or it may cause them to be mindful.
text_en_yusufali: Thus have We sent this down - an arabic Qur’an - and explained therein in detail some of the warnings, in order that they may fear God, or that it may cause their remembrance (of Him).
text_en_pickthall: Thus we have revealed it as a Lecture in Arabic, and have displayed therein certain threats, that peradventure they may keep from evil or that it may cause them to take heed.
text_en_arberry: Even so We have sent it down as an Arabic Koran, and We have turned about in it something of threats, that haply they may be godfearing, or it may arouse in them remembrance.

text_ar: فَتَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱلْحَقُّ ۗ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ ۖ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِى عِلْمًۭا
text_en_primary: Exalted is Allah, the True King! Do not rush to recite ˹a revelation of˺ the Quran ˹O Prophet˺ before it is ˹properly˺ conveyed to you, and pray, “My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.”
text_en_yusufali: High above all is God, the King, the Truth! Be not in haste with the Qur’an before its revelation to thee is completed, but say, "O my Lord! advance me in knowledge."
text_en_pickthall: Then exalted be Allah, the True King! And hasten not (O Muhammad) with the Qur’an ere its revelation hath been perfected unto thee, and say: My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.
text_en_arberry: So high exalted be God, the true King! And hasten not with the Koran ere its revelation is accomplished unto thee; and say, ’O my Lord, increase me in knowledge.’

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبْلُ فَنَسِىَ وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُۥ عَزْمًۭا
text_en_primary: And indeed, We once made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot, and ˹so˺ We did not find determination in him.
text_en_yusufali: We had already, beforehand, taken the covenant of Adam, but he forgot: and We found on his part no firm resolve.
text_en_pickthall: And verily We made a covenant of old with Adam, but he forgot, and We found no constancy in him.
text_en_arberry: And We made covenant with Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no constancy.

text_ar: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ
text_en_primary: And ˹remember˺ when We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,” so they all did—but not Iblis, who refused ˹arrogantly˺.
text_en_yusufali: When We said to the angels, "Prostrate yourselves to Adam", they prostrated themselves, but not Iblis: he refused.
text_en_pickthall: And when We said unto the angels: Fall prostrate before Adam, they fell prostrate (all) save Iblis; he refused.
text_en_arberry: And when We said to the angels, ’Bow yourselves to Adam’; so they bowed themselves, save Iblis; he refused.

text_ar: فَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ إِنَّ هَٰذَا عَدُوٌّۭ لَّكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَىٰٓ
text_en_primary: So We cautioned, “O Adam! This is surely an enemy to you and to your wife. So do not let him drive you both out of Paradise, for you ˹O Adam˺ would then suffer ˹hardship˺.
text_en_yusufali: Then We said: "O Adam! verily, this is an enemy to thee and thy wife: so let him not get you both out of the Garden, so that thou art landed in misery.
text_en_pickthall: Therefor we said: O Adam! This is an enemy unto thee and unto thy wife, so let him not drive you both out of the Garden so that thou come to toil.
text_en_arberry: Then We said, ’Adam, surely this is an enemy to thee and thy wife. So let him not expel you both from the Garden, so that thou art unprosperous.

text_ar: إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعْرَىٰ
text_en_primary: Here it is guaranteed that you will never go hungry or unclothed,
text_en_yusufali: "There is therein (enough provision) for thee not to go hungry nor to go naked,
text_en_pickthall: It is (vouchsafed) unto thee that thou hungerest not therein nor art naked,
text_en_arberry: It is assuredly given to thee neither to hunger therein, nor to go naked,

text_ar: وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظْمَؤُا۟ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضْحَىٰ
text_en_primary: nor will you ˹ever˺ suffer from thirst or ˹the sun’s˺ heat.”
text_en_yusufali: "Nor to suffer from thirst, nor from the sun’s heat."
text_en_pickthall: And that thou thirstest not therein nor art exposed to the sun’s heat.
text_en_arberry: neither to thirst therein, nor to suffer the sun.’

text_ar: فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍۢ لَّا يَبْلَىٰ
text_en_primary: But Satan whispered to him, saying, “O Adam! Shall I show you the Tree of Immortality and a kingdom that does not fade away?”
text_en_yusufali: But Satan whispered evil to him: he said, "O Adam! shall I lead thee to the Tree of Eternity and to a kingdom that never decays?"
text_en_pickthall: But the devil whispered to him, saying: O Adam! Shall I show thee the tree of immortality and power that wasteth not away ?
text_en_arberry: Then Satan whispered to him saying, ’Adam, shall I point thee to the Tree of Eternity, and a Kingdom that decays not?’

text_ar: فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ۚ وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُۥ فَغَوَىٰ
text_en_primary: So they both ate from the tree and then their nakedness was exposed to them, prompting them to cover themselves with leaves from Paradise. So Adam disobeyed his Lord, and ˹so˺ lost his way.
text_en_yusufali: In the result, they both ate of the tree, and so their nakedness appeared to them: they began to sew together, for their covering, leaves from the Garden: thus did Adam disobey his Lord, and allow himself to be seduced.
text_en_pickthall: Then they twain ate thereof, so that their shame became apparent unto them, and they began to hide by heaping on themselves some of the leaves of the Garden. And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so went astray.
text_en_arberry: So the two of them ate of it, and their shameful parts revealed to them, and they took to stitching upon themselves leaves of the Garden. And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he erred.

text_ar: ثُمَّ ٱجْتَبَٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَىٰ
text_en_primary: Then his Lord chose him ˹for His grace˺, accepted his repentance, and guided him ˹rightly˺.
text_en_yusufali: But his Lord chose him (for His Grace): He turned to him, and gave him Guidance.
text_en_pickthall: Then his Lord chose him, and relented toward him, and guided him.
text_en_arberry: Thereafter his Lord chose him, and turned again unto him, and He guided him.

text_ar: قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۢا ۖ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّۭ ۖ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًۭى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ
text_en_primary: Allah said, “Descend, both of you, from here together ˹with Satan˺ as enemies to each other. Then when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray ˹in this life˺ nor suffer ˹in the next˺.
text_en_yusufali: He said: "Get ye down, both of you,- all together, from the Garden, with enmity one to another: but if, as is sure, there comes to you Guidance from Me, whosoever follows My Guidance, will not lose his way, nor fall into misery.
text_en_pickthall: He said: Go down hence, both of you, one of you a foe unto the other. But when there come unto you from Me a guidance, then whoso followeth My guidance, he will not go astray nor come to grief.
text_en_arberry: Said He, ’Get you down, both of you together, out of it, each of you an enemy to each; but if there comes to you from Me guidance, then whosoever follows My guidance shall not go astray, neither shall he be unprosperous;

text_ar: وَمَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَن ذِكْرِى فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ مَعِيشَةًۭ ضَنكًۭا وَنَحْشُرُهُۥ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ أَعْمَىٰ
text_en_primary: But whoever turns away from My Reminder will certainly have a miserable life, then We will raise them up blind on the Day of Judgment.”
text_en_yusufali: "But whosoever turns away from My Message, verily for him is a life narrowed down, and We shall raise him up blind on the Day of Judgment."
text_en_pickthall: But he who turneth away from remembrance of Me, his will be a narrow life, and I shall bring him blind to the assembly on the Day of Resurrection.
text_en_arberry: but whosoever turns away from My remembrance, his shall be a life of narrowness, and on the Resurrection Day We shall raise him blind.’

text_ar: قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِىٓ أَعْمَىٰ وَقَدْ كُنتُ بَصِيرًۭا
text_en_primary: They will cry, “My Lord! Why have you raised me up blind, although I used to see?”
text_en_yusufali: He will say: "O my Lord! why hast Thou raised me up blind, while I had sight (before)?"
text_en_pickthall: He will say: My Lord! Wherefor hast Thou gathered me (hither) blind, when I was wont to see ?
text_en_arberry: He shall say, ’O my Lord, why hast thou raised me blind, and I was wont to see?’

text_ar: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ أَتَتْكَ ءَايَٰتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَا ۖ وَكَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ تُنسَىٰ
text_en_primary: Allah will respond, “It is so, just as Our revelations came to you and you neglected them, so Today you are neglected.”
text_en_yusufali: (God) will say: "Thus didst Thou, when Our Signs came unto thee, disregard them: so wilt thou, this day, be disregarded."
text_en_pickthall: He will say: So (it must be). Our revelations came unto thee but thou didst forget them. In like manner thou art forgotten this Day.
text_en_arberry: God shall say, ’Even so it is. Our signs came unto thee, and thou didst forget them; and so today thou art forgotten.’

text_ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى مَنْ أَسْرَفَ وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنۢ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِۦ ۚ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ أَشَدُّ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ
text_en_primary: This is how We reward whoever transgresses and does not believe in the revelations of their Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe and more lasting.
text_en_yusufali: And thus do We recompense him who transgresses beyond bounds and believes not in the Sings of his Lord: and the Penalty of the Hereafter is far more grievous and more enduring.
text_en_pickthall: Thus do We reward him who is prodigal and believeth not the revelations of his Lord; and verily the doom of the Hereafter will be sterner and more lasting.
text_en_arberry: So We recompense him who is prodigal and believes not in the signs of his Lord; and the chastisement of the world to come is more terrible and more enduring.

text_ar: أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ يَمْشُونَ فِى مَسَٰكِنِهِمْ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلنُّهَىٰ
text_en_primary: Is it not yet clear to them how many peoples We destroyed before them, whose ruins they still pass by? Surely in this are signs for people of sound judgment.
text_en_yusufali: Is it not a warning to such men (to call to mind) how many generations before them We destroyed, in whose haunts they (now) move? Verily, in this are Signs for men endued with understanding.
text_en_pickthall: Is it not a guidance for them (to know) how many a generation We destroyed before them, amid whose dwellings they walk ? Lo! therein verily are signs for men of thought.
text_en_arberry: Is it not a guidance to them, how many generations We destroyed before them in whose dwelling-places they walk? Surely in that are signs for men possessing reason.

text_ar: وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌۭ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ لَكَانَ لِزَامًۭا وَأَجَلٌۭ مُّسَمًّۭى
text_en_primary: Had it not been for a prior decree from your Lord ˹O Prophet˺ and a term already set, their ˹instant˺ doom would have been inevitable.
text_en_yusufali: Had it not been for a Word that went forth before from thy Lord, (their punishment) must necessarily have come; but there is a Term appointed (for respite).
text_en_pickthall: And but for a decree that had already gone forth from thy Lord, and a term already fixed, the judgment would have been inevitable (in this world).
text_en_arberry: And but for a word that preceded from thy Lord, and a stated term, it had been fastened.

text_ar: فَٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا ۖ وَمِنْ ءَانَآئِ ٱلَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْ وَأَطْرَافَ ٱلنَّهَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَىٰ
text_en_primary: So be patient ˹O Prophet˺ with what they say. And glorify the praises of your Lord before sunrise and before sunset, and glorify Him in the hours of the night and at both ends of the day, so that you may be pleased ˹with the reward˺.
text_en_yusufali: Therefore be patient with what they say, and celebrate (constantly) the praises of thy Lord, before the rising of the sun, and before its setting; yea, celebrate them for part of the hours of the night, and at the sides of the day: that thou mayest have (spiritual) joy.
text_en_pickthall: Therefor (O Muhammad), bear with what they say, and celebrate the praise of thy Lord ere the rising of the sun and ere the going down thereof. And glorify Him some hours of the night and at the two ends of the day, that thou mayst find acceptance.
text_en_arberry: So be thou patient under what they say, and proclaim thy Lord’s praise before the rising of the sun, and before its setting, and proclaim thy Lord’s praise in the watches of the night, and at the ends of the day; haply thou wilt be well-pleasing.

text_ar: وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزْوَٰجًۭا مِّنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ ۚ وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰ
text_en_primary: Do not let your eyes crave what We have allowed some of the disbelievers to enjoy; the ˹fleeting˺ splendour of this worldly life, which We test them with. But your Lord’s provision ˹in the Hereafter˺ is far better and more lasting.
text_en_yusufali: Nor strain thine eyes in longing for the things We have given for enjoyment to parties of them, the splendour of the life of this world, through which We test them: but the provision of thy Lord is better and more enduring.
text_en_pickthall: And strain not thine eyes toward that which We cause some wedded pairs among them to enjoy, the flower of the life of the world, that We may try them thereby. The provision of thy Lord is better and more lasting.
text_en_arberry: Stretch not thine eyes to that We have given pairs of them to enjoy - the flower of the present life, that We may try them therein and thy Lord’s provision is better, and more enduring.

text_ar: وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا ۖ لَا نَسْـَٔلُكَ رِزْقًۭا ۖ نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ ۗ وَٱلْعَٰقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ
text_en_primary: Bid your people to pray, and be diligent in ˹observing˺ it. We do not ask you to provide. It is We Who provide for you. And the ultimate outcome is ˹only˺ for ˹the people of˺ righteousness.
text_en_yusufali: Enjoin prayer on thy people, and be constant therein. We ask thee not to provide sustenance: We provide it for thee. But the (fruit of) the Hereafter is for righteousness.
text_en_pickthall: And enjoin upon thy people worship, and be constant therein. We ask not of thee a provision: We provided for thee. And the sequel is for righteousness.
text_en_arberry: And bid thy family to pray, and be thou patient in it; We ask of thee no provision, but it is We who provide thee and the issue ultimate is to godfearing.

text_ar: وَقَالُوا۟ لَوْلَا يَأْتِينَا بِـَٔايَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦٓ ۚ أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِم بَيِّنَةُ مَا فِى ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ
text_en_primary: They demand, “If only he could bring us a sign from his Lord!”
text_en_yusufali: They say: "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" Has not a Clear Sign come to them of all that was in the former Books of revelation?
text_en_pickthall: And they say: If only he would bring us a miracle from his Lord! Hath there not come unto them the proof of what is in the former scriptures ?
text_en_arberry: They say, ’Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?’ Has there not come to them the clear sign of what is in the former scrolls?

text_ar: وَلَوْ أَنَّآ أَهْلَكْنَٰهُم بِعَذَابٍۢ مِّن قَبْلِهِۦ لَقَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَا لَوْلَآ أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولًۭا فَنَتَّبِعَ ءَايَٰتِكَ مِن قَبْلِ أَن نَّذِلَّ وَنَخْزَىٰ
text_en_primary: Had We destroyed them with a torment before this ˹Prophet came˺, they would have surely argued, “Our Lord! If only You had sent us a messenger, we would have followed Your revelations before being humiliated and put to shame.”
text_en_yusufali: And if We had inflicted on them a penalty before this, they would have said: "Our Lord! If only Thou hadst sent us an apostle, we should certainly have followed Thy Signs before we were humbled and put to shame."
text_en_pickthall: And if we had destroyed them with some punishment before it, they would assuredly have said: Our Lord! If only Thou hadst sent unto us a messenger, so that we might have followed Thy revelations before we were (thus) humbled and disgraced!
text_en_arberry: Had We destroyed them with a chastisement aforetime, they would have said, ’Our Lord, why didst Thou not send us a Messenger, so that we might have followed Thy signs before that we were humiliated and degraded?’

text_ar: قُلْ كُلٌّۭ مُّتَرَبِّصٌۭ فَتَرَبَّصُوا۟ ۖ فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ ٱلسَّوِىِّ وَمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ
text_en_primary: Say ˹to them, O  Prophet˺, “Each ˹of us˺ is waiting, so keep waiting! You will soon know who is on the Straight Path and is ˹rightly˺ guided.”
text_en_yusufali: Say: "Each one (of us) is waiting: wait ye, therefore, and soon shall ye know who it is that is on the straight and even way, and who it is that has received Guidance."
text_en_pickthall: Say: Each is awaiting; so await ye! Ye will come to know who are the owners of the path of equity, and who is right.
text_en_arberry: Say: ’Everyone is waiting; so wait, and assuredly you shall know who are the travellers on the even path, and who is guided.’

text_ar: ٱقْتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَابُهُمْ وَهُمْ فِى غَفْلَةٍۢ مُّعْرِضُونَ
text_en_primary: ˹The time of˺ people’s judgment has drawn near, yet they are heedlessly turning away.
text_en_yusufali: Closer and closer to mankind comes their Reckoning: yet they heed not and they turn away.
text_en_pickthall: Their reckoning draweth nigh for mankind, while they turn away in heedlessness.
text_en_arberry: Nigh unto men has drawn their reckoning, while they in heedlessness are yet turning away;

text_ar: مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّهِم مُّحْدَثٍ إِلَّا ٱسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ
text_en_primary: Whatever new reminder comes to them from their Lord, they only listen to it jokingly,
text_en_yusufali: Never comes (aught) to them of a renewed Message from their Lord, but they listen to it as in jest,-
text_en_pickthall: Never cometh there unto them a new reminder from their Lord but they listen to it while they play,
text_en_arberry: no Remembrance from their Lord comes to them lately renewed, but they listen to it yet playing,

text_ar: لَاهِيَةًۭ قُلُوبُهُمْ ۗ وَأَسَرُّوا۟ ٱلنَّجْوَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ هَلْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا بَشَرٌۭ مِّثْلُكُمْ ۖ أَفَتَأْتُونَ ٱلسِّحْرَ وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ
text_en_primary: with their hearts ˹totally˺ distracted. The evildoers would converse secretly, ˹saying,˺ “Is this ˹one˺ not human like yourselves? Would you fall for ˹this˺ witchcraft, even though you can ˹clearly˺ see?”
text_en_yusufali: Their hearts toying as with trifles. The wrong-doers conceal their private counsels, (saying), "Is this (one) more than a man like yourselves? Will ye go to witchcraft with your eyes open?"
text_en_pickthall: With hearts preoccupied. And they confer in secret. The wrong- doers say: Is this other than a mortal like you ? Will ye then succumb to magic when ye see (it) ?
text_en_arberry: diverted their hearts. The evildoers whisper one to another, ’Is this aught but a mortal like to yourselves? What, will you take to sorcery with your eyes open?’

text_ar: قَالَ رَبِّى يَعْلَمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
text_en_primary: The Prophet responded, “My Lord ˹fully˺ knows every word spoken in the heavens and the earth. For He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.”
text_en_yusufali: Say: "My Lord knoweth (every) word (spoken) in the heavens and on earth: He is the One that heareth and knoweth (all things)."
text_en_pickthall: He saith: My Lord knoweth what is spoken in the heaven and the earth. He is the Hearer, the Knower.
text_en_arberry: He says: ’My Lord knows what is said in the heavens and the earth, and He is the All-hearing, the All-knowing.’

text_ar: بَلْ قَالُوٓا۟ أَضْغَٰثُ أَحْلَٰمٍۭ بَلِ ٱفْتَرَىٰهُ بَلْ هُوَ شَاعِرٌۭ فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِـَٔايَةٍۢ كَمَآ أُرْسِلَ ٱلْأَوَّلُونَ
text_en_primary: Yet they say, “This ˹Quran˺ is a set of confused dreams! No, he has fabricated it! No, he must be a poet! So let him bring us a ˹tangible˺ sign like those ˹prophets˺ sent before.”
text_en_yusufali: "Nay," they say, "(these are) medleys of dream! - Nay, He forged it! - Nay, He is (but) a poet! Let him then bring us a Sign like the ones that were sent to (Prophets) of old!"
text_en_pickthall: Nay, say they, (these are but) muddled dreams; nay, he hath but invented it; nay, he is but a poet. Let him bring us a portent even as those of old (who were God’s messengers) were sent (with portents).
text_en_arberry: Nay, but they say: ’A hotchpotch of nightmares! Nay, he has forged it; nay, he is a poet! Now therefore let him bring us a sign, even as the ancient ones were sent as Messengers.’

text_ar: مَآ ءَامَنَتْ قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَٰهَآ ۖ أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ
text_en_primary: Not a ˹single˺ society We destroyed before them ever believed ˹after receiving the signs˺. Will these ˹pagans˺ then believe?
text_en_yusufali: (As to those) before them, not one of the populations which We destroyed believed: will these believe?
text_en_pickthall: Not a township believed of those which We destroyed before them (though We sent them portents): would they then believe ?
text_en_arberry: Not one city that We destroyed before them believed; what then, will they not believe?

text_ar: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًۭا نُّوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ ۖ فَسْـَٔلُوٓا۟ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ إِن كُنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
text_en_primary: We did not send ˹messengers˺ before you ˹O Prophet˺ except mere men inspired by Us. If you ˹polytheists˺ do not know ˹this already˺, then ask those who have knowledge ˹of the Scriptures˺.
text_en_yusufali: Before thee, also, the apostles We sent were but men, to whom We granted inspiration: If ye realise this not, ask of those who possess the Message.
text_en_pickthall: And We sent not (as Our messengers) before thee other than men, whom We inspired. Ask the followers of the Reminder if ye know not ?
text_en_arberry: And We sent none before thee, but men to whom We made revelation -- question the People of the Remembrance, if you do not know --

text_ar: وَمَا جَعَلْنَٰهُمْ جَسَدًۭا لَّا يَأْكُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰلِدِينَ
text_en_primary: We did not give those messengers ˹supernatural˺ bodies that did not need food, nor were they immortal.
text_en_yusufali: Nor did We give them bodies that ate no food, nor were they exempt from death.
text_en_pickthall: We gave them not bodies that would not eat food, nor were they immortals.
text_en_arberry: nor did We fashion them as bodies that ate not food, neither were they immortal;

text_ar: ثُمَّ صَدَقْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْوَعْدَ فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُمْ وَمَن نَّشَآءُ وَأَهْلَكْنَا ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ
text_en_primary: Then We fulfilled Our promise to them, saving them along with whoever We willed and destroying the transgressors.
text_en_yusufali: In the end We fulfilled to them Our Promise, and We saved them and those whom We pleased, but We destroyed those who transgressed beyond bounds.
text_en_pickthall: Then we fulfilled the promise unto them. So we delivered them and whom We would, and We destroyed the prodigals.
text_en_arberry: then We made true the promise We gave them and We delivered them, and whomsoever We would; and We destroyed the prodigal.

text_ar: لَقَدْ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكُمْ كِتَٰبًۭا فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ ۖ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
text_en_primary: We have surely revealed to you a Book, in which there is glory for you. Will you not then understand?
text_en_yusufali: We have revealed for you (O men!) a book in which is a Message for you: will ye not then understand?
text_en_pickthall: Now We have revealed unto you a Scripture wherein is your Reminder. Have ye then no sense ?
text_en_arberry: Now We have sent down to you a Book wherein is your Remembrance; will you not understand?

text_ar: وَكَمْ قَصَمْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍۢ كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةًۭ وَأَنشَأْنَا بَعْدَهَا قَوْمًا ءَاخَرِينَ
text_en_primary: ˹Imagine˺ how many societies of wrongdoers We have destroyed, raising up other people after them!
text_en_yusufali: How many were the populations We utterly destroyed because of their iniquities, setting up in their places other peoples?
text_en_pickthall: How many a community that dealt unjustly have We shattered, and raised up after them another folk!
text_en_arberry: How many a city that was evildoing We have shattered, and set up after it another people!

text_ar: فَلَمَّآ أَحَسُّوا۟ بَأْسَنَآ إِذَا هُم مِّنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ
text_en_primary: When the wrongdoers sensed ˹the arrival of˺ Our torment, they started to run away from their cities.
text_en_yusufali: Yet, when they felt Our Punishment (coming), behold, they (tried to) flee from it.
text_en_pickthall: And, when they felt Our might, behold them fleeing from it!
text_en_arberry: Then, when they perceived Our might, behold, they ran headlong out of it.

text_ar: لَا تَرْكُضُوا۟ وَٱرْجِعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ مَآ أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِيهِ وَمَسَٰكِنِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْـَٔلُونَ
text_en_primary: ˹They were told,˺ “Do not run away! Return to your luxuries and your homes, so you may be questioned ˹about your fate˺.”
text_en_yusufali: Flee not, but return to the good things of this life which were given you, and to your homes in order that ye may be called to account.
text_en_pickthall: (But it was said unto them): Flee not, but return to that (existence) which emasculated you and to your dwellings, that ye may be questioned.
text_en_arberry: ’Run not! Return you unto the luxury that you exulted in, and your dwelling-places; haply you shall be questioned.’

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
text_en_primary: They cried, “Woe to us! We have surely been wrongdoers.”
text_en_yusufali: They said: "Ah! woe to us! We were indeed wrong-doers!"
text_en_pickthall: They cried: Alas for us! we were wrong-doers.
text_en_arberry: They said, ’Alas for us! We have been evildoers.’

text_ar: فَمَا زَالَت تِّلْكَ دَعْوَىٰهُمْ حَتَّىٰ جَعَلْنَٰهُمْ حَصِيدًا خَٰمِدِينَ
text_en_primary: They kept repeating their cry until We mowed them down, ˹leaving them˺ lifeless.
text_en_yusufali: And that cry of theirs ceased not, till We made them as a field that is mown, as ashes silent and quenched.
text_en_pickthall: And this their crying ceased not till We made them as reaped corn, extinct.
text_en_arberry: So they ceased not to cry, until We made them stubble, silent and still.

text_ar: وَمَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَٰعِبِينَ
text_en_primary: We did not create the heavens and the earth and everything in between for sport.
text_en_yusufali: Not for (idle) sport did We create the heavens and the earth and all that is between!
text_en_pickthall: We created not the heaven and the earth and all that is between them in play.
text_en_arberry: We created not the heaven and the earth, and whatsoever between them is, as playing;

text_ar: لَوْ أَرَدْنَآ أَن نَّتَّخِذَ لَهْوًۭا لَّٱتَّخَذْنَٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّآ إِن كُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ
text_en_primary: Had We intended to take ˹some˺ amusement, We could have found it in Our presence, if that had been Our Will.
text_en_yusufali: If it had been Our wish to take (just) a pastime, We should surely have taken it from the things nearest to Us, if We would do (such a thing)!
text_en_pickthall: If We had wished to find a pastime, We could have found it in Our presence - if We ever did.
text_en_arberry: had We desired to take to Us a diversion We would have taken it to Us from Ourselves, had We done aught.

text_ar: بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِٱلْحَقِّ عَلَى ٱلْبَٰطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُۥ فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌۭ ۚ وَلَكُمُ ٱلْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ
text_en_primary: In fact, We hurl the truth against falsehood, leaving it crushed, and it quickly vanishes. And woe be to you for what you claim!
text_en_yusufali: Nay, We hurl the Truth against falsehood, and it knocks out its brain, and behold, falsehood doth perish! Ah! woe be to you for the (false) things ye ascribe (to Us).
text_en_pickthall: Nay, but We hurl the true against the false, and it doth break its head and lo! it vanisheth. And yours will be woe for that which ye ascribe (unto Him).
text_en_arberry: Nay, but We hurl the truth against falsehood and it prevails over it, and behold, falsehood vanishes away. Then woe to you for that you describe!

text_ar: وَلَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ وَمَنْ عِندَهُۥ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِۦ وَلَا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ
text_en_primary: To Him belong all those in the heavens and the earth. And those nearest to Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they tire.
text_en_yusufali: To Him belong all (creatures) in the heavens and on earth: Even those who are in His (very) Presence are not too proud to serve Him, nor are they (ever) weary (of His service):
text_en_pickthall: Unto Him belongeth whosoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those who dwell in His presence are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they weary;
text_en_arberry: To Him belongs whosoever is in the heavens and the earth; and those who are with Him wax not too proud to do Him service neither grow weary,

text_ar: يُسَبِّحُونَ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ لَا يَفْتُرُونَ
text_en_primary: They glorify ˹Him˺ day and night, never wavering.
text_en_yusufali: They celebrate His praises night and day, nor do they ever flag or intermit.
text_en_pickthall: They glorify (Him) night and day; they flag not.
text_en_arberry: glorifying Him by night and in the daytime and never failing.

text_ar: أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ هُمْ يُنشِرُونَ
text_en_primary: Or have they taken gods from the earth, who can raise the dead?
text_en_yusufali: Or have they taken (for worship) gods from the earth who can raise (the dead)?
text_en_pickthall: Or have they chosen gods from the earth who raise the dead ?
text_en_arberry: Or have they taken gods out of the earth who raise the dead?

text_ar: لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَآ ءَالِهَةٌ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا ۚ فَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
text_en_primary: Had there been other gods besides Allah in the heavens or the earth, both ˹realms˺ would have surely been corrupted. So Glorified is Allah, Lord of the Throne, far above what they claim.
text_en_yusufali: If there were, in the heavens and the earth, other gods besides God, there would have been confusion in both! but glory to God, the Lord of the Throne: (High is He) above what they attribute to Him!
text_en_pickthall: If there were therein gods beside Allah, then verily both (the heavens and the earth) had been disordered. Glorified be Allah, the Lord of the Throne, from all that they ascribe (unto Him).
text_en_arberry: Why, were there gods in earth and heaven other than God, they would surely go to ruin; so glory be to God, the Lord of the Throne, above that they describe!

text_ar: لَا يُسْـَٔلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْـَٔلُونَ
text_en_primary: He cannot be questioned about what He does, but they will ˹all˺ be questioned.
text_en_yusufali: He cannot be questioned for His acts, but they will be questioned (for theirs).
text_en_pickthall: He will not be questioned as to that which He doeth, but they will be questioned.
text_en_arberry: He shall not be questioned as to what He does, but they shall he questioned.

text_ar: أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةًۭ ۖ قُلْ هَاتُوا۟ بُرْهَٰنَكُمْ ۖ هَٰذَا ذِكْرُ مَن مَّعِىَ وَذِكْرُ مَن قَبْلِى ۗ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ ٱلْحَقَّ ۖ فَهُم مُّعْرِضُونَ
text_en_primary: Or have they taken other gods besides Him? Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Show ˹me˺ your proof. Here is ˹the Quran,˺ the Reminder for those with me; along with ˹earlier Scriptures,˺ the Reminder for those before me.” But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.
text_en_yusufali: Or have they taken for worship (other) gods besides him? Say, "Bring your convincing proof: this is the Message of those with me and the Message of those before me." But most of them know not the Truth, and so turn away.
text_en_pickthall: Or have they chosen other gods beside Him ? say: Bring your proof (of their godhead). This is the Reminder of those with me and those before me, but most of them know not the Truth and so they are averse.
text_en_arberry: Or have they taken gods apart from Him? Say: ’Bring your proof! This is the Remembrance of him who is with me, and the Remembrance of those before me. Nay, but the most part of them know not the truth, so therefore they are turning away.

text_ar: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعْبُدُونِ
text_en_primary: We never sent a messenger before you ˹O Prophet˺ without revealing to him: “There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Me, so worship Me ˹alone˺.”
text_en_yusufali: Not an apostle did We send before thee without this inspiration sent by Us to him: that there is no god but I; therefore worship and serve Me.
text_en_pickthall: And We sent no messenger before thee but We inspired him, (saying): There is no God save Me (Allah), so worship Me.
text_en_arberry: And We sent never a Messenger before thee except that We revealed to him, saying, ’There is no god but I; so serve Me.’

text_ar: وَقَالُوا۟ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَلَدًۭا ۗ سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ ۚ بَلْ عِبَادٌۭ مُّكْرَمُونَ
text_en_primary: And they say, “The Most Compassionate has offspring!” Glory be to Him! In fact, those ˹angels˺ are only ˹His˺ honoured servants,
text_en_yusufali: And they say: "(God) Most Gracious has begotten offspring." Glory to Him! they are (but) servants raised to honour.
text_en_pickthall: And they say: The Beneficent hath taken unto Himself a son. Be He Glorified! Nay, but (those whom they call sons) are honoured slaves;
text_en_arberry: They say:’ ’The All-merciful has taken to Him a son.’ Glory be to Him! Nay, but they are honoured servants

text_ar: لَا يَسْبِقُونَهُۥ بِٱلْقَوْلِ وَهُم بِأَمْرِهِۦ يَعْمَلُونَ
text_en_primary: who do not speak until He has spoken, ˹only˺ acting at His command.
text_en_yusufali: They speak not before He speaks, and they act (in all things) by His Command.
text_en_pickthall: They speak not until He hath spoken, and they act by His command.
text_en_arberry: that outstrip Him not in speech, and perform as He commands.

text_ar: يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ٱرْتَضَىٰ وَهُم مِّنْ خَشْيَتِهِۦ مُشْفِقُونَ
text_en_primary: He ˹fully˺ knows what is ahead of them and what is behind them. They do not intercede except for whom He approves, and they tremble in awe of Him.
text_en_yusufali: He knows what is before them, and what is behind them, and they offer no intercession except for those who are acceptable, and they stand in awe and reverence of His (Glory).
text_en_pickthall: He knoweth what is before them and what is behind them, and they cannot intercede except for him whom He accepteth, and they quake for awe of Him.
text_en_arberry: He knows what is before them and behind them, and they intercede not save for him with whom He is well-pleased, and they tremble in awe of Him.

text_ar: ۞ وَمَن يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّىٓ إِلَٰهٌۭ مِّن دُونِهِۦ فَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِيهِ جَهَنَّمَ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
text_en_primary: Whoever of them were to say, “I am a god besides Him,” they would be rewarded with Hell by Us. This is how We reward the wrongdoers.
text_en_yusufali: If any of them should say, "I am a god besides Him", such a one We should reward with Hell: thus do We reward those who do wrong.
text_en_pickthall: And one of them who should say: Lo! I am a god beside Him, that one We should repay with hell. Thus We Repay wrong-doers.
text_en_arberry: If any of them says, ’I am a god apart from Him’, such a one We recompense with Gehenna; even so We recompense the evildoers.

text_ar: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًۭا فَفَتَقْنَٰهُمَا ۖ وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ ۖ أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
text_en_primary: Do the disbelievers not realize that the heavens and earth were ˹once˺ one mass then We split them apart? And We created from water every living thing. Will they not then believe?
text_en_yusufali: Do not the Unbelievers see that the heavens and the earth were joined together (as one unit of creation), before we clove them asunder? We made from water every living thing. Will they not then believe?
text_en_pickthall: Have not those who disbelieve known that the heavens and the earth were of one piece, then We parted them, and we made every living thing of water ? Will they not then believe ?
text_en_arberry: Have not the unbelievers then beheld that the heavens and the earth were a mass all sewn up, and then We unstitched them and of water fashioned every living thing? Will they not believe?

text_ar: وَجَعَلْنَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ رَوَٰسِىَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًۭا سُبُلًۭا لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ
text_en_primary: And We have placed firm mountains upon the earth so it does not shake with them, and made in it broad pathways so they may find their way.
text_en_yusufali: And We have set on the earth mountains standing firm, lest it should shake with them, and We have made therein broad highways (between mountains) for them to pass through: that they may receive Guidance.
text_en_pickthall: And We have placed in the earth firm hills lest it quake with them, and We have placed therein ravines as roads that haply they may find their way.
text_en_arberry: And We set in the earth firm mountains lest it should shake with them, and We set in it ravines to serve as ways, that haply so they may be guided;

text_ar: وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ سَقْفًۭا مَّحْفُوظًۭا ۖ وَهُمْ عَنْ ءَايَٰتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ
text_en_primary: And We have made the sky a well-protected canopy, still they turn away from its signs.
text_en_yusufali: And We have made the heavens as a canopy well guarded: yet do they turn away from the Signs which these things (point to)!
text_en_pickthall: And we have made the sky a roof withheld (from them). Yet they turn away from its portents.
text_en_arberry: and We set up the heaven as a roof well-protected; yet still from Our signs they are turning away.

text_ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ ۖ كُلٌّۭ فِى فَلَكٍۢ يَسْبَحُونَ
text_en_primary: And He is the One Who created the day and the night, the sun and the moon—each travelling in an orbit.
text_en_yusufali: It is He Who created the Night and the Day, and the sun and the moon: all (the celestial bodies) swim along, each in its rounded course.
text_en_pickthall: And He it is Who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. They float, each in an orbit.
text_en_arberry: It is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon, each swimming in a sky.

text_ar: وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍۢ مِّن قَبْلِكَ ٱلْخُلْدَ ۖ أَفَإِي۟ن مِّتَّ فَهُمُ ٱلْخَٰلِدُونَ
text_en_primary: We have not granted immortality to any human before you ˹O Prophet˺: so if you die, will they live forever?
text_en_yusufali: We granted not to any man before thee permanent life (here): if then thou shouldst die, would they live permanently?
text_en_pickthall: We appointed immortality for no mortal before thee. What! if thou diest, can they be immortal!
text_en_arberry: We have not assigned to any mortal before thee to live forever; therefore, if thou diest, will they live forever?

text_ar: كُلُّ نَفْسٍۢ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلْمَوْتِ ۗ وَنَبْلُوكُم بِٱلشَّرِّ وَٱلْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةًۭ ۖ وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ
text_en_primary: Every soul will taste death. And We test you ˹O humanity˺ with good and evil as a trial, then to Us you will ˹all˺ be returned.
text_en_yusufali: Every soul shall have a taste of death: and We test you by evil and by good by way of trial. to Us must ye return.
text_en_pickthall: Every soul must taste of death, and We try you with evil and with good, for ordeal. And unto Us ye will be returned.
text_en_arberry: Every soul shall taste of death; and We try you with evil and good for a testing, then unto Us you shall be returned

text_ar: وَإِذَا رَءَاكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ إِن يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى يَذْكُرُ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ وَهُم بِذِكْرِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ هُمْ كَٰفِرُونَ
text_en_primary: When the disbelievers see you ˹O Prophet˺, they only make fun of you, ˹saying,˺ “Is this the one who speaks ˹ill˺ of your gods?” while they disbelieve at the mention of the Most Compassionate.
text_en_yusufali: When the Unbelievers see thee, they treat thee not except with ridicule. "Is this," (they say), "the one who talks of your gods?" and they blaspheme at the mention of (God) Most Gracious!
text_en_pickthall: And when those who disbelieve behold thee, they but choose thee out for mockery, (saying): Is this he who maketh mention of your gods ? And they would deny all mention of the Beneficent.
text_en_arberry: When the unbelievers behold thee, they take thee only for mockery: ’Ha, is this the one who makes mention of your gods?’ Yet they in the Remembrance of the All-merciful are unbelievers.

text_ar: خُلِقَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ مِنْ عَجَلٍۢ ۚ سَأُو۟رِيكُمْ ءَايَٰتِى فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ
text_en_primary: Humankind is made of haste. I will soon show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten them.
text_en_yusufali: Man is a creature of haste: soon (enough) will I show you My Signs; then ye will not ask Me to hasten them!
text_en_pickthall: Man is made of haste. I shall show you My portents, but ask Me not to hasten.
text_en_arberry: Man was created of haste. Assuredly I shall show you My signs; so demand not that I make haste.

text_ar: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
text_en_primary: They ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass if what you say is true?”
text_en_yusufali: They say: "When will this promise come to pass, if ye are telling the truth?"
text_en_pickthall: And they say: When will this promise (be fulfilled), if ye are truthful ?
text_en_arberry: They say, ’And when shall the promise come to pass, if you speak truly?’

text_ar: لَوْ يَعْلَمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ عَن وُجُوهِهِمُ ٱلنَّارَ وَلَا عَن ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ
text_en_primary: If only the disbelievers knew that a time will come when they will not be able to keep the Fire off their faces or backs, nor will they be helped.
text_en_yusufali: If only the Unbelievers knew (the time) when they will not be able to ward off the fire from their faces, nor yet from their backs, and (when) no help can reach them!
text_en_pickthall: If those who disbelieved but knew the time when they will not be able to drive off the fire from their faces and from their backs, and they will not be helped!
text_en_arberry: If the unbelievers but knew when that they shall not ward off the Fire from their faces nor from their backs, neither shall they be helped!

text_ar: بَلْ تَأْتِيهِم بَغْتَةًۭ فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنظَرُونَ
text_en_primary: In fact, the Hour will take them by surprise, leaving them stunned. So they will not be able to avert it, nor will it be delayed from them.
text_en_yusufali: Nay, it may come to them all of a sudden and confound them: no power will they have then to avert it, nor will they (then) get respite.
text_en_pickthall: Nay, but it will come upon them unawares so that it will stupefy them, and they will be unable to repel it, neither will they be reprieved.
text_en_arberry: Nay, but it shall come upon them suddenly, dumbfounding them, and they shall not be able to repel it, nor shall they be respited.

text_ar: وَلَقَدِ ٱسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍۢ مِّن قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِٱلَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا۟ مِنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
text_en_primary: ˹Other˺ messengers had already been ridiculed before you ˹O Prophet˺, but those who mocked them were overtaken by what they used to ridicule.
text_en_yusufali: Mocked were (many) apostle before thee; But their scoffers were hemmed in by the thing that they mocked.
text_en_pickthall: Messengers before thee, indeed, were mocked, but that whereat they mocked surrounded those who scoffed at them.
text_en_arberry: Messengers indeed were mocked at before thee, but those that scoffed at them were encompassed by that they mocked at.

text_ar: قُلْ مَن يَكْلَؤُكُم بِٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ۗ بَلْ هُمْ عَن ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِم مُّعْرِضُونَ
text_en_primary: Ask ˹them, O  Prophet,˺ “Who can defend you by day or by night against the Most Compassionate?” Still they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord.
text_en_yusufali: Say: "Who can keep you safe by night and by day from (the Wrath of) (God) Most Gracious?" Yet they turn away from the mention of their Lord.
text_en_pickthall: Say: Who guardeth you in the night or in the day from the Beneficent ? Nay, but they turn away from mention of their Lord!
text_en_arberry: Say: ’Who shall guard you by night and in the daytime from the All-merciful?’ Nay, but from the Remembrance of their Lord they are turning away.

text_ar: أَمْ لَهُمْ ءَالِهَةٌۭ تَمْنَعُهُم مِّن دُونِنَا ۚ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَلَا هُم مِّنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ
text_en_primary: Or do they have gods—other than Us—that can protect them? They cannot ˹even˺ protect themselves, nor will they be aided against Us.
text_en_yusufali: Or have they gods that can guard them from Us? They have no power to aid themselves, nor can they be defended from Us.
text_en_pickthall: Or have they gods who can shield them from Us ? They cannot help themselves nor can they be defended from Us.
text_en_arberry: Or have they gods that shall defend them apart from Us? Why, they are not able to help themselves, nor shall they be guarded in safety from Us.

text_ar: بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ وَءَابَآءَهُمْ حَتَّىٰ طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْعُمُرُ ۗ أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِى ٱلْأَرْضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَآ ۚ أَفَهُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ
text_en_primary: In fact, We have allowed enjoyment for these ˹Meccans˺ and their forefathers for such a long time ˹that they took it for granted˺. Do they not see that We gradually reduce ˹their˺ land from its borders? Is it they who will then prevail?
text_en_yusufali: Nay, We gave the good things of this life to these men and their fathers until the period grew long for them; See they not that We gradually reduce the land (in their control) from its outlying borders? Is it then they who will win?
text_en_pickthall: Nay, but We gave these and their fathers ease until life grew long for them. See they not how we aim to the land, reducing it of its outlying parts ? Can they then be the victors ?
text_en_arberry: Nay, but Ourselves gave these and their fathers enjoyment of days, until their life had lasted long while upon them. What, do they not see how We come to the land, diminishing it in its extremities? Or are they the victors?

text_ar: قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أُنذِرُكُم بِٱلْوَحْىِ ۚ وَلَا يَسْمَعُ ٱلصُّمُّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا مَا يُنذَرُونَ
text_en_primary: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I warn you only by revelation.” But the deaf cannot hear the call when they are warned!
text_en_yusufali: Say, "I do but warn you according to revelation": But the deaf will not hear the call, (even) when they are warned!
text_en_pickthall: Say (O Muhammad, unto mankind): I warn you only by the Inspiration. But the deaf hear not the call when they are warned.
text_en_arberry: Say: ’I warn you only by the Revelation’; but they that are deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.

text_ar: وَلَئِن مَّسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌۭ مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يَٰوَيْلَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
text_en_primary: If they were touched by even a breath of your Lord’s torment, they would certainly cry, “Woe to us! We have really been wrongdoers.”
text_en_yusufali: If but a breath of the Wrath of thy Lord do touch them, they will then say, "Woe to us! we did wrong indeed!"
text_en_pickthall: And if a breath of thy Lord’s punishment were to touch them, they assuredly would say: Alas for us! Lo! we were wrong-doers.
text_en_arberry: If but a breath of thy Lord’s chastisement touched them, they would surely say, ’Alas for us! We were evildoers.’

text_ar: وَنَضَعُ ٱلْمَوَٰزِينَ ٱلْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌۭ شَيْـًۭٔا ۖ وَإِن كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍۢ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَٰسِبِينَ
text_en_primary: We will set up the scales of justice on the Day of Judgment, so no soul will be wronged in the least. And ˹even˺ if a deed is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as a ˹vigilant˺ Reckoner.
text_en_yusufali: We shall set up scales of justice for the Day of Judgment, so that not a soul will be dealt with unjustly in the least, and if there be (no more than) the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it (to account): and enough are We to take account.
text_en_pickthall: And We set a just balance for the Day of Resurrection so that no soul is wronged in aught. Though it be of the weight of a grain of mustard seed, We bring it. And We suffice for reckoners.
text_en_arberry: And We shall set up the just balances for the Resurrection Day, so that not one soul shall be wronged anything; even if it be the weight of one grain of mustard-seed We shall produce it, and sufficient are We for reckoners.

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ ٱلْفُرْقَانَ وَضِيَآءًۭ وَذِكْرًۭا لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
text_en_primary: Indeed, We granted Moses and Aaron the standard ˹to distinguish between right and wrong˺—a light and a reminder for the righteous,
text_en_yusufali: In the past We granted to Moses and Aaron the criterion (for judgment), and a Light and a Message for those who would do right,-
text_en_pickthall: And We verily gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion (of right and wrong) and a light and a Reminder for those who keep from evil,
text_en_arberry: We gave Moses and Aaron the Salvation and a Radiance, and a Remembrance for the godfearing

text_ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَهُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ
text_en_primary: who are in awe of their Lord without seeing Him, and are fearful of the Hour.
text_en_yusufali: Those who fear their Lord in their most secret thoughts, and who hold the Hour (of Judgment) in awe.
text_en_pickthall: Those who fear their Lord in secret and who dread the Hour (of doom).
text_en_arberry: such as fear God in the Unseen, trembling because of the Hour.

text_ar: وَهَٰذَا ذِكْرٌۭ مُّبَارَكٌ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ ۚ أَفَأَنتُمْ لَهُۥ مُنكِرُونَ
text_en_primary: And this ˹Quran˺ is a blessed reminder which We have revealed. Will you ˹pagans˺ then deny it?
text_en_yusufali: And this is a blessed Message which We have sent down: will ye then reject it?
text_en_pickthall: This is a blessed Reminder that we have revealed: Will ye then reject it ?
text_en_arberry: And this is a blessed Remembrance that We have sent down; so are you now denying it?

text_ar: ۞ وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ رُشْدَهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِۦ عَٰلِمِينَ
text_en_primary: And indeed, We had granted Abraham sound judgment early on, for We knew him well ˹to be worthy of it˺.
text_en_yusufali: We bestowed aforetime on Abraham his rectitude of conduct, and well were We acquainted with him.
text_en_pickthall: And We verily gave Abraham of old his proper course, and We were Aware of him,
text_en_arberry: We gave Abraham aforetime his rectitude -- for We knew him --

text_ar: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنتُمْ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ
text_en_primary: ˹Remember˺ when he questioned his father and his people, “What are these statues to which you are so devoted?”
text_en_yusufali: Behold! he said to his father and his people, "What are these images, to which ye are (so assiduously) devoted?"
text_en_pickthall: When he said unto his father and his folk: What are these images unto which ye pay devotion ?
text_en_arberry: when he said to his father and his people, ’What are these statues unto which you are cleaving?’

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا لَهَا عَٰبِدِينَ
text_en_primary: They replied, “We found our forefathers worshipping them.”
text_en_yusufali: They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."
text_en_pickthall: They said: We found our fathers worshippers of them.
text_en_arberry: They said, ’We found our fathers serving them.’

text_ar: قَالَ لَقَدْ كُنتُمْ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُمْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
text_en_primary: He responded, “Indeed, you and your forefathers have been clearly astray.”
text_en_yusufali: He said, "Indeed ye have been in manifest error - ye and your fathers."
text_en_pickthall: He said: Verily ye and your fathers were in plain error.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’Then assuredly you and your fathers have been in manifest error.’

text_ar: قَالُوٓا۟ أَجِئْتَنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ أَمْ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱللَّٰعِبِينَ
text_en_primary: They asked, “Have you come to us with the truth, or is this a joke?”
text_en_yusufali: They said, "Have you brought us the Truth, or are you one of those who jest?"
text_en_pickthall: They said: Bringest thou unto us the truth, or art thou some jester ?
text_en_arberry: They said, ’What, hast thou come to us with the truth, or art thou one of those that play?’

text_ar: قَالَ بَل رَّبُّكُمْ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا۠ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
text_en_primary: He replied, “In fact, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Who created them ˹both˺. And to that I bear witness.”
text_en_yusufali: He said, "Nay, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, He Who created them (from nothing): and I am a witness to this (Truth).
text_en_pickthall: He said: Nay, but your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Who created them; and I am of those who testify unto that.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’Nay, but your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth who originated them, and I am one of those that bear witness thereunto.

text_ar: وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَٰمَكُم بَعْدَ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
text_en_primary: ˹Then he said to himself,˺ “By Allah! I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned your backs and gone away.”
text_en_yusufali: "And by God, I have a plan for your idols - after ye go away and turn your backs"..
text_en_pickthall: And, by Allah, I shall circumvent your idols after ye have gone away and turned your backs.
text_en_arberry: And, by God, I shall assuredly outwit your idols, after you have gone away turning your backs.’

text_ar: فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذَٰذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرًۭا لَّهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ يَرْجِعُونَ
text_en_primary: So he smashed them into pieces, except the biggest of them, so they might turn to it ˹for answers˺.
text_en_yusufali: So he broke them to pieces, (all) but the biggest of them, that they might turn (and address themselves) to it.
text_en_pickthall: Then he reduced them to fragments, all save the chief of them, that haply they might have recourse to it.
text_en_arberry: So he broke them into fragments, all but a great one they had, for haply they would return to it.

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ مَن فَعَلَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
text_en_primary: They protested, “Who dared do this to our gods? It must be an evildoer!”
text_en_yusufali: They said, "Who has done this to our gods? He must indeed be some man of impiety!"
text_en_pickthall: They said: Who hath done this to our gods ? Surely it must be some evil-doer.
text_en_arberry: They said, ’Who has. done this with our gods? Surely he is one of the evildoers.’

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا فَتًۭى يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقَالُ لَهُۥٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ
text_en_primary: Some said, “We heard a young man, called Abraham, speaking ˹ill˺ of them.”
text_en_yusufali: They said, "We heard a youth talk of them: He is called Abraham."
text_en_pickthall: They said: We heard a youth make mention of them, who is called Abraham.
text_en_arberry: They said, ’We heard a young man making mention of them, and he was called Abraham.’

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ فَأْتُوا۟ بِهِۦ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْيُنِ ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ
text_en_primary: They demanded, “Bring him before the eyes of the people, so that they may witness ˹his trial˺.”
text_en_yusufali: They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people, that they may bear witness."
text_en_pickthall: They said: Then bring him (hither) before the people’s eyes that they may testify.
text_en_arberry: They said, ’Bring him before the people’s eyes; haply they shall bear witness.’

text_ar: قَالُوٓا۟ ءَأَنتَ فَعَلْتَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَا يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ
text_en_primary: They asked, “Was it you who did this to our gods, O  Abraham?”
text_en_yusufali: They said, "Art thou the one that did this with our gods, O Abraham?"
text_en_pickthall: They said: Is it thou who hast done this to our gods, O Abraham ?
text_en_arberry: They said, ’So, art thou the man who did this unto our gods, Abraham?’

text_ar: قَالَ بَلْ فَعَلَهُۥ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَٰذَا فَسْـَٔلُوهُمْ إِن كَانُوا۟ يَنطِقُونَ
text_en_primary: He replied ˹sarcastically˺, “No, this one—the biggest of them—did it! So ask them, if they can talk!”
text_en_yusufali: He said: "Nay, this was done by - this is their biggest one! ask them, if they can speak intelligently!"
text_en_pickthall: He said: But this, their chief hath done it. So question them, if they can speak.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’No; it was this great one of them that did it. Question them; if they are able to speak!’

text_ar: فَرَجَعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ فَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّكُمْ أَنتُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
text_en_primary: So they came back to their senses, saying ˹to one another˺, “You yourselves are truly the wrongdoers!”
text_en_yusufali: So they turned to themselves and said, "Surely ye are the ones in the wrong!"
text_en_pickthall: Then gathered they apart and said: Lo! ye yourselves are the wrong- doers.
text_en_arberry: So they returned one to another, and they said, ’Surely it is you who are the evildoers.’

text_ar: ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا۟ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمْ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يَنطِقُونَ
text_en_primary: Then they ˹quickly˺ regressed to their ˹original˺ mind-set, ˹arguing,˺ “You already know that those ˹idols˺ cannot talk.”
text_en_yusufali: Then were they confounded with shame: (they said), "Thou knowest full well that these (idols) do not speak!"
text_en_pickthall: And they were utterly confounded, and they said: Well thou knowest that these speak not.
text_en_arberry: Then they were utterly put to confusion saying, ’Very well indeed thou knowest these do not speak.’

text_ar: قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ
text_en_primary: He rebuked ˹them˺, “Do you then worship—instead of Allah—what can neither benefit nor harm you in any way?
text_en_yusufali: (Abraham) said, "Do ye then worship, besides God, things that can neither be of any good to you nor do you harm?
text_en_pickthall: He said: Worship ye then instead of Allah that which cannot profit you at all, nor harm you ?
text_en_arberry: He said, ’What, and do you serve, apart from God, that which profits you nothing; neither hurts you?

text_ar: أُفٍّۢ لَّكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
text_en_primary: Shame on you and whatever you worship instead of Allah! Do you not have any sense?”
text_en_yusufali: "Fie upon you, and upon the things that ye worship besides God! Have ye no sense?"..
text_en_pickthall: Fie on you and all that ye worship instead of Allah! Have ye then no sense ?
text_en_arberry: Fie upon you and that you serve apart from God! Do you not understand?’

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ حَرِّقُوهُ وَٱنصُرُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ
text_en_primary: They concluded, “Burn him up to avenge your gods, if you must act.”
text_en_yusufali: They said, "Burn him and protect your gods, If ye do (anything at all)!"
text_en_pickthall: They cried: Burn him and stand by your gods, if ye will be doing.
text_en_arberry: They said, ’Burn him, and help your gods, if you would do aught.’

text_ar: قُلْنَا يَٰنَارُ كُونِى بَرْدًۭا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
text_en_primary: We ordered, “O fire! Be cool and safe for Abraham!”
text_en_yusufali: We said, "O Fire! be thou cool, and (a means of) safety for Abraham!"
text_en_pickthall: We said: O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham,
text_en_arberry: We said, ’O fire, be coolness and safety for Abraham!’

text_ar: وَأَرَادُوا۟ بِهِۦ كَيْدًۭا فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْأَخْسَرِينَ
text_en_primary: They had sought to harm him, but We made them the worst losers.
text_en_yusufali: Then they sought a stratagem against him: but We made them the ones that lost most!
text_en_pickthall: And they wished to set a snare for him, but We made them the greater losers.
text_en_arberry: They desired to outwit him; so We made them the worse losers,

text_ar: وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَلُوطًا إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّتِى بَٰرَكْنَا فِيهَا لِلْعَٰلَمِينَ
text_en_primary: Then We delivered him, along with Lot, to the land We had showered with blessings for all people.
text_en_yusufali: But We delivered him and (his nephew) Lut (and directed them) to the land which We have blessed for the nations.
text_en_pickthall: And We rescued him and Lot (and brought them) to the land which We have blessed for (all) peoples.
text_en_arberry: and We delivered him, and Lot, unto the land that We had blessed for all beings.

text_ar: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةًۭ ۖ وَكُلًّۭا جَعَلْنَا صَٰلِحِينَ
text_en_primary: And We blessed him with Isaac ˹as a son˺ and Jacob ˹as a grandson˺, as an additional favour—making all of them righteous.
text_en_yusufali: And We bestowed on him Isaac and, as an additional gift, (a grandson), Jacob, and We made righteous men of every one (of them).
text_en_pickthall: And We bestowed upon him Isaac, and Jacob as a grandson. Each of them We made righteous.
text_en_arberry: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob in superfluity, and every one made We righteous

text_ar: وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ أَئِمَّةًۭ يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِمْ فِعْلَ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَإِقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَإِيتَآءَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةِ ۖ وَكَانُوا۟ لَنَا عَٰبِدِينَ
text_en_primary: We ˹also˺ made them leaders, guiding by Our command, and inspired them to do good deeds, establish prayer, and pay alms-tax. And they were devoted to Our worship.
text_en_yusufali: And We made them leaders, guiding (men) by Our Command, and We sent them inspiration to do good deeds, to establish regular prayers, and to practise regular charity; and they constantly served Us (and Us only).
text_en_pickthall: And We made them chiefs who guide by Our command, and We inspired in them the doing of good deeds and the right establishment of worship and the giving of alms, and they were worshippers of Us (alone).
text_en_arberry: and appointed them to be leaders guiding by Our command, and We revealed to them the doing of good deeds, and to perform the prayer, and to pay the alms, and Us they served.

text_ar: وَلُوطًا ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ حُكْمًۭا وَعِلْمًۭا وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ٱلَّتِى كَانَت تَّعْمَلُ ٱلْخَبَٰٓئِثَ ۗ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمَ سَوْءٍۢ فَٰسِقِينَ
text_en_primary: And to Lot We gave wisdom and knowledge, and delivered him from the society engrossed in shameful practices. They were certainly an evil, rebellious people.
text_en_yusufali: And to Lut, too, We gave Judgment and Knowledge, and We saved him from the town which practised abominations: truly they were a people given to Evil, a rebellious people.
text_en_pickthall: And unto Lot we gave judgment and knowledge, and We delivered him from the community that did abominations. Lo! they were folk of evil, lewd.
text_en_arberry: And Lot -- to him We gave judgment and knowledge; and we delivered him from the city that had been doing deeds of corruption; they were an evil people, truly ungodly;

text_ar: وَأَدْخَلْنَٰهُ فِى رَحْمَتِنَآ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
text_en_primary: And We admitted him into Our mercy, ˹for˺ he was truly one of the righteous.
text_en_yusufali: And We admitted him to Our Mercy: for he was one of the Righteous
text_en_pickthall: And We brought him in unto Our mercy. Lo! he was of the righteous.
text_en_arberry: and We admitted him into Our mercy; he was of the righteous.

text_ar: وَنُوحًا إِذْ نَادَىٰ مِن قَبْلُ فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
text_en_primary: And ˹remember˺ when Noah had cried out to Us earlier, so We responded to him and delivered him and his family from the great distress.
text_en_yusufali: (Remember) Noah, when he cried (to Us) aforetime: We listened to his (prayer) and delivered him and his family from great distress.
text_en_pickthall: And Noah, when he cried of old, We heard his prayer and saved him and his household from the great affliction.
text_en_arberry: And Noah -- when he called before, and We answered him, and delivered him and his people from the great distress,

text_ar: وَنَصَرْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ ۚ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمَ سَوْءٍۢ فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
text_en_primary: And We made him prevail over those who had rejected Our signs. They were truly an evil people, so We drowned them all.
text_en_yusufali: We helped him against people who rejected Our Signs: truly they were a people given to Evil: so We drowned them (in the Flood) all together.
text_en_pickthall: And delivered him from the people who denied Our revelations. Lo! they were folk of evil, therefor did We drown them all.
text_en_arberry: and We helped him against the people who cried lies to Our signs; surely they were an evil people, so We drowned them all together.

text_ar: وَدَاوُۥدَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ إِذْ يَحْكُمَانِ فِى ٱلْحَرْثِ إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ ٱلْقَوْمِ وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَٰهِدِينَ
text_en_primary: And ˹remember˺ when David and Solomon passed judgment regarding the crops ruined ˹at night˺ by someone’s sheep, and We were witness to their judgments.
text_en_yusufali: And remember David and Solomon, when they gave judgment in the matter of the field into which the sheep of certain people had strayed by night: We did witness their judgment.
text_en_pickthall: And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field, when people’s sheep had strayed and browsed therein by night; and We were witnesses to their judgment.
text_en_arberry: And David and Solomon -- when they gave judgment concerning the tillage, when the sheep of the people strayed there, and We bore witness to their judgment;

text_ar: فَفَهَّمْنَٰهَا سُلَيْمَٰنَ ۚ وَكُلًّا ءَاتَيْنَا حُكْمًۭا وَعِلْمًۭا ۚ وَسَخَّرْنَا مَعَ دَاوُۥدَ ٱلْجِبَالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ وَٱلطَّيْرَ ۚ وَكُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ
text_en_primary: We guided ˹young˺ Solomon to a fairer settlement, and granted each of them wisdom and knowledge. We subjected the mountains as well as the birds to hymn ˹Our praises˺ along with David. It is We Who did ˹it all˺.
text_en_yusufali: To Solomon We inspired the (right) understanding of the matter: to each (of them) We gave Judgment and Knowledge; it was Our power that made the hills and the birds celebrate Our praises, with David: it was We Who did (all these things).
text_en_pickthall: And We made Solomon to understand (the case); and unto each of them We gave judgment and knowledge. And we subdued the hills and the birds to hymn (His) praise along with David. We were the doers (thereof).
text_en_arberry: and We made Solomon to understand it, and unto each gave We judgment and knowledge. And with David We subjected the mountains to give glory, and the birds, and We were doers.

text_ar: وَعَلَّمْنَٰهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍۢ لَّكُمْ لِتُحْصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأْسِكُمْ ۖ فَهَلْ أَنتُمْ شَٰكِرُونَ
text_en_primary: We taught him the art of making body armour to protect you in battle. Will you then be grateful?
text_en_yusufali: It was We Who taught him the making of coats of mail for your benefit, to guard you from each other’s violence: will ye then be grateful?
text_en_pickthall: And We taught him the art of making garments (of mail) to protect you in your daring. Are ye then thankful ?
text_en_arberry: And We taught him the fashioning of garments for you, to fortify you against your violence; then are you thankful?

text_ar: وَلِسُلَيْمَٰنَ ٱلرِّيحَ عَاصِفَةًۭ تَجْرِى بِأَمْرِهِۦٓ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّتِى بَٰرَكْنَا فِيهَا ۚ وَكُنَّا بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَٰلِمِينَ
text_en_primary: And to Solomon We subjected the raging winds, blowing by his command to the land We had showered with blessings. It is We Who know everything.
text_en_yusufali: (It was Our power that made) the violent (unruly) wind flow (tamely) for Solomon, to his order, to the land which We had blessed: for We do know all things.
text_en_pickthall: And unto Solomon (We subdued) the wind in its raging. It set by his command toward the land which We had blessed. And of everything We are Aware.
text_en_arberry: And to Solomon the wind, strongly blowing, that ran at his command unto the land that We had blessed; and We had knowledge of everything;

text_ar: وَمِنَ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينِ مَن يَغُوصُونَ لَهُۥ وَيَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلًۭا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ ۖ وَكُنَّا لَهُمْ حَٰفِظِينَ
text_en_primary: And ˹We subjected˺ some jinn and performed other duties. It is We Who kept them in check.
text_en_yusufali: And of the evil ones, were some who dived for him, and did other work besides; and it was We Who guarded them.
text_en_pickthall: And of the evil ones (subdued We unto him) some who dived (for pearls) for him and did other work, and We were warders unto them.
text_en_arberry: and of the Satans some dived for him and did other work besides; and We were watching over them.

text_ar: ۞ وَأَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
text_en_primary: And ˹remember˺ when Job cried out to his Lord, “I have been touched with adversity, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.”
text_en_yusufali: And (remember) Job, when He cried to his Lord, "Truly distress has seized me, but Thou art the Most Merciful of those that are merciful."
text_en_pickthall: And Job, when he cried unto his Lord, (saying): Lo! adversity afflicteth me, and Thou art Most Merciful of all who show mercy.
text_en_arberry: And Job -- when he called unto his Lord, ’Behold, affliction has visited me, and Thou art the most merciful of the merciful.’

text_ar: فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ فَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِۦ مِن ضُرٍّۢ ۖ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ أَهْلَهُۥ وَمِثْلَهُم مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةًۭ مِّنْ عِندِنَا وَذِكْرَىٰ لِلْعَٰبِدِينَ
text_en_primary: So We answered his prayer and removed his adversity, and gave him back his family, twice as many, as a mercy from Us and a lesson for the ˹devoted˺ worshippers.
text_en_yusufali: So We listened to him: We removed the distress that was on him, and We restored his people to him, and doubled their number,- as a Grace from Ourselves, and a thing for commemoration, for all who serve Us.
text_en_pickthall: Then We heard his prayer and removed that adversity from which he suffered, and We gave him his household (that he had lost) and the like thereof along with them, a mercy from Our store, and a remembrance for the worshippers;
text_en_arberry: So We answered him, and removed the affliction that was upon him, and We gave his people, and the like of them with them, mercy from Us, and a Reminder to those who serve.

text_ar: وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ ۖ كُلٌّۭ مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
text_en_primary: And ˹remember˺ Ishmael, Enoch, and Ⱬul-Kifl. They were all steadfast.
text_en_yusufali: And (remember) Isma’il, Idris, and Zul-kifl, all (men) of constancy and patience;
text_en_pickthall: And (mention) Ishmael, and Idris, and Dhu’l-Kifl. All were of the steadfast.
text_en_arberry: And Ishmael, Idris, Dhul Kifl -- each was of the patient,

text_ar: وَأَدْخَلْنَٰهُمْ فِى رَحْمَتِنَآ ۖ إِنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
text_en_primary: We admitted them into Our mercy, for they were truly of the righteous.
text_en_yusufali: We admitted them to Our mercy: for they were of the righteous ones.
text_en_pickthall: And We brought them in unto Our mercy. Lo! they are among the righteous.
text_en_arberry: and We admitted them into Our mercy; they were of the righteous.

text_ar: وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَٰضِبًۭا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
text_en_primary: And ˹remember˺ when the Man of the Whale stormed off ˹from his city˺ in a rage, thinking We would not restrain him. he cried out, “There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except You. Glory be to You! I have certainly done wrong.”
