text_en_pickthall: And touch her not with ill lest there come on you the retribution of an awful day.
text_en_arberry: and do not touch her with malice so that there seize you the chastisement of a dreadful day.’

text_ar: فَعَقَرُوهَا فَأَصْبَحُوا۟ نَٰدِمِينَ
text_en_primary: But they killed her, becoming regretful.
text_en_yusufali: But they ham-strung her: then did they become full of regrets.
text_en_pickthall: But they hamstrung her, and then were penitent.
text_en_arberry: But they hamstrung her, and in the morning they were remorseful,

text_ar: فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
text_en_primary: So the punishment overtook them. Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.
text_en_yusufali: But the Penalty seized them. Verily in this is a Sign: but most of them do not believe.
text_en_pickthall: So the retribution came on them. Lo! herein is indeed a portent, yet most of them are not believers.
text_en_arberry: and the chastisement seized them. Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.

text_ar: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
text_en_primary: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.
text_en_yusufali: And verily thy Lord is He, the Exalted in Might, Most Merciful.
text_en_pickthall: And lo! thy Lord! He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful.
text_en_arberry: Surely thy Lord, He is the All-mighty, the All-compassionate.

text_ar: كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
text_en_primary: The people of Lot rejected the messengers
text_en_yusufali: The people of Lut rejected the apostles.
text_en_pickthall: The folk of Lot denied the messengers (of Allah),
text_en_arberry: The people of Lot cried lies to the Envoys

text_ar: إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ لُوطٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
text_en_primary: when their brother Lot said to them, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?
text_en_yusufali: Behold, their brother Lut said to them: "Will ye not fear (God)?
text_en_pickthall: When their brother Lot said unto them: Will ye not ward off (evil) ?
text_en_arberry: when their brother Lot said to them, ’Will you not be godfearing?

text_ar: إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ
text_en_primary: I am truly a trustworthy messenger to you.
text_en_yusufali: "I am to you an apostle worthy of all trust.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you,
text_en_arberry: am for you a faithful Messenger,

text_ar: فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
text_en_primary: So fear Allah, and obey me.
text_en_yusufali: "So fear God and obey me.
text_en_pickthall: So keep your duty to Allah and obey me.
text_en_arberry: so fear you God, and obey you me.

text_ar: وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
text_en_primary: I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺. My reward is only from the Lord of all worlds.
text_en_yusufali: "No reward do I ask of you for it: my reward is only from the lord of the Worlds.
text_en_pickthall: And I ask of you no wage therefor; my wage is the concern only of the Lord of the Worlds.
text_en_arberry: I ask of you no wage for this; my wage falls only upon the Lord of all Being.

text_ar: أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلذُّكْرَانَ مِنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
text_en_primary: Why do you ˹men˺ lust after fellow men,
text_en_yusufali: "Of all the creatures in the world, will ye approach males,
text_en_pickthall: What! Of all creatures do ye come unto the males,
text_en_arberry: What, do you come to male beings,

text_ar: وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم ۚ بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ عَادُونَ
text_en_primary: leaving the wives that your Lord has created for you? In fact, you are a transgressing people.”
text_en_yusufali: "And leave those whom God has created for you to be your mates? Nay, ye are a people transgressing (all limits)!"
text_en_pickthall: And leave the wives your Lord created for you ? Nay, but ye are froward folk.
text_en_arberry: leaving your wives that your Lord created for you? Nay, but you are a people of transgressors.

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ يَٰلُوطُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمُخْرَجِينَ
text_en_primary: They threatened, “If you do not desist, O  Lot, you will surely be expelled.”
text_en_yusufali: They said: "If thou desist not, O Lut! thou wilt assuredly be cast out
text_en_pickthall: They said: If thou cease not, O Lot, thou wilt soon be of the outcast.
text_en_arberry: They said, ’If thou givest not over, Lot, thou shalt assuredly be one of the expelled.’

text_ar: قَالَ إِنِّى لِعَمَلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلْقَالِينَ
text_en_primary: Lot responded, “I am truly one of those who despise your ˹shameful˺ practice.
text_en_yusufali: He said: "I do detest your doings."
text_en_pickthall: He said: I am in truth of those who hate your conduct.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’Truly I am a detester of what you do.

text_ar: رَبِّ نَجِّنِى وَأَهْلِى مِمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ
text_en_primary: My Lord! Save me and my family from ˹the consequences of˺ what they do.”
text_en_yusufali: "O my Lord! deliver me and my family from such things as they do!"
text_en_pickthall: My Lord! Save me and my household from what they do.
text_en_arberry: My Lord, deliver me and my people from that they do.’

text_ar: فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ أَجْمَعِينَ
text_en_primary: So We saved him and all of his family,
text_en_yusufali: So We delivered him and his family,- all
text_en_pickthall: So We saved him and his household, every one,
text_en_arberry: My Lord, deliver me and my people from that they do.’

text_ar: إِلَّا عَجُوزًۭا فِى ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ
text_en_primary: except an old woman, who was one of the doomed.
text_en_yusufali: Except an old woman who lingered behind.
text_en_pickthall: Save an old woman among those who stayed behind.
text_en_arberry: save an old woman among those that tarried;

text_ar: ثُمَّ دَمَّرْنَا ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ
text_en_primary: Then We utterly destroyed the rest,
text_en_yusufali: But the rest We destroyed utterly.
text_en_pickthall: Then afterward We destroyed the others.
text_en_arberry: then We destroyed the others,

text_ar: وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًۭا ۖ فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
text_en_primary: pouring upon them a rain ˹of brimstone˺. How evil was the rain of those who had been warned!
text_en_yusufali: We rained down on them a shower (of brimstone): and evil was the shower on those who were admonished (but heeded not)!
text_en_pickthall: And We rained on them a rain. And dreadful is the rain of those who have been warned.
text_en_arberry: and We rained on them a rain; and evil is the rain of them that are warned.

text_ar: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
text_en_primary: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.
text_en_yusufali: Verily in this is a Sign: but most of them do not believe.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! herein is indeed a portent, yet most of them are not believers.
text_en_arberry: Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.

text_ar: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
text_en_primary: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.
text_en_yusufali: And verily thy Lord is He, the Exalted in Might Most Merciful.
text_en_pickthall: And lo! thy Lord, He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful.
text_en_arberry: Surely thy Lord, He is the All-mighty, the All-compassionate.

text_ar: كَذَّبَ أَصْحَٰبُ لْـَٔيْكَةِ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
text_en_primary: The residents of the Forest rejected the messengers
text_en_yusufali: The Companions of the Wood rejected the apostles.
text_en_pickthall: The dwellers in the wood (of Midian) denied the messengers (of Allah),
text_en_arberry: The men of the Thicket cried lies to the Envoys

text_ar: إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ شُعَيْبٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
text_en_primary: when Shu’aib said to them, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?
text_en_pickthall: When Shu’eyb said unto them: Will ye not ward off (evil) ?
text_en_arberry: when Shuaib said to them, ’Will you not be godfearing?

text_ar: إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ
text_en_primary: I am truly a trustworthy messenger to you.
text_en_yusufali: Behold, Shu’aib said to them: "Will ye not fear (God)?
text_en_pickthall: Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you,
text_en_arberry: I am for you a faithful Messenger, so fear you God, and obey you me.

text_ar: فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
text_en_primary: So fear Allah, and obey me.
text_en_yusufali: "I am to you an apostle worthy of all trust.
text_en_pickthall: So keep your duty to Allah and obey me.
text_en_arberry: I ask of you no wage for this;

text_ar: وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
text_en_primary: I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺. My reward is only from the Lord of all worlds.
text_en_yusufali: "So fear God and obey me.
text_en_pickthall: And I ask of you no wage for it; my wage is the concern only of the Lord of the Worlds.
text_en_arberry: my wage falls only upon the Lord of all Being.

text_ar: ۞ أَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْكَيْلَ وَلَا تَكُونُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلْمُخْسِرِينَ
text_en_primary: Give full measure, and cause no loss ˹to others˺.
text_en_yusufali: "No reward do I ask of you for it: my reward is only from the Lord of the Worlds.
text_en_pickthall: Give full measure, and be not of those who give less (than the due).
text_en_arberry: Fill up the measure, and be not cheaters,

text_ar: وَزِنُوا۟ بِٱلْقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ
text_en_primary: Weigh with an even balance,
text_en_yusufali: "Give just measure, and cause no loss (to others by fraud).
text_en_pickthall: And weigh with the true balance.
text_en_arberry: and weigh with the straight balance,

text_ar: وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا۟ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشْيَآءَهُمْ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ
text_en_primary: and do not defraud people of their property. Nor go about spreading corruption in the land.
text_en_yusufali: "And weigh with scales true and upright.
text_en_pickthall: Wrong not mankind in their goods, and do not evil, making mischief, in the earth.
text_en_arberry: and diminish not the goods of the people, and do not mischief in the earth, working corruption.

text_ar: وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُمْ وَٱلْجِبِلَّةَ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
text_en_primary: And fear the One Who created you and ˹all˺ earlier peoples.”
text_en_yusufali: "And withhold not things justly due to men, nor do evil in the land, working mischief.
text_en_pickthall: And keep your duty unto Him Who created you and the generations of the men of old.
text_en_arberry: Fear Him who created you, and the generations of the ancients.’

text_ar: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسَحَّرِينَ
text_en_primary: They replied, “You are simply bewitched!
text_en_yusufali: "And fear Him Who created you and (who created) the generations before (you)"
text_en_pickthall: They said: Thou art but one of the bewitched;
text_en_arberry: They said, ’Thou art merely one of those that are bewitched;

text_ar: وَمَآ أَنتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌۭ مِّثْلُنَا وَإِن نَّظُنُّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
text_en_primary: Also, you are only a human being like us, and we think you are indeed a liar.
text_en_yusufali: They said: "Thou art only one of those bewitched!
text_en_pickthall: Thou art but a mortal like us, and lo! we deem thee of the liars.
text_en_arberry: thou art naught but a mortal, like us; indeed, we think that thou art one of the liars.

text_ar: فَأَسْقِطْ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًۭا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
text_en_primary: So cause ˹deadly˺ pieces of the sky to fall upon us, if what you say is true.”
text_en_yusufali: "Thou art no more than a mortal like us, and indeed we think thou art a liar!
text_en_pickthall: Then make fragments of the heaven fall upon us, if thou art of the truthful.
text_en_arberry: Then drop down on us lumps from heaven, if thou art one of the truthful.’

text_ar: قَالَ رَبِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
text_en_primary: Shu’aib responded, “My Lord knows best whatever you do.”
text_en_yusufali: "Now cause a piece of the sky to fall on us, if thou art truthful!"
text_en_pickthall: He said: My Lord is Best Aware of what ye do.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’My Lord knows very well what you are doing.’

text_ar: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمِ ٱلظُّلَّةِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
text_en_primary: So they rejected him, and ˹so˺ were overtaken by the torment of the day of the ˹deadly˺ cloud. That was really a torment of a tremendous day.
text_en_yusufali: He said: "My Lord knows best what ye do."
text_en_pickthall: But they denied him, so there came on them the retribution of the day of gloom. Lo! it was the retribution of an awful day.
text_en_arberry: But they cried him lies; then there seized them the chastisement of the Day of Shadow; assuredly it was the chastisement of a dreadful day.

text_ar: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
text_en_primary: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.
text_en_yusufali: But they rejected him. Then the punishment of a day of overshadowing gloom seized them, and that was the Penalty of a Great Day.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! herein is indeed a portent; yet most of them are not believers.
text_en_arberry: Surely in that is a sign, yet most of them are not believers.

text_ar: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
text_en_primary: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.
text_en_yusufali: Verily in that is a Sign: but most of them do not believe.
text_en_pickthall: And lo! thy Lord! He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful.
text_en_arberry: Surely thy Lord, He is the All-mighty, the All-compassionate.

text_ar: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَتَنزِيلُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
text_en_primary: This is certainly a revelation from the Lord of all worlds,
text_en_yusufali: And verily thy Lord is He, the Exalted in Might, Most Merciful.
text_en_pickthall: And lo! it is a revelation of the Lord of the Worlds,
text_en_arberry: Truly it is the revelation of the Lord of all Being,

text_ar: نَزَلَ بِهِ ٱلرُّوحُ ٱلْأَمِينُ
text_en_primary: which the trustworthy spirit ˹Gabriel˺ brought down
text_en_yusufali: Verily this is a Revelation from the Lord of the Worlds:
text_en_pickthall: Which the True Spirit hath brought down
text_en_arberry: brought down by the Faithful Spirit

text_ar: عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنذِرِينَ
text_en_primary: into your heart ˹O Prophet˺—so that you may be one of the warners—
text_en_yusufali: With it came down the spirit of Faith and Truth-
text_en_pickthall: Upon thy heart, that thou mayst be (one) of the warners,
text_en_arberry: upon thy heart, that thou mayest be one of the warners,

text_ar: بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِىٍّۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
text_en_primary: in a clear Arabic tongue.
text_en_yusufali: To thy heart and mind, that thou mayest admonish.
text_en_pickthall: In plain Arabic speech.
text_en_arberry: in a clear, Arabic tongue.

text_ar: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَفِى زُبُرِ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
text_en_primary: And it has indeed been ˹foretold˺ in the Scriptures of those before.
text_en_yusufali: In the perspicuous Arabic tongue.
text_en_pickthall: And lo! it is in the Scriptures of the men of old.
text_en_arberry: Truly it is in the Scriptures of the ancients.

text_ar: أَوَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُمْ ءَايَةً أَن يَعْلَمَهُۥ عُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
text_en_primary: Was it not sufficient proof for the deniers that it has been recognized by the knowledgeable among the Children of Israel?
text_en_yusufali: Without doubt it is (announced) in the mystic Books of former peoples.
text_en_pickthall: Is it not a token for them that the doctors of the Children of Israel know it ?
text_en_arberry: Was it not a sign for them, that it is known to the learned of the Children of Israel?

text_ar: وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَٰهُ عَلَىٰ بَعْضِ ٱلْأَعْجَمِينَ
text_en_primary: Had We revealed it to a non-Arab,
text_en_yusufali: * v.196: The word Zubur, used here, is plural of Zabar, which is mentioned in the Qur-in as the Book revealed to the prophet Da’ud. It has also been used in the Qur-in in generic sense of "Book" (LIV: 52). Here the word refers to the earlier Revelations.
text_en_pickthall: And if We had revealed it unto one of any other nation than the Arabs,
text_en_arberry: If We had sent it down on a barbarian

text_ar: فَقَرَأَهُۥ عَلَيْهِم مَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ مُؤْمِنِينَ
text_en_primary: who would then recite it to the deniers ˹in fluent Arabic˺, still they would not have believed in it!
text_en_yusufali: Is it not a Sign to them that the Learned of the Children of Israel knew it (as true)?
text_en_pickthall: And he had read it unto them, they would not have believed in it.
text_en_arberry: and he had recited it to them, they would not have believed in it.

text_ar: كَذَٰلِكَ سَلَكْنَٰهُ فِى قُلُوبِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
text_en_primary: This is how We allow denial ˹to steep˺ into the hearts of the wicked.
text_en_yusufali: Had We revealed it to any of the non-Arabs,
text_en_pickthall: Thus do We make it traverse the hearts of the guilty.
text_en_arberry: Even so We have caused it to enter into the hearts of the sinners,

text_ar: لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِۦ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَلِيمَ
text_en_primary: They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment,
text_en_yusufali: And had he recited it to them, they would not have believed in it.
text_en_pickthall: They will not believe in it till they behold the painful doom,
text_en_arberry: who will not believe in it, until they see the painful chastisement

text_ar: فَيَأْتِيَهُم بَغْتَةًۭ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
text_en_primary: which will take them by surprise when they least expect ˹it˺.
text_en_yusufali: Thus have We caused it to enter the hearts of the sinners.
text_en_pickthall: So that it will come upon them suddenly, when they perceive not.
text_en_arberry: so that it will come upon them suddenly, while they are not aware,

text_ar: فَيَقُولُوا۟ هَلْ نَحْنُ مُنظَرُونَ
text_en_primary: Then they will cry, “Can we be allowed more time?”
text_en_yusufali: They will not believe in it until they see the grievous Penalty;
text_en_pickthall: Then they will say: Are we to be reprieved ?
text_en_arberry: and they will say, ’Shall we be respited?’

text_ar: أَفَبِعَذَابِنَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونَ
text_en_primary: Do they ˹really˺ seek to hasten Our torment?
text_en_yusufali: But the (Penalty) will come to them of a sudden, while they perceive it not;
text_en_pickthall: Would they (now) hasten on Our doom ?
text_en_arberry: What, do they seek to hasten Our chastisement?

text_ar: أَفَرَءَيْتَ إِن مَّتَّعْنَٰهُمْ سِنِينَ
text_en_primary: Imagine ˹O Prophet˺ if We allowed them enjoyment for years,
text_en_yusufali: Then they will say: "Shall we be respited?"
text_en_pickthall: Hast thou then seen, if We content them for (long) years,
text_en_arberry: What thinkest thou? If We give them enjoyment of days for many years,

text_ar: ثُمَّ جَآءَهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يُوعَدُونَ
text_en_primary: then there came to them what they had been threatened with:
text_en_yusufali: Do they then ask for Our Penalty to be hastened on?
text_en_pickthall: And then cometh that which they were promised,
text_en_arberry: then there comes on them that they were promised,

text_ar: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يُمَتَّعُونَ
text_en_primary: would that enjoyment be of any benefit to them ˹at all˺?
text_en_yusufali: Seest thou? If We do let them enjoy (this life) for a few years,
text_en_pickthall: (How) that wherewith they were contented naught availeth them ?
text_en_arberry: what will it then avail them, the enjoyment of days they were given?

text_ar: وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلَّا لَهَا مُنذِرُونَ
text_en_primary: We have never destroyed a society without warners
text_en_yusufali: Yet there comes to them at length the (Punishment) which they were promised!
text_en_pickthall: And We destroyed no township but it had its warners
text_en_arberry: Never a city We destroyed, but it had warners

text_ar: ذِكْرَىٰ وَمَا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
text_en_primary: to remind ˹them˺, for We would never wrong ˹anyone˺.
text_en_yusufali: It will profit them not that they enjoyed (this life)!
text_en_pickthall: For reminder, for We never were oppressors.
text_en_arberry: for a reminder; and never did We wrong.

text_ar: وَمَا تَنَزَّلَتْ بِهِ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينُ
text_en_primary: It was not the devils who brought this ˹Quran˺ down:
text_en_yusufali: Never did We destroy a population, but had its warners -
text_en_pickthall: The devils did not bring it down.
text_en_arberry: Not by the Satans has it been brought down;

text_ar: وَمَا يَنۢبَغِى لَهُمْ وَمَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ
text_en_primary: it is not for them ˹to do so˺, nor can they,
text_en_yusufali: By way of reminder; and We never are unjust.
text_en_pickthall: It is not meet for them, nor is it in their power,
text_en_arberry: it behoves them not, neither are they able.

text_ar: إِنَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّمْعِ لَمَعْزُولُونَ
text_en_primary: for they are strictly barred from ˹even˺ overhearing ˹it˺.
text_en_yusufali: No evil ones have brought down this (Revelation):
text_en_pickthall: Lo! verily they are banished from the hearing.
text_en_arberry: Truly, they are expelled from hearing.

text_ar: فَلَا تَدْعُ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُعَذَّبِينَ
text_en_primary: So do not ever call upon any other god besides Allah, or you will be one of the punished.
text_en_yusufali: It would neither suit them nor would they be able (to produce it).
text_en_pickthall: Therefor invoke not with Allah another god, lest thou be one of the doomed.
text_en_arberry: So call thou not upon another god with God, lest thou shouldst be one of those that are chastised.

text_ar: وَأَنذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ ٱلْأَقْرَبِينَ
text_en_primary: And warn ˹all, starting with˺ your closest relatives,
text_en_yusufali: Indeed they have been removed far from even (a chance of) hearing it.
text_en_pickthall: And warn thy tribe of near kindred,
text_en_arberry: And warn thy clan, thy nearest kin.

text_ar: وَٱخْفِضْ جَنَاحَكَ لِمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
text_en_primary: and be gracious to the believers who follow you.
text_en_yusufali: So call not on any other god with God, or thou wilt be among those under the Penalty.
text_en_pickthall: And lower thy wing (in kindness) unto those believers who follow thee.
text_en_arberry: Lower thy wing to those who follow thee, being believers;

text_ar: فَإِنْ عَصَوْكَ فَقُلْ إِنِّى بَرِىٓءٌۭ مِّمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
text_en_primary: But if they disobey you, say, “I am certainly free of what you do.”
text_en_yusufali: And admonish thy nearest kinsmen,
text_en_pickthall: And if they (thy kinsfolk) disobey thee, say: Lo! I am innocent of what they do.
text_en_arberry: then, if they disobey thee, say, ’I am quit of that you do.’

text_ar: وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
text_en_primary: Put your trust in the Almighty, Most Merciful,
text_en_yusufali: And lower thy wing to the Believers who follow thee.
text_en_pickthall: And put thy trust in the Mighty, the Merciful.
text_en_arberry: Put thy trust in the All-mighty, the All-compassionate

text_ar: ٱلَّذِى يَرَىٰكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ
text_en_primary: Who sees you when you rise ˹for prayer at night˺,
text_en_yusufali: Then if they disobey thee, say: "I am free (of responsibility) for what ye do!"
text_en_pickthall: Who seeth thee when thou standest up (to pray)
text_en_arberry: who sees thee when thou standest

text_ar: وَتَقَلُّبَكَ فِى ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ
text_en_primary: as well as your movements ˹in prayer˺ along with ˹fellow˺ worshippers.
text_en_yusufali: And put thy trust on the Exalted in Might, the Merciful,-
text_en_pickthall: And (seeth) thine abasement among those who fall prostrate (in worship).
text_en_arberry: and when thou turnest about among those who bow.

text_ar: إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
text_en_primary: He ˹alone˺ is indeed the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
text_en_yusufali: Who seeth thee standing forth (in prayer),
text_en_pickthall: Lo! He, only He, is the Hearer, the Knower.
text_en_arberry: Surely He is the All-hearing, the All-knowing.

text_ar: هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن تَنَزَّلُ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينُ
text_en_primary: Shall I inform you of whom the devils ˹actually˺ descend upon?
text_en_yusufali: And thy movements among those who prostrate themselves,
text_en_pickthall: Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend ?
text_en_arberry: Shall I tell you on whom the Satans come down?

text_ar: تَنَزَّلُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ أَثِيمٍۢ
text_en_primary: They descend upon every sinful liar,
text_en_yusufali: For it is He Who heareth and knoweth all things.
text_en_pickthall: They descend on every sinful, false one.
text_en_arberry: They come down on every guilty impostor.

text_ar: يُلْقُونَ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ كَٰذِبُونَ
text_en_primary: who gives an ˹attentive˺ ear ˹to half-truths˺, mostly passing on sheer lies.
text_en_yusufali: Shall I inform you, (O people!), on whom it is that the evil ones descend?
text_en_pickthall: They listen eagerly, but most of them are liars.
text_en_arberry: They give ear, but most of them are liars.

text_ar: وَٱلشُّعَرَآءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ ٱلْغَاوُۥنَ
text_en_primary: As for poets, they are followed ˹merely˺ by deviants.
text_en_yusufali: They descend on every lying, wicked person,
text_en_pickthall: As for poets, the erring follow them.
text_en_arberry: And the poets -- the perverse follow them;

text_ar: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِى كُلِّ وَادٍۢ يَهِيمُونَ
text_en_primary: Do you not see how they rant in every field,
text_en_yusufali: (Into whose ears) they pour hearsay vanities, and most of them are liars.
text_en_pickthall: Hast thou not seen how they stray in every valley,
text_en_arberry: hast thou not seen how they wander in every valley

text_ar: وَأَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ مَا لَا يَفْعَلُونَ
text_en_primary: only saying what they never do?
text_en_yusufali: And the Poets,- It is those straying in Evil, who follow them:
text_en_pickthall: And how they say that which they do not ?
text_en_arberry: and how they say that which they do not?

text_ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَذَكَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرًۭا وَٱنتَصَرُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُوا۟ ۗ وَسَيَعْلَمُ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ أَىَّ مُنقَلَبٍۢ يَنقَلِبُونَ
text_en_primary: Except those who believe, do good, remember Allah often, and ˹poetically˺ avenge ˹the believers˺ after being wrongfully slandered. The wrongdoers will come to know what ˹evil˺ end they will meet.
text_en_yusufali: Seest thou not that they wander distracted in every valley?-
text_en_pickthall: Save those who believe and do good works, and remember Allah much, and vindicate themselves after they have been wronged. Those who do wrong will come to know by what a (great) reverse they will be overturned!
text_en_arberry: Save those that believe, and do righteous deeds, and remember God oft, and help themselves after being wronged; and those who do wrong shall surely know by what overturning they will he overturned.

text_ar: طسٓ ۚ تِلْكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلْقُرْءَانِ وَكِتَابٍۢ مُّبِينٍ
text_en_primary: Ṭa-Sĩn. These are the verses of the Quran; the clear Book.
text_en_yusufali: These are verses of the Qur’an,-a book that makes (things) clear;
text_en_pickthall: Ta. Sin. These are revelations of the Qur’an and a Scripture that maketh plain;
text_en_arberry: Ta Sin. Those are the signs of the Koran and a Manifest Book,

text_ar: هُدًۭى وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
text_en_primary: ˹It is˺ a guide and good news for the believers:
text_en_yusufali: A guide: and glad tidings for the believers,-
text_en_pickthall: A guidance and good tidings for believers
text_en_arberry: a guidance, and good tidings unto the believers

text_ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَهُم بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ
text_en_primary: ˹those˺ who establish prayer, pay alms-tax, and have sure faith in the Hereafter.
text_en_yusufali: Those who establish regular prayers and give in regular charity, and also have (full) assurance of the hereafter.
text_en_pickthall: Who establish worship and pay the poor-due and are sure of the Hereafter.
text_en_arberry: who perform the prayer, and pay the alms, and have sure faith in the Hereafter.

text_ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ زَيَّنَّا لَهُمْ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ فَهُمْ يَعْمَهُونَ
text_en_primary: As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have certainly made their ˹evil˺ deeds appealing to them, so they wander blindly.
text_en_yusufali: As to those who believe not in the Hereafter, We have made their deeds pleasing in their eyes; and so they wander about in distraction.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! as for those who believe not in the Hereafter, We have made their works fairseeming unto them so that they are all astray.
text_en_arberry: Those who believe not in the Hereafter, We have decked out fair for them their works, and they wander blindly;

text_ar: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَهُمْ سُوٓءُ ٱلْعَذَابِ وَهُمْ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ هُمُ ٱلْأَخْسَرُونَ
text_en_primary: It is they who will suffer a dreadful torment, and in the Hereafter they will ˹truly˺ be the greatest losers.
text_en_yusufali: Such are they for whom a grievous Penalty is (waiting); and in the Hereafter theirs will be the greatest loss.
text_en_pickthall: Those are they for whom is the worst of punishment, and in the Hereafter they will be the greatest losers.
text_en_arberry: those are they whom an evil chastisement awaits, and they will be the greatest losers in the Hereafter.

text_ar: وَإِنَّكَ لَتُلَقَّى ٱلْقُرْءَانَ مِن لَّدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ
text_en_primary: And indeed, you ˹O Prophet˺ are receiving the Quran from the One ˹Who is˺ All-Wise, All-Knowing.
text_en_yusufali: As to thee, the Qur’an is bestowed upon thee from the presence of one who is wise and all-knowing.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! as for thee (Muhammad), thou verily receivest the Qur’an from the presence of One Wise, Aware.
text_en_arberry: Thou receivest the Koran from One All-wise, All-knowing.

text_ar: إِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِأَهْلِهِۦٓ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًۭا سَـَٔاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ ءَاتِيكُم بِشِهَابٍۢ قَبَسٍۢ لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ
text_en_primary: ˹Remember˺ when Moses said to his family, “I have spotted a fire. I will either bring you some directions from there, or a burning torch so you may warm yourselves.”
text_en_yusufali: Behold! Moses said to his family: "I perceive a fire; soon will I bring you from there some information, or I will bring you a burning brand to light our fuel, that ye may warn yourselves.
text_en_pickthall: (Remember) when Moses said unto his household: Lo! I spy afar off a fire; I will bring you tidings thence, or bring to you a borrowed flame that ye may warm yourselves.
text_en_arberry: When Moses said to his people ’I observe a fire, and will bring you news of it, or I will bring you a flaming brand, that haply you shall warm yourselves.’

text_ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهَا نُودِىَ أَنۢ بُورِكَ مَن فِى ٱلنَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا وَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
text_en_primary: But when he came to it, he was called ˹by Allah˺, “Blessed is the one at the fire, and whoever is around it! Glory be to Allah, the Lord of all worlds.
text_en_yusufali: But when he came to the (fire), a voice was heard: "Blessed are those in the fire and those around: and glory to God, the Lord of the worlds.
text_en_pickthall: But when he reached it, he was called, saying: Blessed is Whosoever is in the fire and Whosoever is round about it! And Glorified be Allah, the Lord of the Worlds!
text_en_arberry: So, when he came to it, he was called: ’Blessed is he who is in the fire, and he who is about it. Glory be to God, the Lord of all Being!

text_ar: يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
text_en_primary: O  Moses! It is truly I. I am Allah—the Almighty, All-Wise.
text_en_yusufali: "O Moses! verily, I am God, the exalted in might, the wise!....
text_en_pickthall: O Moses! Lo! it is I, Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.
text_en_arberry: Moses, behold, it is I, God, the All-mighty, the All-wise.

text_ar: وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ ۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّۭ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًۭا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ ۚ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَا تَخَفْ إِنِّى لَا يَخَافُ لَدَىَّ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
text_en_primary: Now, throw down your staff!” But when he saw it slithering like a snake, he ran away without looking back. ˹Allah reassured him,˺ “O Moses! Do not be afraid! Messengers should have no fear in My presence.
text_en_yusufali: "Now do thou throw thy rod!" But when he saw it moving (of its own accord)as if it had been a snake, he turned back in retreat, and retraced not his steps: "O Moses!" (it was said), "Fear not: truly, in My presence, those called as apostles have no fear,-
text_en_pickthall: And throw down thy staff! But when he saw it writhing as it were a demon, he turned to flee headlong; (but it was said unto him): O Moses! Fear not! the emissaries fear not in My presence,
text_en_arberry: Cast down thy staff.’ And when he saw it quivering like a serpent he turned about, retreating, and turned not back. ’Moses, fear not; surely the Envoys do not fear in My presence,

text_ar: إِلَّا مَن ظَلَمَ ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْنًۢا بَعْدَ سُوٓءٍۢ فَإِنِّى غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
text_en_primary: ˹Fear is˺ only for those who do wrong. But if they later mend ˹their˺ evil ˹ways˺ with good, then I am certainly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
text_en_yusufali: "But if any have done wrong and have thereafter substituted good to take the place of evil, truly, I am Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
text_en_pickthall: Save him who hath done wrong and afterward hath changed evil for good. And lo! I am Forgiving, Merciful.
text_en_arberry: save him who has done evil, then; after evil, has changed into good; All-forgiving am I, All-compassionate.

text_ar: وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍۢ ۖ فِى تِسْعِ ءَايَٰتٍ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ ۚ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًۭا فَٰسِقِينَ
text_en_primary: Now put your hand through ˹the opening of˺ your collar, it will come out ˹shining˺ white, unblemished. They have truly been a rebellious people.”
text_en_yusufali: "Now put thy hand into thy bosom, and it will come forth white without stain (or harm): (these are) among the nine Signs (thou wilt take) to Pharaoh and his people: for they are a people rebellious in transgression."
text_en_pickthall: And put thy hand into the bosom of thy robe, it will come forth white but unhurt. (This will be one) among nine tokens unto Pharaoh and his people Lo! they were ever evil-living folk.
text_en_arberry: Thrust thy hand in thy bosom and it will come forth white without evil-among nine signs to Pharaoh and his people; they are an ungodly people.’

text_ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْهُمْ ءَايَٰتُنَا مُبْصِرَةًۭ قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا سِحْرٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
text_en_primary: But when Our enlightening signs came to them, they said, “This is pure magic.”
text_en_yusufali: But when Our Signs came to them, that should have opened their eyes, they said: "This is sorcery manifest!"
text_en_pickthall: But when Our tokens came unto them, plain to see, they said: This is mere magic,
text_en_arberry: But when Our signs came to them visibly, they said, ’This is a manifest sorcery’;

text_ar: وَجَحَدُوا۟ بِهَا وَٱسْتَيْقَنَتْهَآ أَنفُسُهُمْ ظُلْمًۭا وَعُلُوًّۭا ۚ فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ
text_en_primary: And, although their hearts were convinced the signs were true, they still denied them wrongfully and arrogantly. See then what was the end of the corruptors!
text_en_yusufali: And they rejected those Signs in iniquity and arrogance, though their souls were convinced thereof: so see what was the end of those who acted corruptly!
text_en_pickthall: And they denied them, though their souls acknowledged them, for spite and arrogance. Then see the nature of the consequence for the wrong- doers!
text_en_arberry: and they denied them, though their souls acknowledged them, wrongfully and out of pride. Behold, how was the end of the workers of corruption!

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا دَاوُۥدَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ عِلْمًۭا ۖ وَقَالَا ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى فَضَّلَنَا عَلَىٰ كَثِيرٍۢ مِّنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
text_en_primary: Indeed, We granted knowledge to David and Solomon. And they said ˹in acknowledgment˺, “All praise is for Allah Who has privileged us over many of His faithful servants.”
text_en_yusufali: We gave (in the past) knowledge to David and Solomon: And they both said: "Praise be to God, Who has favoured us above many of his servants who believe!"
text_en_pickthall: And We verily gave knowledge unto David and Solomon, and they said: Praise be to Allah, Who hath preferred us above many of His believing slaves!
text_en_arberry: And We gave David and Solomon knowledge and they said, ’Praise belongs to God who has preferred us over many of His believing servants.’

text_ar: وَوَرِثَ سُلَيْمَٰنُ دَاوُۥدَ ۖ وَقَالَ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ عُلِّمْنَا مَنطِقَ ٱلطَّيْرِ وَأُوتِينَا مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍ ۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْفَضْلُ ٱلْمُبِينُ
text_en_primary: And David was succeeded by Solomon, who said, “O people! We have been taught the language of birds, and been given everything ˹we need˺. This is indeed a great privilege.”
text_en_yusufali: And Solomon was David’s heir. He said: "O ye people! We have been taught the speech of birds, and on us has been bestowed (a little) of all things: this is indeed Grace manifest (from God.)"
text_en_pickthall: And Solomon was David’s heir. And he said: O mankind! Lo! we have been taught the language of birds, and have been given (abundance) of all things. This surely is evident favour.
text_en_arberry: And Solomon was David’s heir, and he said, ’Men, we have been taught the speech of the birds, and we have been given of everything; surely this is indeed the manifest bounty.’

text_ar: وَحُشِرَ لِسُلَيْمَٰنَ جُنُودُهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلْإِنسِ وَٱلطَّيْرِ فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ
text_en_primary: Solomon’s forces of jinn, humans, and birds were rallied for him, perfectly organized.
text_en_yusufali: And before Solomon were marshalled his hosts,- of Jinns and men and birds, and they were all kept in order and ranks.
text_en_pickthall: And there were gathered together unto Solomon his armies of the jinn and humankind, and of the birds, and they were set in battle order;
text_en_arberry: And his hosts were mustered to Solomon, jinn, men and birds, duly disposed;

text_ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَتَوْا۟ عَلَىٰ وَادِ ٱلنَّمْلِ قَالَتْ نَمْلَةٌۭ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّمْلُ ٱدْخُلُوا۟ مَسَٰكِنَكُمْ لَا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ سُلَيْمَٰنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
text_en_primary: And when they came across a valley of ants, an ant warned, “O ants! Go quickly into your homes so Solomon and his armies do not crush you, unknowingly.”
text_en_yusufali: At length, when they came to a (lowly) valley of ants, one of the ants said: "O ye ants, get into your habitations, lest Solomon and his hosts crush you (under foot) without knowing it."
text_en_pickthall: Till, when they reached the Valley of the Ants, an ant exclaimed: O ants! Enter your dwellings lest Solomon and his armies crush you, unperceiving.
text_en_arberry: till, when they came on the Valley of Ants, an ant said, ’Ants, enter your dwelling-places, lest Solomon and his hosts crush you, being unaware!’

text_ar: فَتَبَسَّمَ ضَاحِكًۭا مِّن قَوْلِهَا وَقَالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِىٓ أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَىَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَىَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَٰلِحًۭا تَرْضَىٰهُ وَأَدْخِلْنِى بِرَحْمَتِكَ فِى عِبَادِكَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
text_en_primary: So Solomon smiled in amusement at her words, and prayed, “My Lord! Inspire me to ˹always˺ be thankful for Your favours which You have blessed me and my parents with, and to do good deeds that please you. Admit me, by Your mercy, into ˹the company of˺ Your righteous servants.”
text_en_yusufali: So he smiled, amused at her speech; and he said: "O my Lord! so order me that I may be grateful for Thy favours, which thou hast bestowed on me and on my parents, and that I may work the righteousness that will please Thee: And admit me, by Thy Grace, to the ranks of Thy righteous Servants."
text_en_pickthall: And (Solomon) smiled, laughing at her speech, and said: My Lord, arouse me to be thankful for Thy favour wherewith Thou hast favoured me and my parents, and to do good that shall be pleasing unto Thee, and include me in (the number of) Thy righteous slaves.
text_en_arberry: But he smiled, laughing at its words, and he said, ’My Lord, dispose me that I may be thankful for Thy blessing wherewith Thou hast blessed me and my father and mother, and that I may do righteousness well-pleasing to Thee; and do Thou admit me, by Thy mercy, amongst Thy righteous servants.’

text_ar: وَتَفَقَّدَ ٱلطَّيْرَ فَقَالَ مَا لِىَ لَآ أَرَى ٱلْهُدْهُدَ أَمْ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْغَآئِبِينَ
text_en_primary: ˹One day˺ he inspected the birds, and wondered, “Why is it that I cannot see the hoopoe? Or could he be absent?
text_en_yusufali: And he took a muster of the Birds; and he said: "Why is it I see not the Hoopoe? Or is he among the absentees?
text_en_pickthall: And he sought among the birds and said: How is it that I see not the hoopoe, or is he among the absent ?
text_en_arberry: And he reviewed the birds; then he said, ’How is it with me, that I do not see the hoopoe? Or is he among the absent?

text_ar: لَأُعَذِّبَنَّهُۥ عَذَابًۭا شَدِيدًا أَوْ لَأَا۟ذْبَحَنَّهُۥٓ أَوْ لَيَأْتِيَنِّى بِسُلْطَٰنٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
text_en_primary: I will surely subject him to a severe punishment, or ˹even˺ slaughter him, unless he brings me a compelling excuse.”
text_en_yusufali: "I will certainly punish him with a severe penalty, or execute him, unless he bring me a clear reason (for absence)."
text_en_pickthall: I verily will punish him with hard punishment or I verily will slay him, or he verily shall bring me a plain excuse.
text_en_arberry: Assuredly I will chastise him with a terrible chastisement, or I will slaughter him, or he bring me a clear authority.’

text_ar: فَمَكَثَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍۢ فَقَالَ أَحَطتُ بِمَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِۦ وَجِئْتُكَ مِن سَبَإٍۭ بِنَبَإٍۢ يَقِينٍ
text_en_primary: It was not long before the bird came and said, “I have found out something you do not know. I have just come to you from Sheba with sure news.
text_en_yusufali: But the Hoopoe tarried not far: he (came up and) said: "I have compassed (territory) which thou hast not compassed, and I have come to thee from Saba with tidings true.
text_en_pickthall: But he was not long in coming, and he said: I have found out (a thing) that thou apprehendest not, and I come unto thee from Sheba with sure tidings.
text_en_arberry: But he tarried not long, and said, ’I have comprehended that which thou hast not comprehended, and I have come from Sheba to thee with a sure tiding.

text_ar: إِنِّى وَجَدتُّ ٱمْرَأَةًۭ تَمْلِكُهُمْ وَأُوتِيَتْ مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ وَلَهَا عَرْشٌ عَظِيمٌۭ
text_en_primary: Indeed, I found a woman ruling over them, who has been given everything ˹she needs˺, and who has a magnificent throne.
text_en_yusufali: "I found (there) a woman ruling over them and provided with every requisite; and she has a magnificent throne.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! I found a woman ruling over them, and she hath been given (abundance) of all things, and hers is a mighty throne.
text_en_arberry: I found a woman ruling over them, and she has been given of everything, and she possesses a mighty throne.

text_ar: وَجَدتُّهَا وَقَوْمَهَا يَسْجُدُونَ لِلشَّمْسِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ فَهُمْ لَا يَهْتَدُونَ
text_en_primary: I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah. For Satan has made their deeds appealing to them—hindering them from the ˹Right˺ Way and leaving them unguided—
text_en_yusufali: "I found her and her people worshipping the sun besides God: Satan has made their deeds seem pleasing in their eyes, and has kept them away from the Path,- so they receive no guidance,-
text_en_pickthall: I found her and her people worshipping the sun instead of Allah; and Satan maketh their works fairseeming unto them, and debarreth them from the way (of Truth), so that they go not aright;
text_en_arberry: I found her and her people prostrating to the sun, apart from God; Satan has decked out fair their deeds to them and he has barred them from the way, and therefore they are not guided,

text_ar: أَلَّا يَسْجُدُوا۟ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى يُخْرِجُ ٱلْخَبْءَ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تُخْفُونَ وَمَا تُعْلِنُونَ
text_en_primary: so they do not prostrate to Allah, Who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and knows what you ˹all˺ conceal and what you reveal.
text_en_yusufali: "(Kept them away from the Path), that they should not worship God, Who brings to light what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and knows what ye hide and what ye reveal.
text_en_pickthall: So that they worship not Allah, Who bringeth forth the hidden in the heavens and the earth, and knoweth what ye hide and what ye proclaim,
text_en_arberry: so that they prostrate not themselves to God, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and earth; and He knows what you conceal and what you publish.

text_ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ ۩
text_en_primary: ˹He is˺ Allah! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him, the Lord of the Mighty Throne.”
text_en_yusufali: "God!- there is no god but He!- Lord of the Throne Supreme!"
text_en_pickthall: Allah; there is no God save Him, the Lord of the Tremendous Throne.
text_en_arberry: God: there is no god but He, the Lord of the Mighty Throne.’

text_ar: ۞ قَالَ سَنَنظُرُ أَصَدَقْتَ أَمْ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
text_en_primary: Solomon said, “We will see whether you are telling the truth or lying.
text_en_yusufali: (Solomon) said: "Soon shall we see whether thou hast told the truth or lied!
text_en_pickthall: (Solomon) said: We shall see whether thou speakest truth or whether thou art of the liars.
text_en_arberry: Said he, ’Now We will see whether thou hast spoken truly, or whether thou art amongst those that lie.

text_ar: ٱذْهَب بِّكِتَٰبِى هَٰذَا فَأَلْقِهْ إِلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا يَرْجِعُونَ
text_en_primary: Go with this letter of mine and deliver it to them, then stand aside and see how they will respond.”
text_en_yusufali: "Go thou, with this letter of mine, and deliver it to them: then draw back from them, and (wait to) see what answer they return"...
text_en_pickthall: Go with this my letter and throw it down unto them; then turn away and see what (answer) they return,
text_en_arberry: Take this letter of mine, and cast it unto them, then turn back from them and see what they shall return ’

text_ar: قَالَتْ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ إِنِّىٓ أُلْقِىَ إِلَىَّ كِتَٰبٌۭ كَرِيمٌ
text_en_primary: The Queen ˹later˺ announced, “O chiefs! Indeed, a noble letter has been delivered to me.
text_en_yusufali: (The queen) said: "Ye chiefs! here is delivered to me - a letter worthy of respect.
text_en_pickthall: (The Queen of Sheba) said (when she received the letter): O chieftains! Lo! there hath been thrown unto me a noble letter.
text_en_arberry: She said, ’O Council, see, a letter honourable has been cast unto me.

text_ar: إِنَّهُۥ مِن سُلَيْمَٰنَ وَإِنَّهُۥ بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
text_en_primary: It is from Solomon, and it reads: ‘In the Name of Allah—the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful.
text_en_yusufali: "It is from Solomon, and is (as follows): ’In the name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful:
text_en_pickthall: Lo! it is from Solomon, and lo! it is: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful;
text_en_arberry: It is from Solomon, and it is "In the Name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

text_ar: أَلَّا تَعْلُوا۟ عَلَىَّ وَأْتُونِى مُسْلِمِينَ
text_en_primary: Do not be arrogant with me, but come to me, fully submitting ˹to Allah˺.’”
text_en_yusufali: "’Be ye not arrogant against me, but come to me in submission (to the true Religion).’"
text_en_pickthall: Exalt not yourselves against me, but come unto me as those who surrender.
text_en_arberry: Rise not up against me, but come to me in surrender." ’

text_ar: قَالَتْ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ أَفْتُونِى فِىٓ أَمْرِى مَا كُنتُ قَاطِعَةً أَمْرًا حَتَّىٰ تَشْهَدُونِ
text_en_primary: She said, “O chiefs! Advise me in this matter of mine, for I would never make any decision without you.”
text_en_yusufali: She said: "Ye chiefs! advise me in (this) my affair: no affair have I decided except in your presence."
text_en_pickthall: She said: O chieftains! Pronounce for me in my case. I decide no case till ye are present with me.
text_en_arberry: She said, ’O Council, pronounce to me concerning my affair; I am not used to decide an affair until you bear me witness.’

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ نَحْنُ أُو۟لُوا۟ قُوَّةٍۢ وَأُو۟لُوا۟ بَأْسٍۢ شَدِيدٍۢ وَٱلْأَمْرُ إِلَيْكِ فَٱنظُرِى مَاذَا تَأْمُرِينَ
text_en_primary: They responded, “We are a people of strength and great ˹military˺ might, but the decision is yours, so decide what you will command.”
text_en_yusufali: They said: "We are endued with strength, and given to vehement war: but the command is with thee; so consider what thou wilt command."
text_en_pickthall: They said: We are lords of might and lords of great prowess, but it is for thee to command; so consider what thou wilt command.
text_en_arberry: They said, ’We possess force and we possess great might. The affair rests with thee; so consider what thou wilt command.’

text_ar: قَالَتْ إِنَّ ٱلْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُوا۟ قَرْيَةً أَفْسَدُوهَا وَجَعَلُوٓا۟ أَعِزَّةَ أَهْلِهَآ أَذِلَّةًۭ ۖ وَكَذَٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ
text_en_primary: She reasoned, “Indeed, when kings invade a land, they ruin it and debase its nobles. They really do so!
text_en_yusufali: She said: "Kings, when they enter a country, despoil it, and make the noblest of its people its meanest thus do they behave.
text_en_pickthall: She said: Lo! kings, when they enter a township, ruin it and make the honour of its people shame. Thus will they do.
text_en_arberry: She said, ’Kings, when they enter a city, disorder it and make the mighty ones of its inhabitants abased. Even so they too will do.

text_ar: وَإِنِّى مُرْسِلَةٌ إِلَيْهِم بِهَدِيَّةٍۢ فَنَاظِرَةٌۢ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
text_en_primary: But I will certainly send him a gift, and see what ˹response˺ my envoys will return with.”
text_en_yusufali: "But I am going to send him a present, and (wait) to see with what (answer) return (my) ambassadors."
text_en_pickthall: But lo! I am going to send a present unto them, and to see with what (answer) the messengers return.
text_en_arberry: Now I will send them a present, and see what the envoys bring back.’

text_ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَ سُلَيْمَٰنَ قَالَ أَتُمِدُّونَنِ بِمَالٍۢ فَمَآ ءَاتَىٰنِۦَ ٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌۭ مِّمَّآ ءَاتَىٰكُم بَلْ أَنتُم بِهَدِيَّتِكُمْ تَفْرَحُونَ
text_en_primary: When the chief-envoy came to him, Solomon said, “Do you offer me wealth? What Allah has granted me is far greater than what He has granted you. No! It is you who rejoice in ˹receiving˺ gifts.
text_en_yusufali: Now when (the embassy) came to Solomon, he said: "Will ye give me abundance in wealth? But that which God has given me is better than that which He has given you! Nay it is ye who rejoice in your gift!
text_en_pickthall: So when (the envoy) came unto Solomon, (the King) said: What! Would ye help me with wealth ? But that which Allah hath given me is better than that which He hath given you. Nay it is ye (and not I) who exult in your gift.
text_en_arberry: But when he came to Solomon he said, ’What, would you succour me with wealth, and what God gave me is better than what He has given you? Nay, but instead you rejoice in your gift!

text_ar: ٱرْجِعْ إِلَيْهِمْ فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّهُم بِجُنُودٍۢ لَّا قِبَلَ لَهُم بِهَا وَلَنُخْرِجَنَّهُم مِّنْهَآ أَذِلَّةًۭ وَهُمْ صَٰغِرُونَ
text_en_primary: Go back to them, for we will certainly mobilize against them forces which they can never resist, and we will drive them out from there in disgrace, fully humbled.”
text_en_yusufali: "Go back to them, and be sure we shall come to them with such hosts as they will never be able to meet: We shall expel them from there in disgrace, and they will feel humbled (indeed)."
text_en_pickthall: Return unto them. We verily shall come unto them with hosts that they cannot resist, and we shall drive them out from thence with shame, and they will be abased.
text_en_arberry: Return thou to them; we shall assuredly come against them with hosts they have not power to resist, and we shall expel them from there, abased and utterly humbled.’

text_ar: قَالَ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ أَيُّكُمْ يَأْتِينِى بِعَرْشِهَا قَبْلَ أَن يَأْتُونِى مُسْلِمِينَ
text_en_primary: Solomon asked, “O chiefs! Which of you can bring me her throne before they come to me in ˹full˺ submission?”
text_en_yusufali: He said (to his own men): "Ye chiefs! which of you can bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?"
text_en_pickthall: He said: O chiefs! Which of you will bring me her throne before they come unto me, surrendering ?
text_en_arberry: He said, ’O Council, which one of you will bring me her throne, before they come to me in surrender?’

text_ar: قَالَ عِفْرِيتٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ أَنَا۠ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ قَبْلَ أَن تَقُومَ مِن مَّقَامِكَ ۖ وَإِنِّى عَلَيْهِ لَقَوِىٌّ أَمِينٌۭ
text_en_primary: One mighty jinn responded, “I can bring it to you before you rise from this council of yours. And I am quite strong and trustworthy for this ˹task˺.”
text_en_yusufali: Said an ’Ifrit, of the Jinns: "I will bring it to thee before thou rise from thy council: indeed I have full strength for the purpose, and may be trusted."
text_en_pickthall: A stalwart of the jinn said: I will bring it thee before thou canst rise from thy place. Lo! I verily am strong and trusty for such work.
text_en_arberry: An efreet of the jinns said, ’I will bring it to thee, before thou risest from thy place; I have strength for it

text_ar: قَالَ ٱلَّذِى عِندَهُۥ عِلْمٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ أَنَا۠ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ قَبْلَ أَن يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ ۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهُ مُسْتَقِرًّا عِندَهُۥ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِن فَضْلِ رَبِّى لِيَبْلُوَنِىٓ ءَأَشْكُرُ أَمْ أَكْفُرُ ۖ وَمَن شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ رَبِّى غَنِىٌّۭ كَرِيمٌۭ
text_en_primary: But the one who had knowledge of the Scripture said, “I can bring it to you in the blink of an eye.” So when Solomon saw it placed before him, he exclaimed, “This is by the grace of my Lord to test me whether I am grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful, it is only for their own good. But whoever is ungrateful, surely my Lord is Self-Sufficient, Most Generous.”
text_en_yusufali: Said one who had knowledge of the Book: "I will bring it to thee within the twinkling of an eye!" Then when (Solomon) saw it placed firmly before him, he said: "This is by the Grace of my Lord!- to test me whether I am grateful or ungrateful! and if any is grateful, truly his gratitude is (a gain) for his own soul; but if any is ungrateful, truly my Lord is Free of all Needs, Supreme in Honour !"
text_en_pickthall: One with whom was knowledge of the Scripture said: I will bring it thee before thy gaze returneth unto thee. And when he saw it set in his presence, (Solomon) said: This is of the bounty of my Lord, that He may try me whether I give thanks or am ungrateful. Whosoever giveth thanks he only giveth thanks for (the good of) his own soul; and whosoever is ungrateful (is ungrateful only to his own soul’s hurt). For lo! my Lord is Absolute in independence, Bountiful.
text_en_arberry: and I am trusty.’ Said he who possessed knowledge of the Book, ’I will bring it to thee, before ever thy glance returns to thee.’ Then, when he saw it settled before him, he said, ’This is of my Lord’s bounty that He may try me, whether I am thankful or ungrateful. Whosoever gives thanks gives thanks only for his own soul’s good, and whosoever is ungrateful -- my Lord is surely All-sufficient, All-generous.’

text_ar: قَالَ نَكِّرُوا۟ لَهَا عَرْشَهَا نَنظُرْ أَتَهْتَدِىٓ أَمْ تَكُونُ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَهْتَدُونَ
text_en_primary: ˹Then˺ Solomon said, “Disguise her throne for her so we may see whether she will recognize ˹it˺ or she will not be able to.”
text_en_yusufali: He said: "Transform her throne out of all recognition by her: let us see whether she is guided (to the truth) or is one of those who receive no guidance."
text_en_pickthall: He said: Disguise her throne for her that we may see whether she will go aright or be of those not rightly guided.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’Disguise her throne for her, and we shall behold whether she is guided or if she is of those that are not guided.’

text_ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَتْ قِيلَ أَهَٰكَذَا عَرْشُكِ ۖ قَالَتْ كَأَنَّهُۥ هُوَ ۚ وَأُوتِينَا ٱلْعِلْمَ مِن قَبْلِهَا وَكُنَّا مُسْلِمِينَ
text_en_primary: So when she arrived, it was said ˹to her˺, “Is your throne like this?” She replied, “It looks to be the same. We have ˹already˺ received knowledge ˹of Solomon’s prophethood˺ and have submitted ˹to Allah˺.”
text_en_yusufali: So when she arrived, she was asked, "Is this thy throne?" She said, "It was just like this; and knowledge was bestowed on us in advance of this, and we have submitted to God (in Islam)."
text_en_pickthall: So, when she came, it was said (unto her): Is thy throne like this ? She said: (It is) as though it were the very one. And (Solomon said): We were given the knowledge before her and we had surrendered (to Allah).
text_en_arberry: So, when she came, it was said, ’Is thy throne like this?’ She said, ’It seems the same.’ ’And we were given the knowledge before her, and we were in surrender,

text_ar: وَصَدَّهَا مَا كَانَت تَّعْبُدُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ مِن قَوْمٍۢ كَٰفِرِينَ
text_en_primary: But she had been hindered by what she used to worship instead of Allah, for she was indeed from a disbelieving people.
text_en_yusufali: And he diverted her from the worship of others besides God: for she was (sprung) of a people that had no faith.
text_en_pickthall: And (all) that she was wont to worship instead of Allah hindered her, for she came of disbelieving folk.
text_en_arberry: but that she served, apart from God, barred her, for she was of a people of unbelievers.’

text_ar: قِيلَ لَهَا ٱدْخُلِى ٱلصَّرْحَ ۖ فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ حَسِبَتْهُ لُجَّةًۭ وَكَشَفَتْ عَن سَاقَيْهَا ۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ صَرْحٌۭ مُّمَرَّدٌۭ مِّن قَوَارِيرَ ۗ قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِى وَأَسْلَمْتُ مَعَ سُلَيْمَٰنَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
text_en_primary: Then she was told, “Enter the palace.” But when she saw the hall, she thought it was a body of water, so she bared her legs. Solomon said. “It is just a palace paved with crystal.” ˹At last˺ she declared, “My Lord! I have certainly wronged my soul. Now I ˹fully˺ submit myself along with Solomon to Allah, the Lord of all worlds.”
text_en_yusufali: She was asked to enter the lofty Palace: but when she saw it, she thought it was a lake of water, and she (tucked up her skirts), uncovering her legs. He said: "This is but a palace paved smooth with slabs of glass." She said: "O my Lord! I have indeed wronged my soul: I do (now) submit (in Islam), with Solomon, to the Lord of the Worlds."
text_en_pickthall: It was said unto her: Enter the hall. And when she saw it she deemed it a pool and bared her legs. (Solomon) said: Lo! it is a hall, made smooth, of glass. She said: My Lord! Lo! I have wronged myself, and I surrender with Solomon unto Allah, the Lord of the Worlds.
text_en_arberry: It was said to her, ’Enter the pavilion.’ But when she saw it, she supposed it was a spreading water, and she bared her legs. He said, ’It is a pavilion smoothed of crystal. She said, ’My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I surrender with Solomon to God, the Lord of all Being.’

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَٰلِحًا أَنِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ فَإِذَا هُمْ فَرِيقَانِ يَخْتَصِمُونَ
text_en_primary: And We certainly sent to the people of Thamûd their brother salih, proclaiming, “Worship Allah,” but they suddenly split into two opposing groups.
text_en_yusufali: We sent (aforetime), to the Thamud, their brother Salih, saying, "Serve God": But behold, they became two factions quarrelling with each other.
text_en_pickthall: And We verily sent unto Thamud their brother Salih, saying: Worship Allah. And lo! they (then became two parties quarrelling.
text_en_arberry: And We sent to Thamood their brother Salih: ’Serve you God!’ And behold, they were two parties, that were disputing one with another.

text_ar: قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ لِمَ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ ۖ لَوْلَا تَسْتَغْفِرُونَ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ
text_en_primary: He urged ˹the disbelieving group˺, “O my people! Why do you ˹seek to˺ hasten the torment If only you sought Allah’s forgiveness so you may be shown mercy!”
text_en_yusufali: He said: "O my people! why ask ye to hasten on the evil in preference to the good? If only ye ask God for forgiveness, ye may hope to receive mercy.
text_en_pickthall: He said: O my people! Why will ye hasten on the evil rather than the good ? Why will ye not ask pardon of Allah, that ye may receive mercy.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’O my people, why do you seek to hasten evil before good? Why do you not ask forgiveness of God? Haply so you will find mercy.’

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ ٱطَّيَّرْنَا بِكَ وَبِمَن مَّعَكَ ۚ قَالَ طَٰٓئِرُكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ۖ بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌۭ تُفْتَنُونَ
text_en_primary: They replied, “You and your followers are a bad omen for us.” He responded, “Your omens are destined by Allah. In fact, you are ˹only˺ a people being tested.”
text_en_yusufali: They said: "Ill omen do we augur from thee and those that are with thee". He said: "Your ill omen is with God; yea, ye are a people under trial."
text_en_pickthall: They said: We augur evil of thee and those with thee. He said: Your evil augury is with Allah. Nay, but ye are folk that are being tested.
text_en_arberry: They said, ’We augur ill of thee and of those that are with thee.’ He said, ’Your augury is with God; nay, but you are a people being proved.’

text_ar: وَكَانَ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍۢ يُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا يُصْلِحُونَ
text_en_primary: And there were in the city nine ˹elite˺ men who spread corruption in the land, never doing what is right.
text_en_yusufali: There were in the city nine men of a family, who made mischief in the land, and would not reform.
text_en_pickthall: And there were in the city nine persons who made mischief in the land and reformed not.
text_en_arberry: Now in the city there were nine persons who did corruption in the land, and put not things right;

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ تَقَاسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُۥ وَأَهْلَهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَقُولَنَّ لِوَلِيِّهِۦ مَا شَهِدْنَا مَهْلِكَ أَهْلِهِۦ وَإِنَّا لَصَٰدِقُونَ
text_en_primary: They vowed, “Let us swear by Allah that we will take him and his family down by night. Then we will certainly say to his ˹closest˺ heirs, ‘We did not witness the murder of his family. We are definitely telling the truth.’”
text_en_yusufali: They said: "Swear a mutual oath by God that we shall make a secret night attack on him and his people, and that we shall then say to his heir (when he seeks vengeance): ’We were not present at the slaughter of his people, and we are positively telling the truth.’"
text_en_pickthall: They said: Swear one to another by Allah that we verily will attack him and his household by night, and afterward we will surely say unto his friend: We witnessed not the destruction of his household. And lo! we are truthtellers.
text_en_arberry: they said, ’Swear you, one to another, by God, "We will attack him and his family by night, then we will tell his protector, We were not witnesses of the destruction of his family; and assuredly we are truthful men."’

text_ar: وَمَكَرُوا۟ مَكْرًۭا وَمَكَرْنَا مَكْرًۭا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
text_en_primary: And ˹so˺ they made a plan, but We too made a plan, while they were unaware.
text_en_yusufali: They plotted and planned, but We too planned, even while they perceived it not.
text_en_pickthall: So they plotted a plot: and We plotted a plot, while they perceived not.
text_en_arberry: And they devised a device, and We likewise devised a device, while they were not aware;

text_ar: فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَٰهُمْ وَقَوْمَهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
text_en_primary: See then what the consequences of their plan were: We ˹utterly˺ destroyed them and their people all together.
text_en_yusufali: Then see what was the end of their plot!- this, that We destroyed them and their people, all (of them).
text_en_pickthall: Then see the nature of the consequence of their plotting, for lo! We destroyed them and their people, every one.
text_en_arberry: and behold, how was the end of their device! For We destroyed them and their people all together.

text_ar: فَتِلْكَ بُيُوتُهُمْ خَاوِيَةًۢ بِمَا ظَلَمُوٓا۟ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَعْلَمُونَ
text_en_primary: So their homes are there, ˹but completely˺ ruined because of their wrongdoing. Surely in this is a lesson for people of knowledge.
text_en_yusufali: Now such were their houses, - in utter ruin, - because they practised wrong- doing. Verily in this is a Sign for people of knowledge.
text_en_pickthall: See, yonder are their dwellings empty and in ruins because they did wrong. Lo! herein is indeed a portent for a people who have knowledge.
text_en_arberry: Those are their houses, all fallen down because of the evil they committed; surely in that is a sign for a people who have knowledge.

text_ar: وَأَنجَيْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ يَتَّقُونَ
text_en_primary: And We delivered those who were faithful and were mindful ˹of Allah˺.
text_en_yusufali: And We saved those who believed and practised righteousness.
text_en_pickthall: And we saved those who believed and used to ward off (evil).
text_en_arberry: And We delivered those who believed and were godfearing.

text_ar: وَلُوطًا إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَٰحِشَةَ وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ
text_en_primary: And ˹remember˺ Lot, when he rebuked ˹the men of˺ his people, “Do you commit that shameful deed while you can see ˹one another˺?
text_en_yusufali: (We also sent) Lut (as an apostle): behold, He said to his people, "Do ye do what is shameful though ye see (its iniquity)?
text_en_pickthall: And Lot! when he said unto his folk: Will ye commit abomination knowingly ?
text_en_arberry: And Lot, when he said to his people, ’What, do you commit indecency with your eyes open?

text_ar: أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلرِّجَالَ شَهْوَةًۭ مِّن دُونِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ ۚ بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌۭ تَجْهَلُونَ
text_en_primary: Do you really lust after men instead of women? In fact, you are ˹only˺ a people acting ignorantly.”
text_en_yusufali: Would ye really approach men in your lusts rather than women? Nay, ye are a people (grossly) ignorant!
text_en_pickthall: Must ye needs lust after men instead of women ? Nay, but ye are folk who act senselessly.
text_en_arberry: What, do you approach men lustfully instead of women? No, you are a people that are ignorant.’

text_ar: ۞ فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوٓا۟ أَخْرِجُوٓا۟ ءَالَ لُوطٍۢ مِّن قَرْيَتِكُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌۭ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ
text_en_primary: But his people’s only response was to say, “Expel Lot’s followers from your land! They are a people who wish to remain chaste!”
text_en_yusufali: But his people gave no other answer but this: they said, "Drive out the followers of Lut from your city: these are indeed men who want to be clean and pure!"
text_en_pickthall: But the answer of his folk was naught save that they said: Expel the household of Lot from your township, for they (forsooth) are folk who would keep clean!
text_en_arberry: And the only answer of his people was that they said, ’Expel the folk of Lot from your city; they are men that keep themselves clean!’

text_ar: فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُۥ قَدَّرْنَٰهَا مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ
text_en_primary: So We delivered him and his family, except his wife. We had destined her to be one of the doomed.
text_en_yusufali: But We saved him and his family, except his wife; her We destined to be of those who lagged behind.
text_en_pickthall: Then We saved him and his household save his wife; We destined her to be of those who stayed behind.
text_en_arberry: So We delivered him and his family, except his wife; We decreed she should be of those that tarried.

text_ar: وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًۭا ۖ فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
text_en_primary: And We poured upon them a rain ˹of brimstone˺. How evil was the rain of those who had been warned!
text_en_yusufali: And We rained down on them a shower (of brimstone): and evil was the shower on those who were admonished (but heeded not)!
text_en_pickthall: And We rained a rain upon them. Dreadful is the rain of those who have been warned.
text_en_arberry: And We rained on them a rain; and evil indeed is the rain of them that are warned.

text_ar: قُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَسَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ عِبَادِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَىٰٓ ۗ ءَآللَّهُ خَيْرٌ أَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
text_en_primary: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Praise be to Allah, and peace be upon the servants He has chosen.” ˹Ask the disbelievers,˺ “Which is better: Allah or whatever ˹gods˺ they associate ˹with Him˺?”
text_en_yusufali: Say: Praise be to God, and Peace on his servants whom He has chosen (for his Message). (Who) is better?- God or the false gods they associate (with Him)?
text_en_pickthall: Say (O Muhammad): Praise be to Allah, and peace be on His slaves whom He hath chosen! Is Allah best, or (all) that ye ascribe as partners (unto Him) ?
text_en_arberry: Say: ’Praise belongs to God, and peace be on His servants whom He has chosen.’ What, is God better, or that they associate?

text_ar: أَمَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ فَأَنۢبَتْنَا بِهِۦ حَدَآئِقَ ذَاتَ بَهْجَةٍۢ مَّا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَن تُنۢبِتُوا۟ شَجَرَهَآ ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌۭ يَعْدِلُونَ
text_en_primary: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who created the heavens and the earth, and sends down rain for you from the sky, by which We cause delightful gardens to grow? You could never cause their trees to grow. Was it another god besides Allah?” Absolutely not! But they are a people who set up equals ˹to Allah˺!
text_en_yusufali: Or, Who has created the heavens and the earth, and Who sends you down rain from the sky? Yea, with it We cause to grow well-planted orchards full of beauty of delight: it is not in your power to cause the growth of the trees in them. (Can there be another) god besides God? Nay, they are a people who swerve from justice.
text_en_pickthall: Is not He (best) Who created the heavens and the earth, and sendeth down for you water from the sky wherewith We cause to spring forth joyous orchards, whose trees it never hath been yours to cause to grow. Is there any God beside Allah ? Nay, but they are folk who ascribe equals (unto Him)!
text_en_arberry: He who created the heavens and earth, and sent down for you out of heaven water; and We caused to grow therewith gardens full of loveliness whose trees you could never grow. Is there a god with God? Nay, but they are a people who assign to Him equals!

text_ar: أَمَّن جَعَلَ ٱلْأَرْضَ قَرَارًۭا وَجَعَلَ خِلَٰلَهَآ أَنْهَٰرًۭا وَجَعَلَ لَهَا رَوَٰسِىَ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ حَاجِزًا ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
text_en_primary: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who made the earth a place of settlement, caused rivers to flow through it, placed firm mountains upon it, and set a barrier between ˹fresh and salt˺ bodies of water? Was it another god besides Allah?” Absolutely not! But most of them do not know.
text_en_yusufali: Or, Who has made the earth firm to live in; made rivers in its midst; set thereon mountains immovable; and made a separating bar between the two bodies of flowing water? (can there be another) god besides God? Nay, most of them know not.
text_en_pickthall: Is not He (best) Who made the earth a fixed abode, and placed rivers in the folds thereof, and placed firm hills therein, and hath set a barrier between the two seas ? Is there any God beside Allah ? Nay, but most of them know not!
text_en_arberry: He who made the earth a fixed place and set amidst it rivers and appointed for it firm mountains and placed a partition between the two seas. Is there a god with God? Nay, but the most of them have no knowledge.

text_ar: أَمَّن يُجِيبُ ٱلْمُضْطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَيَكْشِفُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَيَجْعَلُكُمْ خُلَفَآءَ ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ قَلِيلًۭا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ
text_en_primary: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who responds to the distressed when they cry to Him, relieving ˹their˺ affliction, and ˹Who˺ makes you successors in the earth? Is it another god besides Allah? Yet you are hardly mindful!”
text_en_yusufali: Or, Who listens to the (soul) distressed when it calls on Him, and Who relieves its suffering, and makes you (mankind) inheritors of the earth? (Can there be another) god besides God? Little it is that ye heed!
text_en_pickthall: Is not He (best) Who answereth the wronged one when he crieth unto Him and removeth the evil, and hath made you viceroys of the earth ? Is there any God beside Allah ? Little do they reflect!
text_en_arberry: He who answers the constrained, when he calls unto Him, and removes the evil and appoints you to be successors in the earth. Is there a god with God? Little indeed do you remember.

text_ar: أَمَّن يَهْدِيكُمْ فِى ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ وَمَن يُرْسِلُ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ بُشْرًۢا بَيْنَ يَدَىْ رَحْمَتِهِۦٓ ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ تَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
text_en_primary: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who guides you in the darkness of the land and sea, Is it another god besides Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate ˹with Him˺!
text_en_yusufali: Or, Who guides you through the depths of darkness on land and sea, and Who sends the winds as heralds of glad tidings, going before His Mercy? (Can there be another) god besides God?- High is God above what they associate with Him!
text_en_pickthall: Is not He (best) Who guideth you in the darkness of the land and the sea, He Who sendeth the winds as heralds of His mercy ? Is there any God beside Allah ? High Exalted be Allah from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)!
text_en_arberry: He who guides you in the shadows of the land and the sea and looses the winds, bearing good tidings before His mercy. Is there a god with God? High exalted be God, above that which they associate!

text_ar: أَمَّن يَبْدَؤُا۟ ٱلْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُۥ وَمَن يَرْزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ أَءِلَٰهٌۭ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ قُلْ هَاتُوا۟ بُرْهَٰنَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
text_en_primary: Or ˹ask them,˺ “Who originates the creation then resurrects it, and gives you provisions from the heavens and the earth? Is it another god besides Allah?” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Show ˹me˺ your proof, if what you say is true.”
text_en_yusufali: Or, Who originates creation, then repeats it, and who gives you sustenance from heaven and earth? (Can there be another) god besides God? Say, "Bring forth your argument, if ye are telling the truth!"
text_en_pickthall: Is not He (best) Who produceth creation, then reproduceth it, and Who provideth for you from the heaven and the earth ? Is there any God beside Allah ? Say: Bring your proof, if ye are truthful!
text_en_arberry: Who originates creation, then brings it back again, and provides you out of heaven and earth. Is there a god with God? Say: ’Produce your proof, if you speak truly.’

text_ar: قُل لَّا يَعْلَمُ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْغَيْبَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ ۚ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ
text_en_primary: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “None in the heavens and the earth has knowledge of the unseen except Allah. Nor do they know when they will be resurrected.
text_en_yusufali: Say: None in the heavens or on earth, except God, knows what is hidden: nor can they perceive when they shall be raised up (for Judgment).
text_en_pickthall: Say (O Muhammad): None in the heavens and the earth knoweth the Unseen save Allah; and they know not when they will be raised (again).
text_en_arberry: Say: ’None knows the Unseen in the heavens and earth except God. And they are not aware when they shall be raised;

text_ar: بَلِ ٱدَّٰرَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ ۚ بَلْ هُمْ فِى شَكٍّۢ مِّنْهَا ۖ بَلْ هُم مِّنْهَا عَمُونَ
text_en_primary: No! Their knowledge of the Hereafter amounts to ignorance. In fact, they are in doubt about it. In truth, they are ˹totally˺ blind to it.
text_en_yusufali: Still less can their knowledge comprehend the Hereafter: Nay, they are in doubt and uncertainty thereanent; nay, they are blind thereunto!
text_en_pickthall: Nay, but doth their knowledge reach to the Hereafter ? Nay, for they are in doubt concerning it. Nay, for they cannot see it.
text_en_arberry: nay, but their knowledge fails as to the Hereafter; nay, they are in doubt of it; nay, they are blind to it.

text_ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَءِذَا كُنَّا تُرَٰبًۭا وَءَابَآؤُنَآ أَئِنَّا لَمُخْرَجُونَ
text_en_primary: The disbelievers ask, “When we and our fathers are reduced to dust, will we really be brought forth ˹alive˺?
text_en_yusufali: The Unbelievers say: "What! when we become dust,- we and our fathers,- shall we really be raised (from the dead)?
text_en_pickthall: Yet those who disbelieve say: When we have become dust like our fathers, shall we verily be brought forth (again) ?
text_en_arberry: The unbelievers say, ’What, when we are dust, and our fathers, shall we indeed be brought forth?

text_ar: لَقَدْ وُعِدْنَا هَٰذَا نَحْنُ وَءَابَآؤُنَا مِن قَبْلُ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
text_en_primary: We have already been promised this, as well as our forefathers earlier. This is nothing but ancient fables!”
text_en_yusufali: "It is true we were promised this,- we and our fathers before (us): these are nothing but tales of the ancients."
text_en_pickthall: We were promised this, forsooth, we and our fathers. (All) this is naught but fables of the men of old.
text_en_arberry: We have been promised this, and our fathers before; this is naught but the fairy-tales of the ancients.’

text_ar: قُلْ سِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
text_en_primary: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Travel throughout the land and see the fate of the wicked.”
text_en_yusufali: Say: "Go ye through the earth and see what has been the end of those guilty (of sin)."
text_en_pickthall: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Travel in the land and see the nature of the sequel for the guilty!
text_en_arberry: Say: ’Journey in the land, then behold how was the end of the sinners.’

text_ar: وَلَا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا تَكُن فِى ضَيْقٍۢ مِّمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ
text_en_primary: Do not grieve for them, nor be distressed by their schemes.
text_en_yusufali: But grieve not over them, nor distress thyself because of their plots.
text_en_pickthall: And grieve thou not for them, nor be in distress because of what they plot (against thee).
text_en_arberry: Do not sorrow for them, nor be thou straitened for what they devise.

text_ar: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
text_en_primary: They ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass, if what you say is true?”
text_en_yusufali: They also say: "When will this promise (come to pass)? (Say) if ye are truthful."
text_en_pickthall: And they say: When (will) this promise (be fulfilled), if ye are truthful ?
text_en_arberry: They say, ’When shall this promise come to pass, if you speak the truth?’
