text_ar: بَيْضَآءَ لَذَّةٍۢ لِّلشَّٰرِبِينَ
text_en_primary: crystal-white, delicious to drink.
text_en_yusufali: Crystal-white, of a taste delicious to those who drink (thereof),
text_en_pickthall: White, delicious to the drinkers,
text_en_arberry: white, a delight to the drinkers,

text_ar: لَا فِيهَا غَوْلٌۭ وَلَا هُمْ عَنْهَا يُنزَفُونَ
text_en_primary: It will neither harm ˹them˺, nor will they be intoxicated by it.
text_en_yusufali: Free from headiness; nor will they suffer intoxication therefrom.
text_en_pickthall: Wherein there is no headache nor are they made mad thereby.
text_en_arberry: wherein no sickness is, neither intoxication;

text_ar: وَعِندَهُمْ قَٰصِرَٰتُ ٱلطَّرْفِ عِينٌۭ
text_en_primary: And with them will be maidens of modest gaze and gorgeous eyes,
text_en_yusufali: And besides them will be chaste women, restraining their glances, with big eyes (of wonder and beauty).
text_en_pickthall: And with them are those of modest gaze, with lovely eyes,
text_en_arberry: and with them wide-eyed maidens restraining their glances

text_ar: كَأَنَّهُنَّ بَيْضٌۭ مَّكْنُونٌۭ
text_en_primary: as if they were pristine pearls.
text_en_yusufali: As if they were (delicate) eggs closely guarded.
text_en_pickthall: (Pure) as they were hidden eggs (of the ostrich).
text_en_arberry: as if they were hidden pearls.

text_ar: فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
text_en_primary: Then they will turn to one another inquisitively.
text_en_yusufali: Then they will turn to one another and question one another.
text_en_pickthall: And some of them draw near unto others, mutually questioning.
text_en_arberry: They advance one upon another, asking each other questions.

text_ar: قَالَ قَآئِلٌۭ مِّنْهُمْ إِنِّى كَانَ لِى قَرِينٌۭ
text_en_primary: One of them will say, “I once had a companion ˹in the world˺
text_en_yusufali: One of them will start the talk and say: "I had an intimate companion (on the earth),
text_en_pickthall: A speaker of them saith: Lo! I had a comrade
text_en_arberry: One of them says, ’I had a comrade

text_ar: يَقُولُ أَءِنَّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُصَدِّقِينَ
text_en_primary: who used to ask ˹me˺, ‘Do you actually believe ˹in resurrection˺?
text_en_yusufali: "Who used to say, ’what! art thou amongst those who bear witness to the Truth (of the Message)?
text_en_pickthall: Who used to say: Art thou in truth of those who put faith (in his words) ?
text_en_arberry: who would say, "Are you a confirmer?

text_ar: أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًۭا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَدِينُونَ
text_en_primary: When we are dead and reduced to dust and bones, will we really be brought to judgment?’”
text_en_yusufali: "’When we die and become dust and bones, shall we indeed receive rewards and punishments?’"
text_en_pickthall: Can we, when we are dead and have become mere dust and bones - can we (then) verily be brought to book ?
text_en_arberry: What, when we are dead and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be requited?"

text_ar: قَالَ هَلْ أَنتُم مُّطَّلِعُونَ
text_en_primary: He will ˹then˺ ask, “Would you care to see ˹his fate˺?”
text_en_yusufali: (A voice) said: "Would ye like to look down?"
text_en_pickthall: He saith: Will ye look ?
text_en_arberry: He says, ’Are you looking down?’

text_ar: فَٱطَّلَعَ فَرَءَاهُ فِى سَوَآءِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
text_en_primary: Then he ˹and the others˺ will look and spot him in the midst of the Hellfire.
text_en_yusufali: He looked down and saw him in the midst of the Fire.
text_en_pickthall: Then looketh he and seeth him in the depth of hell.
text_en_arberry: Then he looks, and sees him in the midst of Hell.

text_ar: قَالَ تَٱللَّهِ إِن كِدتَّ لَتُرْدِينِ
text_en_primary: He will ˹then˺ say, “By Allah! You nearly ruined me.
text_en_yusufali: He said: "By God! thou wast little short of bringing me to perdition!
text_en_pickthall: He saith: By Allah, thou verily didst all but cause my ruin,
text_en_arberry: He says, ’By God, wellnigh thou didst destroy me;

text_ar: وَلَوْلَا نِعْمَةُ رَبِّى لَكُنتُ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْضَرِينَ
text_en_primary: Had it not been for the grace of my Lord, I ˹too˺ would have certainly been among those brought ˹to Hell˺.”
text_en_yusufali: "Had it not been for the Grace of my Lord, I should certainly have been among those brought (there)!
text_en_pickthall: And had it not been for the favour of my Lord, I too had been of those haled forth (to doom).
text_en_arberry: But for my Lord’s blessing, I were one of the arraigned.

text_ar: أَفَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَيِّتِينَ
text_en_primary: ˹Then he will ask his fellow believers,˺ “Can you imagine that we will never die,
text_en_yusufali: "Is it (the case) that we shall not die,
text_en_pickthall: Are we then not to die
text_en_arberry: What, do we then not die

text_ar: إِلَّا مَوْتَتَنَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ
text_en_primary: except our first death, nor be punished ˹like the others˺?”
text_en_yusufali: "Except our first death, and that we shall not be punished?"
text_en_pickthall: Saving our former death, and are we not to be punished ?
text_en_arberry: except for our first death, and are we not chastised?

text_ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
text_en_primary: This is truly the ultimate triumph.
text_en_yusufali: Verily this is the supreme achievement!
text_en_pickthall: Lo! this is the supreme triumph.
text_en_arberry: This is indeed the mighty triumph,

text_ar: لِمِثْلِ هَٰذَا فَلْيَعْمَلِ ٱلْعَٰمِلُونَ
text_en_primary: For such ˹honour˺ all should strive.
text_en_yusufali: For the like of this let all strive, who wish to strive.
text_en_pickthall: For the like of this, then, let the workers work.
text_en_arberry: for the like of this let the workers work.’

text_ar: أَذَٰلِكَ خَيْرٌۭ نُّزُلًا أَمْ شَجَرَةُ ٱلزَّقُّومِ
text_en_primary: Is this ˹bliss˺ a better accommodation or the tree of Zaqqûm?
text_en_yusufali: Is that the better entertainment or the Tree of Zaqqum?
text_en_pickthall: Is this better as a welcome, or the tree of Zaqqum ?
text_en_arberry: Is that better as a hospitality, or the Tree of Ez-Zakkoum?

text_ar: إِنَّا جَعَلْنَٰهَا فِتْنَةًۭ لِّلظَّٰلِمِينَ
text_en_primary: We have surely made it a test for the wrongdoers.
text_en_yusufali: For We have truly made it (as) a trial for the wrong-doers.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! We have appointed it a torment for wrong-doers.
text_en_arberry: We have appointed it as a trial for the evildoers.

text_ar: إِنَّهَا شَجَرَةٌۭ تَخْرُجُ فِىٓ أَصْلِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
text_en_primary: Indeed, it is a tree that grows in the depths of Hell,
text_en_yusufali: For it is a tree that springs out of the bottom of Hell-Fire:
text_en_pickthall: Lo! it is a tree that springeth in the heart of hell.
text_en_arberry: It is a tree that comes forth in the root of Hell;

text_ar: طَلْعُهَا كَأَنَّهُۥ رُءُوسُ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينِ
text_en_primary: bearing fruit like devils’ heads.
text_en_yusufali: The shoots of its fruit-stalks are like the heads of devils:
text_en_pickthall: Its crop is as it were the heads of devils
text_en_arberry: its spathes are as the heads of Satans,

text_ar: فَإِنَّهُمْ لَءَاكِلُونَ مِنْهَا فَمَالِـُٔونَ مِنْهَا ٱلْبُطُونَ
text_en_primary: The evildoers will certainly ˹be left to˺ eat from it, filling up their bellies with it.
text_en_yusufali: Truly they will eat thereof and fill their bellies therewith.
text_en_pickthall: And lo! they verily must eat thereof, and fill (their) bellies therewith.
text_en_arberry: and they eat of it, and of it fill their bellies,

text_ar: ثُمَّ إِنَّ لَهُمْ عَلَيْهَا لَشَوْبًۭا مِّنْ حَمِيمٍۢ
text_en_primary: Then on top of that they will be given a blend of boiling drink.
text_en_yusufali: Then on top of that they will be given a mixture made of boiling water.
text_en_pickthall: And afterward, lo! thereupon they have a drink of boiling water
text_en_arberry: then on top of it they have a brew of boiling water,

text_ar: ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَرْجِعَهُمْ لَإِلَى ٱلْجَحِيمِ
text_en_primary: Then they will ultimately return to ˹their place in˺ Hell.
text_en_yusufali: Then shall their return be to the (Blazing) Fire.
text_en_pickthall: And afterward, lo! their return is surely unto hell.
text_en_arberry: then their return is unto Hell.

text_ar: إِنَّهُمْ أَلْفَوْا۟ ءَابَآءَهُمْ ضَآلِّينَ
text_en_primary: Indeed, they found their forefathers astray,
text_en_yusufali: Truly they found their fathers on the wrong Path;
text_en_pickthall: They indeed found their fathers astray,
text_en_arberry: They found their fathers erring,

text_ar: فَهُمْ عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ
text_en_primary: so they rushed in their footsteps!
text_en_yusufali: So they (too) were rushed down on their footsteps!
text_en_pickthall: But they make haste (to follow) in their footsteps.
text_en_arberry: and they run in their footsteps.

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ ضَلَّ قَبْلَهُمْ أَكْثَرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
text_en_primary: And surely most of the earlier generations had strayed before them,
text_en_yusufali: And truly before them, many of the ancients went astray;-
text_en_pickthall: And verily most of the men of old went astray before them,
text_en_arberry: Before them erred most of the ancients,

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا فِيهِم مُّنذِرِينَ
text_en_primary: although We had certainly sent warners among them.
text_en_yusufali: But We sent aforetime, among them, (apostles) to admonish them;-
text_en_pickthall: And verily We sent among them warners.
text_en_arberry: and We sent among them warners;

text_ar: فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
text_en_primary: See then what was the end of those who had been warned.
text_en_yusufali: Then see what was the end of those who were admonished (but heeded not),-
text_en_pickthall: Then see the nature of the consequence for those warned,
text_en_arberry: and behold, how was the end of them that were warned,

text_ar: إِلَّا عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
text_en_primary: But not the chosen servants of Allah.
text_en_yusufali: Except the sincere (and devoted) Servants of God.
text_en_pickthall: Save single-minded slaves of Allah.
text_en_arberry: except for God’s sincere servants.

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ نَادَىٰنَا نُوحٌۭ فَلَنِعْمَ ٱلْمُجِيبُونَ
text_en_primary: Indeed, Noah cried out to Us, and how excellent are We in responding!
text_en_yusufali: (In the days of old), Noah cried to Us, and We are the best to hear prayer.
text_en_pickthall: And Noah verily prayed unto Us, and gracious was the Hearer of his prayer
text_en_arberry: Noah called to Us; and how excellent were the Answerers!

text_ar: وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
text_en_primary: We delivered him and his family from the great distress,
text_en_yusufali: And We delivered him and his people from the Great Calamity,
text_en_pickthall: And We saved him and his household from the great distress,
text_en_arberry: And We delivered him and his people from the great distress,

text_ar: وَجَعَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُۥ هُمُ ٱلْبَاقِينَ
text_en_primary: and made his descendants the sole survivors.
text_en_yusufali: And made his progeny to endure (on this earth);
text_en_pickthall: And made his seed the survivors,
text_en_arberry: and We made his seed the survivors,

text_ar: وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
text_en_primary: And We blessed him ˹with honourable mention˺ among later generations:
text_en_yusufali: And We left (this blessing) for him among generations to come in later times:
text_en_pickthall: And left for him among the later folk (the salutation):
text_en_arberry: and left for him among the later folk

text_ar: سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ نُوحٍۢ فِى ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
text_en_primary: “Peace be upon Noah among all peoples.”
text_en_yusufali: "Peace and salutation to Noah among the nations!"
text_en_pickthall: Peace be unto Noah among the peoples!
text_en_arberry: ’Peace be upon Noah among all beings!’

text_ar: إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
text_en_primary: Indeed, this is how We reward the good-doers.
text_en_yusufali: Thus indeed do we reward those who do right.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! thus do We reward the good.
text_en_arberry: Even so We recompense the good-doers;

text_ar: إِنَّهُۥ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
text_en_primary: ˹For˺ he was truly one of Our faithful servants.
text_en_yusufali: For he was one of our believing Servants.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! he is one of Our believing slaves.
text_en_arberry: he was among Our believing servants.

text_ar: ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ
text_en_primary: Then We drowned the others.
text_en_yusufali: Then the rest we overwhelmed in the Flood.
text_en_pickthall: Then We did drown the others.
text_en_arberry: Then afterwards We drowned the rest.

text_ar: ۞ وَإِنَّ مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ لَإِبْرَٰهِيمَ
text_en_primary: And indeed, one of those who followed his way was Abraham.
text_en_yusufali: Verily among those who followed his Way was Abraham.
text_en_pickthall: And lo! of his persuasion verily was Abraham
text_en_arberry: Of his party was also Abraham;

text_ar: إِذْ جَآءَ رَبَّهُۥ بِقَلْبٍۢ سَلِيمٍ
text_en_primary: ˹Remember˺ when he came to his Lord with a pure heart,
text_en_yusufali: Behold! he approached his Lord with a sound heart.
text_en_pickthall: When he came unto his Lord with a whole heart;
text_en_arberry: when he came unto his Lord with a pure heart,

text_ar: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَاذَا تَعْبُدُونَ
text_en_primary: and said to his father and his people, “What are you worshipping?
text_en_yusufali: Behold! he said to his father and to his people, "What is that which ye worship?
text_en_pickthall: When he said unto his father and his folk: What is it that ye worship ?
text_en_arberry: when he said to his father and his folk, ’What do you serve?

text_ar: أَئِفْكًا ءَالِهَةًۭ دُونَ ٱللَّهِ تُرِيدُونَ
text_en_primary: Is it false gods that you desire instead of Allah?
text_en_yusufali: "Is it a falsehood- gods other than God- that ye desire?
text_en_pickthall: Is it a falsehood - gods beside Allah - that ye desire ?
text_en_arberry: Is it a calumny, gods apart from God, that you desire?

text_ar: فَمَا ظَنُّكُم بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
text_en_primary: What then do you expect from the Lord of all worlds?”
text_en_yusufali: "Then what is your idea about the Lord of the worlds?"
text_en_pickthall: What then is your opinion of the Lord of the Worlds ?
text_en_arberry: What think you then of the Lord of all Being?’

text_ar: فَنَظَرَ نَظْرَةًۭ فِى ٱلنُّجُومِ
text_en_primary: He later looked up to the stars ˹in contemplation˺,
text_en_yusufali: Then did he cast a glance at the Stars.
text_en_pickthall: And he glanced a glance at the stars
text_en_arberry: And he cast a glance at the stars,

text_ar: فَقَالَ إِنِّى سَقِيمٌۭ
text_en_primary: then said, “I am really sick.”
text_en_yusufali: And he said, "I am indeed sick (at heart)!"
text_en_pickthall: Then said: Lo! I feel sick!
text_en_arberry: and he said, ’Surely I am sick.’

text_ar: فَتَوَلَّوْا۟ عَنْهُ مُدْبِرِينَ
text_en_primary: So they turned their backs on him and went away.
text_en_yusufali: So they turned away from him, and departed.
text_en_pickthall: And they turned their backs and went away from him.
text_en_arberry: But they went away from him, turning their backs.

text_ar: فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ ءَالِهَتِهِمْ فَقَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ
text_en_primary: Then he ˹stealthily˺ advanced towards their gods, and said ˹mockingly˺, “Will you not eat ˹your offerings˺?
text_en_yusufali: Then did he turn to their gods and said, "will ye not eat (of the offerings before you)?...
text_en_pickthall: Then turned he to their gods and said: Will ye not eat ?
text_en_arberry: Then he turned to their gods, and said, ’What do you eat?

text_ar: مَا لَكُمْ لَا تَنطِقُونَ
text_en_primary: What is wrong with you that you cannot speak?”
text_en_yusufali: "What is the matter with you that ye speak not (intelligently)?"
text_en_pickthall: What aileth you that ye speak not ?
text_en_arberry: What ails you, that you speak not?’

text_ar: فَرَاغَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضَرْبًۢا بِٱلْيَمِينِ
text_en_primary: Then he swiftly turned on them, striking ˹them˺ with his right hand.
text_en_yusufali: Then did he turn upon them, striking (them) with the right hand.
text_en_pickthall: Then he attacked them, striking with his right hand.
text_en_arberry: And he turned upon them smiting them with his right hand.

text_ar: فَأَقْبَلُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ يَزِفُّونَ
text_en_primary: Later, his people came rushing towards him ˹furiously˺.
text_en_yusufali: Then came (the worshippers) with hurried steps, and faced (him).
text_en_pickthall: And (his people) came toward him, hastening.
text_en_arberry: Then came the others to him hastening.

text_ar: قَالَ أَتَعْبُدُونَ مَا تَنْحِتُونَ
text_en_primary: He argued, “How can you worship what you carve ˹with your own hands˺,
text_en_yusufali: He said: "Worship ye that which ye have (yourselves) carved?
text_en_pickthall: He said: Worship ye that which ye yourselves do carve
text_en_arberry: He said, ’Do you serve what you hew,

text_ar: وَٱللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
text_en_primary: when it is Allah Who created you and whatever you do?”
text_en_yusufali: "But God has created you and your handwork!"
text_en_pickthall: When Allah hath created you and what ye make ?
text_en_arberry: and God created you and what you make?’

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ ٱبْنُوا۟ لَهُۥ بُنْيَٰنًۭا فَأَلْقُوهُ فِى ٱلْجَحِيمِ
text_en_primary: They said ˹to one another˺, “Build him a furnace and cast him into the blazing fire.”
text_en_yusufali: They said, "Build him a furnace, and throw him into the blazing fire!"
text_en_pickthall: They said: Build for him a building and fling him in the red- hotfire.
text_en_arberry: They said, ’Build him a building, and cast him into the furnace!’

text_ar: فَأَرَادُوا۟ بِهِۦ كَيْدًۭا فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ
text_en_primary: And so they sought to harm him, but We made them inferior.
text_en_yusufali: (This failing), they then sought a stratagem against him, but We made them the ones most humiliated!
text_en_pickthall: And they designed a snare for him, but We made them the undermost.
text_en_arberry: They desired to outwit him; so We made them the lower ones.

text_ar: وَقَالَ إِنِّى ذَاهِبٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ
text_en_primary: He later said, “I am leaving ˹in obedience˺ to my Lord. He will guide me.
text_en_yusufali: He said: "I will go to my Lord! He will surely guide me!
text_en_pickthall: And he said: Lo! I am going unto my Lord Who will guide me.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’I am going to my Lord; He will guide me.

text_ar: رَبِّ هَبْ لِى مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
text_en_primary: My Lord! Bless me with righteous offspring.”
text_en_yusufali: "O my Lord! Grant me a righteous (son)!"
text_en_pickthall: My Lord! Vouchsafe me of the righteous.
text_en_arberry: My Lord, give me one of the righteous.’

text_ar: فَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ حَلِيمٍۢ
text_en_primary: So We gave him good news of a forbearing son.
text_en_yusufali: So We gave him the good news of a boy ready to suffer and forbear.
text_en_pickthall: So We gave him tidings of a gentle son.
text_en_arberry: Then We gave him the good tidings of a prudent boy;

text_ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْىَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ فِى ٱلْمَنَامِ أَنِّىٓ أَذْبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ ۚ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ ۖ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
text_en_primary: Then when the boy reached the age to work with him, Abraham said, “O my dear son! I have seen in a dream that I ˹must˺ sacrifice you. So tell me what you think.” He replied, “O my dear father! Do as you are commanded. Allah willing, you will find me steadfast.”
text_en_yusufali: Then, when (the son) reached (the age of) (serious) work with him, he said: "O my son! I see in vision that I offer thee in sacrifice: Now see what is thy view!" (The son) said: "O my father! Do as thou art commanded: thou will find me, if God so wills one practising Patience and Constancy!"
text_en_pickthall: And when (his son) was old enough to walk with him, (Abraham) said: O my dear son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee. So look, what thinkest thou ? He said: O my father! Do that which thou art commanded. Allah willing, thou shalt find me of the steadfast.
text_en_arberry: and when he had reached the age of running with him, he said, ’My son, I see in a dream that I shall sacrifice thee; consider, what thinkest thou?’ He said, ’My father, do as thou art bidden; thou shalt find me, God willing, one of the steadfast.’

text_ar: فَلَمَّآ أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُۥ لِلْجَبِينِ
text_en_primary: Then when they submitted ˹to Allah’s Will˺, and Abraham laid him on the side of his forehead ˹for sacrifice˺,
text_en_yusufali: So when they had both submitted their wills (to God), and he had laid him prostrate on his forehead (for sacrifice),
text_en_pickthall: Then, when they had both surrendered (to Allah), and he had flung him down upon his face,
text_en_arberry: When they had surrendered, and he flung him upon his brow,

text_ar: وَنَٰدَيْنَٰهُ أَن يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ
text_en_primary: We called out to him, “O Abraham!
text_en_yusufali: We called out to him "O Abraham!
text_en_pickthall: We called unto him: O Abraham!
text_en_arberry: We called unto him, ’Abraham,

text_ar: قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ ٱلرُّءْيَآ ۚ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
text_en_primary: You have already fulfilled the vision.” Indeed, this is how We reward the good-doers.
text_en_yusufali: "Thou hast already fulfilled the vision!" - thus indeed do We reward those who do right.
text_en_pickthall: Thou hast already fulfilled the vision. Lo! thus do We reward the good.
text_en_arberry: thou hast confirmed the vision; even so We recompense the good-doers.

text_ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْبَلَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْمُبِينُ
text_en_primary: That was truly a revealing test.
text_en_yusufali: For this was obviously a trial-
text_en_pickthall: Lo! that verily was a clear test.
text_en_arberry: This is indeed the manifest trial.’

text_ar: وَفَدَيْنَٰهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍۢ
text_en_primary: And We ransomed his son with a great sacrifice,
text_en_yusufali: And We ransomed him with a momentous sacrifice:
text_en_pickthall: Then We ransomed him with a tremendous victim.
text_en_arberry: And We ransomed him with a mighty sacrifice,

text_ar: وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
text_en_primary: and blessed Abraham ˹with honourable mention˺ among later generations:
text_en_yusufali: And We left (this blessing) for him among generations (to come) in later times:
text_en_pickthall: And We left for him among the later folk (the salutation):
text_en_arberry: and left for him among the later folk

text_ar: سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
text_en_primary: “Peace be upon Abraham.”
text_en_yusufali: "Peace and salutation to Abraham!"
text_en_pickthall: Peace be unto Abraham!
text_en_arberry: ’Peace be upon Abraham!’

text_ar: كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
text_en_primary: This is how We reward the good-doers.
text_en_yusufali: Thus indeed do We reward those who do right.
text_en_pickthall: Thus do We reward the good.
text_en_arberry: Even so We recompense the good-doers;

text_ar: إِنَّهُۥ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
text_en_primary: He was truly one of Our faithful servants.
text_en_yusufali: For he was one of our believing Servants.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! he is one of Our believing slaves.
text_en_arberry: he was among Our believing servants.

text_ar: وَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِإِسْحَٰقَ نَبِيًّۭا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
text_en_primary: We ˹later˺ gave him good news of Isaac—a prophet, and one of the righteous.
text_en_yusufali: And We gave him the good news of Isaac - a prophet,- one of the Righteous.
text_en_pickthall: And we gave him tidings of the birth of Isaac, a prophet of the righteous.
text_en_arberry: Then We gave him the good tidings of Isaac, a Prophet, one of the righteous.

text_ar: وَبَٰرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَىٰٓ إِسْحَٰقَ ۚ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحْسِنٌۭ وَظَالِمٌۭ لِّنَفْسِهِۦ مُبِينٌۭ
text_en_primary: We blessed him and Isaac as well. Some of their descendants did good, while others clearly wronged themselves.
text_en_yusufali: We blessed him and Isaac: but of their progeny are (some) that do right, and (some) that obviously do wrong, to their own souls.
text_en_pickthall: And We blessed him and Isaac. And of their seed are some who do good, and some who plainly wrong themselves.
text_en_arberry: And We blessed him, and Isaac; and of their seed some are good-doers, and some manifest self-wrongers.

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ
text_en_primary: And We certainly showed favour to Moses and Aaron,
text_en_yusufali: Again (of old) We bestowed Our favour on Moses and Aaron,
text_en_pickthall: And We verily gave grace unto Moses and Aaron,
text_en_arberry: We also favoured Moses and Aaron,

text_ar: وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُمَا وَقَوْمَهُمَا مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
text_en_primary: and delivered them and their people from the great distress.
text_en_yusufali: And We delivered them and their people from (their) Great Calamity;
text_en_pickthall: And saved them and their people from the great distress,
text_en_arberry: and We delivered them and their people from the great distress.

text_ar: وَنَصَرْنَٰهُمْ فَكَانُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ
text_en_primary: We helped them so it was they who prevailed.
text_en_yusufali: And We helped them, so they overcame (their troubles);
text_en_pickthall: And helped them so that they became the victors.
text_en_arberry: And We helped them, so that they were the victors;

text_ar: وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُمَا ٱلْكِتَٰبَ ٱلْمُسْتَبِينَ
text_en_primary: We gave them the clear Scripture,
text_en_yusufali: And We gave them the Book which helps to make things clear;
text_en_pickthall: And We gave them the clear Scripture
text_en_arberry: and We gave them the Manifesting Book,

text_ar: وَهَدَيْنَٰهُمَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ
text_en_primary: and guided them to the Straight Path.
text_en_yusufali: And We guided them to the Straight Way.
text_en_pickthall: And showed them the right path.
text_en_arberry: and guided them in the straight path,

text_ar: وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِمَا فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
text_en_primary: And We blessed them ˹with honourable mention˺ among later generations:
text_en_yusufali: And We left (this blessing) for them among generations (to come) in later times:
text_en_pickthall: And We left for them among the later folk (the salutation):
text_en_arberry: and left for them among the later folk

text_ar: سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ
text_en_primary: “Peace be upon Moses and Aaron.”
text_en_yusufali: "Peace and salutation to Moses and Aaron!"
text_en_pickthall: Peace be unto Moses and Aaron!
text_en_arberry: ’Peace be upon Moses and, Aaron!’

text_ar: إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
text_en_primary: Indeed, this is how We reward the good-doers.
text_en_yusufali: Thus indeed do We reward those who do right.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! thus do We reward the good.
text_en_arberry: Even so We recompense the good-doers;

text_ar: إِنَّهُمَا مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
text_en_primary: They were truly ˹two˺ of Our faithful servants.
text_en_yusufali: For they were two of our believing Servants.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! they are two of Our believing slaves.
text_en_arberry: they were among Our believing servants.

text_ar: وَإِنَّ إِلْيَاسَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
text_en_primary: And Elias was indeed one of the messengers.
text_en_yusufali: So also was Elias among those sent (by Us).
text_en_pickthall: And lo! Elias was of those sent (to warn),
text_en_arberry: Elias too was one of the Envoys;

text_ar: إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
text_en_primary: ˹Remember˺ when he said to his people, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?
text_en_yusufali: Behold, he said to his people, "Will ye not fear (God)?
text_en_pickthall: When he said unto his folk: Will ye not ward off (evil) ?
text_en_arberry: when he said to his people, ’Will you not be godfearing?

text_ar: أَتَدْعُونَ بَعْلًۭا وَتَذَرُونَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْخَٰلِقِينَ
text_en_primary: Do you call upon ˹the idol of˺ Ba’l and abandon the Best of Creators—
text_en_yusufali: "Will ye call upon Baal and forsake the Best of Creators,-
text_en_pickthall: Will ye cry unto Baal and forsake the Best of creators,
text_en_arberry: Do you call on Baal, and abandon the Best of creators?

text_ar: ٱللَّهَ رَبَّكُمْ وَرَبَّ ءَابَآئِكُمُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
text_en_primary: Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers?”
text_en_yusufali: "God, your Lord and Cherisher and the Lord and Cherisher of your fathers of old?"
text_en_pickthall: Allah, your Lord and Lord of your forefathers ?
text_en_arberry: God, your Lord, and the Lord of your fathers, the ancients?’

text_ar: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَإِنَّهُمْ لَمُحْضَرُونَ
text_en_primary: But they rejected him, so they will certainly be brought ˹for punishment˺.
text_en_yusufali: But they rejected him, and they will certainly be called up (for punishment),-
text_en_pickthall: But they denied him, so they surely will be haled forth (to the doom)
text_en_arberry: But they cried him lies; so they will be among the arraigned,

text_ar: إِلَّا عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
text_en_primary: But not the chosen servants of Allah.
text_en_yusufali: Except the sincere and devoted Servants of God (among them).
text_en_pickthall: Save single-minded slaves of Allah.
text_en_arberry: except for God’s sincere servants;

text_ar: وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
text_en_primary: We blessed him ˹with honourable mention˺ among later generations:
text_en_yusufali: And We left (this blessing) for him among generations (to come) in later times:
text_en_pickthall: And we left for him among the later folk (the salutation):
text_en_arberry: and We left for him among the later folk

text_ar: سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰٓ إِلْ يَاسِينَ
text_en_primary: “Peace be upon Elias.”
text_en_yusufali: "Peace and salutation to such as Elias!"
text_en_pickthall: Peace be unto Elias!
text_en_arberry: ’Peace be upon Elias!’

text_ar: إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
text_en_primary: Indeed, this is how We reward the good-doers.
text_en_yusufali: Thus indeed do We reward those who do right.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! thus do We reward the good.
text_en_arberry: Even so We recompense the good-doers;

text_ar: إِنَّهُۥ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
text_en_primary: He was truly one of Our faithful servants.
text_en_yusufali: For he was one of our believing Servants.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! he is one of our believing slaves.
text_en_arberry: he was among Our believing servants.

text_ar: وَإِنَّ لُوطًۭا لَّمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
text_en_primary: And Lot was indeed one of the messengers.
text_en_yusufali: So also was Lut among those sent (by Us).
text_en_pickthall: And lo! Lot verily was of those sent (to warn).
text_en_arberry: Lot too was one of the Envoys;

text_ar: إِذْ نَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ أَجْمَعِينَ
text_en_primary: ˹Remember˺ when We delivered him and all of his family,
text_en_yusufali: Behold, We delivered him and his adherents, all
text_en_pickthall: When We saved him and his household, every one,
text_en_arberry: when We delivered him and his people all together,

text_ar: إِلَّا عَجُوزًۭا فِى ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ
text_en_primary: except an old woman, who was one of the doomed.
text_en_yusufali: Except an old woman who was among those who lagged behind:
text_en_pickthall: Save an old woman among those who stayed behind;
text_en_arberry: save an old woman among those that tarried;

text_ar: ثُمَّ دَمَّرْنَا ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ
text_en_primary: Then We ˹utterly˺ destroyed the rest.
text_en_yusufali: Then We destroyed the rest.
text_en_pickthall: Then We destroyed the others.
text_en_arberry: then We destroyed the others,

text_ar: وَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهِم مُّصْبِحِينَ
text_en_primary: You ˹Meccans˺ certainly pass by their ruins day
text_en_yusufali: Verily, ye pass by their (sites), by day-
text_en_pickthall: And lo! ye verily pass by (the ruin of) them in the morning
text_en_arberry: and you pass by them in the morning

text_ar: وَبِٱلَّيْلِ ۗ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
text_en_primary: and night. Will you not then understand?
text_en_yusufali: And by night: will ye not understand?
text_en_pickthall: And at night-time; have ye then no sense ?
text_en_arberry: and in the night; will you not understand?

text_ar: وَإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
text_en_primary: And Jonah was indeed one of the messengers.
text_en_yusufali: So also was Jonah among those sent (by Us).
text_en_pickthall: And lo! Jonah verily was of those sent (to warn)
text_en_arberry: Jonah too was one of the Envoys;

text_ar: إِذْ أَبَقَ إِلَى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ
text_en_primary: ˹Remember˺ when he fled to the overloaded ship.
text_en_yusufali: When he ran away (like a slave from captivity) to the ship (fully) laden,
text_en_pickthall: When he fled unto the laden ship,
text_en_arberry: when he ran away to the laden ship

text_ar: فَسَاهَمَ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُدْحَضِينَ
text_en_primary: Then ˹to save it from sinking,˺ he drew straws ˹with other passengers˺. He lost ˹and was thrown overboard˺.
text_en_yusufali: He (agreed to) cast lots, and he was condemned:
text_en_pickthall: And then drew lots and was of those rejected;
text_en_arberry: and cast lots, and was of the rebutted,

text_ar: فَٱلْتَقَمَهُ ٱلْحُوتُ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌۭ
text_en_primary: Then the whale engulfed him while he was blameworthy.
text_en_yusufali: Then the big Fish did swallow him, and he had done acts worthy of blame.
text_en_pickthall: And the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy;
text_en_arberry: then the whale swallowed him down, and he blameworthy.

text_ar: فَلَوْلَآ أَنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسَبِّحِينَ
text_en_primary: Had he not ˹constantly˺ glorified ˹Allah˺,
text_en_yusufali: Had it not been that he (repented and) glorified God,
text_en_pickthall: And had he not been one of those who glorify (Allah)
text_en_arberry: Now had he not been of those that glorify God,

text_ar: لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطْنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
text_en_primary: he would have certainly remained in its belly until the Day of Resurrection.
text_en_yusufali: He would certainly have remained inside the Fish till the Day of Resurrection.
text_en_pickthall: He would have tarried in its belly till the day when they are raised;
text_en_arberry: he would have tarried in its belly until the day they shall be raised;

text_ar: ۞ فَنَبَذْنَٰهُ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ سَقِيمٌۭ
text_en_primary: But We cast him onto the open ˹shore˺, ˹totally˺ worn out,
text_en_yusufali: But We cast him forth on the naked shore in a state of sickness,
text_en_pickthall: Then We cast him on a desert shore while he was sick;
text_en_arberry: but We cast him upon the wilderness, and he was sick,

text_ar: وَأَنۢبَتْنَا عَلَيْهِ شَجَرَةًۭ مِّن يَقْطِينٍۢ
text_en_primary: and caused a squash plant to grow over him.
text_en_yusufali: And We caused to grow, over him, a spreading plant of the gourd kind.
text_en_pickthall: And We caused a tree of gourd to grow above him;
text_en_arberry: and We caused to grow over him a tree of gourds.

text_ar: وَأَرْسَلْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ مِا۟ئَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ
text_en_primary: We ˹later˺ sent him ˹back˺ to ˹his city of˺ at least one hundred thousand people,
text_en_yusufali: And We sent him (on a mission) to a hundred thousand (men) or more.
text_en_pickthall: And We sent him to a hundred thousand (folk) or more
text_en_arberry: Then We sent him unto a hundred thousand, or more,

text_ar: فَـَٔامَنُوا۟ فَمَتَّعْنَٰهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍۢ
text_en_primary: who then believed ˹in him˺, so We allowed them enjoyment for a while.
text_en_yusufali: And they believed; so We permitted them to enjoy (their life) for a while.
text_en_pickthall: And they believed, therefor We gave them comfort for a while.
text_en_arberry: and they believed; so We gave them enjoyment for a while.

text_ar: فَٱسْتَفْتِهِمْ أَلِرَبِّكَ ٱلْبَنَاتُ وَلَهُمُ ٱلْبَنُونَ
text_en_primary: Ask them ˹O Prophet˺ if your Lord has daughters, while the pagans ˹prefer to˺ have sons.
text_en_yusufali: Now ask them their opinion: Is it that thy Lord has (only) daughters, and they have sons?-
text_en_pickthall: Now ask them (O Muhammad): Hath thy Lord daughters whereas they have sons ?
text_en_arberry: So ask them for a pronouncement -- Has thy Lord daughters, and they sons?

text_ar: أَمْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ إِنَٰثًۭا وَهُمْ شَٰهِدُونَ
text_en_primary: Or ˹ask them˺ if We created the angels as females right before their eyes.
text_en_yusufali: Or that We created the angels female, and they are witnesses (thereto)?
text_en_pickthall: Or created We the angels females while they were present ?
text_en_arberry: Or did We create the angels females, while they were witnesses?

text_ar: أَلَآ إِنَّهُم مِّنْ إِفْكِهِمْ لَيَقُولُونَ
text_en_primary: Indeed, it is one of their ˹outrageous˺ fabrications to say,
text_en_yusufali: Is it not that they say, from their own invention,
text_en_pickthall: Lo! it is of their falsehood that they say:
text_en_arberry: Is it not of their own calumny that they say,

text_ar: وَلَدَ ٱللَّهُ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
text_en_primary: “Allah has children.” They are simply liars.
text_en_yusufali: "God has begotten children"? but they are liars!
text_en_pickthall: Allah hath begotten. Allah! verily they tell a lie.
text_en_arberry: ’God has begotten?’ They are truly liars.

text_ar: أَصْطَفَى ٱلْبَنَاتِ عَلَى ٱلْبَنِينَ
text_en_primary: Has He chosen daughters over sons?
text_en_yusufali: Did He (then) choose daughters rather than sons?
text_en_pickthall: (And again of their falsehood): He hath preferred daughters to sons.
text_en_arberry: Has He chosen daughters above sons?

text_ar: مَا لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ
text_en_primary: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
text_en_yusufali: What is the matter with you? How judge ye?
text_en_pickthall: What aileth you ? How judge ye ?
text_en_arberry: What ails you then, how you judge?

text_ar: أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
text_en_primary: Will you not then be mindful?
text_en_yusufali: Will ye not then receive admonition?
text_en_pickthall: Will ye not then reflect ?
text_en_arberry: What, and will you not remember?

text_ar: أَمْ لَكُمْ سُلْطَٰنٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
text_en_primary: Or do you have ˹any˺ compelling proof?
text_en_yusufali: Or have ye an authority manifest?
text_en_pickthall: Or have ye a clear warrant ?
text_en_arberry: Or have you a clear authority?

text_ar: فَأْتُوا۟ بِكِتَٰبِكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
text_en_primary: Then bring ˹us˺ your scripture, if what you say is true!
text_en_yusufali: Then bring ye your Book (of authority) if ye be truthful!
text_en_pickthall: Then produce your writ, if ye are truthful.
text_en_arberry: Bring your Book, if you speak truly!

text_ar: وَجَعَلُوا۟ بَيْنَهُۥ وَبَيْنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ نَسَبًۭا ۚ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمَتِ ٱلْجِنَّةُ إِنَّهُمْ لَمُحْضَرُونَ
text_en_primary: They have also established a ˹marital˺ relationship between Him and the jinn. Yet the jinn ˹themselves˺ know well that such people will certainly be brought ˹for punishment˺.
text_en_yusufali: And they have invented a blood-relationship between Him and the Jinns: but the Jinns know (quite well) that they have indeed to appear (before his Judgment- Seat)!
text_en_pickthall: And they imagine kinship between him and the jinn, whereas the jinn know well that they will be brought before (Him).
text_en_arberry: They have set up a kinship between Him and the jinn; and the jinn know that they shall be arraigned.

text_ar: سُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
text_en_primary: Glorified is Allah far above what they claim!
text_en_yusufali: Glory to God! (He is free) from the things they ascribe (to Him)!
text_en_pickthall: Glorified be Allah from that which they attribute (unto Him),
text_en_arberry: Glory be to God above that they describe,

text_ar: إِلَّا عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
text_en_primary: But not the chosen servants of Allah.
text_en_yusufali: Not (so do) the Servants of God, sincere and devoted.
text_en_pickthall: Save single-minded slaves of Allah.
text_en_arberry: except for God’s sincere servants.

text_ar: فَإِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ
text_en_primary: Surely you ˹pagans˺ and whatever ˹idols˺ you worship
text_en_yusufali: For, verily, neither ye nor those ye worship-
text_en_pickthall: Lo! verily, ye and that which ye worship,
text_en_arberry: But as for you, and that you serve,

text_ar: مَآ أَنتُمْ عَلَيْهِ بِفَٰتِنِينَ
text_en_primary: can never lure ˹anyone˺ away from Him
text_en_yusufali: Can lead (any) into temptation concerning God,
text_en_pickthall: Ye cannot excite (anyone) against Him.
text_en_arberry: you shall not tempt any against Him

text_ar: إِلَّا مَنْ هُوَ صَالِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
text_en_primary: except those ˹destined˺ to burn in Hell.
text_en_yusufali: Except such as are (themselves) going to the blazing Fire!
text_en_pickthall: Save him who is to burn in hell.
text_en_arberry: except him who shall roast in Hell.

text_ar: وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلَّا لَهُۥ مَقَامٌۭ مَّعْلُومٌۭ
text_en_primary: ˹The angels respond,˺ “There is not one of us without an assigned station ˹of worship˺.
text_en_yusufali: (Those ranged in ranks say): "Not one of us but has a place appointed;
text_en_pickthall: There is not one of us but hath his known position.
text_en_arberry: None of us is there, but has a known station;

text_ar: وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلصَّآفُّونَ
text_en_primary: We are indeed the ones lined up in ranks ˹for Allah˺.
text_en_yusufali: "And we are verily ranged in ranks (for service);
text_en_pickthall: Lo! we, even we are they who set the ranks,
text_en_arberry: we are the rangers,

text_ar: وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلْمُسَبِّحُونَ
text_en_primary: And we are indeed the ones ˹constantly˺ glorifying ˹His praise˺.”
text_en_yusufali: "And we are verily those who declare (God’s) glory!"
text_en_pickthall: Lo! we, even we are they who hymn His praise
text_en_arberry: we are they that give glory.

text_ar: وَإِن كَانُوا۟ لَيَقُولُونَ
text_en_primary: They certainly used to say,
text_en_yusufali: And there were those who said,
text_en_pickthall: And indeed they used to say:
text_en_arberry: What though they would say,

text_ar: لَوْ أَنَّ عِندَنَا ذِكْرًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
text_en_primary: “If only we had a Reminder like ˹those of˺ earlier peoples,
text_en_yusufali: "If only we had had before us a Message from those of old,
text_en_pickthall: If we had but a reminder from the men of old
text_en_arberry: ’If only we had had a Reminder from the ancients,

text_ar: لَكُنَّا عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
text_en_primary: we would have truly been Allah’s devoted servants.”
text_en_yusufali: "We should certainly have been Servants of God, sincere (and devoted)!"
text_en_pickthall: We would be single-minded slaves of Allah.
text_en_arberry: then were we God’s sincere servants.’

text_ar: فَكَفَرُوا۟ بِهِۦ ۖ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ
text_en_primary: But ˹now˺ they reject it, so they will soon know.
text_en_yusufali: But (now that the Qur’an has come), they reject it: But soon will they know!
text_en_pickthall: Yet (now that it is come) they disbelieve therein; but they will come to know.
text_en_arberry: But they disbelieved in it; soon they shall know!

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ سَبَقَتْ كَلِمَتُنَا لِعِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
text_en_primary: Our Word has already gone forth to Our servants, the messengers,
text_en_yusufali: Already has Our Word been passed before (this) to our Servants sent (by Us),
text_en_pickthall: And verily Our word went forth of old unto Our bondmen sent (to warn)
text_en_arberry: Already Our Word has preceded to Our servants, the Envoys;

text_ar: إِنَّهُمْ لَهُمُ ٱلْمَنصُورُونَ
text_en_primary: that they would surely be helped,
text_en_yusufali: That they would certainly be assisted,
text_en_pickthall: That they verily would be helped,
text_en_arberry: assuredly they shall be helped,

text_ar: وَإِنَّ جُندَنَا لَهُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ
text_en_primary: and that Our forces will certainly prevail.
text_en_yusufali: And that Our forces,- they surely must conquer.
text_en_pickthall: And that Our host, they verily would be the victors.
text_en_arberry: and Our host -- they are the victors.

text_ar: فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍۢ
text_en_primary: So turn away from the deniers for a while ˹O Prophet˺.
text_en_yusufali: So turn thou away from them for a little while,
text_en_pickthall: So withdraw from them (O Muhammad) awhile,
text_en_arberry: So turn thou from them for a while,

text_ar: وَأَبْصِرْهُمْ فَسَوْفَ يُبْصِرُونَ
text_en_primary: You will see ˹what will happen to˺ them, and they too will see!
text_en_yusufali: And watch them (how they fare), and they soon shall see (how thou farest)!
text_en_pickthall: And watch, for they will (soon) see.
text_en_arberry: and see them; soon they shall see!

text_ar: أَفَبِعَذَابِنَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونَ
text_en_primary: Do they ˹really˺ wish to hasten Our punishment?
text_en_yusufali: Do they wish (indeed) to hurry on our Punishment?
text_en_pickthall: Would they hasten on Our doom ?
text_en_arberry: What, do they seek to hasten Our chastisement?

text_ar: فَإِذَا نَزَلَ بِسَاحَتِهِمْ فَسَآءَ صَبَاحُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
text_en_primary: Yet when it descends upon them: how evil will that morning be for those who had been warned!
text_en_yusufali: But when it descends into the open space before them, evil will be the morning for those who were warned (and heeded not)!
text_en_pickthall: But when it cometh home to them, then it will be a hapless morn for those who have been warned.
text_en_arberry: When it lights in their courtyard, how evil will be the morning of them that are warned!

text_ar: وَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍۢ
text_en_primary: And turn away from them for a while.
text_en_yusufali: So turn thou away from them for a little while,
text_en_pickthall: Withdraw from them awhile
text_en_arberry: So turn thou from them for a while,

text_ar: وَأَبْصِرْ فَسَوْفَ يُبْصِرُونَ
text_en_primary: You will see, and they too will see!
text_en_yusufali: And watch (how they fare) and they soon shall see (how thou farest)!
text_en_pickthall: And watch, for they will (soon) see.
text_en_arberry: and see; soon they shall see!

text_ar: سُبْحَٰنَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ ٱلْعِزَّةِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
text_en_primary: Glorified is your Lord—the Lord of Honour and Power—above what they claim!
text_en_yusufali: Glory to thy Lord, the Lord of Honour and Power! (He is free) from what they ascribe (to Him)!
text_en_pickthall: Glorified be thy Lord, the Lord of Majesty, from that which they attribute (unto Him)
text_en_arberry: Glory be to thy Lord, the Lord of Glory, above that they describe!

text_ar: وَسَلَٰمٌ عَلَى ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
text_en_primary: Peace be upon the messengers.
text_en_yusufali: And Peace on the apostles!
text_en_pickthall: And peace be unto those sent (to warn).
text_en_arberry: And peace be upon the Envoys;

text_ar: وَٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
text_en_primary: And praise be to Allah—Lord of all worlds.
text_en_yusufali: And Praise to God, the Lord and Cherisher of the Worlds.
text_en_pickthall: And praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds!
text_en_arberry: and praise belongs to God, the Lord of all Being.

text_ar: صٓ ۚ وَٱلْقُرْءَانِ ذِى ٱلذِّكْرِ
text_en_primary: sãd. By the Quran, full of reminders!
text_en_yusufali: Sad: By the Qur’an, Full of Admonition: (This is the Truth).
text_en_pickthall: Sad. By the renowned Qur’an,
text_en_arberry: Sad. By the Koran, containing the Remembrance --

text_ar: بَلِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ فِى عِزَّةٍۢ وَشِقَاقٍۢ
text_en_primary: ˹This is the truth,˺ yet the disbelievers are ˹entrenched˺ in arrogance and opposition.
text_en_yusufali: But the Unbelievers (are steeped) in self-glory and Separatism.
text_en_pickthall: Nay, but those who disbelieve are in false pride and schism.
text_en_arberry: nay, but the unbelievers glory in their schism.

text_ar: كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن قَرْنٍۢ فَنَادَوا۟ وَّلَاتَ حِينَ مَنَاصٍۢ
text_en_primary: ˹Imagine˺ how many peoples We destroyed before them, and they cried out when it was too late to escape.
text_en_yusufali: How many generations before them did We destroy? In the end they cried (for mercy)- when there was no longer time for being saved!
text_en_pickthall: How many a generation We destroyed before them, and they cried out when it was no longer the time for escape!
text_en_arberry: How many a generation We destroyed before them, and they called, but time was none to escape.

text_ar: وَعَجِبُوٓا۟ أَن جَآءَهُم مُّنذِرٌۭ مِّنْهُمْ ۖ وَقَالَ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا سَٰحِرٌۭ كَذَّابٌ
text_en_primary: Now, the pagans are astonished that a warner has come to them from among themselves. And the disbelievers say, “This is a magician, a total liar!
text_en_yusufali: So they wonder that a Warner has come to them from among themselves! and the Unbelievers say, "This is a sorcerer telling lies!
text_en_pickthall: And they marvel that a warner from among themselves hath come unto them, and the disbelievers say: This is a wizard, a charlatan.
text_en_arberry: Now they marvel that a warner has come to them from among them; and the unbelievers say, ’This is a lying sorcerer.

text_ar: أَجَعَلَ ٱلْءَالِهَةَ إِلَٰهًۭا وَٰحِدًا ۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَىْءٌ عُجَابٌۭ
text_en_primary: Has he reduced ˹all˺ the gods to One God? Indeed, this is something totally astonishing.”
text_en_yusufali: "Has he made the gods (all) into one God? Truly this is a wonderful thing!"
text_en_pickthall: Maketh he the gods One God ? Lo! that is an astounding thing.
text_en_arberry: What, has he made the gods One God? This is indeed a marvellous thing.’

text_ar: وَٱنطَلَقَ ٱلْمَلَأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ ٱمْشُوا۟ وَٱصْبِرُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ ءَالِهَتِكُمْ ۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَىْءٌۭ يُرَادُ
text_en_primary: The chiefs among them went forth saying, “Carry on, and stand firm in devotion to your gods. Certainly this is just a scheme ˹for power˺.
text_en_yusufali: And the leader among them go away (impatiently), (saying), "Walk ye away, and remain constant to your gods! For this is truly a thing designed (against you)!
text_en_pickthall: The chiefs among them go about, exhorting: Go and be staunch to your gods! Lo! this is a thing designed.
text_en_arberry: And the Council of them depart, saying ’Go! Be steadfast to your gods; this is a thing to be desired.

text_ar: مَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِى ٱلْمِلَّةِ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا ٱخْتِلَٰقٌ
text_en_primary: We have never heard of this in the previous faith. This is nothing but a fabrication.
text_en_yusufali: "We never heard (the like) of this among the people of these latter days: this is nothing but a made-up tale!"
text_en_pickthall: We have not heard of this in later religion. This is naught but an invention.
text_en_arberry: We have not heard of this in the last religion; this is surely an invention.

text_ar: أَءُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلذِّكْرُ مِنۢ بَيْنِنَا ۚ بَلْ هُمْ فِى شَكٍّۢ مِّن ذِكْرِى ۖ بَل لَّمَّا يَذُوقُوا۟ عَذَابِ
text_en_primary: Has the Reminder been revealed ˹only˺ to him out of ˹all of˺ us?” In fact, they are ˹only˺ in doubt of My ˹revealed˺ Reminder. In fact, ˹they do so because˺ they have not yet tasted My punishment.
text_en_yusufali: "What! has the Message been sent to him - (Of all persons) among us?"...but they are in doubt concerning My (Own) Message! Nay, they have not yet tasted My Punishment!
text_en_pickthall: Hath the reminder been unto him (alone) among us ? Nay, but they are in doubt concerning My reminder; nay but they have not yet tasted My doom.
text_en_arberry: What, has the Remembrance been sent down on him out of us all?’ Nay, but they are in doubt of My Remembrance; nay, they have not yet tasted My chastisement.

text_ar: أَمْ عِندَهُمْ خَزَآئِنُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْوَهَّابِ
text_en_primary: Or ˹is it because˺ they possess the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord—the Almighty, the Giver ˹of all bounties˺.
text_en_yusufali: Or have they the treasures of the mercy of thy Lord,- the Exalted in Power, the Grantor of Bounties without measure?
text_en_pickthall: Or are theirs the treasures of the mercy of thy Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower ?
text_en_arberry: Or have they the treasuries of thy Lord’s mercy, the All-mighty, the All-giving?

text_ar: أَمْ لَهُم مُّلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ۖ فَلْيَرْتَقُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَسْبَٰبِ
text_en_primary: Or ˹is it because˺ the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and everything in between belongs to them? Let them then climb their way ˹to heaven, if their claim is true˺.
text_en_yusufali: Or have they the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all between? If so, let them mount up with the ropes and means (to reach that end)!
text_en_pickthall: Or is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them theirs ? Then let them ascend by ropes!
text_en_arberry: Or is theirs the kingdom of the heavens and earth and of what between them is? Why, then let them ascend the cords!

text_ar: جُندٌۭ مَّا هُنَالِكَ مَهْزُومٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْأَحْزَابِ
text_en_primary: This is just another ˹enemy˺ force bound for defeat out there.
text_en_yusufali: But there - will be put to flight even a host of confederates.
text_en_pickthall: A defeated host are (all) the factions that are there.
text_en_arberry: A very host of parties is routed there!

text_ar: كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍۢ وَعَادٌۭ وَفِرْعَوْنُ ذُو ٱلْأَوْتَادِ
text_en_primary: Before them, the people of Noah denied ˹the truth˺, as did ’ad, Pharaoh of the mighty structures,
text_en_yusufali: Before them (were many who) rejected apostles,- the people of Noah, and ’Ad, and Pharaoh, the Lord of Stakes,
text_en_pickthall: The folk of Noah before them denied (their messenger) and (so did the tribe of) A’ad, and Pharaoh firmly planted,
text_en_arberry: Cried lies before them the people of Noah, and Ad, and Pharaoh, he of the tent-pegs,

text_ar: وَثَمُودُ وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍۢ وَأَصْحَٰبُ لْـَٔيْكَةِ ۚ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلْأَحْزَابُ
text_en_primary: Thamûd, the people of Lot, and the residents of the Forest. These were ˹all˺ enemy forces.
text_en_yusufali: And Thamud, and the people of Lut, and the Companions of the Wood; - such were the Confederates.
text_en_pickthall: And (the tribe of) Thamud, and the folk of Lot, and the dwellers in the wood: these were the factions.
text_en_arberry: and Thamood, and the people of Lot, and the men of the Thicket - those were the parties;

text_ar: إِن كُلٌّ إِلَّا كَذَّبَ ٱلرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ عِقَابِ
text_en_primary: Each rejected their messenger, so My punishment was justified.
text_en_yusufali: Not one (of them) but rejected the apostles, but My punishment came justly and inevitably (on them).
text_en_pickthall: Not one of them but did deny the messengers, therefor My doom was justified,
text_en_arberry: not one, that cried not lies to the Messengers, so My retribution was just.

text_ar: وَمَا يَنظُرُ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِلَّا صَيْحَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ مَّا لَهَا مِن فَوَاقٍۢ
text_en_primary: These ˹pagans˺ are awaiting nothing but a single Blast that cannot be stopped.
text_en_yusufali: These (today) only wait for a single mighty Blast, which (when it comes) will brook no delay.
text_en_pickthall: These wait for but one Shout, there will be no second thereto.
text_en_arberry: These are only awaiting for a single Cry, to which there is no delay.

text_ar: وَقَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَا عَجِّل لَّنَا قِطَّنَا قَبْلَ يَوْمِ ٱلْحِسَابِ
text_en_primary: They say ˹mockingly˺, “Our Lord! Hasten for us our share ˹of the punishment˺ before the Day of Reckoning.”
text_en_yusufali: They say: "Our Lord! hasten to us our sentence (even) before the Day of Account!"
text_en_pickthall: They say: Our Lord! Hasten on for us our fate before the Day of Reckoning.
text_en_arberry: They say, ’Our Lord, hasten to us our share before the Day of Reckoning.’

text_ar: ٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَا دَاوُۥدَ ذَا ٱلْأَيْدِ ۖ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ
text_en_primary: Be patient ˹O Prophet˺ with what they say. And remember Our servant, David, the man of strength. Indeed, he ˹constantly˺ turned ˹to Allah˺.
text_en_yusufali: Have patience at what they say, and remember our servant David, the man of strength: for he ever turned (to God).
text_en_pickthall: Bear with what they say, and remember Our bondman David, lord of might, Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (toward Allah).
text_en_arberry: Bear patiently what they say, and remember Our servant David, the man of might; he was a penitent.

text_ar: إِنَّا سَخَّرْنَا ٱلْجِبَالَ مَعَهُۥ يُسَبِّحْنَ بِٱلْعَشِىِّ وَٱلْإِشْرَاقِ
text_en_primary: We truly subjected the mountains to hymn ˹Our praises˺ along with him in the evening and after sunrise.
text_en_yusufali: It was We that made the hills declare, in unison with him, Our Praises, at eventide and at break of day,
text_en_pickthall: Lo! We subdued the hills to hymn the praises (of their Lord) with him at nightfall and sunrise,
text_en_arberry: With him We subjected the mountains to give glory at evening and sunrise,

text_ar: وَٱلطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةًۭ ۖ كُلٌّۭ لَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌۭ
text_en_primary: And ˹We subjected˺ the birds, flocking together. All turned to him ˹echoing his hymns˺.
text_en_yusufali: And the birds gathered (in assemblies): all with him did turn (to God).
text_en_pickthall: And the birds assembled; all were turning unto Him.
text_en_arberry: and the birds, duly mustered, every one to him reverting;

text_ar: وَشَدَدْنَا مُلْكَهُۥ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ ٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَفَصْلَ ٱلْخِطَابِ
text_en_primary: We strengthened his kingship, and gave him wisdom and sound judgment.
text_en_yusufali: We strengthened his kingdom, and gave him wisdom and sound judgment in speech and decision.
text_en_pickthall: We made his kingdom strong and gave him wisdom and decisive speech.
text_en_arberry: We strengthened his kingdom, and gave him wisdom and speech decisive.

text_ar: ۞ وَهَلْ أَتَىٰكَ نَبَؤُا۟ ٱلْخَصْمِ إِذْ تَسَوَّرُوا۟ ٱلْمِحْرَابَ
text_en_primary: Has the story of the two plaintiffs, who scaled the ˹wall of David’s˺ sanctuary, reached you ˹O Prophet˺?
text_en_yusufali: Has the Story of the Disputants reached thee? Behold, they climbed over the wall of the private chamber;
text_en_pickthall: And hath the story of the litigants come unto thee ? How they climbed the wall into the royal chamber;
text_en_arberry: Has the tiding of the dispute come to thee? When they scaled the Sanctuary,

text_ar: إِذْ دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ دَاوُۥدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنْهُمْ ۖ قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ ۖ خَصْمَانِ بَغَىٰ بَعْضُنَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ فَٱحْكُم بَيْنَنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَا تُشْطِطْ وَٱهْدِنَآ إِلَىٰ سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ
text_en_primary: When they came into David’s presence, he was startled by them. They said, “Have no fear. ˹We are merely˺ two in a dispute: one of us has wronged the other. So judge between us with truth—do not go beyond ˹it˺—and guide us to the right way.
text_en_yusufali: When they entered the presence of David, and he was terrified of them, they said: "Fear not: we are two disputants, one of whom has wronged the other: Decide now between us with truth, and treat us not with injustice, but guide us to the even Path..
text_en_pickthall: How they burst in upon David, and he was afraid of them. They said: Be not afraid! (We are) two litigants, one of whom hath wronged the other, therefor judge aright between us; be not unjust; and show us the fair way.
text_en_arberry: when they entered upon David, and he took fright at them; and they said, ’Fear not; two disputants we are -- one of us has injured the other; so judge between us justly, and transgress not, and guide us to the right path.’

text_ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَآ أَخِى لَهُۥ تِسْعٌۭ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةًۭ وَلِىَ نَعْجَةٌۭ وَٰحِدَةٌۭ فَقَالَ أَكْفِلْنِيهَا وَعَزَّنِى فِى ٱلْخِطَابِ
text_en_primary: This is my brother. He has ninety-nine sheep while I have ˹only˺ one. ˹Still˺ he asked me to give it up to him, overwhelming me with ˹his˺ argument.”
text_en_yusufali: "This man is my brother: He has nine and ninety ewes, and I have (but) one: Yet he says, ’commit her to my care,’ and is (moreover) harsh to me in speech."
text_en_pickthall: Lo! this my brother hath ninety and nine ewes while I had one ewe; and he said: Entrust it to me, and he conquered me in speech.
text_en_arberry: ’Behold, this my brother has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe. So he said, "Give her into my charge"; and he overcame me in the argument.’

text_ar: قَالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِۦ ۖ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبْغِى بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَقَلِيلٌۭ مَّا هُمْ ۗ وَظَنَّ دَاوُۥدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّٰهُ فَٱسْتَغْفَرَ رَبَّهُۥ وَخَرَّ رَاكِعًۭا وَأَنَابَ ۩
text_en_primary: David ˹eventually˺ ruled, “He has definitely wronged you in demanding ˹to add˺ your sheep to his. And certainly many partners wrong each other, except those who believe and do good—but how few are they!” Then David realized that We had tested him so he asked for his Lord’s forgiveness, fell down in prostration, and turned ˹to Him in repentance˺.
text_en_yusufali: (David) said: "He has undoubtedly wronged thee in demanding thy (single) ewe to be added to his (flock of) ewes: truly many are the partners (in business) who wrong each other: Not so do those who believe and work deeds of righteousness, and how few are they?"...and David gathered that We had tried him: he asked forgiveness of his Lord, fell down, bowing (in prostration), and turned (to God in repentance).
text_en_pickthall: (David) said: He hath wronged thee in demanding thine ewe in addition to his ewes, and lo! many partners oppress one another, save such as believe and do good works, and they are few. And David guessed that We had tried him, and he sought forgiveness of his Lord, and he bowed himself and fell down prostrate and repented.
text_en_arberry: Said he, ’Assuredly he has wronged thee in asking for thy ewe in addition to his sheep; and indeed many intermixers do injury one against the other, save those who believe, and do deeds of righteousness -- and how few they are!’ And David thought that We had only tried him; therefore he sought forgiveness of his Lord, and he fell down, bowing, and he repented.

text_ar: فَغَفَرْنَا لَهُۥ ذَٰلِكَ ۖ وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلْفَىٰ وَحُسْنَ مَـَٔابٍۢ
text_en_primary: So We forgave that for him. And he will indeed have ˹a status of˺ closeness to Us and an honourable destination!
text_en_yusufali: So We forgave him this (lapse): he enjoyed, indeed, a Near Approach to Us, and a beautiful place of (Final) Return.
text_en_pickthall: So We forgave him that; and lo! he had access to Our presence and a happy journey’s end.
text_en_arberry: Accordingly We forgave him that, and he has a near place in Our presence and a fair resort.

text_ar: يَٰدَاوُۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَٰكَ خَلِيفَةًۭ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱحْكُم بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌۭ شَدِيدٌۢ بِمَا نَسُوا۟ يَوْمَ ٱلْحِسَابِ
text_en_primary: ˹We instructed him:˺ “O David! We have surely made you an authority in the land, so judge between people with truth. And do not follow ˹your˺ desires or they will lead you astray from Allah’s Way. Surely those who go astray from Allah’s Way will suffer a severe punishment for neglecting the Day of Reckoning.”
text_en_yusufali: O David! We did indeed make thee a vicegerent on earth: so judge thou between men in truth (and justice): Nor follow thou the lusts (of thy heart), for they will mislead thee from the Path of God: for those who wander astray from the Path of God, is a Penalty Grievous, for that they forget the Day of Account.
text_en_pickthall: (And it was said unto him): O David! Lo! We have set thee as a viceroy in the earth; therefor judge aright between mankind, and follow not desire that it beguile thee from the way of Allah. Lo! those who wander from the way of Allah have an awful doom, forasmuch as they forgot the Day of Reckoning.
text_en_arberry: ’David, behold, We have appointed thee a viceroy in the earth; therefore judge between men justly, and follow not caprice, lest it lead thee astray from the way of God. Surely those who go astray from the way of God -- there awaits them a terrible chastisement, for that they have forgotten the Day of Reckoning.’

text_ar: وَمَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا بَٰطِلًۭا ۚ ذَٰلِكَ ظَنُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ۚ فَوَيْلٌۭ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
text_en_primary: We have not created the heavens and earth and everything in between without purpose—as the disbelievers think. So woe to the disbelievers because of the Fire!
text_en_yusufali: Not without purpose did We create heaven and earth and all between! that were the thought of Unbelievers! but woe to the Unbelievers because of the Fire (of Hell)!
text_en_pickthall: And We created not the heaven and the earth and all that is between them in vain. That is the opinion of those who disbelieve. And woe unto those who disbelieve, from the Fire!
text_en_arberry: We have not created the heavens and earth, and what between them is, for vanity; such is the thought of the unbelievers, wherefore woe unto the unbelievers because of the Fire!

text_ar: أَمْ نَجْعَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ كَٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ أَمْ نَجْعَلُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ كَٱلْفُجَّارِ
text_en_primary: Or should We treat those who believe and do good like those who make mischief throughout the land? Or should We treat the righteous like the wicked?
text_en_yusufali: Shall We treat those who believe and work deeds of righteousness, the same as those who do mischief on earth? Shall We treat those who guard against evil, the same as those who turn aside from the right?
text_en_pickthall: Shall We treat those who believe and do good works as those who spread corruption in the earth; or shall We treat the pious as the wicked ?
text_en_arberry: Or shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds as the workers of corruption in the earth, or shall We make the godfearing as the transgressors?

text_ar: كِتَٰبٌ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَٰرَكٌۭ لِّيَدَّبَّرُوٓا۟ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ
text_en_primary: ˹This is˺ a blessed Book which We have revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ so that they may contemplate its verses, and people of reason may be mindful.
text_en_yusufali: (Here is) a Book which We have sent down unto thee, full of blessings, that they may mediate on its Signs, and that men of understanding may receive admonition.
text_en_pickthall: (This is) a Scripture that We have revealed unto thee, full of blessing, that they may ponder its revelations, and that men of understanding may reflect.
text_en_arberry: A Book We have sent down to thee, Blessed, that men possessed of minds may ponder its signs and so remember.

text_ar: وَوَهَبْنَا لِدَاوُۥدَ سُلَيْمَٰنَ ۚ نِعْمَ ٱلْعَبْدُ ۖ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ
text_en_primary: And We blessed David with Solomon—what an excellent servant ˹he was˺! Indeed, he ˹constantly˺ turned ˹to Allah˺.
text_en_yusufali: To David We gave Solomon (for a son),- How excellent in Our service! Ever did he turn (to Us)!
text_en_pickthall: And We bestowed on David, Solomon. How excellent a slave! Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (toward Allah).
text_en_arberry: And We gave unto David Solomon; how excellent a servant he was! He was a penitent.

text_ar: إِذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِٱلْعَشِىِّ ٱلصَّٰفِنَٰتُ ٱلْجِيَادُ
text_en_primary: ˹Remember˺ when the well-trained, swift horses were paraded before him in the evening.
text_en_yusufali: Behold, there were brought before him, at eventide coursers of the highest breeding, and swift of foot;
text_en_pickthall: When there were shown to him at eventide lightfooted coursers
text_en_arberry: When in the evening were presented to him the standing steeds,

text_ar: فَقَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ ٱلْخَيْرِ عَن ذِكْرِ رَبِّى حَتَّىٰ تَوَارَتْ بِٱلْحِجَابِ
text_en_primary: He then proclaimed, “I am truly in love with ˹these˺ fine things out of remembrance for Allah,” until they went out of sight.
text_en_yusufali: And he said, "Truly do I love the love of good, with a view to the glory of my Lord,"- until (the sun) was hidden in the veil (of night):
text_en_pickthall: And he said: Lo! I have preferred the good things (of the world) to the remembrance of my Lord; till they were taken out of sight behind the curtain.
text_en_arberry: he said, ’Lo, I have loved the love of good things better than the remembrance of my Lord, until the sun was bidden behind the veil.

text_ar: رُدُّوهَا عَلَىَّ ۖ فَطَفِقَ مَسْحًۢا بِٱلسُّوقِ وَٱلْأَعْنَاقِ
text_en_primary: ˹He ordered,˺ “Bring them back to me!” Then he began to rub down their legs and necks.
text_en_yusufali: "Bring them back to me." then began he to pass his hand over (their) legs and their necks.
text_en_pickthall: (Then he said): Bring them back to me, and fell to slashing (with his sword their) legs and necks.
text_en_arberry: Return them to me!’ And he began to stroke their shanks and necks.

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمَٰنَ وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَىٰ كُرْسِيِّهِۦ جَسَدًۭا ثُمَّ أَنَابَ
text_en_primary: And indeed, We tested Solomon, placing a ˹deformed˺ body on his throne, then he turned ˹to Allah in repentance˺.
text_en_yusufali: And We did try Solomon: We placed on his throne a body (without life); but he did turn (to Us in true devotion):
text_en_pickthall: And verily We tried Solomon, and set upon his throne a (mere) body. Then did he repent.
text_en_arberry: Certainly We tried Solomon, and We cast upon his throne a mere body; then he repented.

text_ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِى وَهَبْ لِى مُلْكًۭا لَّا يَنۢبَغِى لِأَحَدٍۢ مِّنۢ بَعْدِىٓ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْوَهَّابُ
text_en_primary: He prayed, “My Lord! Forgive me, and grant me an authority that will never be matched by anyone after me. You are indeed the Giver ˹of all bounties˺.”
text_en_yusufali: He said, "O my Lord! Forgive me, and grant me a kingdom which, (it may be), suits not another after me: for Thou art the Grantor of Bounties (without measure).
text_en_pickthall: He said: My Lord! Forgive me and bestow on me sovereignty such as shall not belong to any after me. Lo! Thou art the Bestower.
text_en_arberry: He said, ’My Lord, forgive me, and give me a kingdom such as may not befall anyone after me; surely Thou art the All-giver.’

text_ar: فَسَخَّرْنَا لَهُ ٱلرِّيحَ تَجْرِى بِأَمْرِهِۦ رُخَآءً حَيْثُ أَصَابَ
text_en_primary: So We subjected to him the wind, blowing gently at his command to wherever he pleased.
text_en_yusufali: Then We subjected the wind to his power, to flow gently to his order, Whithersoever he willed,-
text_en_pickthall: So We made the wind subservient unto him, setting fair by his command whithersoever he intended.
text_en_arberry: So We subjected to him the wind, that ran at his commandment, softly, wherever he might light on,

text_ar: وَٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ كُلَّ بَنَّآءٍۢ وَغَوَّاصٍۢ
text_en_primary: And ˹We subjected to him˺ every builder and diver of the jinn,
text_en_yusufali: As also the evil ones, (including) every kind of builder and diver,-
text_en_pickthall: And the unruly, every builder and diver (made We subservient),
text_en_arberry: and the Satans, every builder and diver

text_ar: وَءَاخَرِينَ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِى ٱلْأَصْفَادِ
text_en_primary: and others bound together in chains.
text_en_yusufali: As also others bound together in fetters.
text_en_pickthall: And others linked together in chains,
text_en_arberry: and others also, coupled in fetters:

text_ar: هَٰذَا عَطَآؤُنَا فَٱمْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍۢ
text_en_primary: ˹Allah said,˺ “This is Our gift, so give or withhold ˹as you wish˺, never to be called to account.”
text_en_yusufali: "Such are Our Bounties: whether thou bestow them (on others) or withhold them, no account will be asked."
text_en_pickthall: (Saying): This is Our gift, so bestow thou, or withhold, without reckoning.
text_en_arberry: ’This is Our gift; bestow or withhold without reckoning.’

text_ar: وَإِنَّ لَهُۥ عِندَنَا لَزُلْفَىٰ وَحُسْنَ مَـَٔابٍۢ
text_en_primary: And he will indeed have ˹a status of˺ closeness to Us and an honourable destination!
text_en_yusufali: And he enjoyed, indeed, a Near Approach to Us, and a beautiful Place of (Final) Return.
text_en_pickthall: And lo! he hath favour with Us, and a happy journey’s end.
text_en_arberry: And he had a near place in Our presence and a fair resort.

text_ar: وَٱذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَآ أَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ بِنُصْبٍۢ وَعَذَابٍ
text_en_primary: And remember Our servant Job, when he cried out to his Lord, “Satan has afflicted me with distress and suffering.”
text_en_yusufali: Commemorate Our Servant Job. Behold he cried to his Lord: "The Evil One has afflicted me with distress and suffering!"
text_en_pickthall: And make mention (O Muhammad) of Our bondman Job, when he cried unto his Lord (saying): Lo! the devil doth afflict me with distress and torment.
text_en_arberry: Remember also Our servant Job; when he called to his Lord, ’Behold, Satan has visited me with weariness and chastisement.’

text_ar: ٱرْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ ۖ هَٰذَا مُغْتَسَلٌۢ بَارِدٌۭ وَشَرَابٌۭ
text_en_primary: ˹We responded,˺ “Stomp your foot: ˹now˺ here is a cool ˹and refreshing˺ spring for washing and drinking.”
text_en_yusufali: (The command was given:) "Strike with thy foot: here is (water) wherein to wash, cool and refreshing, and (water) to drink."
text_en_pickthall: (And it was said unto him): Strike the ground with thy foot. This (spring) is a cool bath and a refreshing drink.
text_en_arberry: ’Stamp thy foot! This is a laving-place cool, and a drink.’

text_ar: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ أَهْلَهُۥ وَمِثْلَهُم مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةًۭ مِّنَّا وَذِكْرَىٰ لِأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ
text_en_primary: And We gave him back his family, twice as many, as a mercy from Us and a lesson for people of reason.
text_en_yusufali: And We gave him (back) his people, and doubled their number,- as a Grace from Ourselves, and a thing for commemoration, for all who have Understanding.
text_en_pickthall: And We bestowed on him (again) his household and therewith the like thereof, a mercy from Us, and a memorial for men of understanding.
text_en_arberry: And We gave to him his family, and the like of them with them, as a mercy from us, and a reminder unto men possessed of minds;

text_ar: وَخُذْ بِيَدِكَ ضِغْثًۭا فَٱضْرِب بِّهِۦ وَلَا تَحْنَثْ ۗ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَٰهُ صَابِرًۭا ۚ نِّعْمَ ٱلْعَبْدُ ۖ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌۭ
text_en_primary: ˹And We said to him,˺ “Take in your hand a bundle of grass, and strike ˹your wife˺ with it, and do not break your oath.” We truly found him patient. What an excellent servant ˹he was˺! Indeed, he ˹constantly˺ turned ˹to Allah˺.
text_en_yusufali: "And take in thy hand a little grass, and strike therewith: and break not (thy oath)." Truly We found him full of patience and constancy. How excellent in Our service! ever did he turn (to Us)!
text_en_pickthall: And (it was said unto him): Take in thine hand a branch and smite therewith, and break not thine oath. Lo! We found him steadfast, how excellent a slave! Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (to his Lord).
text_en_arberry: and, ’Take in thy hand a bundle of rushes, and strike therewith, and do not fail in thy oath.’ Surely We found him a steadfast man. How excellent a servant he was! He was a penitent.

text_ar: وَٱذْكُرْ عِبَٰدَنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ أُو۟لِى ٱلْأَيْدِى وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرِ
text_en_primary: And remember Our servants: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—the men of strength and insight.
text_en_yusufali: And commemorate Our Servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, possessors of Power and Vision.
text_en_pickthall: And make mention of Our bondmen, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, men of parts and vision.
text_en_arberry: Remember also Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob -- men of might they and of vision.

text_ar: إِنَّآ أَخْلَصْنَٰهُم بِخَالِصَةٍۢ ذِكْرَى ٱلدَّارِ
text_en_primary: We truly chose them for the honour of proclaiming the Hereafter.
text_en_yusufali: Verily We did choose them for a special (purpose)- proclaiming the Message of the Hereafter.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! We purified them with a pure thought, remembrance of the Home (of the Hereafter).
text_en_arberry: Assuredly We purified them with a quality most pure, the remembrance of the Abode,

text_ar: وَإِنَّهُمْ عِندَنَا لَمِنَ ٱلْمُصْطَفَيْنَ ٱلْأَخْيَارِ
text_en_primary: And in Our sight they are truly among the chosen and the finest.
text_en_yusufali: They were, in Our sight, truly, of the company of the Elect and the Good.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! in Our sight they are verily of the elect, the excellent.
text_en_arberry: and in Our sight they are of the chosen, the excellent.

text_ar: وَٱذْكُرْ إِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَٱلْيَسَعَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ ۖ وَكُلٌّۭ مِّنَ ٱلْأَخْيَارِ
text_en_primary: Also remember Ishmael, Elisha, and Ⱬul-Kifl. All are among the best.
text_en_yusufali: And commemorate Isma’il, Elisha, and Zul-Kifl: Each of them was of the Company of the Good.
text_en_pickthall: And make mention of Ishmael and Elisha and Dhu’l-Kifl. All are of the chosen.
text_en_arberry: Remember also Our servants Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhul Kifl; each is among the excellent.

text_ar: هَٰذَا ذِكْرٌۭ ۚ وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَـَٔابٍۢ
text_en_primary: This is ˹all˺ a reminder. And the righteous will certainly have an honourable destination:
text_en_yusufali: This is a Message (of admonition): and verily, for the righteous, is a beautiful Place of (Final) Return,-
text_en_pickthall: This is a reminder. And lo! for those who ward off (evil) is a happy journey’s end,
text_en_arberry: This is a Remembrance; and for the godfearing is a fair resort,

text_ar: جَنَّٰتِ عَدْنٍۢ مُّفَتَّحَةًۭ لَّهُمُ ٱلْأَبْوَٰبُ
text_en_primary: the Gardens of Eternity, whose gates will be open for them.
text_en_yusufali: Gardens of Eternity, whose doors will (ever) be open to them;
text_en_pickthall: Gardens of Eden, whereof the gates are opened for them,
text_en_arberry: Gardens of Eden, whereof the gates are open to them,

text_ar: مُتَّكِـِٔينَ فِيهَا يَدْعُونَ فِيهَا بِفَٰكِهَةٍۢ كَثِيرَةٍۢ وَشَرَابٍۢ
text_en_primary: There they will recline, calling for abundant fruit and drink.
text_en_yusufali: Therein will they recline (at ease): Therein can they call (at pleasure) for fruit in abundance, and (delicious) drink;
text_en_pickthall: Wherein, reclining, they call for plenteous fruit and cool drink (that is) therein.
text_en_arberry: wherein they recline, and wherein they call for fruits abundant, and sweet potions,

text_ar: ۞ وَعِندَهُمْ قَٰصِرَٰتُ ٱلطَّرْفِ أَتْرَابٌ
text_en_primary: And with them will be maidens of modest gaze and equal age.
text_en_yusufali: And beside them will be chaste women restraining their glances, (companions) of equal age.
text_en_pickthall: And with them are those of modest gaze, companions.
text_en_arberry: and with them maidens restraining their glances of equal age.

text_ar: هَٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِيَوْمِ ٱلْحِسَابِ
text_en_primary: This is what you are promised for the Day of Reckoning.
text_en_yusufali: Such is the Promise made, to you for the Day of Account!
text_en_pickthall: This it is that ye are promised for the Day of Reckoning.
text_en_arberry: ’This is what you were promised for the Day of Reckoning;

text_ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَرِزْقُنَا مَا لَهُۥ مِن نَّفَادٍ
text_en_primary: This is indeed Our provision that will never end.
text_en_yusufali: Truly such will be Our Bounty (to you); it will never fail;-
text_en_pickthall: Lo! this in truth is Our provision, which will never waste away.
text_en_arberry: this is Our provision, unto which there is no end.’

text_ar: هَٰذَا ۚ وَإِنَّ لِلطَّٰغِينَ لَشَرَّ مَـَٔابٍۢ
text_en_primary: That is that. And the transgressors will certainly have the worst destination:
text_en_yusufali: Yea, such! but - for the wrong-doers will be an evil place of (Final) Return!-
