text_en_primary: Allah is the One Who created seven heavens ˹in layers˺, and likewise for the earth. The ˹divine˺ command descends between them so you may know that Allah is Most Capable of everything and that Allah certainly encompasses all things in ˹His˺ knowledge.
text_en_yusufali: God is He Who created seven Firmaments and of the earth a similar number. Through the midst of them (all) descends His Command: that ye may know that God has power over all things, and that God comprehends, all things in (His) Knowledge.
text_en_pickthall: Allah it is who hath created seven heavens, and of the earth the like thereof. The commandment cometh down among them slowly, that ye may know that Allah is Able to do all things, and that Allah surroundeth all things in knowledge.
text_en_arberry: It is God who created seven heavens, and of earth their like, between them the Command descending, that you may know that God is powerful over everything and that God encompasses everything in knowledge.

text_ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكَ ۖ تَبْتَغِى مَرْضَاتَ أَزْوَٰجِكَ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
text_en_primary: O Prophet! Why do you prohibit ˹yourself˺ from what Allah has made lawful to you, seeking to please your wives? And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
text_en_yusufali: O Prophet! Why holdest thou to be forbidden that which God has made lawful to thee? Thou seekest to please thy consorts. But God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
text_en_pickthall: O Prophet! Why bannest thou that which Allah hath made lawful for thee, seeking to please thy wives ? And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
text_en_arberry: It is God who created seven heavens, and of earth their like, between them the Command descending, that you may know that God is powerful over everything and that God encompasses everything in knowledge.

text_ar: قَدْ فَرَضَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمَٰنِكُمْ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ مَوْلَىٰكُمْ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
text_en_primary: Allah has already ordained for you ˹believers˺ the way to absolve yourselves from your oaths. For Allah is your Guardian. And He is the All-Knowing, All-Wise.
text_en_yusufali: God has already ordained for you, (O men), the dissolution of your oaths (in some cases): and God is your Protector, and He is Full of Knowledge and Wisdom.
text_en_pickthall: Allah hath made lawful for you (Muslims) absolution from your oaths (of such a kind), and Allah is your Protector. He is the Knower, the Wise.
text_en_arberry: God has ordained for you the absolution of your oaths. God is your Protector, and He is the All-knowing, the All-wise.

text_ar: وَإِذْ أَسَرَّ ٱلنَّبِىُّ إِلَىٰ بَعْضِ أَزْوَٰجِهِۦ حَدِيثًۭا فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَتْ بِهِۦ وَأَظْهَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُۥ وَأَعْرَضَ عَنۢ بَعْضٍۢ ۖ فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَهَا بِهِۦ قَالَتْ مَنْ أَنۢبَأَكَ هَٰذَا ۖ قَالَ نَبَّأَنِىَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْخَبِيرُ
text_en_primary: ˹Remember˺ when the Prophet had ˹once˺ confided something to one of his wives, then when she disclosed it ˹to another wife˺ and Allah made it known to him, he presented ˹to her˺ part of what was disclosed and overlooked a part. So when he informed her of it, she exclaimed, “Who told you this?” He replied, “I was informed by the All-Knowing, All-Aware.”
text_en_yusufali: When the Prophet disclosed a matter in confidence to one of his consorts, and she then divulged it (to another), and God made it known to him, he confirmed part thereof and repudiated a part. Then when he told her thereof, she said, "Who told thee this? "He said, "He told me Who knows and is well-acquainted (with all things)."
text_en_pickthall: When the Prophet confided a fact unto one of his wives and when she afterward divulged it and Allah apprised him thereof, he made known (to her) part thereof and passed over part. And when he told it her she said: Who hath told thee ? He said: The Knower, the Aware hath told me.
text_en_arberry: And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a certain matter; and then, when she told of it, and God disclosed that to him, he made known part of it, and turned aside from part; then, when he told her of it, she said, ’Who told thee this?’ He said, ’I was told of it by the All-knowing, the All-aware.’

text_ar: إِن تَتُوبَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا ۖ وَإِن تَظَٰهَرَا عَلَيْهِ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ مَوْلَىٰهُ وَجِبْرِيلُ وَصَٰلِحُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ۖ وَٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ
text_en_primary: ˹It will be better˺ if you ˹wives˺ both turn to Allah in repentance, for your hearts have certainly faltered. But if you ˹continue to˺ collaborate against him, then ˹know that˺ Allah Himself is his Guardian. And Gabriel, the righteous believers, and the angels are ˹all˺ his supporters as well.
text_en_yusufali: If ye two turn in repentance to Him, your hearts are indeed so inclined; But if ye back up each other against him, truly God is his Protector, and Gabriel, and (every) righteous one among those who believe,- and furthermore, the angels - will back (him) up.
text_en_pickthall: If ye twain turn unto Allah repentant, (ye have cause to do so) for your hearts desired (the ban); and if ye aid one another against him (Muhammad) then lo! Allah, even He, is his Protecting Friend, and Gabriel and the righteous among the believers; and furthermore the angels are his helpers.
text_en_arberry: If you two repent to God, yet your hearts certainly inclined; but if you support one another against him, God is his Protector, and Gabriel, and the righteous among the believers; and, after that, the angels are his supporters.

text_ar: عَسَىٰ رَبُّهُۥٓ إِن طَلَّقَكُنَّ أَن يُبْدِلَهُۥٓ أَزْوَٰجًا خَيْرًۭا مِّنكُنَّ مُسْلِمَٰتٍۢ مُّؤْمِنَٰتٍۢ قَٰنِتَٰتٍۢ تَٰٓئِبَٰتٍ عَٰبِدَٰتٍۢ سَٰٓئِحَٰتٍۢ ثَيِّبَٰتٍۢ وَأَبْكَارًۭا
text_en_primary: Perhaps, if he were to divorce you ˹all˺, his Lord would replace you with better wives who are submissive ˹to Allah˺, faithful ˹to Him˺, devout, repentant, dedicated to worship and fasting—previously married or virgins.
text_en_yusufali: It may be, if he divorced you (all), that God will give him in exchange consorts better than you,- who submit (their wills), who believe, who are devout, who turn to God in repentance, who worship (in humility), who travel (for Faith) and fast,- previously married or virgins.
text_en_pickthall: It may happen that his Lord, if he divorce you, will give him in your stead wives better than you, submissive (to Allah), believing, pious, penitent, devout, inclined to fasting, widows and maids.
text_en_arberry: It is possible that, if he divorces you, his Lord will give him in exchange wives better than you, women who have surrendered, believing, obedient, penitent, devout, given to fasting, who have been married and virgins too.

text_ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ قُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَارًۭا وَقُودُهَا ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلْحِجَارَةُ عَلَيْهَا مَلَٰٓئِكَةٌ غِلَاظٌۭ شِدَادٌۭ لَّا يَعْصُونَ ٱللَّهَ مَآ أَمَرَهُمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ
text_en_primary: O believers! Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, overseen by formidable and severe angels, who never disobey whatever Allah orders—always doing as commanded.
text_en_yusufali: O ye who believe! save yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is Men and Stones, over which are (appointed) angels stern (and) severe, who flinch not (from executing) the Commands they receive from God, but do (precisely) what they are commanded.
text_en_pickthall: O ye who believe! Ward off from yourselves and your families a Fire whereof the fuel is men and stones, over which are set angels strong, severe, who resist not Allah in that which He commandeth them, but do that which they are commanded.
text_en_arberry: Believers, guard yourselves and your families against a Fire whose fuel is men and stones, and over which are harsh, terrible angels who disobey not God in what He commands them and do what they are commanded.

text_ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَا تَعْتَذِرُوا۟ ٱلْيَوْمَ ۖ إِنَّمَا تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
text_en_primary: ˹The deniers will then be told,˺ “O disbelievers! Make no excuses this Day! You are only rewarded for what you used to do.”
text_en_yusufali: (They will say), "O ye Unbelievers! Make no excuses this Day! Ye are being but requited for all that ye did!"
text_en_pickthall: (Then it will be said): O ye who disbelieve! Make no excuses for yourselves this day. Ye are only being paid for what ye used to do.
text_en_arberry: ’O you unbelievers, do not excuse yourselves today; you are only being recompensed for what you were doing.’

text_ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ تُوبُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوْبَةًۭ نَّصُوحًا عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمْ أَن يُكَفِّرَ عَنكُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمْ وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ جَنَّٰتٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ يَوْمَ لَا يُخْزِى ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّبِىَّ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ ۖ نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَىٰ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَٰنِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَٱغْفِرْ لَنَآ ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌۭ
text_en_primary: O believers! Turn to Allah in sincere repentance, so your Lord may absolve you of your sins and admit you into Gardens, under which rivers flow, on the Day Allah will not disgrace the Prophet or the believers with him. Their light will shine ahead of them and on their right. They will say, “Our Lord! Perfect our light for us, and forgive us. ˹For˺ You are truly Most Capable of everything.”
text_en_yusufali: O ye who believe! Turn to God with sincere repentance: In the hope that your Lord will remove from you your ills and admit you to Gardens beneath which Rivers flow,- the Day that God will not permit to be humiliated the Prophet and those who believe with him. Their Light will run forward before them and by their right hands, while they say, "Our Lord! Perfect our Light for us, and grant us Forgiveness: for Thou hast power over all things."
text_en_pickthall: O ye who believe! Turn unto Allah in sincere repentance! It may be that your Lord will remit from you your evil deeds and bring you into Gardens underneath which rivers flow, on the day when Allah will not abase the Prophet and those who believe with him. Their light will run before them and on their right hands; they will say: Our Lord! Perfect our light for us, and forgive us! Lo! Thou art Able to do all things.
text_en_arberry: Believers, turn to God in sincere repentance; it may be that your Lord will acquit you of your evil deeds, and will admit you into gardens underneath which rivers flow. Upon the day when God will not degrade the Prophet and those who believe with him, their light running before them, and on their right hands; and they say, ’Our ’Lord, perfect for us our light, and forgive us; surely Thou art powerful over everything.’

text_ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ جَٰهِدِ ٱلْكُفَّارَ وَٱلْمُنَٰفِقِينَ وَٱغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ وَمَأْوَىٰهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ ۖ وَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
text_en_primary: O Prophet! Struggle against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be firm with them. Hell will be their home. What an evil destination!
text_en_yusufali: O Prophet! Strive hard against the Unbelievers and the Hypocrites, and be firm against them. Their abode is Hell,- an evil refuge (indeed).
text_en_pickthall: O Prophet! Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them. Hell will be their home, a hapless journey’s end.
text_en_arberry: O Prophet, struggle with the unbelievers and the hypocrites, and be thou harsh with them; their refuge shall be Gehenna -- an evil homecoming!

text_ar: ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًۭا لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ٱمْرَأَتَ نُوحٍۢ وَٱمْرَأَتَ لُوطٍۢ ۖ كَانَتَا تَحْتَ عَبْدَيْنِ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا صَٰلِحَيْنِ فَخَانَتَاهُمَا فَلَمْ يُغْنِيَا عَنْهُمَا مِنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيْـًۭٔا وَقِيلَ ٱدْخُلَا ٱلنَّارَ مَعَ ٱلدَّٰخِلِينَ
text_en_primary: Allah sets forth an example for the disbelievers: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. Each was married to one of Our righteous servants, yet betrayed them. So their husbands were of no benefit to them against Allah whatsoever. Both were told, “Enter the Fire, along with the others!”
text_en_yusufali: God sets forth, for an example to the Unbelievers, the wife of Noah and the wife of Lut: they were (respectively) under two of our righteous servants, but they were false to their (husbands), and they profited nothing before God on their account, but were told: "Enter ye the Fire along with (others) that enter!"
text_en_pickthall: Allah citeth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot, who were under two of Our righteous slaves yet betrayed them so that they (the husbands) availed them naught against Allah and it was said (unto them): Enter the Fire along with those who enter.
text_en_arberry: God has struck a similitude for the unbelievers -- the wife of Noah, and the wife of Lot; for they were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, so they availed them nothing whatsoever against God; so it was said, ’Enter, you two, the Fire with those who enter.’

text_ar: وَضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًۭا لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱمْرَأَتَ فِرْعَوْنَ إِذْ قَالَتْ رَبِّ ٱبْنِ لِى عِندَكَ بَيْتًۭا فِى ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَنَجِّنِى مِن فِرْعَوْنَ وَعَمَلِهِۦ وَنَجِّنِى مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
text_en_primary: And Allah sets forth an example for the believers: the wife of Pharaoh, who prayed, “My Lord! Build me a house in Paradise near You, deliver me from Pharaoh and his ˹evil˺ doing, and save me from the wrongdoing people.”
text_en_yusufali: And God sets forth, as an example to those who believe the wife of Pharaoh: Behold she said: "O my Lord! Build for me, in nearness to Thee, a mansion in the Garden, and save me from Pharaoh and his doings, and save me from those that do wrong";
text_en_pickthall: And Allah citeth an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh when she said: My Lord! Build for me a home with thee in the Garden, and deliver me from Pharaoh and his work, and deliver me from evil- doing folk;
text_en_arberry: God has struck a similitude for the believers -- the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, ’My Lord, build for me a house in Paradise, in Thy presence, and deliver me from Pharaoh and his work, and do Thou deliver me from the people of the evildoers.’

text_ar: وَمَرْيَمَ ٱبْنَتَ عِمْرَٰنَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِنَا وَصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِمَٰتِ رَبِّهَا وَكُتُبِهِۦ وَكَانَتْ مِنَ ٱلْقَٰنِتِينَ
text_en_primary: ˹There is˺ also ˹the example of˺ Mary, the daughter of ’Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her ˹womb˺ through Our angel ˹Gabriel˺. She testified to the words of her Lord and His Scriptures, and was one of the ˹sincerely˺ devout.
text_en_yusufali: And Mary the daughter of ’Imran, who guarded her chastity; and We breathed into (her body) of Our spirit; and she testified to the truth of the words of her Lord and of His Revelations, and was one of the devout (servants).
text_en_pickthall: And Mary, daughter of ’Imran, whose body was chaste, therefor We breathed therein something of Our Spirit. And she put faith in the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and was of the obedient.
text_en_arberry: And Mary, Imran’s daughter, who guarded her virginity, so We breathed into her of Our Spirit, and she confirmed the Words of her Lord and His Books, and became one of the obedient.

text_ar: تَبَٰرَكَ ٱلَّذِى بِيَدِهِ ٱلْمُلْكُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌ
text_en_primary: Blessed is the One in Whose Hands rests all authority. And He is Most Capable of everything.
text_en_yusufali: Blessed be He in Whose hands is Dominion; and He over all things hath Power;-
text_en_pickthall: Blessed is He in Whose hand is the Sovereignty, and, He is Able to do all things.
text_en_arberry: Blessed be He in whose hand is the Kingdom -- He is powerful over everything --

text_ar: ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلْمَوْتَ وَٱلْحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًۭا ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْغَفُورُ
text_en_primary: ˹He is the One˺ Who created death and life in order to test which of you is best in deeds. And He is the Almighty, All-Forgiving.
text_en_yusufali: He Who created Death and Life, that He may try which of you is best in deed: and He is the Exalted in Might, Oft-Forgiving;-
text_en_pickthall: Who hath created life and death that He may try you which of you is best in conduct; and He is the Mighty, the Forgiving,
text_en_arberry: who created death and life, that He might try you which of you is fairest in works; and He is the All-mighty, the All-forgiving --

text_ar: ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٍۢ طِبَاقًۭا ۖ مَّا تَرَىٰ فِى خَلْقِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ مِن تَفَٰوُتٍۢ ۖ فَٱرْجِعِ ٱلْبَصَرَ هَلْ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورٍۢ
text_en_primary: ˹He is the One˺ Who created seven heavens, one above the other. You will never see any imperfection in the creation of the Most Compassionate. So look again: do you see any flaws?
text_en_yusufali: He Who created the seven heavens one above another: No want of proportion wilt thou see in the Creation of (God) Most Gracious. So turn thy vision again: seest thou any flaw?
text_en_pickthall: Who hath created seven heavens in harmony. Thou (Muhammad) canst see no fault in the Beneficent One’s creation; then look again: Canst thou see any rifts ?
text_en_arberry: who created seven heavens one upon another. Thou seest not in the creation of the All-merciful any imperfection. Return thy gaze; seest thou any fissure?

text_ar: ثُمَّ ٱرْجِعِ ٱلْبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيْنِ يَنقَلِبْ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْبَصَرُ خَاسِئًۭا وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌۭ
text_en_primary: Then look again and again—your sight will return frustrated and weary.
text_en_yusufali: Again turn thy vision a second time: (thy) vision will come back to thee dull and discomfited, in a state worn out.
text_en_pickthall: Then look again and yet again, thy sight will return unto thee weakened and made dim.
text_en_arberry: Then return thy gaze again, and again, and thy gaze comes back to thee dazzled, aweary.

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِمَصَٰبِيحَ وَجَعَلْنَٰهَا رُجُومًۭا لِّلشَّيَٰطِينِ ۖ وَأَعْتَدْنَا لَهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
text_en_primary: And indeed, We adorned the lowest heaven with ˹stars like˺ lamps, and made them ˹as missiles˺ for stoning ˹eavesdropping˺ devils, for whom We have also prepared the torment of the Blaze.
text_en_yusufali: And we have, (from of old), adorned the lowest heaven with Lamps, and We have made such (Lamps) (as) missiles to drive away the Evil Ones, and have prepared for them the Penalty of the Blazing Fire.
text_en_pickthall: And verily We have beautified the world’s heaven with lamps, and We have made them missiles for the devils, and for them We have prepared the doom of flame.
text_en_arberry: And We adorned the lower heaven with lamps, and made them things to stone Satans; and We have prepared for them the chastisement of the Blaze.

text_ar: وَلِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِرَبِّهِمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ ۖ وَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
text_en_primary: Those who disbelieve in their Lord will suffer the punishment of Hell. What an evil destination!
text_en_yusufali: For those who reject their Lord (and Cherisher) is the Penalty of Hell: and evil is (such), Destination.
text_en_pickthall: And for those who disbelieve in their Lord there is the doom of hell, a hapless journey’s end!
text_en_arberry: And for those who disbelieve in their Lord there awaits the chastisement of Gehenna -- an evil homecoming!

text_ar: إِذَآ أُلْقُوا۟ فِيهَا سَمِعُوا۟ لَهَا شَهِيقًۭا وَهِىَ تَفُورُ
text_en_primary: When they are tossed into it, they will hear its roaring as it boils over,
text_en_yusufali: When they are cast therein, they will hear the (terrible) drawing in of its breath even as it blazes forth,
text_en_pickthall: When they are flung therein they hear its roaring as it boileth up,
text_en_arberry: When they are cast into it they will hear it sighing, the while it boils

text_ar: تَكَادُ تَمَيَّزُ مِنَ ٱلْغَيْظِ ۖ كُلَّمَآ أُلْقِىَ فِيهَا فَوْجٌۭ سَأَلَهُمْ خَزَنَتُهَآ أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَذِيرٌۭ
text_en_primary: almost bursting in fury. Every time a group is cast into it, its keepers will ask them, “Did a warner not come to you?”
text_en_yusufali: Almost bursting with fury: Every time a Group is cast therein, its Keepers will ask, "Did no Warner come to you?"
text_en_pickthall: As it would burst with rage. Whenever a (fresh) host is flung therein the wardens thereof ask them: Came there unto you no warner ?
text_en_arberry: and wellnigh bursts asunder with rage. As often as a troop is cast into it, its keepers ask them, ’Came there no warner to you?’;

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ بَلَىٰ قَدْ جَآءَنَا نَذِيرٌۭ فَكَذَّبْنَا وَقُلْنَا مَا نَزَّلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن شَىْءٍ إِنْ أَنتُمْ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ كَبِيرٍۢ
text_en_primary: They will reply, “Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied and said, ‘Allah has revealed nothing. You are extremely astray.’”
text_en_yusufali: They will say: "Yes indeed; a Warner did come to us, but we rejected him and said, ’God never sent down any (Message): ye are nothing but an egregious delusion!’"
text_en_pickthall: They say: Yea, verily, a warner came unto us; but we denied and said: Allah hath naught revealed; ye are in naught but a great error.
text_en_arberry: They say, ’Yes indeed, a warner came to us; but we cried lies, saying, "God has not sent down anything; you are only in great error.

text_ar: وَقَالُوا۟ لَوْ كُنَّا نَسْمَعُ أَوْ نَعْقِلُ مَا كُنَّا فِىٓ أَصْحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
text_en_primary: And they will lament, “If only we had listened and reasoned, we would not be among the residents of the Blaze!”
text_en_yusufali: They will further say: "Had we but listened or used our intelligence, we should not (now) be among the Companions of the Blazing Fire!"
text_en_pickthall: And they say: Had we been wont to listen or have sense, we had not been among the dwellers in the flames.
text_en_arberry: They also say, ’If we had only heard, or had understood, we would not have been of the inhabitants of the Blaze.’

text_ar: فَٱعْتَرَفُوا۟ بِذَنۢبِهِمْ فَسُحْقًۭا لِّأَصْحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
text_en_primary: And so they will confess their sins. So away with the residents of the Blaze!
text_en_yusufali: They will then confess their sins: but far will be (Forgiveness) from the Companions of the Blazing Fire!
text_en_pickthall: So they acknowledge their sins; but far removed (from mercy) are the dwellers in the flames.
text_en_arberry: So they confess their sins. Curse the inhabitants of the Blaze!

text_ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌۭ وَأَجْرٌۭ كَبِيرٌۭ
text_en_primary: Indeed, those in awe of their Lord without seeing Him will have forgiveness and a mighty reward.
text_en_yusufali: As for those who fear their Lord unseen, for them is Forgiveness and a great Reward.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! those who fear their Lord in secret, theirs will be forgiveness and a great reward.
text_en_arberry: Surely those who fear their Lord in the Unseen -- there awaits them forgiveness and a great wage.

text_ar: وَأَسِرُّوا۟ قَوْلَكُمْ أَوِ ٱجْهَرُوا۟ بِهِۦٓ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمٌۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
text_en_primary: Whether you speak secretly or openly—He surely knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart.
text_en_yusufali: And whether ye hide your word or publish it, He certainly has (full) knowledge, of the secrets of (all) hearts.
text_en_pickthall: And keep your opinion secret or proclaim it, lo! He is Knower of all that is in the breasts (of men).
text_en_arberry: Be secret in your speech, or proclaim it, He knows the thoughts within the breasts.

text_ar: أَلَا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ خَلَقَ وَهُوَ ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلْخَبِيرُ
text_en_primary: How could He not know His Own creation? For He ˹alone˺ is the Most Subtle, All-Aware.
text_en_yusufali: Should He not know,- He that created? and He is the One that understands the finest mysteries (and) is well-acquainted (with them).
text_en_pickthall: Should He not know what He created ? And He is the Subtile, the Aware.
text_en_arberry: Shall He not know, who created? And He is the All-subtle, the All-aware.

text_ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ ذَلُولًۭا فَٱمْشُوا۟ فِى مَنَاكِبِهَا وَكُلُوا۟ مِن رِّزْقِهِۦ ۖ وَإِلَيْهِ ٱلنُّشُورُ
text_en_primary: He is the One Who smoothed out the earth for you, so move about in its regions and eat from His provisions. And to Him is the resurrection ˹of all˺.
text_en_yusufali: It is He Who has made the earth manageable for you, so traverse ye through its tracts and enjoy of the Sustenance which He furnishes: but unto Him is the Resurrection.
text_en_pickthall: He it is Who hath made the earth subservient unto you, so Walk in the paths thereof and eat of His providence. And unto Him will be the resurrection (of the dead).
text_en_arberry: It is He who made the earth submissive to you; therefore walk in its tracts, and eat of His provision; to Him is the Uprising.

text_ar: ءَأَمِنتُم مَّن فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يَخْسِفَ بِكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ فَإِذَا هِىَ تَمُورُ
text_en_primary: Do you feel secure that the One Who is in heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you up as it quakes violently?
text_en_yusufali: Do ye feel secure that He Who is in heaven will not cause you to be swallowed up by the earth when it shakes (as in an earthquake)?
text_en_pickthall: Have ye taken security from Him Who is in the heaven that He will not cause the earth to swallow you when lo! it is convulsed ?
text_en_arberry: Do you feel secure that He who is in heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you, the while it rocks?

text_ar: أَمْ أَمِنتُم مَّن فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ حَاصِبًۭا ۖ فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ كَيْفَ نَذِيرِ
text_en_primary: Or do you feel secure that the One Who is in heaven will not unleash upon you a storm of stones. Only then would you know how ˹serious˺ My warning was!
text_en_yusufali: Or do ye feel secure that He Who is in Heaven will not send against you a violent tornado (with showers of stones), so that ye shall know how (terrible) was My warning?
text_en_pickthall: Or have ye taken security from Him Who is in the heaven that He will not let loose on you a hurricane ? But ye shall know the manner of My warning.
text_en_arberry: Do you feel secure that He who is in heaven will not loose against you a squall of pebbles, then you shall know how My warning is?

text_ar: وَلَقَدْ كَذَّبَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ فَكَيْفَ كَانَ نَكِيرِ
text_en_primary: And certainly those before them denied ˹as well˺, then how severe was My response!
text_en_yusufali: But indeed men before them rejected (My warning): then how (terrible) was My rejection (of them)?
text_en_pickthall: And verily those before them denied, then (see) the manner of My wrath (with them)!
text_en_arberry: Those that were before them also cried lies; then how was My horror!

text_ar: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ إِلَى ٱلطَّيْرِ فَوْقَهُمْ صَٰٓفَّٰتٍۢ وَيَقْبِضْنَ ۚ مَا يُمْسِكُهُنَّ إِلَّا ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍۭ بَصِيرٌ
text_en_primary: Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings? None holds them up except the Most Compassionate. Indeed, He is All-Seeing of everything.
text_en_yusufali: Do they not observe the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them in? None can uphold them except (God) Most Gracious: Truly (God) Most Gracious: Truly it is He that watches over all things.
text_en_pickthall: Have they not seen the birds above them spreading out their wings and closing them ? Naught upholdeth them save the Beneficent. Lo! He is Seer of all things.
text_en_arberry: Have they not regarded the birds above them spreading their wings, and closing them? Naught holds them but the All-merciful. Surely He sees everything.

text_ar: أَمَّنْ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى هُوَ جُندٌۭ لَّكُمْ يَنصُرُكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ۚ إِنِ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ إِلَّا فِى غُرُورٍ
text_en_primary: Also, which ˹powerless˺ force will come to your help instead of the Most Compassionate? Indeed, the disbelievers are only ˹lost˺ in delusion.
text_en_yusufali: Nay, who is there that can help you, (even as) an army, besides (God) Most Merciful? In nothing but delusion are the Unbelievers.
text_en_pickthall: Or who is he that will be an army unto you to help you instead of the Beneficent ? The disbelievers are in naught but illusion.
text_en_arberry: Or who is this that shall be a host for you to help you, apart from the All-merciful? The unbelievers are only in delusion.

text_ar: أَمَّنْ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى يَرْزُقُكُمْ إِنْ أَمْسَكَ رِزْقَهُۥ ۚ بَل لَّجُّوا۟ فِى عُتُوٍّۢ وَنُفُورٍ
text_en_primary: Or who is it that will provide for you if He withholds His provision? In fact, they persist in arrogance and aversion ˹to the truth˺.
text_en_yusufali: Or who is there that can provide you with Sustenance if He were to withhold His provision? Nay, they obstinately persist in insolent impiety and flight (from the Truth).
text_en_pickthall: Or who is he that will provide for you if He should withhold His providence ? Nay, but they are set in pride and frowardness.
text_en_arberry: Or who is this that shall provide for you if He withholds His provision? No, but they persist in disdain and aversion.

text_ar: أَفَمَن يَمْشِى مُكِبًّا عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِۦٓ أَهْدَىٰٓ أَمَّن يَمْشِى سَوِيًّا عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍۢ مُّسْتَقِيمٍۢ
text_en_primary: Who is ˹rightly˺ guided: the one who crawls facedown or the one who walks upright on the Straight Path?
text_en_yusufali: Is then one who walks headlong, with his face grovelling, better guided,- or one who walks evenly on a Straight Way?
text_en_pickthall: Is he who goeth groping on his face more rightly guided, or he who walketh upright on a straight road ?
text_en_arberry: What, is he who walks prone upon his face better guided than he who walks upright on a straight path?

text_ar: قُلْ هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَكُمْ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ وَٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةَ ۖ قَلِيلًۭا مَّا تَشْكُرُونَ
text_en_primary: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “He is the One Who brought you into being and gave you hearing, sight, and intellect. ˹Yet˺ you hardly give any thanks.”
text_en_yusufali: Say: "It is He Who has created you (and made you grow), and made for you the faculties of hearing, seeing, feeling and understanding: little thanks it is ye give.
text_en_pickthall: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): He it is who gave you being, and hath assigned unto you ears and eyes and hearts. Small thanks give ye!
text_en_arberry: Say: ’It is He who produced you, and appointed for you hearing and sight and hearts; little thanks you show!’

text_ar: قُلْ هُوَ ٱلَّذِى ذَرَأَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَإِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ
text_en_primary: ˹Also˺ say, “He is the One Who has dispersed you ˹all˺ over the earth, and to Him you will ˹all˺ be gathered.”
text_en_yusufali: Say: "It is He Who has multiplied you through the earth, and to Him shall ye be gathered together."
text_en_pickthall: Say: He it is Who multiplieth you in the earth, and unto Whom ye will be gathered.
text_en_arberry: Say: ’It is He who scattered you in the earth, and unto Him you shall be mustered.’

text_ar: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
text_en_primary: ˹Still˺ they ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass, if what you say is true?”
text_en_yusufali: They ask: When will this promise be (fulfilled)? - If ye are telling the truth.
text_en_pickthall: And they say: When (will) this promise (be fulfilled), if ye are truthful ?
text_en_arberry: They say, ’When shall this promise come to pass, if you speak truly?’

text_ar: قُلْ إِنَّمَا ٱلْعِلْمُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَإِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ نَذِيرٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
text_en_primary: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “That knowledge is with Allah alone, and I am only sent with a clear warning.”
text_en_yusufali: Say: "As to the knowledge of the time, it is with God alone: I am (sent) only to warn plainly in public."
text_en_pickthall: Say: The knowledge is with Allah only, and I am but a plain warner;
text_en_arberry: Say: ’The knowledge is with God; I am only a clear warner.’

text_ar: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ زُلْفَةًۭ سِيٓـَٔتْ وُجُوهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَقِيلَ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَدَّعُونَ
text_en_primary: Then when they see the torment drawing near, the faces of the disbelievers will become gloomy, and it will be said ˹to them˺, “This is what you claimed would never come.”
text_en_yusufali: At length, when they see it close at hand, grieved will be the faces of the Unbelievers, and it will be said (to them): "This is (the promise fulfilled), which ye were calling for!"
text_en_pickthall: But when they see it nigh, the faces of those who disbelieve will be awry, and it will be said (unto them): This is that for which ye used to call.
text_en_arberry: Then, when they see it nigh at hand, the faces of the unbelievers will be vexed, and it will be said, ’This is what you were promised.’

text_ar: قُلْ أَرَءَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَهْلَكَنِىَ ٱللَّهُ وَمَن مَّعِىَ أَوْ رَحِمَنَا فَمَن يُجِيرُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍۢ
text_en_primary: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Consider this: whether Allah causes me and those with me to die or shows us mercy, who will save the disbelievers from a painful punishment?”
text_en_yusufali: Say: "See ye?- If God were to destroy me, and those with me, or if He bestows His Mercy on us,- yet who can deliver the Unbelievers from a grievous Penalty?"
text_en_pickthall: Say (O Muhammad): Have ye thought: Whether Allah causeth me (Muhammad) and those with me to perish or hath mercy on us, still, who will protect the disbelievers from a painful doom ?
text_en_arberry: Say: ’What think you? If God destroys me and those with me, or has mercy on us, then who will protect the unbelievers from a painful chastisement?’

text_ar: قُلْ هُوَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ وَعَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْنَا ۖ فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ هُوَ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
text_en_primary: Say, “He is the Most Compassionate—in Him ˹alone˺ we believe, and in Him ˹alone˺ we trust. You will soon know who is clearly astray.”
text_en_yusufali: Say: "He is (God) Most Gracious: We have believed in Him, and on Him have we put our trust: So, soon will ye know which (of us) it is that is in manifest error."
text_en_pickthall: Say: He is the Beneficent. In Him we believe and in Him we put our trust. And ye will soon know who it is that is in error manifest.
text_en_arberry: Say: ’He is the All-merciful. We believe in Him, and in Him we put all our trust. Assuredly, you will soon, know who is in manifest error.

text_ar: قُلْ أَرَءَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَصْبَحَ مَآؤُكُمْ غَوْرًۭا فَمَن يَأْتِيكُم بِمَآءٍۢ مَّعِينٍۭ
text_en_primary: Say, “Consider this: if your water were to sink ˹into the earth˺, then who ˹else˺ could bring you flowing water?”
text_en_yusufali: Say: "See ye?- If your stream be some morning lost (in the underground earth), who then can supply you with clear-flowing water?"
text_en_pickthall: Say: Have ye thought: If (all) your water were to disappear into the earth, who then could bring you gushing water ?
text_en_arberry: Say: ’What think you? If in the morning your water should have vanished into the earth, then who would bring you running water?’

text_ar: نٓ ۚ وَٱلْقَلَمِ وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ
text_en_primary: Nũn. By the pen and what everyone writes!
text_en_yusufali: Nun. By the Pen and the (Record) which (men) write,-
text_en_pickthall: Nun. By the pen and that which they write (therewith),
text_en_arberry: Nun. By the Pen, and what they inscribe,

text_ar: مَآ أَنتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍۢ
text_en_primary: By the grace of your Lord, you ˹O Prophet˺ are not insane.
text_en_yusufali: Thou art not, by the Grace of thy Lord, mad or possessed.
text_en_pickthall: Thou art not, for thy Lord’s favour unto thee, a madman.
text_en_arberry: thou art not, by the blessing of thy Lord, a man possessed.

text_ar: وَإِنَّ لَكَ لَأَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍۢ
text_en_primary: You will certainly have a never-ending reward.
text_en_yusufali: Nay, verily for thee is a Reward unfailing:
text_en_pickthall: And lo! thine verily will be a reward unfailing.
text_en_arberry: Surely thou shalt have a wage unfailing;

text_ar: وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍۢ
text_en_primary: And you are truly ˹a man˺ of outstanding character.
text_en_yusufali: And thou (standest) on an exalted standard of character.
text_en_pickthall: And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature.
text_en_arberry: surely thou art upon a mighty morality.

text_ar: فَسَتُبْصِرُ وَيُبْصِرُونَ
text_en_primary: Soon you and the pagans will see,
text_en_yusufali: Soon wilt thou see, and they will see,
text_en_pickthall: And thou wilt see and they will see
text_en_arberry: So thou shalt see, and they will see,

text_ar: بِأَييِّكُمُ ٱلْمَفْتُونُ
text_en_primary: which of you is mad.
text_en_yusufali: Which of you is afflicted with madness.
text_en_pickthall: Which of you is the demented.
text_en_arberry: which of you is the demented.

text_ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُهْتَدِينَ
text_en_primary: Surely your Lord ˹alone˺ knows best who has strayed from His Way and who is ˹rightly˺ guided.
text_en_yusufali: Verily it is thy Lord that knoweth best, which (among men) hath strayed from His Path: and He knoweth best those who receive (true) Guidance.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! thy Lord is Best Aware of him who strayeth from His way, and He is Best Aware of those who walk aright.
text_en_arberry: Surely thy Lord knows very well those who have gone astray from His way, and He knows very well those who are guided.

text_ar: فَلَا تُطِعِ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
text_en_primary: So do not give in to the deniers.
text_en_yusufali: So hearken not to those who deny (the Truth).
text_en_pickthall: Therefor obey not thou the rejecters
text_en_arberry: So obey thou not those who cry lies.

text_ar: وَدُّوا۟ لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ
text_en_primary: They wish you would compromise so they would yield ˹to you˺.
text_en_yusufali: Their desire is that thou shouldst be pliant: so would they be pliant.
text_en_pickthall: Who would have had thee compromise, that they may compromise.
text_en_arberry: They wish that thou shouldst compromise, then they would compromise.

text_ar: وَلَا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍۢ مَّهِينٍ
text_en_primary: And do not obey the despicable, vain oath-taker,
text_en_yusufali: Heed not the type of despicable men,- ready with oaths,
text_en_pickthall: Neither obey thou each feeble oath-monger,
text_en_arberry: And obey thou not every mean swearer,

text_ar: هَمَّازٍۢ مَّشَّآءٍۭ بِنَمِيمٍۢ
text_en_primary: slanderer, gossip-monger,
text_en_yusufali: A slanderer, going about with calumnies,
text_en_pickthall: Detracter, spreader abroad of slanders,
text_en_arberry: backbiter, going about with slander,

text_ar: مَّنَّاعٍۢ لِّلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ
text_en_primary: withholder of good, transgressor, evildoer,
text_en_yusufali: (Habitually) hindering (all) good, transgressing beyond bounds, deep in sin,
text_en_pickthall: Hinderer of the good, transgressor, malefactor
text_en_arberry: hinderer of good, guilty aggressor, coarse-grained,

text_ar: عُتُلٍّۭ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ زَنِيمٍ
text_en_primary: brute, and—on top of all that—an illegitimate child.
text_en_yusufali: Violent (and cruel),- with all that, base-born,-
text_en_pickthall: Greedy therewithal, intrusive.
text_en_arberry: moreover ignoble,

text_ar: أَن كَانَ ذَا مَالٍۢ وَبَنِينَ
text_en_primary: Now, ˹simply˺ because he has been blessed with ˹abundant˺ wealth and children,
text_en_yusufali: Because he possesses wealth and (numerous) sons.
text_en_pickthall: It is because he is possessed of wealth and children
text_en_arberry: because he has wealth and sons.

text_ar: إِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ ءَايَٰتُنَا قَالَ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
text_en_primary: whenever Our revelations are recited to him, he says, “Ancient fables!”
text_en_yusufali: When to him are rehearsed Our Signs, "Tales of the ancients", he cries!
text_en_pickthall: That, when Our revelations are recited unto him, he saith: Mere fables of the men of old.
text_en_arberry: When Our signs are recited to him, he says, ’Fairy-tales of the ancients!’

text_ar: سَنَسِمُهُۥ عَلَى ٱلْخُرْطُومِ
text_en_primary: We will soon mark his snout.
text_en_yusufali: Soon shall We brand (the beast) on the snout!
text_en_pickthall: We shall brand him on the nose.
text_en_arberry: We shall brand him upon the muzzle!

text_ar: إِنَّا بَلَوْنَٰهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَآ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ إِذْ أَقْسَمُوا۟ لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ
text_en_primary: Indeed, We have tested those ˹Meccans˺ as We tested the owners of the garden—when they swore they would surely harvest ˹all˺ its fruit in the early morning,
text_en_yusufali: Verily We have tried them as We tried the People of the Garden, when they resolved to gather the fruits of the (garden) in the morning.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! We have tried them as We tried the owners of the garden when they vowed that they would pluck its fruit next morning,
text_en_arberry: Now We have tried them, even as We tried the owners of the garden when they swore they would pluck in the morning

text_ar: وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ
text_en_primary: leaving no thought for Allah’s Will.
text_en_yusufali: But made no reservation, ("If it be God’s Will").
text_en_pickthall: And made no exception (for the Will of Allah);
text_en_arberry: and they added not the saving words.

text_ar: فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَآئِفٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَآئِمُونَ
text_en_primary: Then it was struck by a torment from your Lord while they slept,
text_en_yusufali: Then there came on the (garden) a visitation from thy Lord, (which swept away) all around, while they were asleep.
text_en_pickthall: Then a visitation from thy Lord came upon it while they slept
text_en_arberry: Then a visitation from thy Lord visited it, while they were sleeping,

text_ar: فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَٱلصَّرِيمِ
text_en_primary: so it was reduced to ashes.
text_en_yusufali: So the (garden) became, by the morning, like a dark and desolate spot, (whose fruit had been gathered).
text_en_pickthall: And in the morning it was as if plucked.
text_en_arberry: and in the morning it was as if it were a garden plucked.

text_ar: فَتَنَادَوْا۟ مُصْبِحِينَ
text_en_primary: Then by daybreak they called out to each other,
text_en_yusufali: As the morning broke, they called out, one to another,-
text_en_pickthall: And they cried out one unto another in the morning,
text_en_arberry: In the morning they called to one another,

text_ar: أَنِ ٱغْدُوا۟ عَلَىٰ حَرْثِكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰرِمِينَ
text_en_primary: ˹saying,˺ “Go early to your harvest, if you want to pick ˹all˺ the fruit.”
text_en_yusufali: "Go ye to your tilth (betimes) in the morning, if ye would gather the fruits."
text_en_pickthall: Saying: Run unto your field if ye would pluck (the fruit).
text_en_arberry: ’Come forth betimes upon your tillage, if you would pluck!’

text_ar: فَٱنطَلَقُوا۟ وَهُمْ يَتَخَٰفَتُونَ
text_en_primary: So they went off, whispering to one another,
text_en_yusufali: So they departed, conversing in secret low tones, (saying)-
text_en_pickthall: So they went off, saying one unto another in low tones:
text_en_arberry: So they departed, whispering together,

text_ar: أَن لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُم مِّسْكِينٌۭ
text_en_primary: “Do not let any poor person enter your garden today.”
text_en_yusufali: "Let not a single indigent person break in upon you into the (garden) this day."
text_en_pickthall: No needy man shall enter it to-day against you.
text_en_arberry: ’No needy man shall enter it today against your will.’

text_ar: وَغَدَوْا۟ عَلَىٰ حَرْدٍۢ قَٰدِرِينَ
text_en_primary: And they proceeded early, totally fixated on their purpose.
text_en_yusufali: And they opened the morning, strong in an (unjust) resolve.
text_en_pickthall: They went betimes, strong in (this) purpose.
text_en_arberry: And they went forth early, determined upon their purpose.

text_ar: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهَا قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا لَضَآلُّونَ
text_en_primary: But when they saw it ˹devastated˺, they cried, “We must have lost ˹our˺ way!
text_en_yusufali: But when they saw the (garden), they said: "We have surely lost our way:
text_en_pickthall: But when they saw it, they said: Lo! we are in error!
text_en_arberry: But when they saw it, they said, ’Surely we are gone astray;

text_ar: بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ
text_en_primary: In fact, we have been deprived ˹of our livelihood˺.”
text_en_yusufali: "Indeed we are shut out (of the fruits of our labour)!"
text_en_pickthall: Nay, but we are desolate!
text_en_arberry: nay, rather we have been robbed!’

text_ar: قَالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ لَوْلَا تُسَبِّحُونَ
text_en_primary: The most sensible of them said, “Did I not urge you to say, ‘Allah willing.’?”
text_en_yusufali: Said one of them, more just (than the rest): "Did I not say to you, ’Why not glorify (God)?’"
text_en_pickthall: The best among them said: Said I not unto you: Why glorify ye not (Allah) ?
text_en_arberry: Said the most moderate of them, ’Did I not say to you, "Why do you not give glory?"’

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ سُبْحَٰنَ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
text_en_primary: They replied, “Glory be to our Lord! We have truly been wrongdoers.”
text_en_yusufali: They said: "Glory to our Lord! Verily we have been doing wrong!"
text_en_pickthall: They said: Glorified be our Lord! Lo! we have been wrong-doers.
text_en_arberry: They said, ’Glory be to God, our Lord; truly, we were evildoers.’

text_ar: فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ يَتَلَٰوَمُونَ
text_en_primary: Then they turned on each other, throwing blame.
text_en_yusufali: Then they turned, one against another, in reproach.
text_en_pickthall: Then some of them drew near unto others, self-reproaching.
text_en_arberry: And they advanced one upon another, blaming each other.

text_ar: قَالُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا طَٰغِينَ
text_en_primary: They said, “Woe to us! We have certainly been transgressors.
text_en_yusufali: They said: "Alas for us! We have indeed transgressed!
text_en_pickthall: They said: Alas for us! In truth we were outrageous.
text_en_arberry: They said, ’Woe, alas for us! Truly, we were insolent.

text_ar: عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًۭا مِّنْهَآ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَٰغِبُونَ
text_en_primary: We trust our Lord will give us a better garden than this, ˹for˺ we are indeed turning to our Lord with hope.”
text_en_yusufali: "It may be that our Lord will give us in exchange a better (garden) than this: for we do turn to Him (in repentance)!"
text_en_pickthall: It may be that our Lord will give us better than this in place thereof. Lo! we beseech our Lord.
text_en_arberry: It may be that our Lord will give us in exchange a better than it; to our Lord we humbly turn.’

text_ar: كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْعَذَابُ ۖ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ ۚ لَوْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْلَمُونَ
text_en_primary: That is the ˹way of Our˺ punishment ˹in this world˺. But the punishment of the Hereafter is certainly far worse, if only they knew.
text_en_yusufali: Such is the Punishment (in this life); but greater is the Punishment in the Hereafter,- if only they knew!
text_en_pickthall: Such was the punishment. And verily the punishment of the Hereafter is greater if they did but know.
text_en_arberry: Such is the chastisement; and the chastisement of the world to come, is assuredly greater, did they but know.

text_ar: إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّٰتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
text_en_primary: Indeed, the righteous will have the Gardens of Bliss with their Lord.
text_en_yusufali: Verily, for the Righteous, are Gardens of Delight, in the Presence of their Lord.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! for those who keep from evil are gardens of bliss with their Lord.
text_en_arberry: Surely for the godfearing shall be Gardens of Bliss with their Lord.

text_ar: أَفَنَجْعَلُ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ كَٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
text_en_primary: Should We then treat those who have submitted like the wicked?
text_en_yusufali: Shall We then treat the People of Faith like the People of Sin?
text_en_pickthall: Shall We then treat those who have surrendered as We treat the guilty ?
text_en_arberry: What, shall we make those who have surrendered like to the sinners?

text_ar: مَا لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ
text_en_primary: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
text_en_yusufali: What is the matter with you? How judge ye?
text_en_pickthall: What aileth you ? How foolishly ye judge!
text_en_arberry: What ails you then, how you judge?

text_ar: أَمْ لَكُمْ كِتَٰبٌۭ فِيهِ تَدْرُسُونَ
text_en_primary: Or do you have a scripture, in which you read
text_en_yusufali: Or have ye a book through which ye learn-
text_en_pickthall: Or have ye a scripture wherein ye learn
text_en_arberry: Or have you a Book wherein you study?

text_ar: إِنَّ لَكُمْ فِيهِ لَمَا تَخَيَّرُونَ
text_en_primary: that you will have whatever you choose?
text_en_yusufali: That ye shall have, through it whatever ye choose?
text_en_pickthall: That ye shall indeed have all that ye choose ?
text_en_arberry: Surely therein you shall have whatever you choose!

text_ar: أَمْ لَكُمْ أَيْمَٰنٌ عَلَيْنَا بَٰلِغَةٌ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ ۙ إِنَّ لَكُمْ لَمَا تَحْكُمُونَ
text_en_primary: Or do you have oaths binding on Us until the Day of Judgment that you will have whatever you decide?
text_en_yusufali: Or have ye Covenants with Us to oath, reaching to the Day of Judgment, (providing) that ye shall have whatever ye shall demand?
text_en_pickthall: Or have ye a covenant on oath from Us that reacheth to the Day of Judgment, that yours shall be all that ye ordain ?
text_en_arberry: Or have you oaths from Us, reaching to the Day of Resurrection? Surely you shall have whatever you judge!

text_ar: سَلْهُمْ أَيُّهُم بِذَٰلِكَ زَعِيمٌ
text_en_primary: Ask them ˹O Prophet˺ which of them can guarantee all that.
text_en_yusufali: Ask thou of them, which of them will stand surety for that!
text_en_pickthall: Ask them (O Muhammad) which of them will vouch for that!
text_en_arberry: Ask them, which of them will guarantee that!

text_ar: أَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكَآءُ فَلْيَأْتُوا۟ بِشُرَكَآئِهِمْ إِن كَانُوا۟ صَٰدِقِينَ
text_en_primary: Or do they have associate-gods ˹supporting this claim˺? Then let them bring forth their associate-gods, if what they say is true.
text_en_yusufali: Or have they some "Partners" (in Godhead)? Then let them produce their "partners", if they are truthful!
text_en_pickthall: Or have they other gods ? Then let them bring their other gods if they are truthful
text_en_arberry: Or do they have associates? Then let them bring their associates, if they speak truly.

text_ar: يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَن سَاقٍۢ وَيُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ
text_en_primary: ˹Beware of˺ the Day the Shin ˹of Allah˺ will be bared, and the wicked will be asked to prostrate, but they will not be able to do so,
text_en_yusufali: The Day that the shin shall be laid bare, and they shall be summoned to bow in adoration, but they shall not be able,-
text_en_pickthall: On the day when it befalleth in earnest, and they are ordered to prostrate themselves but are not able,
text_en_arberry: Upon the day when the leg shall be bared, and they shall be summoned to bow themselves, but they cannot;

text_ar: خَٰشِعَةً أَبْصَٰرُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌۭ ۖ وَقَدْ كَانُوا۟ يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سَٰلِمُونَ
text_en_primary: with eyes downcast, totally covered with disgrace. For they were ˹always˺ called to prostrate ˹in the world˺ when they were fully capable ˹but they chose not to˺.
text_en_yusufali: Their eyes will be cast down,- ignominy will cover them; seeing that they had been summoned aforetime to bow in adoration, while they were whole, (and had refused).
text_en_pickthall: With eyes downcast, abasement stupefying them. And they had been summoned to prostrate themselves while they were yet unhurt.
text_en_arberry: humbled shall be their eyes, and abasement shall overspread them, for they had been summoned to bow themselves while they were whole.

text_ar: فَذَرْنِى وَمَن يُكَذِّبُ بِهَٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ ۖ سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُم مِّنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
text_en_primary: So leave to Me ˹O Prophet˺ those who reject this message. We will gradually draw them to destruction in ways they cannot comprehend.
text_en_yusufali: Then leave Me alone with such as reject this Message: by degrees shall We punish them from directions they perceive not.
text_en_pickthall: Leave Me (to deal) with those who give the lie to this pronouncement. We shall lead them on by steps from whence they know not.
text_en_arberry: So leave Me with him who cries lies to this discourse! We will draw them on little by little whence they know not;

text_ar: وَأُمْلِى لَهُمْ ۚ إِنَّ كَيْدِى مَتِينٌ
text_en_primary: I ˹only˺ delay their end for a while, but My planning is flawless.
text_en_yusufali: A (long) respite will I grant them: truly powerful is My Plan.
text_en_pickthall: Yet I bear with them, for lo! My scheme is firm
text_en_arberry: and I shall respite them -- assuredly My guile is sure.

text_ar: أَمْ تَسْـَٔلُهُمْ أَجْرًۭا فَهُم مِّن مَّغْرَمٍۢ مُّثْقَلُونَ
text_en_primary: Or are you asking them for a reward ˹for the message˺ so that they are overburdened by debt?
text_en_yusufali: Or is it that thou dost ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with a load of debt
text_en_pickthall: Or dost thou (Muhammad) ask a fee from them so that they are heavily taxed ?
text_en_arberry: Or askest thou them for a wage, and so they are weighed down with debt?

text_ar: أَمْ عِندَهُمُ ٱلْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ
text_en_primary: Or do they have access to ˹the Record in˺ the unseen, so they copy it ˹for all to see˺?
text_en_yusufali: Or that the Unseen is in their hands, so that they can write it down?
text_en_pickthall: Or is the Unseen theirs that they can write (thereof) ?
text_en_arberry: Or is the Unseen in their keeping, and so they are writing it down?

text_ar: فَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلْحُوتِ إِذْ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌۭ
text_en_primary: So be patient with your Lord’s decree, and do not be like ˹Jonah,˺ the Man of the Whale, who cried out ˹to Allah˺, in total distress.
text_en_yusufali: So wait with patience for the Command of thy Lord, and be not like the Companion of the Fish,- when he cried out in agony.
text_en_pickthall: But wait thou for thy Lord’s decree, and be not like him of the fish, who cried out in despair.
text_en_arberry: So be thou patient under the judgment of thy Lord, and be not as the Man of the Fish, when he called, choking inwardly.

text_ar: لَّوْلَآ أَن تَدَٰرَكَهُۥ نِعْمَةٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ لَنُبِذَ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌۭ
text_en_primary: Had he not been shown grace by his Lord, he would have certainly been cast onto the open ˹shore˺, still blameworthy.
text_en_yusufali: Had not Grace from his Lord reached him, he would indeed have been cast off on the naked shore, in disgrace.
text_en_pickthall: Had it not been that favour from his Lord had reached him he surely had been cast into the wilderness while he was reprobate.
text_en_arberry: Had there not overtaken him a blessing from his Lord he would have been cast upon the wilderness, being condemned.

text_ar: فَٱجْتَبَٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَجَعَلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
text_en_primary: Then his Lord chose him, making him one of the righteous.
text_en_yusufali: Thus did his Lord choose him and make him of the Company of the Righteous.
text_en_pickthall: But his Lord chose him and placed him among the righteous.
text_en_arberry: But his Lord had chosen him, and He placed him among the righteous.

text_ar: وَإِن يَكَادُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصَٰرِهِمْ لَمَّا سَمِعُوا۟ ٱلذِّكْرَ وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُۥ لَمَجْنُونٌۭ
text_en_primary: The disbelievers would almost cut you down with their eyes when they hear ˹you recite˺ the Reminder, and say, “He is certainly a madman.”
text_en_yusufali: And the Unbelievers would almost trip thee up with their eyes when they hear the Message; and they say: "Surely he is possessed!"
text_en_pickthall: And lo! those who disbelieve would fain disconcert thee with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say: Lo! he is indeed mad;
text_en_arberry: The unbelievers wellnigh strike thee down with their glances, when they hear the Reminder, and they say, ’Surely he is a man possessed!’

text_ar: وَمَا هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌۭ لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
text_en_primary: But it is simply a reminder to the whole world.
text_en_yusufali: But it is nothing less than a Message to all the worlds.
text_en_pickthall: When it is naught else than a Reminder to creation.
text_en_arberry: And it is nothing but a Reminder unto all beings.

text_ar: ٱلْحَآقَّةُ
text_en_primary: The Inevitable Hour!
text_en_yusufali: The Sure Reality!
text_en_pickthall: The Reality!
text_en_arberry: The Indubitable!

text_ar: مَا ٱلْحَآقَّةُ
text_en_primary: What is the Inevitable Hour?
text_en_yusufali: What is the Sure Reality?
text_en_pickthall: What is the Reality ?
text_en_arberry: What is the Indubitable?

text_ar: وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا ٱلْحَآقَّةُ
text_en_primary: And what will make you realize what the Inevitable Hour is?
text_en_yusufali: And what will make thee realise what the Sure Reality is?
text_en_pickthall: Ah, what will convey unto thee what the reality is!
text_en_arberry: And what will teach thee what is the Indubitable?

text_ar: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وَعَادٌۢ بِٱلْقَارِعَةِ
text_en_primary: ˹Both˺ Thamûd and ’Ȃd denied the Striking Disaster.
text_en_yusufali: The Thamud and the ’Ad People (branded) as false the Stunning Calamity!
text_en_pickthall: (The tribes of) Thamud and A’ad disbelieved in the judgment to come.
text_en_arberry: Thamood and Ad cried lies to the Clatterer.

text_ar: فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا۟ بِٱلطَّاغِيَةِ
text_en_primary: As for Thamûd, they were destroyed by an overwhelming blast.
text_en_yusufali: But the Thamud,- they were destroyed by a terrible Storm of thunder and lightning!
text_en_pickthall: As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the lightning.
text_en_arberry: As for Thamood, they were destroyed by the Screamer;

text_ar: وَأَمَّا عَادٌۭ فَأُهْلِكُوا۟ بِرِيحٍۢ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍۢ
text_en_primary: And as for ’Ȃd, they were destroyed by a furious, bitter wind
text_en_yusufali: And the ’Ad, they were destroyed by a furious Wind, exceedingly violent;
text_en_pickthall: And as for A’ad, they were destroyed by a fierce roaring wind,
text_en_arberry: and as for Ad, they were destroyed by a wind clamorous,

text_ar: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍۢ وَثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًۭا فَتَرَى ٱلْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍۢ
text_en_primary: which Allah unleashed on them non-stop for seven nights and eight days, so that you would have seen its people lying dead like trunks of uprooted palm trees.
text_en_yusufali: He made it rage against them seven nights and eight days in succession: so that thou couldst see the (whole) people lying prostrate in its (path), as they had been roots of hollow palm-trees tumbled down!
text_en_pickthall: Which He imposed on them for seven long nights and eight long days so that thou mightest have seen men lying overthrown, as they were hollow trunks of palm-trees.
text_en_arberry: violent that He compelled against them seven nights and eight days, uninterruptedly, and thou mightest see the people laid prostrate in it as if they were the stumps of fallen down palm-trees.

text_ar: فَهَلْ تَرَىٰ لَهُم مِّنۢ بَاقِيَةٍۢ
text_en_primary: Do you see any of them left alive?
text_en_yusufali: Then seest thou any of them left surviving?
text_en_pickthall: Canst thou (O Muhammad) see any remnant of them ?
text_en_arberry: Now dost thou see any remnant of them?

text_ar: وَجَآءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَن قَبْلَهُۥ وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَٰتُ بِٱلْخَاطِئَةِ
text_en_primary: Also, Pharaoh and those before him, and ˹the people of˺ the overturned cities ˹of Lot˺ indulged in sin,
text_en_yusufali: And Pharaoh, and those before him, and the Cities Overthrown, committed habitual Sin.
text_en_pickthall: And Pharaoh and those before him, and the communities that were destroyed, brought error,
text_en_arberry: Pharaoh likewise, and those before him, and the Subverted Cities -- they committed error,

text_ar: فَعَصَوْا۟ رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةًۭ رَّابِيَةً
text_en_primary: each disobeying their Lord’s messenger, so He seized them with a crushing grip.
text_en_yusufali: And disobeyed (each) the apostle of their Lord; so He punished them with an abundant Penalty.
text_en_pickthall: And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, therefor did He grip them with a tightening grip.
text_en_arberry: and they rebelled against the Messenger of their Lord, and He seized them with a surpassing grip.

text_ar: إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَا ٱلْمَآءُ حَمَلْنَٰكُمْ فِى ٱلْجَارِيَةِ
text_en_primary: Indeed, when the floodwater had overflowed, We carried you in the floating Ark ˹with Noah˺,
text_en_yusufali: We, when the water (of Noah’s Flood) overflowed beyond its limits, carried you (mankind), in the floating (Ark),
text_en_pickthall: Lo! when the waters rose, We carried you upon the ship
text_en_arberry: Lo, when the waters rose, We bore you in the running ship

text_ar: لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةًۭ وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنٌۭ وَٰعِيَةٌۭ
text_en_primary: so that We may make this a reminder to you, and that attentive ears may grasp it.
text_en_yusufali: That We might make it a Message unto you, and that ears (that should hear the tale and) retain its memory should bear its (lessons) in remembrance.
text_en_pickthall: That We might make it a memorial for you, and that remembering ears (that heard the story) might remember.
text_en_arberry: that We might make it a reminder for you and for heeding ears to hold.

text_ar: فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌۭ وَٰحِدَةٌۭ
text_en_primary: At last, when the Trumpet will be blown with one blast,
text_en_yusufali: Then, when one blast is sounded on the Trumpet,
text_en_pickthall: And when the trumpet shall sound one blast
text_en_arberry: So, when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast

text_ar: وَحُمِلَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ
text_en_primary: and the earth and mountains will be lifted up and crushed with one blow,
text_en_yusufali: And the earth is moved, and its mountains, and they are crushed to powder at one stroke,-
text_en_pickthall: And the earth with the mountains shall be lifted up and crushed with one crash,
text_en_arberry: and the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with a single blow,

text_ar: فَيَوْمَئِذٍۢ وَقَعَتِ ٱلْوَاقِعَةُ
text_en_primary: on that Day the Inevitable Event will have come to pass.
text_en_yusufali: On that Day shall the (Great) Event come to pass.
text_en_pickthall: Then, on that day will the Event befall.
text_en_arberry: then, on that day, the Terror shall come to pass,

text_ar: وَٱنشَقَّتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَهِىَ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ وَاهِيَةٌۭ
text_en_primary: The sky will then be so torn that it will be frail,
text_en_yusufali: And the sky will be rent asunder, for it will that Day be flimsy,
text_en_pickthall: And the heaven will split asunder, for that day it will be frail.
text_en_arberry: and heaven shall be split, for upon that day it shall be very frail,

text_ar: وَٱلْمَلَكُ عَلَىٰٓ أَرْجَآئِهَا ۚ وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ ثَمَٰنِيَةٌۭ
text_en_primary: with the angels on its sides. On that Day eight ˹mighty angels˺ will bear the Throne of your Lord above them.
text_en_yusufali: And the angels will be on its sides, and eight will, that Day, bear the Throne of thy Lord above them.
text_en_pickthall: And the angels will be on the sides thereof, and eight will uphold the Throne of thy Lord that day, above them.
text_en_arberry: and the angels shall stand upon its borders, and upon that day eight shall carry above them the Throne of thy Lord.

text_ar: يَوْمَئِذٍۢ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌۭ
text_en_primary: You will then be presented ˹before Him for judgment˺, and none of your secrets will stay hidden.
text_en_yusufali: That Day shall ye be brought to Judgment: not an act of yours that ye hide will be hidden.
text_en_pickthall: On that day ye will be exposed; not a secret of you will be hidden.
text_en_arberry: On that day you shall be exposed, not one secret of yours concealed.

text_ar: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ هَآؤُمُ ٱقْرَءُوا۟ كِتَٰبِيَهْ
text_en_primary: As for those given their records in their right hand, they will cry ˹happily˺, “Here ˹everyone˺! Read my record!
text_en_yusufali: Then he that will be given his Record in his right hand will say: "Ah here! Read ye my Record!
text_en_pickthall: Then, as for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: Take, read my book!
text_en_arberry: Then as for him who is given his book in his right hand, he shall say, ’Here, take and read my book!

text_ar: إِنِّى ظَنَنتُ أَنِّى مُلَٰقٍ حِسَابِيَهْ
text_en_primary: I surely knew I would face my reckoning.”
text_en_yusufali: "I did really understand that my Account would (One Day) reach me!"
text_en_pickthall: Surely I knew that I should have to meet my reckoning.
text_en_arberry: Certainly I thought that I should encounter my reckoning.’

text_ar: فَهُوَ فِى عِيشَةٍۢ رَّاضِيَةٍۢ
text_en_primary: They will be in a life of bliss,
text_en_yusufali: And he will be in a life of Bliss,
text_en_pickthall: Then he will be in blissful state
text_en_arberry: So he shall be in a pleasing life

text_ar: فِى جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍۢ
text_en_primary: in an elevated Garden,
text_en_yusufali: In a Garden on high,
text_en_pickthall: In a high garden
text_en_arberry: in a lofty Garden,

text_ar: قُطُوفُهَا دَانِيَةٌۭ
text_en_primary: whose fruit will hang within reach.
text_en_yusufali: The Fruits whereof (will hang in bunches) low and near.
text_en_pickthall: Whereof the clusters are in easy reach.
text_en_arberry: its clusters nigh to gather.

text_ar: كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ هَنِيٓـًٔۢا بِمَآ أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِى ٱلْأَيَّامِ ٱلْخَالِيَةِ
text_en_primary: ˹They will be told,˺ “Eat and drink joyfully for what you did in the days gone by.”
text_en_yusufali: "Eat ye and drink ye, with full satisfaction; because of the (good) that ye sent before you, in the days that are gone!"
text_en_pickthall: (And it will be said unto those therein): Eat and drink at ease for that which ye sent on before you in past days.
text_en_arberry: ’Eat and drink with wholesome appetite for that you did long ago, in the days gone by.’

text_ar: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِشِمَالِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيْتَنِى لَمْ أُوتَ كِتَٰبِيَهْ
text_en_primary: And as for those given their record in their left hand, they will cry ˹bitterly˺, “I wish I had not been given my record,
text_en_yusufali: And he that will be given his Record in his left hand, will say: "Ah! Would that my Record had not been given to me!
text_en_pickthall: But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say: Oh, would that I had not been given my book
text_en_arberry: But as for him who is given his book in his left hand, he shall say, ’Would that I had not been given my book

text_ar: وَلَمْ أَدْرِ مَا حِسَابِيَهْ
text_en_primary: nor known anything of my reckoning!
text_en_yusufali: "And that I had never realised how my account (stood)!
text_en_pickthall: And knew not what my reckoning!
text_en_arberry: and not known my reckoning!

text_ar: يَٰلَيْتَهَا كَانَتِ ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ
text_en_primary: I wish death was the end!
text_en_yusufali: "Ah! Would that (Death) had made an end of me!
text_en_pickthall: Oh, would that it had been death!
text_en_arberry: Would it had been the end!

text_ar: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّى مَالِيَهْ ۜ
text_en_primary: My wealth has not benefited me!
text_en_yusufali: "Of no profit to me has been my wealth!
text_en_pickthall: My wealth hath not availed me,
text_en_arberry: My wealth has not availed me,

text_ar: هَلَكَ عَنِّى سُلْطَٰنِيَهْ
text_en_primary: My authority has been stripped from me.”
text_en_yusufali: "My power has perished from me!"...
text_en_pickthall: My power hath gone from me.
text_en_arberry: my authority is gone from me.’

text_ar: خُذُوهُ فَغُلُّوهُ
text_en_primary: ˹It will be said,˺ “Seize and shackle them,
text_en_yusufali: (The stern command will say): "Seize ye him, and bind ye him,
text_en_pickthall: (It will be said): Take him and fetter him
text_en_arberry: ’Take him, and fetter him,

text_ar: ثُمَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ
text_en_primary: then burn them in Hell,
text_en_yusufali: "And burn ye him in the Blazing Fire.
text_en_pickthall: And then expose him to hell-fire
text_en_arberry: and then roast him in Hell,

text_ar: ثُمَّ فِى سِلْسِلَةٍۢ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعًۭا فَٱسْلُكُوهُ
text_en_primary: then tie them up with chains seventy arms long.
text_en_yusufali: "Further, make him march in a chain, whereof the length is seventy cubits!
text_en_pickthall: And then insert him in a chain whereof the length is seventy cubits.
text_en_arberry: then in a chain of seventy cubits’ length insert him!

text_ar: إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
text_en_primary: For they never had faith in Allah, the Greatest,
text_en_yusufali: "This was he that would not believe in God Most High.
text_en_pickthall: Lo! He used not to believe in Allah the Tremendous,
text_en_arberry: Behold, he never believed in God the All-mighty,

text_ar: وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ
text_en_primary: nor encouraged the feeding of the poor.
text_en_yusufali: "And would not encourage the feeding of the indigent!
text_en_pickthall: And urged not on the feeding of the wretched.
text_en_arberry: and he never urged the feeding of the needy;

text_ar: فَلَيْسَ لَهُ ٱلْيَوْمَ هَٰهُنَا حَمِيمٌۭ
text_en_primary: So this Day they will have no close friend here,
text_en_yusufali: "So no friend hath he here this Day.
text_en_pickthall: Therefor hath he no lover here this day,
text_en_arberry: therefore he today has not here one loyal friend,

text_ar: وَلَا طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍۢ
text_en_primary: nor any food except ˹oozing˺ pus,
text_en_yusufali: "Nor hath he any food except the corruption from the washing of wounds,
text_en_pickthall: Nor any food save filth
text_en_arberry: neither any food saving foul pus,

text_ar: لَّا يَأْكُلُهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱلْخَٰطِـُٔونَ
text_en_primary: which none will eat except the evildoers.”
text_en_yusufali: "Which none do eat but those in sin."
text_en_pickthall: Which none but sinners eat.
text_en_arberry: that none excepting the sinners eat.’

text_ar: فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُونَ
text_en_primary: Now, I do swear by whatever you see,
text_en_yusufali: So I do call to witness what ye see,
text_en_pickthall: But nay! I swear by all that ye see
text_en_arberry: No! I swear by that you see

text_ar: وَمَا لَا تُبْصِرُونَ
text_en_primary: and whatever you cannot see!
text_en_yusufali: And what ye see not,
text_en_pickthall: And all that ye see not
text_en_arberry: and by that you do not see,

text_ar: إِنَّهُۥ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍۢ كَرِيمٍۢ
text_en_primary: Indeed, this ˹Quran˺ is the recitation of a noble Messenger.
text_en_yusufali: That this is verily the word of an honoured apostle;
text_en_pickthall: That it is indeed the speech of an illustrious messenger.
text_en_arberry: it is the speech of a noble Messenger.

text_ar: وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍۢ ۚ قَلِيلًۭا مَّا تُؤْمِنُونَ
text_en_primary: It is not the prose of a poet ˹as you claim˺, ˹yet˺ you hardly have any faith.
text_en_yusufali: It is not the word of a poet: little it is ye believe!
text_en_pickthall: It is not poet’s speech - little is it that ye believe!
text_en_arberry: It is not the speech of a poet (little do you believe)

text_ar: وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍۢ ۚ قَلِيلًۭا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ
text_en_primary: Nor is it the mumbling of a fortune-teller, ˹yet˺ you are hardly mindful.
text_en_yusufali: Nor is it the word of a soothsayer: little admonition it is ye receive.
text_en_pickthall: Nor diviner’s speech - little is it that ye remember!
text_en_arberry: nor the speech of a soothsayer (little do you remember).

text_ar: تَنزِيلٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
text_en_primary: ˹It is˺ a revelation from the Lord of all worlds.
text_en_yusufali: (This is) a Message sent down from the Lord of the Worlds.
text_en_pickthall: It is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds.
text_en_arberry: A sending down from the Lord of all Being.

text_ar: وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنَا بَعْضَ ٱلْأَقَاوِيلِ
text_en_primary: Had the Messenger made up something in Our Name,
text_en_yusufali: And if the apostle were to invent any sayings in Our name,
text_en_pickthall: And if he had invented false sayings concerning Us,
text_en_arberry: Had he invented against Us any sayings,

text_ar: لَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِٱلْيَمِينِ
text_en_primary: We would have certainly seized him by his right hand,
text_en_yusufali: We should certainly seize him by his right hand,
text_en_pickthall: We assuredly had taken him by the right hand
text_en_arberry: We would have seized him by the right hand,

text_ar: ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنَا مِنْهُ ٱلْوَتِينَ
text_en_primary: then severed his aorta,
text_en_yusufali: And We should certainly then cut off the artery of his heart:
text_en_pickthall: And then severed his life-artery,
text_en_arberry: then We would surely have cut his life-vein

text_ar: فَمَا مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَٰجِزِينَ
text_en_primary: and none of you could have shielded him ˹from Us˺!
text_en_yusufali: Nor could any of you withhold him (from Our wrath).
text_en_pickthall: And not one of you could have held Us off from him.
text_en_arberry: and not one of you could have defended him.

text_ar: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَتَذْكِرَةٌۭ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
text_en_primary: Indeed, this ˹Quran˺ is a reminder to those mindful ˹of Allah˺.
text_en_yusufali: But verily this is a Message for the God-fearing.
text_en_pickthall: And lo! it is a warrant unto those who ward off (evil).
text_en_arberry: Surely it is a Reminder to the godfearing;

text_ar: وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنكُم مُّكَذِّبِينَ
text_en_primary: And We certainly know that some of you will persist in denial,
text_en_yusufali: And We certainly know that there are amongst you those that reject (it).
text_en_pickthall: And lo! We know that some among you will deny (it).
text_en_arberry: but We know that some of you will cry lies.

text_ar: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
text_en_primary: and it will surely be a source of regret for the disbelievers.
text_en_yusufali: But truly (Revelation) is a cause of sorrow for the Unbelievers.
text_en_pickthall: And lo! it is indeed an anguish for the disbelievers.
text_en_arberry: Surely it is a sorrow to the unbelievers;

text_ar: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَحَقُّ ٱلْيَقِينِ
text_en_primary: And indeed, this ˹Quran˺ is the absolute truth.
text_en_yusufali: But verily it is Truth of assured certainty.
text_en_pickthall: And lo! it is absolute truth.
text_en_arberry: yet indeed it is the truth of certainty.

text_ar: فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
text_en_primary: So glorify the Name of your Lord, the Greatest.
text_en_yusufali: So glorify the name of thy Lord Most High.
text_en_pickthall: So glorify the name of thy Tremendous Lord.
text_en_arberry: Then magnify the Name of thy Lord, the All-mighty.

text_ar: سَأَلَ سَآئِلٌۢ بِعَذَابٍۢ وَاقِعٍۢ
text_en_primary: A challenger has demanded a punishment bound to come
text_en_yusufali: A questioner asked about a Penalty to befall-
text_en_pickthall: A questioner questioned concerning the doom about to fall
text_en_arberry: A questioner asked of a chastisement about to fall

text_ar: لِّلْكَٰفِرِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُۥ دَافِعٌۭ
text_en_primary: for the disbelievers—to be averted by none—
text_en_yusufali: The Unbelievers, the which there is none to ward off,-
text_en_pickthall: Upon the disbelievers, which none can repel,
text_en_arberry: for the unbelievers, which none may avert,

text_ar: مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ذِى ٱلْمَعَارِجِ
text_en_primary: from Allah, Lord of pathways of ˹heavenly˺ ascent,
text_en_yusufali: (A Penalty) from God, Lord of the Ways of Ascent.
text_en_pickthall: From Allah, Lord of the Ascending Stairways
text_en_arberry: from God, the Lord of the Stairways.

text_ar: تَعْرُجُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيْهِ فِى يَوْمٍۢ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُۥ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍۢ
text_en_primary: ˹through which˺ the angels and the ˹holy˺ spirit
text_en_yusufali: The angels and the spirit ascend unto him in a Day the measure whereof is (as) fifty thousand years:
text_en_pickthall: (Whereby) the angels and the Spirit ascend unto Him in a Day whereof the span is fifty thousand years.
text_en_arberry: To Him the angels and the Spirit mount up, in a day whereof the measure is fifty thousand years.

text_ar: فَٱصْبِرْ صَبْرًۭا جَمِيلًا
text_en_primary: So endure ˹this denial, O  Prophet,˺ with beautiful patience.
text_en_yusufali: Therefore do thou hold Patience,- a Patience of beautiful (contentment).
text_en_pickthall: But be patient (O Muhammad) with a patience fair to see.
text_en_arberry: So be thou patient with a sweet patience;

text_ar: إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُۥ بَعِيدًۭا
text_en_primary: They truly see this ˹Day˺ as impossible,
text_en_yusufali: They see the (Day) indeed as a far-off (event):
text_en_pickthall: Lo! they behold it afar off
text_en_arberry: behold, they see it as if far off;

text_ar: وَنَرَىٰهُ قَرِيبًۭا
text_en_primary: but We see it as inevitable.
text_en_yusufali: But We see it (quite) near.
text_en_pickthall: While we behold it nigh:
text_en_arberry: but We see it is nigh.

text_ar: يَوْمَ تَكُونُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ كَٱلْمُهْلِ
text_en_primary: On that Day the sky will be like molten brass
text_en_yusufali: The Day that the sky will be like molten brass,
text_en_pickthall: The day when the sky will become as molten copper,
text_en_arberry: Upon the day when heaven shall be as molten copper

text_ar: وَتَكُونُ ٱلْجِبَالُ كَٱلْعِهْنِ
text_en_primary: and the mountains like ˹tufts of˺ wool.
text_en_yusufali: And the mountains will be like wool,
text_en_pickthall: And the hills become as flakes of wool,
text_en_arberry: and the mountains shall be as plucked wool-tufts,

text_ar: وَلَا يَسْـَٔلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيمًۭا
text_en_primary: And no close friend will ask ˹about˺ their friends,
text_en_yusufali: And no friend will ask after a friend,
text_en_pickthall: And no familiar friend will ask a question of his friend
text_en_arberry: no loyal friend shall question loyal friend,

text_ar: يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ ۚ يَوَدُّ ٱلْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِى مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍۭ بِبَنِيهِ
text_en_primary: ˹although˺ they will be made to see each other. The wicked will wish to ransom themselves from the punishment of that Day by their children,
text_en_yusufali: Though they will be put in sight of each other,- the sinner’s desire will be: Would that he could redeem himself from the Penalty of that Day by (sacrificing) his children,
text_en_pickthall: Though they will be given sight of them. The guilty man will long to be able to ransom himself from the punishment of that day at the price of his children
text_en_arberry: as they are given sight of them. The sinner will wish that he might ransom himself from the chastisement of that day even by his sons,

text_ar: وَصَٰحِبَتِهِۦ وَأَخِيهِ
text_en_primary: their spouses, their siblings,
text_en_yusufali: His wife and his brother,
text_en_pickthall: And his spouse and his brother
text_en_arberry: his companion wife, his brother,

text_ar: وَفَصِيلَتِهِ ٱلَّتِى تُـْٔوِيهِ
text_en_primary: their clan that sheltered them,
text_en_yusufali: His kindred who sheltered him,
text_en_pickthall: And his kin that harboured him
text_en_arberry: his kin who sheltered him,

text_ar: وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
text_en_primary: and everyone on earth altogether, just to save themselves.
text_en_yusufali: And all, all that is on earth,- so it could deliver him:
